job.title: Manager, Talent Management
job.description:
Position Summary

The Manager, Talent Management, is responsible for building and maintaining the organization's talent architecture, development infrastructure and HR communications strategy.

This role serves as the enterprise owner of talent processes, learning and development systems, performance management architecture, Continuity Planning infrastructure and compliance training.

The Manager establishes the frameworks, systems, tools and resources that enable HR Business Partners and leaders to effectively develop, manage and retain talent within their businesses.

This role also provides strategic oversight of recruiting processes and partners closely with the Recruitment Consultant to deliver enterprise recruiting capability.

Key Responsibilities

Talent Acquisition

  • Own the enterprise recruiting framework,processesand standards. 
  • Establish recruiting practices,toolsand metrics.
  • Partner with the Recruitment Consultant on sourcing, recruiting execution and hard-to-fill positions.
  • Support workforce planning and recruitingstrategy.
  • Oversee employer brand and candidate experience. 
  • Coordinate recruiting campaigns, job fairs and community/HBCU recruiting partnerships. 
  • Partner with the Sports HRBP on seasonal and high-volume recruiting needs. 
  • Develop recruiting analytics and reporting. 
  • Identifyopportunities to improve recruiting technology and processes. 

Talent Development

  • Own the enterprise talent development framework. 
  • Develop andmaintaincareer development resources and programs. 
  • Partner with HRBPs toidentifydevelopment needs and translate them into enterprise learning solutions. 
  • Support leadershipdevelopment,architectureand programming.
  • Establish development resources for managers and employees. 
  • Connect learning opportunitiestotalent review and development planning.
  • Support enterprise skills development and emerging capability initiatives. 

Performance Management

Own the architecture; HRBPs deliver it in the businesses.

  • Own the enterprise performance management framework,processand calendar. 
  • Maintain performance management tools,templatesand resources.
  • Develop manager training and enablement. 
  • Support calibrationmethodologyand tools. 
  • Maintain performance management systems and processes. 
  • Analyze performance trends and recommend improvements. 
  • Partner with HRBPs on business implementation and manager support. 

Continuity Planning / Succession

Own the architecture; HRBPs facilitate business talent conversations.

  • Own the enterprise Continuity Planning framework and process. 
  • Develop tools forcritical roleidentification, talent assessment and successor readiness.
  • Maintain the annual talent review/continuity calendar. 
  • Build development planning resources connected to succession needs. 
  • Maintain enterprise reporting and tracking. 
  • Partner with HRBPs to ensure consistent application across businesses. 
  • Support enterprise-level talent discussions led by the VP HR. 

Learning & LMS

  • Own the enterprise LMS and learning framework. 
  • Coordinate required and compliance training. 
  • Develop learning pathways and resources. 
  • Track participation and completion. 
  • Evaluate learning effectiveness. 
  • Partner with HRBPs toidentifybusiness-specific learning needs. 
  • Support manager and leadership development programs. 

Compliance

  • Coordinate enterprise HR compliance training and tracking. 
  • Coordinate annual FCC Filing.
  • Maintain compliance training calendars. 
  • Partner with the Director, HR Operations and Legal/HR Specialist on compliance requirements. 
  • Support audits and documentation. 
  • Develop employee and manager communications related to compliance requirements. 
  • Monitor completion and escalate gaps. 

Qualifications

  • Bachelor'sdegreerequired.
  • SHRM or HRCI certification preferred.
  • 5+ years of progressive HR, talent, learning,recruitingor communications experience.
  • Demonstrated experience designing HR programs and processes. 
  • Strong project management skills. 
  • Experience with HR technology/LMS platforms. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to translate strategy into practical tools and programs. 
  • Experience working across multiple business units preferred.

Benefits: 

  • Competitive salary based on experience.
  • Benefits package including:
    1. Comprehensive health insurance plan options
    2. Vision and Dental Insurance
    3. Company sponsored life insurance
    4. Numerous voluntary benefit options – legal plans, pet insurance, discounted home and auto and more!
    5. 401K with company match
    6. Generous paid time off
    7. 9 paid company holidays
  • Opportunities for professional development and career growth.
  • Dynamic and inclusive work environment with a supportive team culture.
  • Exciting projects and growth opportunities within a leading organization.
  • Opportunities to attend free local events, such as sporting events, concerts, shows, and more.

job.title: Strategic Account Manager
job.description:

The Radio Account Executive for Audio and Digital is responsible for developing and growing key client relationships, driving revenue growth, and delivering customized advertising and marketing solutions for businesses. This role requires a strong understanding of audio, digital and event marketing and the importance of outstanding customer service. The Account Executive will deliver customized solutions that meet the growth objectives of clients and prospects, resulting in long-term partnerships.

Key Responsibilities

  • Self-motivated, results-driven, and highly organized.

job.title: Ticket Scanner
job.description:
Overview:

We are looking for friendly and detail-oriented individuals to join our team as a Ticket Scanner. In this role, you will be responsible for scanning and verifying tickets at stadium entry points, assisting guests with entry procedures, and ensuring a smooth and efficient gate operation. This is a great opportunity to be part of an exciting event experience while providing excellent customer service. This is a part-time, seasonal, event day position that will primarily support holiday and special events, with opportunities to work additional events throughout the year. 

Key Responsibilities and Essential Functions: 

  • Greet guests warmly and scan tickets using electronic scanning devices to verify entry.
  • Ensure tickets are valid and assist with any scanning or access issues.
  • Direct guests to appropriate seating areas, customer service booths, or other stadium locations as needed.
  • Monitor entry points to prevent unauthorized access and address any security concerns.
  • Provide information about venue policies, seating arrangements, event activities, and promotions.
  • Work closely with security and event staff to maintain a safe and organized entry process.
  • Assist guests with mobility challenges or special access needs.
  • Maintain a professional and positive attitude while handling large crowds.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications: 

  • Strong customer service and communication skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and handle large crowds efficiently.
  • Comfortable using electronic ticket scanners and basic technology.
  • Ability to stand for long periods and work outdoors in various weather conditions.
  • Availability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.

Physical Demands: 

  • This role requires the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, often for the entire duration of a shift (typically 4-6 hours per game, with potential for doubleheaders or extended events).
  • Must be able to remain standing at a designated gate or station with limited opportunity to sit.
  • Requires frequent repetitive hand and arm motions for scanning tickets, tearing stubs, and directing guests.
  • Must be able to occasionally lift or carry light items (under 20 lbs), such as a box of supplies, a stanchion, or a signage stand.
  • Needs the ability to bend, stoop, or reach to assist guests, pick up items, or manage entryway equipment.
  • Must possess sufficient manual dexterity to efficiently handle tickets, operate a handheld scanner or tablet, and make quick, accurate exchanges.

Work Conditions: 

  • This position works almost exclusively outdoors at stadium entry gate areas. You will be exposed to all seasonal weather conditions, including intense sun, heat, humidity, rain, and cold.
  • Hours are entirely event driven. This requires absolute availability for all home games, which include evenings, weekends, and holidays. Shifts typically begin 60-90 minutes before gates open and may extend through the end of the game. Flexibility for special events, rain delays, or double-headers is required.
  • Must adhere to all safety and security protocols, including bag check policies and crowd management procedures. You are expected to maintain a professional appearance and demeanor as a representative of the team.

Benefits: 

  • Opportunity to work in an exciting sports environment.
  • Complimentary Durham Bulls branded polo shirt

Pre-Employment Information:

  • A pre-employment drug screening is required. 
  • Capitol Broadcasting Company participates in E-Verify. 

EEO Statement:

Capitol Broadcasting Company is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

CBC Statement:

Capitol Broadcasting Company, Inc. is a diversified communications company which owns and/or operates WRAL-TV, WRAZ-TV, WRAL-FM, WRAL-HD2, WNGT-CD, WCMC-FM, WCMC-HD1, WDNC-AM, WCMC-HD2, WCMC-HD3, WCLY-AM, WCMC-HD4, Microspace, and WRAL Digital in Raleigh, NC; WILM-TV, WILT-LD and Sunrise Broadcasting in Wilmington, NC; The Durham Bulls Baseball Club, Bull City Hospitality, and Coastal Plain League in Durham, NC; The Holly Springs Salamanders in Holly Springs, NC; the American Underground startup hub in Durham, NC; and real estate interests including the American Tobacco Historic District in Durham, NC; Rocky Mount Mills in Rocky Mount, NC; MoJud Lofts in Greensboro, NC; and The Thread in Rock Hill, SC.

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance. 
 
Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-11-09 11:59 PM

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Your Role

If you want to push the boundaries of media technology and are excited by the challenge of bridging creativity with cutting-edge tech, this role is for you!

As a key member of the Architecture and Strategic Development (Media System Architecture) team, you will design and plan CBC/Radio-Canada’s future technology infrastructure. Our mission is to transform our disparate media workflows by integrating hybrid agents, video understanding systems and advanced artificial intelligence architectures operating 24/7.

We are looking for an AI Architect with deep technical expertise in optimizing training and inference for large language models (LLMs), multimodal models and AI systems in a media context. As a technical thought leader, you will design robust systems to make AI faster, more scalable and more reliable, ensuring their seamless integration into our critical production ecosystems (PAM, MAM, studios).

Your Responsibilities

Optimizing Models, Inference and GPU Infrastructure

  • Design and build high-performance training and inference systems for LLMs and multimodal AI models.
  • Optimize end-to-end training, including high throughput data pipelines (streaming, sharding, bucketing), distributed training (parallelism strategies) and mixed precision.
  • Optimize inference and serving engines to guarantee minimum latency using KV caching design/management, batching, quantization and long-context processing.
  • Collaborate with the Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team to design, right-size and evolve our internal GPU cluster into a new-generation infrastructure capable of supporting these massive workloads.

Strategy, Architecture and Media Ecosystem

  • Plan, develop and architect the integration of AI solutions within CBC/Radio-Canada’s media production environments (PAM, MAM, television and radio studios).
  • Evaluate and standardize integration protocols such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) architectures to interconnect our models with complex production platforms (Avid, Dalet, Adobe).
  • Ensure absolute data security while developing video understanding systems that can interact with both file-based workflows (codecs, wrappers) and IP live workflows (SMPTE‑2110).

Technical Leadership, Mentoring and MLOps

  • Provide expert guidance on system efficiency, spearheading initiatives to dramatically improve architectural scalability, latency and reliability.
  • Mentor and elevate the organization’s engineers and data scientists in large-scale ML system design and performance engineering.
  • Develop robust MLOps/LLMOps pipelines with a constant focus on observability, performance profiling and automated testing.
  • Summarize and explain technological innovations to make them understandable to decision-makers and production teams and influence our strategic investments.

Featured Technology Environment

  • Inference Modelling and Optimization: PyTorch, vLLM, DeepSpeed, Accelerate, KV caching architectures, quantization techniques.
  • Infrastructure, Cloud and Compute: internal GPU clusters, distributed architectures, AWS, Azure, GCP, containers, Kubernetes.
  • Orchestration and Agents: Open WebUI, integration protocols (MCP, A2A), LiteLLM, LangChain, LangGraph, Strands.
  • Media Production: SMPTE-2110 protocols, PAM/MAM (Avid Interplay, Dalet), Adobe suite, media processing (audio/video codecs).
  • MLOps and Observability: Langfuse, Weights & Biases (W&B), MLflow, performance profiling tools.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in software engineering, information technology, artificial intelligence, mathematics or a related natural science field.
  • Functional bilingualism (English and French) essential for Canada-wide communications.
  • At least five years’ proven experience developing and deploying AI/ML solutions.
  • At least eight years’ experience building tools and platforms in a software engineering role.
  • Demonstrated experience working with language models and designing solutions optimized for cost efficiency and scale.
  • Strong conceptual understanding of LLM, RAG and AI agent architectures, including their frameworks and operational constraints.
  • Experience selecting AI framework architectures (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch, Hugging Face), cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, GCP) and orchestration tools (Docker, Kubernetes) for scalable enterprise AI solutions.
  • Knowledge of ModelOps, AI engineering, DevOps and MLOps practices (including CI/CD pipelines).
  • Solid understanding of machine learning and deep learning fundamentals.
  • Strong technical documentation skills, with the ability to produce diagrams, demos and technical artifacts that make AI architectures understandable and actionable.
  • Hands-on technical experience working with media production platforms (MAM/PAM) and designing scalable solutions in a highly available, 24/7 environment.
  • Solid working knowledge of cloud technologies (AWS, Azure or GCP), virtualization, networking and storage.

Nice-to-Have Skills (Assets)

  • Experience with modern video software architectures (e.g., NVIDIA Holoscan for Media) or ultra-high-performance IP transfer protocols.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex workflows through cloud or hybrid data pipelines.
  • Active contributions to open-source high-performance AI projects and published research, or deep understanding of security frameworks for responsible AI.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.
 

We thank all applicants for their interest, but only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

As part of our recruitment process, candidates who advance to the next

step will be asked to complete a background check. This includes:  

  • A mandatory Criminal record check. 

  • Other background checks may be conducted based on the operational requirements of the position.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we all have a story to tell. What’s yours?

 

If you share our passion for Canadian storytelling, and you wish to help us engage with individuals and communities across our various digital platforms, this is where you’ll want to be!

 

Every day, you will have an opportunity to shape the way in which Canadians see themselves reflected in our digital services. Your work will have a direct impact on how millions of Canadians from various communities connect with our products, with one another, and with the diverse voices that make our country so unique.

 

You will have the opportunity to play a part in enlightening and entertaining Canadians through our innovative work in building the mediums that deliver our content. We are an innovative hub, where the talented professionals we work with are respected and valued for their contributions. Our product teams are vibrant and our work culture strives to achieve the highest standards of diversity and inclusion. We believe that hiring people with different career paths and backgrounds is fundamental in our shared success and in building healthy and highly performant teams.

 

When you join our mission, you are not only shaping the vision of CBC/Radio-Canada, but the future of our country.

 

We know that commitment to equity, inclusion and diversity is essential to creating content that mirrors and resonates with the rich and evolving makeup of our country.  We’re also committed to reaching out and connecting with our audience on multiple platforms this includes creating virtual places where communities can come together.


This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why is this role important?

 

You will be an important element of our over-the-top platform team. As such, working closely with the product owners, architects and technical managers, your role is to ensure the smooth execution of product front-end development and coordinate the technical work required to deliver requested features, while adhering to the standards and practices agreed to by the development management team.

 

The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.


Perks you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • Pair programming and mentorship opportunities, where you can learn from the best in the industry and help coach new talent.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.
  • An environment which favours experimentation and an iterative approach in order to achieve the highest form of technical innovation.

 

Your responsibilities:

  • Design and/or modify reusable components for Radio-Canada's digital platforms; such as the audio/video player.
  • Ensure compliance with standards and control the quality of the product throughout the project's execution.
  • Stay informed of new trends in the various fields of digital development.
  • By being proactive, propose solutions to the challenges encountered.
  • Participate in Agile Scrum activities designed to review ongoing production projects in order to make necessary corrections and adjustments, or completed projects to measure their results.
  • Participate in the development of user stories for our various products.
  • Ensure the good performance of developed applications to handle high loads.
  • Participate in sprint planning, retrospectives, and application deployments.
  • Participate in code reviews and solution deployments.

We are looking for a candidate matching the following profile:

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • At least 3 years of experience in software development.
  • Experience in developing complex and high-performance mobile applications.
  • Proficiency in Android Studio, Git, and the Kotlin language.
  • Experience in developing an application published on Google Play.
  • Experience in developing within code review context (pull request).
  • Knowledge of programming patterns (such as MVP or MVVM).
  • Knowledge of SOLID architecture principles is an asset.
  • Ability to read, produce, and adhere to software architecture diagrams (UML, sequence diagram, etc.).
  • Interest in working on an application available on multiple form factors (mobile/tablet/TV).
  • Knowledge of Jetpack Compose, Exoplayer, Kotlin Multiplatform is an asset.
  • Knowledge of the libraries Dagger, Hilt, Koin is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Google architecture components is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Maven (including the design/maintenance of internal libraries) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of audio-video broadcasting on the web (streaming) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of other programming languages is an asset.
  • Knowledge of design patterns is an asset.
  • Good general knowledge and strong intellectual curiosity (to acquire and develop new knowledge and skills).
  • Critical thinking (to question and propose new ideas).
  • A keen interest in the major trends and challenges of the digital world.
  • Meticulousness, independence, and resourcefulness.
  • Excellent stress management and priority setting.
  • Analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
  • Flexibility, initiative, and dynamism.
  • Ability to work in a team, excellent communicator.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) spoken and written is mandatory.

 

Please note that due to the nature of the mandates and responsibilities of this role, all candidates will be required to work in a multilingual environment, where business will be conducted in both official languages (English and French). Therefore, employees working in this role will be expected to make the required efforts and adjustments to navigate this multilingual environment in a respectful manner for all.

 

Please note this is a 12-month contract position, renewable annually. This regular position is not a consulting assignment but a long-term opportunity with attractive CBC/Radio-Canada employee benefits.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance. 
 
Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-11-08 11:59 PM

Your Role


ICI Windsor’s morning radio show Matins sans frontières is looking for a reporter assigned to arts and culture across all of our platforms, with a primary focus on radio. 


Your primary responsibility is to conceive and produce audio content focused on the culture and community life of the region, while occasionally adapting it into web and digital video formats with support.


Creative and curious, you know how to unearth original stories. You have a strong interest in community life, Franco-Ontarian arts and culture, and Francophone communities in all their diversity. Team-oriented and resilient under pressure, you have a thorough command of CBC/Radio-Canada’s journalistic standards and practices.


In this role, you will be the driving force behind our cultural and local engagement strategy. Your mission: design captivating audio and video content on the arts to engage and grow our audiences.


You embody and promote the values of inclusion and respect in the workplace. You are familiar with the population, communities, and culture of the Southwestern Ontario region.


This is a permanent, full-time position for a morning show. The shift is from 5:00 a.m. to 1:15 p.m., Monday to Friday, with a 30-minute lunch break. The successful candidate may be required to work overtime, and the schedule is subject to change based on operational needs.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Pitch story ideas and produce daily radio reports and/or interviews.
  • Build and maintain a network of contacts within the Francophone cultural and community sectors in Windsor, London, and the surrounding areas.
  • Monitor news related to the arts, cultural, and community sectors in Southwestern Ontario.
  • Occasionally adapt interviews and content for other platforms—such as the shows La billetterie and L’Escale culturelle—or into vertical videos and radio-visual content.
  • Participate in regional media editorial committees to highlight cultural content from the Windsor station.
  • Participate in coverage plans and special deployments as needed.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.


Your profile:

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • Three (3) years of directly relevant experience in the field.
  • Superior writing skills.
  • Proven ability to present interviews and reports on air.
  • Ability to select relevant, audience-focused stories that reflect issues being discussed by the general public.
  • Strong curiosity and the ability to easily build rapport with people.
  • In-depth knowledge of Southwestern Ontario’s cultural landscape.
  • Innovative mindset.
  • Ability to work in a high-pressure environment with tight deadlines.
  • Commitment to reflecting the community and its diversity.

This role requires full time on site presence. 


CBC News is designing new ways for Canadians to understand and navigate their finances, helping them make sense of a myriad of complex economic realities through expanded financial and consumer storytelling. 

To help audiences discover that content when they want it, on their platform of choice, we’re hiring a Senior Coordinating Producer to join the CBC Audience Growth team. This is an opportunity to help shape and grow a new destination for practical, news-you-can-use financial journalism.


In this role, you’ll sit right where editorial meets audience growth, collaborating with content teams across CBC News, Entertainment and Sports to make CBC a top destination for financial journalism and related content. 


You play a critical role in identifying new audiences, and advising on the best strategies and tactics to reach them across CBC digital properties, FAST channels, CBC Gem, CBC linear channels, as well as on third-party platforms including Youtube and Tik Tok. You understand how to move people beyond discoverability and into loyal audiences who actively engage with our content, whether subscribing to newsletters, engaging with content and sharing videos. You search for opportunities to reflect a broad range of perspectives and voices in the content we share. 


You are passionate about using audience insights to inform journalism decisions, capable of analyzing reach and engagement time and adjusting your tactics to ensure the best audience experience. You have knowledge of digital products, and our owned and operated, and third party platforms.

You are future-focused, open to experimenting with new technologies, audio/visual formats and content to meet changing audience needs. 


You’re a collaborator, able to work with everyone from  front-line journalists and program leaders, to colleagues across CBC genres to optimize CBC’s best digital, social, and broadcast journalism into one easy-to-find audience experience.


What you’ll do:

  • Own the digital publishing strategy for cross division financial reporting,  working in close association with the CBC News publishing team, including aggregation, packaging, lineup management and other direct publishing functions.
  • Help manage push alerts, newsletters, YouTube and TikTok packaging, alongside and as a part of the CBC News Audience Growth team. 
  • Play a key role in planning and live event plans for major financial and money-related journalism. As required, verify user-generated content to ensure accuracy.
  • Coordinate work with business unit content teams currently based in Calgary and Toronto, as well as audio syndication, current affairs and podcasting to ensure a smooth workflow between platforms.
  • Aggregate, showcase and promote financial, business and consumer content from CBC News, CBC Entertainment and CBC Sports.
  • Use data and analytics to shape our headlines, thumbnails, and rollout plans.
  • Guide, coach and support colleagues on best-of-practices and through change as required, across local and network newsrooms.
  • Ensure that CBC journalistic standards are met and that our stories are fair, balanced, accurate, thoughtful, immediate and resonate with the communities we serve. 

What you bring: 


  • At least seven (7) years of recent experience in a large digital news environment,
  • Substantial experience writing, editing, packaging and copy editing digital content in a compelling way. 
  • Some experience helping to launch or create new content initiatives. 
  • Experience with content management systems such as Moveable Type, Media Central, MPX/The Platform, including ability to edit, photoshop and publish within those platforms; and basic HTML/CSS
  • Advanced knowledge of social platforms, including YouTube, Tik Tok, Snapchat and WhatsApp, including their algorithms and community features. 
  • Proven ability to analyze performance metrics and audience data using  measurement tools such as Chartbeat, Adobe analytics, Google Analytics. 
  • Strong visualization skills, including experience in using graphics, charts and explainers to distill complex financial data into easily digestible and actionable content. 
  • Ability to manage large volumes of fast-moving information and ensure material is distributed appropriately 24/7.
  • Excellent journalism skills with a strong general knowledge about Canadian and international economics, financial, business and consumer issues.
  • Ability to assign, manage and motivate staff and to coordinate with colleagues across departments in a productive manner and ability to mediate disputes as they arise. 
  • Excellent journalistic and critical thinking skills, including a deep knowledge of the legal and ethical issues related to business and consumer journalism.
  • Demonstrated ability to bring new perspectives, voices and lived experiences into your daily journalism. 
  • Strong communication, collaboration and interpersonal skills. 
  • Ability and willingness to work flexible hours as required.
  • Possession of a valid driver’s license as well as a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada's insurance company.

Your role:

CBC Atlantic is looking for a Communications Officer to join the local CBC Marketing, Communications and Brand team.


The successful candidate will work with a team of communication professionals in a fast-paced environment to execute a variety of marketing/communications strategies, projects and brand events to support CBC’s digital, radio and television programming across Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland and Labrador, and Quebec.


This position reports to the Manager of Communications, Marketing and Brand in Halifax, representing Quebec and the Atlantic region, and requires someone with a passion for storytelling and relationship building, a flair and genuine joy for engaging with people, and a deep understanding of the diverse and changing demographics of the region.


This position is hybrid. An in-office presence in the CBC Halifax station is required, as is the ability to travel and work at community events and locations across the region as required. 


Duties for this position may include:

  • Advancing strategic objectives to grow CBC’s connections with younger, diverse audiences, creating strategies to identify new audiences and reach people where they are, both in-person and online.
  • Supporting community engagement activities for CBC in the Atlantic region and Quebec both virtually and in person, including working closely with community partners and editorial colleagues on station initiatives, outreach opportunities, community events and stakeholder engagement.
  • Supporting the development of media materials including chat notes and community page posts.
  • Supporting social media strategies by creating, editing, and posting creative social media content for established and emerging platforms. This may require photography and basic design skills.
  • Supporting the development of initiatives such as newsletters for both internal and external audiences.
  • Researching information regarding special projects, new initiatives and administrative matters, including managing newsroom tours.
  • Research, review and source suppliers for CBC branded promotional materials. Lead and coordinate orders, receiving and cataloguing. 
  • Collaborating with cross-functional and marketing communications teams across CBC to develop and elevate national priorities and campaigns that attract audiences and foster engagement while supporting editorial objectives and journalism standards and practices.
  • Supporting and nurturing relationships with internal and external partners including audience members, partner organizations and vendors.
  • Work with Audience Relations to develop messaging in response to audience enquiries and reactions.

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

  • Three (3) years’ or more of relevant experience that demonstrates superior writing, editing and proofreading skills, a working knowledge of a wide range of communications and marketing materials, excellent interpersonal and organizational skills and the ability to work under deadline pressures.
  • Connection to the communities we serve across the Atlantic region, and experience developing strategies to connect with new, younger and more diverse audiences.
  • Strong organization and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects on tight deadlines and with attention to detail.
  • Experience in community event logistics and brand activation execution, both in-person and virtual, including development of critical path and run of show, and coordination of swag and onsite needs.
  • Ability to take initiative and demonstrate creativity as well as good judgment.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of local CBC programming. 
  • Demonstrated customer service and problem-solving ability.
  • Experience with Google Suite tools (Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Meet).
  • Experience with Dash Social or similar social media tools, and video editing tools with an understanding of creation, editing, captions for social media content purposes.
  • Experience with Adestra or other newsletter building tools is an asset.
  • A results-oriented, enthusiastic and reliable team player with excellent interpersonal skills, a demonstrated solutions-focus and a positive attitude.
  • A strong desire to promote the values of diversity, inclusion and a respectful work culture.
  • Flexibility in work hours as workflow demands, including the ability to work shift work, including evenings, weekends and holidays, as required.
  • Availability to travel for short periods if required. Must possess a valid driver’s licence as well as a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada's insurance company.
  • Knowledge of languages other than English is considered an asset, particularly French.
  • Personal or professional experience working in / knowledge of the Quebec region is considered an asset.  
  • Post-secondary education with certificate, diploma or a university degree in communications/public relations or marketing, or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.

Helping Canadians make sense of our world is our mission. Trade wars and talk of Canada becoming the 51st American state have made this mission more important than ever. And covering an unpredictable administration in Washington, DC brings new challenges as well.


We’re looking for an experienced correspondent who is keen to dive in and help us tell stories about this pivotal time in Canada’s history – as we work to tell these stories in new ways to grow new audiences.


We are hiring a correspondent for our Washington DC bureau. The successful candidate will be an exceptional journalist who thrives on breaking news, building contacts and working in a team to turn political stories that can feel hard to grasp into creative stories that connect. They bring a broad range of storytelling skills and are excited to produce strong social media-first content, aimed at mobile and streaming audiences. 


You thrive in a demanding daily news environment meeting multiple deadlines. You understand how to hook an audience on TikTok, write comprehensive analysis pieces and can go live when news breaks. You build a list of trusted sources and work to break news about the Canada - U.S. relationship. You are a storyteller who can navigate a variety of audio and video formats.  All of your journalism adheres to the CBC News Journalistic Standards and Practices. 


In this position, you will be supported by the Senior Producer in Washington DC who will assign American coverage, and supported by the World News teams in Toronto.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Cover the news in the United States: join the team of journalists reporting on news there, and other locations, as assigned. Working with the assignment team and other reporters in Washington, DC  the correspondent will generate and produce journalism guided by our audience news needs, across our platforms. 
  • Go live on any platform whenever a story requires it.
  • Produce original content while also responding to breaking news and emerging stories in a fast-paced environment.
  • Pitch and cover stories that resonate with our national audience, with an ability to find the significance in world events for a Canadian audience.
  • Research and analyze complex issues using specialized sources to ensure our audience gets a deep, nuanced understanding of important topics.
  • Develop and maintain a strong network of contacts with a wide range of sources.

What is required: 

  • You are a journalist with a minimum of 7 years of comparable experience, including significant reporting experience at a network/national level
  • Exceptional storytelling skills, with a proven ability to produce memorable social, written, audio and visual content
  • Demonstrated ability to produce compelling vertical visuals and social media content
  • Strong on-air presence and skill with live reporting.
  • Exceptional critical thinking skills, with an ability to breakdown complex issues and explain them clearly to audiences
  • Your extensive experience demonstrates that you can pivot quickly when a story changes, you remain respectful to colleagues when there are competing deadlines and content demands, and be open to social-centric presenting / hosting.
  • Extensive knowledge of world news and current affairs issues
  • A collaborative team player with strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and willingness to work long and flexible hours, including overtime, evenings and weekends as needed.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills combined with a successful track record of working as part of a small team
  • Strong grasp of CBC News Journalistic Standards and Practices, with an ability to understand how they apply in your daily storytelling.
  • A university degree in journalism or an equivalent combination of education and experience is preferred.

Your application will be evaluated on your experience, as well as your portfolio of work. 


Please include at least two examples of: 

  • Digital / social stories you produced and shot
  • Packaged daily news video content you shot and edited 
  • A cover letter that tells us why you want this role, and how you will use your experience to support the bureau

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Your role

As a Program/Project Delivery Finance Advisor, you will play a critical role in supporting a large-scale and transformative agile/hybrid program. You will act as a vital financial bridge between delivery squads, program leadership, and Governance. Working closely with a Program Director and the Program Office, Product Owners, and Corporate Finance, you will be responsible for stewardship of complex project/program financials. You will navigate multiple funding models to ensure accurate tracking and reporting.

The opportunity

CBC/Radio-Canada is running a large-scale agile program with rigorous financial, tracking, and reporting requirements. This role offers the opportunity to synthesize complex financial data into actionable insights for various stakeholder groups, ultimately supporting critical reporting within the corporation and, via Finance, to external institutions involved in financing of the program.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Oversee and aggregate program-level financials, applying strong Capital and non-Capital accounting knowledge while supporting empowered agile squads and Product Owners in managing their individual financial accountability.
  • Working with the Program Director and Finance, establish appropriate financial guardrails and provide program-level monitoring across categories of spend (e.g., vendors, resourcing, licensing), supporting the Product Owners who maintain ownership/accountability for their initiative/project financials.
  • Align financial tracking with the program's resource sheet for labour and travel burn rates, including squad membership and percentage allocations to projects.
  • Develop "what-if" scenarios and financial plans to support program agility and decision-making.
  • Fluently translate progress, risk, and financial metrics between technical teams and corporate partners, ensuring information is fit-for-purpose for high-level stewardship and control.
  • Collaborate with Program Director in preparing financial reporting for Governance.
  • Communicate financial statuses and requirements effectively to diverse groups, including Corporate Finance, the Program Director, and Product Owners/Squad Leads.

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

  • 7 years relevant experience with 3 or more years managing project financials including agile/hybrid environments.
  • Strong financial acumen, a deep understanding of financial mechanisms on projects and programs in the context of transformational and innovation projects.
  • Able to understand actuals, and build short and long term forecasts in agile, traditional, and hybrid environments.
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity within an evolving program environment, bringing flexibility to financial forecasting as requirements and delivery details become more clearly defined over time.
  • Understanding of different expenditure types in large transformative projects.
  • Understanding of multiple funding models, from standard corporate budgets to loans paid via leases.
  • Strong proficiency in utilizing data tools to track and report on financial performance metrics and turn complex information into tailored summaries.
  • Experience building and using tools and reporting on financials in transformational/innovative initiatives.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, capable of interacting seamlessly with both highly technical and director-level governance.
  • University degree in a relevant field or equivalent combination of training and experience.
  • Functional bilingualism is an asset.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.
 

We thank all applicants for their interest, but only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

As part of our recruitment process, candidates who advance to the next

step will be asked to complete a background check. This includes:  

  • A mandatory Criminal record check.

This role is a hybrid work arrangement. Work schedule to be discussed with the Hiring Manager according to the guidelines defined by the department.

The Director, Modernization and Change Enablement will drive the establishment and embedding of the People & Culture Change Leadership workstream.   This individual will design enterprise-wide change management strategies to foster collaborationminimize resistance, optimize workforce agility, and ensure a smooth transition toward achieving the organization’s modern talent and strategic goals.

Reporting into the Executive Director, Talent, Organizational Effectiveness and Change, this role acts as a critical bridge between human resources strategy and business operations.  The Director will partner closely with project teams, business leaders, and employees to embed sustainable capabilities and drive continuous improvement across the organization.

Working across functions, the Director will design and implement key structures, such as the Enterprise Change Council, to align portfolio demands with employee capacity.  Operating as an enterprise subject-matter expert, this role provides the thought leadership, analytical frameworks, and strategic guidance that equip the organization to successfully deliver on its modernization and change enablement agenda.

Your work will directly support CBC/Radio-Canada’s strategic pillars of Proximity, Digital agility, and Bringing people together.

This position can be based in Ottawa, Toronto or Montreal.

Main Responsibilities and Impact:

1. Enterprise Change Governance & Council Leadership 

  • Establish Governance: Design, stand up, and govern the newly formed Enterprise Change Council to serve as the central governing body for cross-functional change alignment.

  • Define Operations: Formulate the Council’s charter, objectives, membership, and operational cadence, ensuring active, collaborative representation across all components and key stakeholders.

  • Manage the Portfolio: Lead Council sessions to aggregate, review, and evaluate the enterprise change portfolio, proactively identifying change collision risks, sequencing conflicts, and organizational saturation points.

  • Facilitate Decisions: Drive strategic decision-making and prioritization within the Council to balance modernization velocities with employee absorbency and operational stability.

2. Strategic Change Leadership & Transformation 

  • Develop Strategy: Formulate and execute a comprehensive change management and organizational transformation strategy aligned with the broader talent and engagement roadmap.

  • Assess Impact: Identify the deep cultural and operational impacts of major modernization initiatives across diverse functions, processes, and teams, creating highly tailored intervention plans.

  • Embed Best Practices: Standardize and embed enterprise-wide change management methodologies, uniting human resources, operations, and leadership across various functions and regions.

  • Measure Readiness: Co-design organizational change readiness and cultural pulse frameworks aligned with the enterprise Employee Listening strategy to gauge and build the capacity for continuous strategic evolution.

3. Talent and Stakeholder Engagement 

  • Build Partnerships: Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with key business leaders and partners to drive deep buy-in and commitment to workforce modernization efforts.

  • Coach Leadership: Act as a trusted advisor and executive coach to leadership teams, guiding them on their roles as active, visible sponsors of change.

  • Drive Communications: Develop and execute strategic communication plans that elevate employee voices, promote transparency, and maximize engagement throughout transformation lifecycles.

4. Organizational Capability & Learning Integration 

  • Design Capability Programs: Oversee the coordination and design of integrated training programs to equip employees with the new skills, competencies, and mindsets required to embrace modern working models.

  • Align Systems: Ensure complete alignment between modern talent programs, organizational development initiatives, and learning systems to facilitate high adoption rates.

  • Support Transitions: Provide ongoing, empathetic support and framework resources to teams and individuals navigating complex structural transitions.

5. Implementation, Analytics & Cultural Sustainability 

  • Integrate with HR: Collaborate across broader People & Culture teams to seamlessly integrate change management actions into existing workforce initiatives and program lifecycles.

  • Mitigate Fatigue: Monitor progress and address change fatigue or institutional resistance proactively through data-driven, analytical approaches.

  • Sustain Success: Promote deep alignment between organizational culture, workforce behavior, and long-term strategic objectives to ensure sustainable, long-term success.

  • Support Pillars: Lead ad hoc strategic initiatives as assigned to support and advance CBC/Radio-Canada’s core strategic pillars.

Qualifications, Experience & Skills: 

Education & Certifications

  • Required: Bachelor’s Degree in Organizational Development, Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field (required)

  • Advanced certification in Change Management (e.g. Prosci, ACMP, or equivalent)

Experience

  • 8+ years of progressive leadership experience in change management, organizational development, talent management, or related fields

  • Proven success leading enterprise-wide modernization or human resources transformation initiatives within complex, cross-functional, and matrixed environments.

  • Direct, proven experience establishing, standing up, or operating an executive-level governance body or steering committee (such as a Change Council) 

  • Experience operating in public service, media, or similarly regulated/bilingual landscapes is preferred

Knowledge & Skills

  • Deep mastery of change management frameworks, portfolio governance, and workforce transformation methodologies.

  • Exceptional facilitation, communication, and emotional intelligence, with a natural ability to resolve conflicts and align matrixed stakeholders at the executive level.

  • Strong project management discipline, specifically regarding how to map portfolio-level change saturation and embed agile frameworks into massive organizational shifts.

  • An analytical and strategic mindset capable of turning workforce data and engagement metrics into actionable insights.

  • Experience with collaboration and project management tools, e.g. Google Suite (Gmail, Drive, Docs, Slides, Sheets, Meet)

  • Bilingualism (English/French) is required.

  • Occasional travel may be required 

Leadership Competencies:

  • Strategic mindset: Attains strategic goals by systematically reflecting on priorities and objectives to be pursued along with consequences

  • Persuasive communication: Helps people shift toward a different perspective in a collaborative and positive manner

  • Accountability:  Recognizes, takes ownership, and engages in course correction of decisions and subsequent actions

  • Critical thinking: Engages in reflective thinking and challenges one’s personal assumptions in light of new arguments and verifiable information

  • Empathy: Acknowledges and appreciates others’ feelings, perspectives, and aspirations on the basis of their experiences

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

CBC News is seeking an Executive Producer of Publishing to lead the team responsible for curating CBCNews.ca and the CBC News app, strengthening digital story packaging and guiding publishing best practices. You anticipate changing audience needs and help shape the future of how we present and deliver our journalism.

Your guiding purpose is to connect audiences with what matters to them. You lead a team that turns CBC News’  journalism into an essential daily experience for Canadians. At the intersection of journalism, audience insight and product, you shape the future of how people discover and experience CBC News, reaching new audiences and making us a destination people seek out, return to and can’t imagine their day without.

You are a journalist first, bringing strong editorial judgment to every publishing decision. You lead a team of journalists who combine editorial expertise, audience insight and digital strategy to make our content relevant, engaging and responsive.

You build strong relationships with regional leaders and colleagues across Live & Daily News, Current Affairs & Investigative, and Newsgathering, Assignment & Story Development. Working closely with discovery, product and data teams, you continually look for ways to improve the audience journey. You make it easier for people to find more of the journalism they want and move easily between related stories, formats and experiences. Your team establishes, updates and shares best practices for digital story packaging, video, lineups, the use of video and audio in stories and lineups, photo selection, newsletters and other publishing functions.


You’re a strong editorial leader with exceptional communication, decision-making and interpersonal skills. You can motivate and develop a team, set clear priorities and adapt to changing demands. You have a comprehensive understanding of CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.


You put audience needs at the centre of publishing decisions, ensuring our platforms showcase journalism reflecting a diversity of perspectives, ideas and experiences. You inspire others to do the same.


You live and promote the values of an inclusive and respectful work culture.


This is a permanent, full-time position based in Toronto. You are part of the Audience Growth team, reporting to the Managing Editor, Publishing and Transparency.


Job responsibilities

  • Lead the 24/7 publishing team responsible for curating CBCNews.ca and the CBC News app, setting expectations for lineups that respond to breaking news, audience needs and editorial priorities.
  • Set direction for publishing decisions that connect audiences with what matters to them through compelling story selection, packaging, placement and timing.
  • Oversee the updating and sharing of best practices for headlines, photography, digital story packaging, content packages, site and app curation, newsletters and other publishing functions.
  • Establish strong working relationships across Live & Daily News, Current Affairs & Investigative, and Newsgathering, Assignment & Story Development to ensure our journalism is effectively presented and reaches relevant audiences.
  • Guide the team’s strategy for search and emerging discovery tools, adapting publishing practices so audiences can find our journalism as digital platforms and habits evolve.
  • Oversee the team’s collaboration with local and network colleagues to improve story packaging and visibility, build on audience interest and identify opportunities for our best journalism to reach people.
  • Guide the publishing team’s collaboration with planning and discovery teams on major stories to create compelling digital audience experiences that increase engagement and time spent.
  • Oversee best practices for push alerts, newsletters, email and other publishing platforms as they evolve across CBC News, and the team’s coordination of delivery with those responsible for editorial content and decisions.
  • Establish priorities with product and data teams to understand how people find and navigate our journalism, identify barriers and improve the audience journey.
  • Represent publishing needs in product planning for CBCNews.ca and the CBC News app, guiding the team’s contribution to improvements that help people discover relevant content and move easily between stories and formats.
  • Ensure the team uses daily and hourly audience data, research and testing to inform publishing decisions, evaluate improvements and share findings with local and network teams.
  • Provide clear direction, feedback and coaching to senior producers and producers, supporting consistent publishing practices across shifts, dayparts and weekends.
  • Oversee staff scheduling and financial and production resource planning to support the publishing operation.
  • Anticipate changes in digital publishing trends, tools and audience habits, and ensure the team has the training and support to respond.
  • Ensure publishing decisions and practices adhere to CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.

Relevant skills & experience

  • Minimum seven years of recent experience leading people and/or editorial operations in a digital news environment.
  • Proven ability to manage, motivate and develop teams, including senior journalists.
  • Excellent journalistic judgment and a comprehensive understanding of CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices and the legal and ethical issues related to journalism.
  • Substantial experience in digital publishing, including homepage and app curation, sharp headlines, photography and compelling story packaging.
  • Strong understanding of digital audience needs and habits, and how publishing decisions help people discover, engage with and return to journalism.
  • Ability to interpret audience data and research in the context of editorial and strategic goals, and guide teams in applying findings to publishing decisions.
  • Experience collaborating with product and data teams to improve how audiences find and navigate content, using research, testing and audience feedback to guide changes.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to build productive relationships across regional newsrooms, network teams and departments.
  • Understanding of newsletters, push alerts and other direct audience channels, including their role in engagement and return visits.
  • Aptitude with content management systems and publishing tools, and the ability to guide teams through technical and workflow challenges.
  • Knowledge of audience experience, design and digital accessibility is an asset.
  • Demonstrated coaching skills and the ability to support staff through changes in tools, workflows and responsibilities.
  • Ability to make timely decisions, manage competing priorities and lead teams effectively under the pressures of a 24/7 news operation.
  • Strong knowledge of Canadian national and regional news, international affairs and the diverse communities CBC News serves.
  • Cultural awareness and sensitivity, and openness to different perspectives and ideas.
  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • Ability to work flexible hours as required, including early mornings, evenings, weekends and holidays.

Host, Blue Sky


CBC Saskatchewan is looking for a dynamic new host for Blue Sky, our noon hour current affairs radio program. The position can be based in either Regina or Saskatoon. This is a term position that will end in January, 2028.


You are the most curious person in the room. You relate well to guests. You care deeply about their stories. You know when to laugh, and you know when to hold people accountable. You are confident in what you know, and are interested in what you don’t.


You understand that audiences want to be both entertained and informed over the lunch hour, and you make audiences feel welcome and part of a community. You know that using a full range of tone and perspective is key to strong radio current affairs programming.


You have a sense of adventure, an eclectic range of interests and a keen desire to meet new people, explore our province, and learn other perspectives. You are passionate about championing stories from Saskatchewan’s under-represented communities, and you love meeting listeners where they live through in-person public appearances and remote broadcasts.


An exceptional journalist and a keen observer, you must be able to quickly analyze a broad range of issues and thrive in the fast-paced, high-pressure world of live, local radio. You have a strong grasp on Saskatchewan’s political landscape and its energy-driven and ag-driven economy. You understand how these issues affect the day-to-day lives of the people who live here.


As a leader on the Blue Sky team, it’s clear you care about your colleagues on the show and in the newsroom. You act as a team unifier and collaborator, and are always looking for creative solutions to challenges.


You live for our audiences. You care as much about our traditional audiences as you do about getting your storytelling in front of entirely new audiences. You are keen to explore how we can do that in video and social spaces.



Your responsibilities:


  • Pitch and produce original stories that deepen Blue Sky’s community connections, elevate a range of voices and reflect the day’s top local news.
  • Host Blue Sky live on air between 12:00-1:00 pm weekdays, conducting interviews on a wide variety of current events.
  • Interact spontaneously with program participants such as guests, reporters, experts and members of the audience.
  • Conduct research and interviews, gather audio, write and package audio content.
  • Write and package digital content.
  • Participate in community outreach activities to deepen CBC’s connection with audiences. 

Your profile:


  • An engaging, curious, and spontaneous on-air personality, with a wide range of genuine interests, knowledge and insight, reflecting curiosity in many current affairs topics, and an ability to make them relevant to existing and new audiences.
  • Strong journalistic skills, demonstrated through original story ideas, live interviewing, innovative storytelling, and writing and vetting abilities.
  • Excellent critical thinking skills, including knowledge of and familiarity with CBC Journalistic Standards as well as the legal and ethical issues related to journalism.
  • Ability to react quickly to changing circumstances and breaking news; comfortable going off-script when needed.
  • A strong proven connection to the communities we serve in Saskatchewan, and an openness to diverse perspectives and ideas.
  • Familiarity with digital and social storytelling and a willingness to learn and tackle new tasks across all CBC platforms (TV, radio, digital).
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across teams and locations.
  • A proven work ethic and a positive attitude. 
  • A strong desire to live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture.
  • A passion for public outreach and an enthusiastic ambassador of public broadcasting and the program.
  • Possession of a valid driver’s licence as well as a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada's insurance company – other classes considered an asset.
  • Ability to work a variety of shifts including early starts, late finishes and weekends.
  • University degree or equivalent in a related field, with a minimum of five years of relevant or comparable experience.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Your Role


CBC/Radio-Canada is seeking a Lead Analyst, Vulnerability and External Attack Surface Management, to optimize the Corporation’s vulnerability management program and design, build and deploy its external attack surface management (EASM) service. 

In this role, you will take strategic and operational ownership of this domain. You will establish a comprehensive map of the Corporation’s external digital footprint — including internet-exposed assets, domains, certificates, cloud accounts, public APIs and exposed data — while driving continuous improvements to internal and hybrid vulnerability management. As a recognized subject matter expert, you will serve as a technical authority for leadership, maintain the vulnerability and exposure risk register, and adjudicate security exemption requests across the organization.

This position can be based in Montreal or Toronto.

What’s in It for You

Challenges. We spend our days solving problems of all kinds. Media files are highly nuanced and incredibly complicated; updating, installing and supporting technologies that are organization-wide and that impact broadcasting content is a time-sensitive, complex technical feat. And that’s just the beginning. You’ll be working with leading-edge data management, cloud, IP broadcasting, AI, security and reliability technologies.

As Lead Analyst, you will:

  • Map the digital footprint: Identify, classify and inventory CBC/Radio-Canada’s complete external attack surface for the first time, establishing the baseline for domain names, subdomains, public IP address ranges, exposed services, public cloud environments and APIs.
  • Implement continuous detection: Develop and execute procedures to detect inadvertently exposed services, expired or vulnerable certificates and leaked credentials or source code on the public web.
  • Lead the vulnerability life cycle: Define and optimize end-to-end processes for vulnerability detection, triage, impact analysis, prioritization, remediation and verification.
  • Define the scanning strategy: Establish the scope and frequency of automated and manual vulnerability scans across the entire IT environment.
  • Assess risk in context: Evaluate discovered vulnerabilities by cross-referencing CVSS scores with business context, asset criticality, existing compensating controls and active threat intelligence (e.g., known exploits).
  • Develop remediation plans: Recommend targeted corrective measures — such as patch management, system reconfigurations, temporary workarounds or WAF/firewall rules — for internal teams.
  • Lead zero-day response: Provide technical leadership during critical zero-day vulnerabilities and incidents (e.g., Log4j, major OS/hardware flaws), co-ordinating rapid detection and mitigation.
  • Evaluate and adjudicate security exemptions: Conduct in-depth technical reviews of exemption requests when prescribed patching or remediation timelines cannot be met. Assess residual risk based on exploitability and asset criticality, requiring robust compensating controls where necessary.
  • Manage the vulnerability risk register: Document, maintain and map unpatched vulnerabilities, security technical debt and approved exceptions in the Corporation's risk register. Monitor residual risk levels, update mitigation plans and present clear status reports to governance and executive committees to inform adjudication and investment decisions.
  • Partner on compliance and regulatory frameworks: Work closely with the policy and compliance lead to align vulnerability detection and remediation processes with regulatory requirements, internal policies and industry standards.
  • Develop metrics and dashboards: Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) and key risk indicators (KRIs) to monitor program effectiveness.
  • Drive program evolution and threat intelligence: Continually enhance security tools and processes to address emerging threats (e.g., zero-day vulnerabilities). Monitor global vulnerability trends, proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits and evolving frameworks (e.g., CVSS v4, MITRE ATT&CK).
  • Maintain industry expertise: Stay current on information security best practices and industry trends.
     

What You Bring

  • University degree in computer science, IT or information security.
  • Minimum five years' experience in vulnerability management, risk assessment or IT governance, including at least three years in an information security role.
  • Extensive knowledge of security technology and risk assessment methodologies, policies and processes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical decision-makers (e.g., governance committees, business units, legal teams).
  • Excellent analytical, evaluative and problem-solving abilities.
  • Experience with compliance programs as well as their technical and security requirements.
  • Technical expertise across key domains:
    • Standards and Frameworks: Strong command of industry standards such as ISO/IEC 27001, 27002, 27005, NIST SP 800-53 / 800-161, COBIT and ITIL.
    • Cloud and Web Architecture Security: Solid understanding of web infrastructure and cloud environment security.
    • Network and Security Technologies: Thorough understanding of network architectures (LAN/WAN, routers), network security technologies (firewalls, IDS/IPS, DNS, web filtering) and cryptographic principles (encryption at rest and in transit).
    • Architecture and Data Security: Working knowledge of database architecture concepts and secure software development best practices.
    • Operational Resilience and Physical Security: Solid understanding of business continuity and disaster recovery planning (BCP/DRP), operational resilience and physical security controls.
  • Relevant professional security certifications a definite asset (e.g., CISSP, CRISC, CBCP, CISA, CISM or equivalent).
  • Bilingualism (English and French) essential.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

Your role:

 

CBC’s Business & Rights team has a position available, reporting to the Senior Manager, Inhouse Programming.


As a Manager, Business & Rights, Inhouse Programming, you work closely with CBC's in-house production, programmers and external partners across all CBC departments, regions and media lines.  You decide how to approach negotiations and structure deals that meet CBC’s rights strategies and priorities.  You will make recommendations and seek approvals from your Senior Manager on deal terms that best represent CBC’s priorities and interests.


You negotiate and draft content licensing agreements that represent and protect CBC’s interests, and manage those relationships on behalf of CBC.  Your focus on content licensing agreements will be on news suppliers, photo suppliers, and podcast producers, but could include a diverse range of other types of CBC (or Radio-Canada) in-house produced content as well.  


You decide how to approach the research, negotiation, licensing, administration and payment of all rights, residuals and royalties associated with the exploitation of CBC’s programming in accordance with CBC’s collective agreements, contracts, copyright law and CBC policies and practices. 


You design training programs and related communication tools to provide business direction, context and rights options to inhouse content creators across English Services departments, both at the network and regional levels across the country.   You deliver training where appropriate, and work with CBC Learning to establish other best means of communicating such information.


You provide leadership and direction to internal partners across the corporation on complex rights, financial, policy, and business matters.   You provide constructive direction, feedback and evaluation to ensure that all production elements and relationships with third parties meet CBC strategic objectives, business and programming standards. 


Your responsibilities would include:


  • Taking a tailored approach to deal and contract negotiations for a wide range of projects intended for CBC’s owned & operated and branded & operated platforms, including but not limited to CBC Radio One and CBC Music, CBC Television and CBC News Network, CBC Gem, CBC FAST Channels and YouTube.
  • Ensuring CBC's contractual requirements and business interests are secured on a consistent and nuanced basis across programs of similar scope.
  • Reviewing third party agreements, including agreements from multi-national news suppliers to ensure harmonization with CBC’s rights and obligations.
  • Applying strategic thinking to balance CBC’s needs and the rights of artists under collective agreements and from under-represented groups.
  • Making decisions during negotiations that have complex logistical, legal and financial implications.
  • Assisting in research, management and presentation of rights data across genres, platforms, and windows of exploitation.
  • Working with other managers, supervise and co-ordinate the activities of B&R InHouse Programming staff, and delegate and assign activities to appropriate staff.
  • Designing and delivering training programs to ensure CBC production units understand and follow copyright law and deal terms for content with which they work. 
  • Refining our business approach through continuous innovation, agile processes, and market-leading thinking about rights and financing models.
  • Authorizing contract payments where required. 



We are looking for candidates with the following: 


  • A minimum of five (5) years relevant experience in drafting and negotiating major contracts. 
  • A law degree is an asset.
  • At least five (5) years of business and/or operational experience, including In-depth knowledge of all forms of current media, negotiating techniques, corporate business practices, and industry union agreements (eg. ACTRA, WGC, CFM).
  • Facility with approved artificial intelligence technologies to improve workflow and data analysis. Eagerness to learn and adapt to emerging technologies.
  • Strong understanding of linear and streaming entertainment business models, social media, and other online platforms including FAST channels.
  • Strong computer skills including Google suite, Excel, Microsoft Office and Adobe.
  • Ability to comprehend and translate the concerns of creative producers/directors/creative heads into appropriate contracts within the constraints of the applicable collective agreements, regulatory bodies, CBC policies and funding guidelines.
  • Creativity and innovative problem-solving skills to address issues in a manner satisfactory to all parties.
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and oral, including an ability to work with both emerging and experienced producers.
  • Ability to handle multiple priorities, and work under pressure.
  • Ability to exercise judgment and work independently taking initiative.
  • Strong analytical skills. 
  • Bilingualism (French/English) would be considered an asset.
