Your role

CBC Yukon has an amazing opportunity in Whitehorse. We’re looking for an experienced journalist to help lead a team that drives local, innovative storytelling on audio, digital, video and social platforms. We’re searching for someone who’s decisive, creative and passionate about everything that makes the Yukon what it is - people, communities, cultures, land, languages, arts, sports, politics and businesses. 

The Yukon is a territory in transition, where there’s space to learn, to experience, to travel, to build a career and a life. 

As a producer assigned primarily to CBC Yukon’s audio-radio shows, your central role is programming our three daily shows, working with dedicated hosts, an associate producer and reporters. You’ll assign, edit and line up segments on Yukon Morning, Midday Cafe and Airplay. You will lead daily team meetings, coordinate story chases, make decisions on audio treatments, write scripts, conduct interviews and coordinate  with News, Digital and Video Producers and reporters across the North and across Canada. 

You will have the opportunity to initiate ideas and projects to engage, serve and grow our audiences by reflecting and amplifying complex Northern stories. There will be latitude for initiative and creativity while adhering to CBC journalistic and/or program policies, standards, and practices. Besides initiating and producing work yourself, there is a regular and ongoing requirement to help coordinate the work of others, within CBC Yukon and with other CBC stations, shows, and hubs.

Working with an editorial leadership team led by CBC Yukon’s Executive Producer, you’ll collaborate with program staff to effectively, efficiently, and empathetically cover stories and issues affecting our diverse audience across the Yukon. Awareness and understanding of local issues and communities across the territory is essential.CBC Yukon also contributes to a N.W.T-Yukon weekend show produced and hosted out of Yellowknife.

Can you see yourself here?

You have a deep and demonstrated understanding of broadcast journalism, responsive, relevant news coverage, digital roll outs and strategic social media storytelling. You’re also keen to consider new ways of telling stories on established and emerging platforms. You understand the role of public media in connecting with and building a strong, flourishing local community. You have experience encouraging and creating content that embraces a diverse range of lived experiences. 

You’re an excellent writer, and all-round communicator. You also have strong vetting skills. You’re insatiably curious, brimming with initiative. You work quickly, thoughtfully and collaboratively. You demonstrate flexibility and adaptability. 

You’re also a confident, compassionate, and inclusive leader. You inspire people to bring out their best. You’ve got experience mentoring, coaching and working alongside a team that brings a broad range of experience, skills and interests. You’re paying attention to what people are talking about and you find ways to bring those voices to the table. You’re open to new ideas and to feedback. 

You’re a great planner and deft organizer who can work in harmony with a small team in a high-pressure, tight-deadline environment from pitch, to gathering, to roll out. You are also committed to creating a trusting relationship with our established and emerging audiences by catalyzing, reflecting and responding to Yukon stories in our daily programming. 

You understand our different platforms and how to shape a story to play into each one’s strengths.You’re on the lookout for new ways to connect, including podcasting, on-demand and streaming audio and video.

We are looking for a candidate with the following: 

  • A relevant post-secondary degree or equivalent years of experience.

  • Minimum of 5 years relevant experience of which 3 must involve work in broadcasting or a closely related industry.

  • Strong understanding of the Yukon’s diverse social, political and cultural landscape

  • Demonstrated experience in leading a team or unit.

  • Experience in gathering sound and voices and producing audio segments for radio broadcasts

  • Experience in producing daily current affairs-driven shows 

  • Demonstrated understanding of digital, video and mobile platforms.

  • Superior editorial decision making, critical thinking and listening skills.

  • A thorough knowledge of CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.

  • Demonstrated ability to exercise quick, decisive and strong editorial judgment.

  • Highly developed vetting skills.

  • Ability to communicate effectively and cooperatively.

  • Highly developed interpersonal skills.

  • Highly developed organizational skills.

  • Excellent editing/production skills in Dalet and other audio editing software 

  • Ability to work independently and also participate as a member of a production team.

  • A valid driver’s license and a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada’s insurance company


As required, you will perform the following tasks: 

  • Coordinate resources and coverage plans for daily content creation, special projects, series, remote broadcasts and streaming content with a focus on CBC Yukon’s three daily audio shows.

  • Lead story meetings.

  • Participate in the preparation of content for local, regional and national audiences, including assigning, researching, gathering, writing and editing.

Are you an exceptional daily news journalist who thrives in the fast-paced, high-pressure world of live, breaking news?


CBC Newfoundland and Labrador is looking for an experienced news editor / presenter to lead our weekday morning newscasts to audiences listening live on the radio and on digital platforms. As the morning newsreader, you will play an integral editorial and leadership role in gathering, preparing and presenting the daily news, keeping our audiences informed about what’s happening now across the province. 


You’re the kind of journalist who loves the adrenaline rush of chasing breaking news and you’re not intimidated by the prospect of changing lineups and rewriting newscasts under very tight deadlines. You embrace the challenge of keeping your newscasts as up-to-date as possible, chasing stories yourself and working to add context and additional content to ensure listeners get the full story.


You understand the diverse and changing population in Newfoundland and Labrador, and the importance of broadening the range of perspectives, experiences and points of view reflected on our programming, especially those from people who have been traditionally underrepresented in the media. In your work, you will ensure CBC journalistic standards are met and that our stories are fair, balanced, accurate, thoughtful and immediate.



Note: This is a temporary position for one year. The successful candidate will generally be assigned to work weekdays, 5:00 to 13:15 hours.


Your responsibilities:

  • Plan, organize, line up and deliver newscasts and news breaks.
  • Collaborate with journalists across platforms and programs to chase breaking news and ensure newscasts are up-to-date.
  • Write and edit scripts; cut audio clips and package stories.
  • Conduct interviews on and off air.

  • Strong news judgment and a demonstrated ability to react quickly to breaking news and changing priorities, and chase multiple stories at once.
  • Excellent critical thinking skills, including knowledge of the legal and ethical issues related to journalism.
  • Engaging on-air presence, a strong presentation style and an ease with live, on-air work.

You will help set the agenda for Indigenous storytelling and will be familiar with the editorial needs of Indigenous and non-Indigenous audiences.


You will be an editorial leader and mentor, someone who demonstrates sound news judgment and critical thinking skills in both news and enterprise reporting, and who inspires others to be innovative and creative.

●  Demonstrated experience leading a team in a multi-platform news environment.

●  Knowledge of and experience in assigning and creating content for all platforms (video, digital, social, radio, television, streaming) as well as vetting, editing, fact-checking and packaging.


●  Superior communication, interpersonal and organizational skills.


●  A strategic thinker with a proven track record of executing on a vision.


●  Demonstrated ability to exercise both quick editorial judgment and long- term planning.


●  A high-energy leader with a positive, team-first attitude and the ability to motivate and coach teams, encourage creativity and embrace experimentation.


●  Experience and commitment to developing content strategies to feature new voices and perspectives and to connect with new, younger and more diverse audiences.


●  A strong proven connection to Indigenous communities and a deep and nuanced understanding and appreciation of diverse perspectives and lived experiences.


●  Strong people management skills with a keen desire to live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture.

Online shopping scams, imposter schemes, deep-fakes and consumer fraud are on the rise in Canada. CBC News is developing  a new Scams unit to unearth deceptive practices and help Canadians make sense of what they can do to protect themselves. 


We’re looking for a Producer who will not only help shape the programming while championing great journalistic content and the people behind it but isn’t afraid to be the face of it when needed. 


You’re a skilled journalist with experience in daily news and enterprise stories. You have exceptional research skills, experience with scams or fraud investigations and are  comfortable using open source information and digital forensic technologies to break new stories. 


Reporting to the Senior Producer, you’re someone who brings both strong editorial leadership and logistical expertise to the role. You understand the important role of a public service broadcaster in helping Canadians make sense of their world. You’re the person on the front-line upholding the upholding the CBC Journalistic Standards and Practices and our core principles of accuracy, fairness, balance, impartiality and integrity. 


You’re an ideas generator, pitching stories and thinking about creative treatments to attract new and younger audiences. While you are adept at writing and editing video, audio and text-based content, you excel at mobile short-form video journalism, understanding what draws a viewer into your story and what keeps them engaged. You put the audience-first in your decision-making, vetting, producing, and are constantly searching for new voices and new perspectives to ensure our story-telling reflects the complexity and rich diversity of Canada.


You demonstrate daily the role of a public broadcaster in a media landscape proliferated with misinformation and rapidly evolving technologies. Verification is a core value. You lean into data, and use it to drive audience-focused storytelling. 


You don’t wait to be assigned. You have initiative and can translate big ideas into tangible actions. 


You’re a trend-setter, able to spot the latest in formats, tools and technologies and a willingness to experiment with same. You understand where new and younger audiences are finding their news - live and on-demand - and you’re focused on meeting them where they are at. 


You understand that stories can break at any time of the day and you have a genuine desire to be on-top of that coverage. While this is a 5 day a week, Monday-Friday role, you recognize that you may be required to work early mornings, evenings, weekends and some overtime when needed to cover breaking news. As collaboration is key with this new team, you will be required to be on-site. 


What you’ll be doing: 

  • Generate and execute compelling journalism, including pitching, researching, writing, shooting, generating and editing written, audio and visual content, with an emphasis on vertical and short-form video.
  • Manage interview schedules, coordinate with other CBC colleagues on shared coverage and ensure safety protocols are followed 
  • Fact checking, verifying names, locations and translations against tight deadlines, ensuring all content adheres to the CBC News Journalistic Standards and Practices. You also bring experience verifying video and other user generated or third party content. 
  • Produce original content, including the visual style, pace, tempo and format for live and on-demand content, including packaged items, photo galleries, soundscapes and current affairs. 
  • Driving production methods incorporating the latest changes to visual storytelling trends, practices, tools and techniques and a desire to experiment with the latest on creative technology. 
  • Performing location surveys and identifying special requirements such as audio, lighting, camera angles and equipment, including production limitations. 

What you bring: 

  • You are a seasoned video-journalist with at least five (5) years of directly related investigative or enterprise experience. 
  • You perform best in a deadline driven, high pressure environment, with an ability to balance the pressure of delivering content quickly against the needs for accuracy and balance
  • Proven record of highly creative, innovative visual storytelling
  •  Has a deep appreciation of diversity of perspective, opinion and experience, with an unwavering commitment to seek out voices from underrepresented groups
  • Must have a strong sense of creativity, initiative and a high degree of responsibility for the accuracy and quality of work throughout the complete production cycle.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal and client service skills are required.  
  • Ability to work independently in a deadline-driven environment while maintaining a professional attitude.
  • Must demonstrate leadership skills and ability to pursue the acquisition of story elements with a minimum of supervision.
  • Ability and willingness to work overtime and various shift patterns including overnights and weekends. 

Your application will be evaluated on your experience, as well as your portfolio of work. Please include at least two examples of: 

  • Packaged short-form video that you produced
  • Packaged vertical video stories that you produced

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.


Your Role

 

You have skills and interest in leadership and communication, and will have project coordination accountability for components / projects / programs of medium to large complexity and scale.  You are comfortable interacting with delivery groups and other stakeholders at the individual contributor and management levels, to coordinate work, track progress, communicate status, and manage risks and issues.  You have solid project management skills and an understanding of what is involved in projects that involve the acquisition, customization, configuration, validation, integration, and transition of business application or infrastructure systems.  You tailor your approach to the needs, comfortable with traditional, and Agile methodologies to coordinate delivery across multiple streams.

 

Working in the Delivery Centre of Expertise as a Project Coordinator reporting to the Director, you are thoroughly organized and structured, analytical and detail-oriented, while taking an interest in understanding the larger picture and driven by project management activities. You are adept at understanding the needs of various stakeholders and supporting teams in the initiation and implementation of the group's strategic projects and eager to learn.

 

The Opportunity:

 

As a project coordinator working on the Content Every Day (CED) product family, you will work closely with Agile PMs, Product Owners, Scrum Masters, and the Product Director.  You will ensure coordination across multiple streams, including but not limited to:

  • Financial Coordination:
    • Budget & forecasting: maintain the initiative's financial registry, updating actuals and monthly forecasts, and identifying key variances or trends.
    • Operational finance: execute reconciliation and of timesheets, manage corporate approval workflows to facilitate timely invoice processing.
  • Facilitate consolidation of project planning updates and status reporting cycles across Agile PMs, Product Owners, and Scrum Masters.
  • Logistical Coordination: partner with Agile PMs, Scrum Masters, and POs to orchestrate execution of program-level workshops and major planning sessions (schedule alignment, agenda distribution, cross-functional participant coordination).
  • Action & Issue Tracking: Document decisions, track action items, and maintain risk/issue registers across multiple streams, ensuring operational follow-up with responsible owners.

 

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience and training.
  • Five (5) or more years of professional experience including three (3) or more years of professional experience in project management/coordination, business administration, or project support.
  • Bilingual (English/French).
  • Experience with document management, Google Suite, spreadsheet, and presentation packages.
  • Knowledge of / experience with budgeting, financial forecasting and scheduling.
  • Knowledge of traditional, hybrid, and Agile project management methodologies including “Agile at scale” - strong asset.
  • Ability to relate to people representing a range of personalities, cultures and hierarchical levels.
  • Ability to handle working on simultaneous workstreams.

 

Nice to have:

  • Experience with CBC/RC organization.
  • Experience with tools (such as Jira) for tracking sprint progress.
  • Experience using scheduling tools (such as MS Project or roadmap visualization software) for roadmaps and traditional milestones.
  • Able to gather, organize, analyze and report on data such as project performance trends, KPIs, dashboards using tools (such as Data Studio, Power BI, Jira/Confluence dashboards).
  • Holding or working toward certification in project management or agile frameworks (e.g. CAPM, PMP, SAFe Agilist, Product Owner).

Your role


Reporting to the Value Management Delivery Office (VMDO), the Project/Program Portfolio Manager (Real Estate Projects) plays a pivotal matrix leadership role. Operating without direct hierarchical authority, you will act as the strategic and tactical orchestrator of the Corporation's real estate transformation. Your mission is to oversee the entire investment portfolio (Capex/Opex), ensuring rigorous alignment with corporate objectives, resource optimization, and standardized risk management.


As the key facilitator for the instances of the new real estate governance model, you will bridge the gap between technical teams, operations, service provider, and senior executive leadership.


You are seen as someone who:

  • Fosters and maintains alignment among diverse stakeholders.
  • Balances strategic thinking with execution and delivery.
  • Demonstrates and encourages continuous improvement and value creation.
  • Effectively reports out to and works with other areas including Finance and Executive Governance.

The opportunity


CBC/Radio-Canada is implementing a rigorous portfolio approach to its real estate assets to achieve critical strategic objectives.  This role offers the opportunity to be a driving force in ensuring that financed real estate projects align with the corporation's strategic goals, while maximizing the efficiency of financial resources. You will champion transparency, resource optimization, and risk management while supporting critical executive reporting.


Primary Duties and Responsibilities


Governance, Facilitation, and Strategic Alignment

  • Committee Leadership: Act as the primary leader and facilitator for the Steering Committee (SteerCo) and the operational Portfolio Sync instance. Actively support the executive Governance Committee.
  • Strategic Alignment (100% Target): Deploy and maintain an evaluation framework to ensure that 100% of funded real estate projects directly align with corporate priorities.
  • Arbitrage and Continuity: Structure prioritization and trade-off files throughout the year to ensure dynamic allocation of financial and human resources during monthly and quarterly reviews.

Capacity Management and Resource Optimization

  • Integrated Roadmap Planning: Maintain global and centralized visibility of the short-, medium-, and long-term real estate roadmap (annual and 5-year plans).
  • Demand/Capacity Balancing: Continuously assess internal and external team workloads against capacity envelopes to proactively anticipate bottlenecks and plan future requirements effectively.
  • Interdependency Management: Cross-analyze critical dependencies across different groups (Facilities Planning, Asset Management, Engineering, Leasing, Major Construction Projects) to eliminate operational conflicts.

Delivery and Synchronization

  • Dashboards and Visibility: Develop and maintain Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and visual tracking tools to provide stakeholders with real-time visibility into costs, timelines, and expected benefits.
  • Data Integrity: Ensure the collection, centralization, and modeling of operational and financial portfolio data to support informed, value-driven decision-making.
  • Escalation process: Identify and resolve escalated tactical issues impeding project delivery, preparing files for the Governance Committee when required. Identify risk or issues that require escalation to the SteerCo for resolution.

Standardized Risk Management and Partner Tracking

  • Risk Management Process: Based on a risk-wise approach, drive informed risk management strategies, tracking action plans to reduce overall portfolio exposure.
  • Partner Performance Monitoring: Monitor the tactical and operational performance of PDS service provider, ensuring adherence to CBC/Radio-Canada’s quality control and compliance standards.

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

  • Seven (7) or more years of experience in project/program management, with at least three (3) years acting in a portfolio management or senior leadership role on complex initiatives.
  • Experience delivering large Real Estate projects and a strong understanding of what is involved in the maintenance of assets, modernization of workspaces, and transformation of owned/leased portfolios.
  • Strong financial acumen and understanding of both capital and operating expenditures within a real estate portfolio.
  • Expert ability to adapt communications and maintain alignment among diverse audiences, bridging the gap between highly technical teams, operational groups, and executive governance.
  • Strong proficiency in utilizing data tools to track portfolio performance metrics, turning complex, multi-location information into tailored summaries and comprehensive dashboards.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and negotiation skills (internal and external) to navigate seemingly-conflicting requirements and manage expectations.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Engineering, Business Administration, or equivalent experience and training.
  • Functional bilingualism (English/French).
  • Experience with Jira, Power BI, MS Project or similar tools is an asset.

This role requires creativity, strong leadership and sound judgment to successfully fulfil the show’s mandate. You’ll also need a keen understanding of digital media to effectively promote content and engage with audiences. 


Work must adhere to CBC/Radio-Canada journalistic and/or programming policies, standards and practices, and you are ultimately responsible for ensuring that this occurs. There is also a regular and ongoing requirement to co-ordinate the work of others.

 

You will have the following duties: 

  • Conceive, develop and execute program ideas and content. Participate in the preparation of program objectives in line with the mandate.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains, and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness, and relevance. 

 

Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on-air, online, or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

 

We are looking to hire a Researcher for CBC Montreal’s morning show Daybreak.


This is for a one-year replacement contract starting in January 2027.


Your role:

 

  • You have fresh ideas and a desire to create high-quality programming Canadians have come to expect from us. You understand Montreal’s English-speaking communities and have a desire to connect with the audience.
  • You are energized by working with a team and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace. 
  • You thrive in a fast-paced deadline-oriented environment.
  • As a researcher, you will attend story meetings and pitch interviews for the host of the radio show to conduct. 
  • You will research and book interviews, and prepare scripts and background information and supporting audio material for the producer and host. 
  • You will fact-check the information. 
  • You will also suggest innovative ways of conducting interviews. 
  • You will help post interviews on other CBC platforms.  
  • You will also work at maintaining a solid network of contacts in many communities in the Montreal region to ensure people from underrepresented communities have a voice on our show.
  • You may go out in the field to gather your interviews and sound and do live reports on air. 

For reference purposes, and at the time of this posting, the Daybreak shift is Monday-Friday, 9:30 am-5:30 pm in office.


Description of duties: 


  • Keep up with current events and maintain contacts with various sources.
  • Suggest and develop program content.
  • Attend production meetings. Suggest concepts, story ideas/angles, and potential guests.
  • Research and select information, ideas, and written, audio and audiovisual documents.
  • Recommend and, if necessary, select interviewees. Conduct pre-interviews. Suggest interview questions, approaches and scripts.
  • Prepare and present written and oral research reports. Constantly follow up with the host, before and during the program. Suggest intros as needed.
  • Provide logistical support (arrival time, fee, parking, etc.) for guests, correspondents and panellists. Inform them of the program’s content and lineup.
  • Create and maintain files on upcoming news stories.
  • Conduct short interviews on request and present your findings on air. Perform rough radio editing.

If necessary:


  • write questions for games or contests;
  • screen audience calls and reply to queries;
  • coordinate the content of columns;
  • conduct special research projects.
  • Perform all other related duties as needed.

We are looking for a candidate with the following: 

Qualifications


  • Bachelor's degree or the equivalent.
  • Two years of work experience. 

Skills:


  • Extensive knowledge of Montreal and surrounding areas.
  • Very good knowledge of current events
  • Fluency in English (spoken and written) and good knowledge of French.
  • Able to work independently and in a team.
  • Strong on-air presence.
  • A keen interest in local radio and radio story-telling.
  • Excellent knowledge of research tools and techniques. 
  • Knowledge of interview techniques. 
  • Able to analyze, synthesize and think critically.
  • Able to discuss a topic clearly. 
  • Must be able to make daily deadlines.

  • Interview
  • Assignment

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.


Your Role

 

The Software Contract and Compliance Management team is looking for a creative, highly skilled and talented Senior Analyst with solid knowledge of Software Compliance and Contract Lifecycle Management, tools and technologies for our downtown Toronto, Montreal or Ottawa office location.

 

Reporting to the Senior Manager of Software Compliance and Contract Management along with other Senior Analysts and working closely with Architects, Contract Owners and other Stakeholders, you will help put in place and improve the Software Compliance Framework and improve our Contract Lifecycle Management by gathering requirements, assessing technology roadmap alignment, providing financial forecasting and improving processes and communication.  You will enjoy innovative work in a creative and dynamic environment, working with leading technologies and having opportunities for continued professional development.  

 

How will you make an impact?

 

As the Contracts and Compliance Senior Analyst, you will:

  • Support Contract Lifecycle alignment between T&I contracts, rapid technology shifts, market changes, compliance readiness, and financial forecasting.
  • Gather the business needs for T&I contracts and foster alignment with the Technology Roadmaps and Capital Planning
  • Develop and implement processes for tracking contract status, timelines, expiration dates and key deliverables
  • Help establish processes supporting the transition of executed contracts from project implementation to operational state.
  • Work with the T&I stakeholders to help implement and maintain the Move, Add and Change processes and develop accurate inventory of deployed software and hardware assets  to facilitate the contract renewal process and software compliance.
  • Participate in contract negotiations and vendor management, as required
  • Help identify process inefficiencies and implement  improvements to enhance the department's effectiveness  and generate cost savings.
  • Participate in defining and implementing the Software Compliance Framework and ensuring software compliance along with our business partners
  • Execute internal audits and participate in external audits and negotiations,provide risk assessment and identify opportunities for improvement
  • Help develop, implement and support tools and metrics to ensure adequate communication of Contract Lifecycle Management and Software Compliance status to all relevant stakeholders
  • Provide In-depth technical and  financial analysis, audit readiness, and executive briefings for the Strategic contracts across all T&I portfolios
  • Provide expertise to our business partners in all aspects of Contract Lifecycle Management and Software Compliance Framework
  • Translate Key strategic initiatives into tactical objectives and manage their execution and delivery
  • Build and foster partnerships with our internal and external business partners to ensure on-time and on budget contract renewals and maintain software compliance

 

Perks you can look forward to:

  • Four weeks of vacation per year.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development - including access to e-learning services, customized courses and certification opportunities.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.

 

What you bring to our team:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, computer science or equivalent.
  • Three or more years of experience in a business analyst role.
  • Familiarity with the agile methodologies and Jira.
  • Good negotiation skills.
  • Demonstrated financial experience.
  • Strong communication skills (both written and oral).
  • Excellent team player with strong interpersonal skills.
  • Good general knowledge and intellectual curiosity (acquire and develop new knowledge and skills).
  • Creativity and Innovation.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) is a requirement.

Role Purpose:

Reporting to the Senior Director, Total Compensation, the Senior Manager, Total Compensation leads a team of two Senior Specialists in the governance, strategic design, implementation, and continuous improvement of CBC/Radio-Canada's core total compensation and associated programs. Serving as an operational leader, this role ensures robust compensation governance, provides expert advisory services across Human Resources and Industrial Relations, and leads the functional oversight of the People and Culture Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP) portfolio.

Key Responsibilities:

Compensation Governance, Strategy & Program Management

  • Establish, review, and evolve corporate standards, policies, and methodologies for all compensation-related programs across the Corporation (including market benchmarking, pay structures, job evaluations, and salary reviews).

  • Lead the annual salary planning (merit review) cycle, external market benchmarking studies, and comprehensive pay scale reviews.

  • Develop, implement, and monitor job evaluation plans to ensure regulatory compliance, process efficiency, and alignment with corporate benchmarks.

  • Conduct regular and specialized research into internal and external market practices; develop revised pay structures, models, and policy recommendations for senior leadership.

  • Recommend and implement updates to compensation and related policies to maintain the Corporation’s target competitive market position while ensuring full regulatory compliance and alignment with the corporate strategy.

Pay Equity & Union Collaboration

  • Participate in the implementation of the Corporation’s Pay Equity Plan in close collaboration with unions, leadership, and external consultants.

  • Oversee and conduct mandatory 5-year Pay Equity Audits in accordance with federal regulations, coordinating directly with union representatives and joint committees.

  • Provide strategic compensation input and recommendations for collective bargaining negotiations; provide support  to the Total Compensation expert representative at the bargaining table when required.

Strategic Partnerships & System Optimization

  • Partner with HRIS and HR Services teams in the continuous enhancement and optimization of HR Information Systems (Workday), identifying opportunities to streamline workflows and improve data efficiency.

  • Collaborate with the Benefits and Pension teams to foster a unified Total Rewards model and deliver clear, compelling Total Rewards employee communications.

  • Maintain an integrated HR approach, partnering closely with Talent Management & OD, Industrial Relations, HR Services, and HR Business Partners to ensure cohesive client service delivery.

ATIP & Regulatory Portfolio Oversight

  • Lead the Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP) portfolio for People & Culture, serving as the primary liaison with the corporate ATIP office and external governing bodies.

  • Manage and coordinate all People & Culture responses to ATIP, Privy Council Office, Statistics Canada, and other government/regulatory requests, ensuring accurate and timely delivery.

  • Provide functional guidance, coaching, and subject-matter expertise to HR Business Partners and Talent Acquisition leads on compensation frameworks and ATIP compliance principles.

Team Leadership & Operational Oversight

  • Direct, coach, and mentor a team of two Senior Specialists, establishing clear performance goals, providing developmental feedback, and fostering high team engagement.

  • Oversee the team’s daily workload to ensure high-quality, compliant execution of specialized compensation projects, advisory services, and continuous process improvements.

  • Influence and collaborate across People & Culture to promote process efficiency and operational productivity linked to Total Rewards and ATIP programs.

  • Go to resource when the Senior Director, Total Compensation is unavailable.

Qualifications, Experience & Skills:

Education & Experience

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Industrial Relations, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).

  • Professional Experience: 8 to 10 years of progressive HR experience, with at least 5 years dedicated to compensation design, governance, and administration.

  • Leadership Experience: Minimum 2 to 3 years of experience directly managing, supervising, or mentoring direct reports or project teams.

  • Environment: Proven experience working within a complex, unionized public, Crown or private sector environment is strongly preferred.

  • Certifications: CCP (Certified Compensation Professional) or CHRL (Certified Human Resources Leader) designation is an asset.

Knowledge & Skills

  • Bilingualism: Fully bilingual in French and English (written and spoken) is mandatory.

  • Compensation Expertise: Advanced expertise in base pay design, job evaluation methodologies, market salary surveys, and federal pay equity legislation.

  • ATIP & Privacy Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of Access to Information and Privacy regulations and governance principles within the public sector context is an asset.

  • Critical Thinking & Decision-Making: Superior analytical capability and sound judgment to resolve complex, precedent-setting issues while balancing business needs with policy compliance.

  • Interpersonal & Strategic Communication: Excellent negotiation, diplomacy, and communication skills with a demonstrated ability to build strong cross-functional partnerships and influence senior executive stakeholders.

CBC News is looking for a creative editorial leader with sharp news judgement to lead our live and daily audio news programming on the weekends.


As Senior Producer, Live & Daily News, Weekend Early Audio, you drive daily programming with a hyper-focus on live and breaking national and international news for our hourly radio news and podcast programs, World Report and The World This Hour.


You bring an audience-first mindset to the role, shaping compelling content that plays equally well as a podcast as it does on terrestrial radio. You are expected to steer daily editorial meetings, stimulate creative discussions, and identify the most impactful stories and treatments for the day.


You react decisively to major developments, track stories in real time and reshape shows on the fly to ensure our audiences are getting the content they need to know, now. Based in Toronto, this is a full-time, permanent position. The successful candidate will work a four-day compressed work week (Thursday to Sunday, roughly 2:30 a.m.-12:45 p.m.). Hours are decided by operational requirements. You can expect some overtime when news is breaking.

● Manage Production & Broadcast: Exercise editorial responsibility over daily production and live broadcasting. Co-ordinate resources and determine the look, style, and pace of the lineup to maintain consistency with network mandates. Thrive under intense deadline pressures.

● Change Agent: Drives continuous improvement, agile and adaptable in transforming newsroom structures and roles and lead transitions. You understand what motivates people. You welcome feedback and carefully consider that input as you align your team around shared goals. You celebrate success.

● Foster Collaboration: Facilitate open, inclusive story meetings. Encourage story pitches and development. Collaborate across CBC News platforms to co-ordinate content, such raw sound, clipped material and packaged audio items.

● Team Leadership: Actively support staff development, provide ongoing constructive feedback and coaching. Connect regularly with senior leadership about staffing and scheduling requirements and team culture.

● Champion Audience Growth: Translate insights and data to guide content decisions to expand our reach to new and younger news consumers, and to deepen our engagement with all Canadians.

● Maintain Standards: Strictly uphold CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices at all times.

● Operational Support: Step in to perform all or part of the functions of an equivalent or lower classification as needed.


Qualifications

● Experience: Minimum of seven years in broadcast journalism, with a university degree or college diploma in journalism, audio production, or a related field.

● Live Broadcast Expertise: Proven experience producing live and breaking news programming, including production planning and resource co-ordination. Demonstrated ability as a programmer with a keen ear for pacing, tone, and presentation.

● Technical Proficiency: Mandatory experience taking programs to air, alongside highly developed audio production skills. Familiarity with technology including iNews, Dalet, Avid Media Central and Google tools for content creation, distribution, and planning.

● Critical thinking: Exceptional problem-solving skills to navigate fast-moving, high- pressure news situations. You're adept at verifying and fact-checking content.

● Broad Knowledge Base: Deep interest and understanding across topics such as politics, business, science, sports, entertainment, and health.

● Mentorship Skills: Superior coaching abilities to support developing journalists, veteran staff, and on-air hosts. Exceptional communication, organizational, and feedback skills.

● Industry Awareness: A deep commitment to public broadcasting, understanding of modern industry trends, ability to identify legal and ethical issues in journalism, and application of CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.

Reporting to the Senior Producer of CBC Scams, you demonstrate exceptional skills in on-camera presentation, interviewing, research, writing, prioritizing mobile and social platforms.


We’re looking for a reporter who lights up the screen, is warm and relatable, knows how to use humour at exactly the right moments, can laugh at themselves,  and can be serious and ask the tough questions when the story demands it. 


You consume short-story videos daily, including on CBC News apps, TikTok and YouTube. While you’re comfortable filing video, text and audio stories, you prioritize mobile-first storytelling, engaging with new and younger audiences where they are at, live and on-demand. 


Vertical storytelling is core to your journalism. You know how to grab viewers’ attention within the first two to three seconds, and keep them engaged with dynamic pacing, fast cut edits, animation, visual layering and high-impact captioning. 


As a senior reporter, you’re working ahead on dynamic video reports, but you’re also prepared to move fast on breaking news, providing updates as they come and pivoting where required. You are confident going live on digital live story pages and programs when required. You bring excellent presentation skills and can break down complex information quickly, simply and accurately on the fly. You thrive in a deadline-driven environment. 


You have a strong Understanding of CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices, upholding our core principles of accuracy, fairness, balance, impartiality and integrity.  


You take initiative and move stories forward with a strong investigative sense. You’re also a team player who welcomes stepping in to assist your colleagues when you see the need. 


This job is 5 days a week, full-time, with an expectation to work overtime, early mornings, evenings and weekends as required. It’s a one-year full time position based in Toronto. As collaborating with teams across CBC News is a priority, you will be required to be on-site for this role.

  • Pitch stories about fraudulent practices, scams and consumer misinformation that will target new and younger audiences. Break news and follow developments.

  • Generate and execute journalism that elevates a range of voices and perspectives.
  • Shape scripts and file stories for all platforms. Prioritize a mobile and streaming audience. 
  • Work collaboratively with editors and vettors to sharpen writing, headlines and text.

  • Be able to remain calm under pressure.

He or she will report to the Senior Head of News and Programming (NS-PEI-NL) and the station’s Digital Producer.


In this role, you will be primarily responsible for creating digital content, collaborating on the Radio-Canada website and associated digital platforms across our large territory. You will write news stories under tight deadlines, review texts created by others, and must be able to create, organize, and prioritize digital news content. You will also enrich texts with multimedia material to increase their value for the audience. You will also be called upon to support programs to help them increase and enhance their digital presence.


Functions:


Demonstrate and cultivate exceptional skills in continuous news writing, editing, and assembly, in compliance with the Radio-Canada style and under tight deadlines. You will work according to CBC/Radio-Canada’s journalistic and programming policies, as well as its journalistic standards and practices. The work is carried out under the direction of the editorial team, but you are expected to show initiative and sound judgment. You will be called upon to coordinate or review the activities of other people.


Key tasks:

  • Write, edit, assemble, and publish digital content clearly and concisely for a regional and national audience.
  • Organize and update the web pages for Radio-Canada Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador.
  • Ensure that websites and reports correspond to the priorities of the day.
  • Support radio teams in promoting their content on digital platforms.
  • Gather information from various sources and report on it.
  • Rewrite texts, as needed, so they better fit the platform’s format.
  • Ensure that all texts respect standard grammar rules and the Radio-Canada site style, notably the correct usage of spelling and capitalization.
  • Write headlines that comply with guidelines for social media research and publication.
  • Select photos and audio/video clips to accompany online reports.
  • Critically review content and items produced by other people.
  • Prepare and write articles and headlines based on information provided by reporters, wire services, the CBC, or original sources.
  • Determine the elements to include in a report, their order, duration, and sequence. Create the required elements.
  • Suggest ideas or content for programs; participate in preparing program objectives for digital platforms.
  • Liaise with other staff members to ensure that the required material is available.
  • Publish Radio-Canada material on social media and other platforms.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

  • University degree or equivalent
  • Five (5) years of experience directly related to the position, including a demonstrated knowledge of online and digital news media
  • Extensive and demonstrable knowledge of regional, national, and international issues
  • Ability to write a wide range of material related to news and current affairs
  • Confirmed experience and aptitude in writing/editing following best practices and style for digital platforms
  • Ability to select and prepare photos and videos to enhance reports
  • Experience in detecting potential legal problems and violations of journalistic policies in digital content

Your Role


CBC/Radio-Canada is seeking a dynamic, curious professional with a passion for emerging technologies and broadcast and digital production to join our Production team in Moncton. As Technical Producer, you will identify and plan technical requirements for television productions, allocate assigned resources effectively and maximize the operational performance of the crews, studios, mobile units, and production and post-production facilities under your supervision — all in alignment with corporate and industry standards.


In this role, you will advise and guide production, programming and management teams on technological capabilities and resource optimization. Working within established operational frameworks, you will collaborate closely with media line partners to determine and confirm staffing needs, balance workloads, build shift schedules that leverage individual strengths, and ensure adherence to collective agreements. You will also co-ordinate internal and external production resources, determine gear and equipment requirements, as well as plan and oversee facility setup and operation while ensuring strict compliance with technical quality standards, applicable legislation, and occupational health and safety regulations.


You will proactively flag operational hurdles, workflow bottlenecks and collective agreement compliance issues to management, while managing crew overtime and leave requests. In addition, you will evaluate employee performance, identify training needs and take part in selecting and hiring staff. When necessary, you will recommend and administer disciplinary measures and communicate them transparently to staff.


You will represent the Corporation in dealings with external vendors and service providers. Operating within your delegated financial authority, you will negotiate and approve lease and procurement terms with suppliers for goods and services required for production. 


You will manage production budgets and technical procurement; prepare financial estimates, summaries and feasibility studies; and recommend recurring and special capital expenditures as well as strategic development plans for your departments.


This position may require irregular hours, occasional travel and shift work (including evenings, weekends and rotating schedules) to meet production demands and operational emergencies.


This role requires full-time on-site presence.

  • College diploma in television production, media arts and technology, or equivalent.

  • Comprehensive, practical knowledge of production workflows, technical equipment and production crafts.
  • General understanding of CBC/Radio-Canada’s cross-platform media operations (radio, television and digital).
  • Strong logistical skills.
  • Proven experience working in both English and French language media environments.
  • Solid knowledge of newsroom operations.
  • Sound editorial judgment and a keen interest in regional, national and international news and current affairs.
  • Demonstrated ability to supervise teams and manage technical production operations ranging from moderate to high complexity. 
  • Proven ability to balance staffing with production demands, resolve operational challenges and mediate workplace issues. 
  • Strong working knowledge of the Canada Labour Code, particularly Part II (Occupational Health and Safety). 
  • Up-to-date knowledge of emerging production, transmission, broadcast and information technologies.

Assignment Producer, Weekends, Saskatchewan

CBC Saskatchewan is looking for an experienced journalist and newsroom leader to drive our daily and enterprise news coverage as an assignment producer. The role can be based in either Regina or Saskatoon. This is a permanent, full-time role that will include weekends and three weekdays.

Reporting to the Executive Producer, News, the successful candidate will join the team that assigns our newsgathering resources, decides what stories to cover, when and by whom. You will help set the news agenda for Saskatchewan on weekends, and continue that work on our assignment desk for three days during the week. You will be familiar with the editorial needs of audiences in both Regina and Saskatoon.

You will be an editorial leader and an experienced mentor, someone who demonstrates sound news judgment and critical thinking skills in both breaking news and enterprise reporting, and who inspires others to be innovative and creative.

As a leader, you are naturally collaborative, skilled at navigating conflict and change, breaking down silos and developing a representative and inclusive culture.

You will have experience in all aspects of news, from breaking events to investigative projects, and you will thrive as part of a team in the fast-paced, high-pressure world of a multi-platform newsroom. You understand that daily news can be a flat-out sprint to deadline, with myriad complex decisions to make along the way, so organizational skills are key.

You will be a strategic thinker who puts audience needs at the centre of your decision-making, ensuring our news content on all of all platforms connects our audiences to the news they need to know, the stories that affect their lives and the issues that resonate in their communities. You will strive to broaden the range of perspectives and experiences reflected in our news content, especially those from people who have been traditionally underrepresented in the media.  

You will ensure that all our work adheres to CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices and that it upholds our core principles of accuracy, fairness, balance, impartiality and integrity. 

Your responsibilities:

  •  Organize and lead news coverage across all platforms (video, digital, social, radio, television, streaming), including making decisions about story priorities and rollouts, allocating resources and assigning staff, and providing editorial oversight to ensure our content is original, relevant and impactful, and meets our journalistic standards.

  • Oversee all aspects of story development including assigning, researching, gathering, writing, copy editing, vetting, packaging and push alerts.

  • Oversee the distribution of our content on multiple platforms, 

  • Ensure assignments and content choices resonate with residents of Saskatchewan and align with CBC’s strategic objectives to connect with and grow audiences.

  • Oversee and collaborate with the other producers on the assignment desk (mornings, afternoons, weekends) to ensure continuity of news coverage.

  • Coordinate and collaborate on story assignments with producers of digital, visuals and current affairs radio, the weekend Radio-Canada team, as well as with producers in other locations and program units.

  • Provide feedback and coaching to journalists to help them develop their skills and produce content of the highest quality.

  • Help lead the planning of newsroom-wide coverage for special projects and events.

  • Help oversee staffing and scheduling decisions. 

Your profile:

  • Demonstrated experience leading a team in a fast-paced daily multi-platform news environment.

  • Excellent journalistic and critical thinking skills, including knowledge of and familiarity with CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices as well as the legal and ethical issues related to journalism.

  • Ability to manage and organize large volumes of fast-moving information and redirect resources to meet priorities and objectives.

  • Knowledge of and experience in assigning and creating content for all platforms (video, digital, social, radio, television, streaming) as well as vetting, editing, fact-checking and packaging.

  • Superior communication, interpersonal and organizational skills.

  • A strategic thinker with a proven track record of executing on a vision.

  • Demonstrated ability to exercise both quick editorial judgment and long-term planning.

  • A high-energy leader with a positive, team-first attitude and the ability to motivate and coach teams, encourage creativity and embrace experimentation.

  • Experience and commitment to developing content strategies to feature new voices and perspectives and to connect with new, younger and more diverse audiences.

¤ CNN is hiring a Senior Technical Program Manager to lead high-impact programs that span product, technology, design, and product operations. This is a deeply technical senior individual-contributor role for someone who can move between architecture, code, product strategy, operating models, and executive decision-making without losing the thread. The role reports directly to the Senior Director of Technical Program Management and will be trusted with ambiguous, multi-quarter programs that do not fit neatly inside one function. The programs in this portfolio often have no single functional owner, require trade-offs across several organizations, and need sustained influence with Vice Presidents, Directors, principal-level practitioners, and the teams doing the work. This is not a coordination-only position. The person in this role will define the problem, establish the program strategy, understand the underlying systems, challenge weak assumptions, create alignment, and drive measurable outcomes through delivery, launch, adoption, and iteration. WHAT YOU WILL OWN Lead a portfolio of high-priority, cross-organization technical programs from early problem framing through execution, launch, adoption, and measurable business or customer impact. Turn broad goals into clear program strategies, outcome metrics, decision rights, sequencing, governance, and executable plans across multiple teams. Build and maintain integrated plans, dependencies, critical paths, decision logs, risk views, and executive-level narratives that make the real state of the work visible. Identify the technical, product, organizational, and operational constraints that will determine success; resolve them directly or drive the right leaders to a timely decision. Work with senior leaders, including VPs, to clarify priorities, expose trade-offs, remove blockers, and create durable alignment without relying on formal authority. Move comfortably between several programs and levels of detail in the same day, while preserving context, commitments, and follow-through. Create the minimum effective operating model for each program: enough structure to move quickly and safely, without adding process that does not improve outcomes. Develop trusted relationships across Product, Engineering, Design, Product Operations, Architecture, Data, Security, Editorial, Revenue, and other partner organizations as the work requires. Raise the quality of program leadership across the organization by modeling strong judgment, direct communication, technical curiosity, and disciplined execution. TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP EXPECTATIONS This role is not a software-engineering position, but it is intentionally more technical than a traditional program-management role. The successful candidate must be able to engage engineers and architects as a credible peer and independently investigate technical questions. Read, write, review, and reason about code. Use (ai) code when it is the fastest way to validate an assumption, automate work, inspect data, reproduce a problem, or demonstrate a solution. Understand modern software-delivery practices, including source control, pull requests, testing, CI/CD, observability, incident response, release strategies, and production operations. Evaluate system architecture, service boundaries, API contracts, event flows, data models, cloud infrastructure, security constraints, reliability concerns, and integration risks well enough to shape the program plan. Lead technical discovery with engineers and architects, translate findings into decisions and sequencing, and recognize when a proposed plan is technically incomplete or unrealistic. Use data and technical evidence to distinguish symptoms from root causes and to challenge estimates, assumptions, or dependencies constructively. Communicate technical choices and consequences in language that product, design, operations, and executive stakeholders can act on. PRODUCT, DESIGN, AND OPERATING JUDGMENT Frame the customer, user, editorial, operational, or business problem before converging on a solution; connect program work to a clear value hypothesis. Partner closely with Product and Design to define intended outcomes, success measures, experience principles, scope boundaries, and the smallest credible path to learning or value. Pressure-test prioritization using customer impact, strategic fit, technical leverage, cost, risk, reversibility, and opportunity cost. Translate product strategy into a delivery approach that includes discovery, design, engineering, operational readiness, launch, measurement, and follow-up—not just a milestone schedule. Work with Product Operations to improve planning, decision-making, portfolio visibility, adoption, feedback loops, and repeatable ways of working across teams. Recognize when a program needs a product decision, a technical decision, an operating-model change, or an executive trade-off, and drive the correct conversation. EXECUTIVE INFLUENCE AND PROGRAM LEADERSHIP Present complex situations to senior leaders with clarity: what changed, why it matters, what choices exist, what you recommend, and what decision is needed. Escalate early and with options. Avoid status-only escalation and make it easy for leaders to take the next action. Build alignment across leaders who may have different goals, incentives, vocabulary, or operating rhythms; surface disagreement rather than allowing false consensus. Make sound decisions independently within the role's mandate and know when additional input or explicit executive sponsorship is required. Stay effective under ambiguity, organizational change, incomplete information, and shifting priorities while maintaining a high bar for quality and accountability. Create an environment in which teams can raise risks, make decisions, and move quickly without losing transparency or ownership. WHAT YOU WILL BRING Required qualifications At least 5 years of direct experience leading complex technical programs, with demonstrated principal- or senior-level scope in a matrixed organization. A strong software-engineering foundation or equivalent hands-on technical background, including the ability to complete a practical coding assessment. Demonstrated ability to understand architecture and implementation details, ask precise technical questions, and convert technical realities into an effective program strategy. Strong product judgment, including problem framing, customer or user thinking, prioritization, metrics, experimentation, and trade-off analysis. A record of driving cross-functional outcomes across Product, Engineering, Design, and Operations from ambiguity through launch and adoption. Experience influencing Directors, VPs, and other senior leaders through clear reasoning, evidence, strong recommendations, and persistent follow-through. Exceptional independence, ownership, context switching, and organizational awareness; able to enter a new domain quickly and determine what matters. Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive updates, decision documents, program narratives, and direct facilitation of difficult conversations. A practical approach to process: rigorous where risk and complexity demand it, lightweight where speed and learning matter more. Preferred qualifications Previous experience as a software engineer, engineering lead, architect, technical product manager, or similarly technical role. Experience with large-scale consumer digital products, media or publishing systems, subscriptions, advertising, data platforms, AI-enabled products, or platform modernization. Experience leading programs that require changes to both technology and the way teams plan, make decisions, or operate. Experience working across multiple time zones, business units, vendors, or shared-platform organizations. Comfort using modern development, analytics, planning, and collaboration tools to investigate work directly rather than relying only on reported status. WHAT STRONG PERFORMANCE LOOKS LIKE First 90 days — Context and trust: Build a clear map of the portfolio, systems, stakeholders, constraints, and unresolved decisions. Establish credibility with technical and product leaders and create momentum on the highest-value issues. By 6 months — Independent program leadership: Run multiple high-stakes programs with reliable visibility, strong technical and product framing, timely decisions, and fewer avoidable surprises. Senior leaders should view the role as a force multiplier, not an additional reporting layer. By 12 months — Durable outcomes: Deliver measurable program results, improve the organization's ability to execute across boundaries, and leave behind reusable decision, planning, and operating patterns that make future work faster and clearer. CANDIDATE ASSESSMENT The interview process will evaluate the complete shape of the role rather than program-management mechanics alone. Candidates should expect: A practical coding assessment focused on problem solving, code comprehension, implementation quality, debugging, automation, data handling, or API/system interaction. job.title: TEMP - Rental Services Coordinator, Boosey & Hawkes
job.description:
Overview

Founded in 2008, BMG is committed to building the world’s most trusted, forward-looking music company. Following its combination with Concord in 2026, BMG brings together global scale, deep expertise, technology, and partnership to unlock new opportunities for creators while protecting and growing the long-term value and cultural impact of their work.  

 

BMG’s repertoire includes works by iconic global artists, songwriters, composers, and playwrights, including will.i.am, Phil Collins, Tina Turner, Lin-Manuel Miranda, Jason Aldean, Jelly Roll, Evanescence, Kylie Minogue, Billie Holiday, Rodgers & Hammerstein, Creedence Clearwater Revival, Tennessee Williams, OneRepublic, Daddy Yankee, and Leonard Bernstein.  

 

Headquartered in Nashville with 18 offices globally, BMG is privately held and part of Bertelsmann, the international media, services and education company, with a minority stake held by affiliates of Great Mountain Partners. 

Responsibilities

Your Mission:

Boosey & Hawkes is the world’s leading publisher of contemporary classical music, with a blue-chip catalogue of 20th-century masters including Bartók, Bernstein, Britten, Copland, Prokofieff, Strauss and Stravinsky alongside an eminent front list of composers that includes John Adams, Louis Andriessen, Harrison Birtwistle, Unsuk Chin, Brett Dean, Detlev Glanert, Osvaldo Golijov, HK Gruber, Karl Jenkins, Magnus Lindberg, James MacMillan, Steve Reich and Mark-Anthony Turnage. The company has offices in London, New York and Berlin and a network of agents around the world. Boosey & Hawkes is proud to be part of the Concord Music family.

 

The Rental Servies Coordinator Temp is responsible for supporting the Boosey and Hawkes Rental Department by managing various administrative duties. Works under direct supervision.

 

What You’ll Be Doing:

• Provides support in licensing rental materials from the Boosey & Hawkes catalog and agency classical music catalogs for orchestras in North & South America• Provides front-line customer service and monitor inquiry queues• Assigns sheet music assets and deliverables in a timely manner• Administers licenses to orchestras, ensembles and universities• Maintains positive relationships with music artists, librarians and presenters• Informs customers on issues regarding copyright and licensing• Works with distribution center regarding the timely delivery of sheet music assets• Manages incoming calls and email correspondence• Provides database/inventory management and general support to the department

Qualifications

What You Bring:

• Previous experience in the customer service sector• College or conservatory degree in music, or equivalent experience in classical music required• Minimum 1-2 years related job experience a plus• Proficiency with Microsoft Office; ability to learn and navigate proprietary software• Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment  Hourly Rate: $25/hr *This is a hybrid role requiring 3 days minimum on-site. BMG is an equal opportunity employer. We employ, train, compensate and promote regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law. We believe that diversity, inclusion and equity is paramount for the creation of music, theater and film that celebrates and empowers all cultures.

Connoisseur Media is looking for a Full-Time Engineer for our North Dallas (Sherman-McKinney, TX) market. The ideal candidate has basic knowledge of, or is willing to learn about, radio broadcast technical systems and equipment to ensure reliable, high-quality audio transmission for our three radio stations - 97.5 KLAK, 93.1 KMKT, and 102.5 KMAD-FM. The ideal candidate works well under pressure, creates solutions, and is a resourceful, diligent, engaged, and creative problem-solver, with not just a “can-do” but a “will-do” attitude. While we seek someone well-versed in, or willingness to learn, broadcast engineering, a candidate’s interpersonal and communication skills, as well as business and personal integrity, are just as important as technical ability.

Responsibilities

for this position include: Compliance with FCC regulations and station policies regarding broadcast standards. Maintenance of safety protocols in all engineering practices. Chief Operator (EAS, Maintenance, and Transmitter Readings log management & review). Regular inspection and maintenance of broadcast equipment, including a mix of solid-state and high-power tube transmitters, audio consoles, studio gear, audio automation systems, remote broadcast systems, and other related equipment. Perform hands-on routine preventive maintenance and repairs on all technical systems. Monitor audio quality and signal strength during radio broadcasts and be able to quickly troubleshoot issues, as needed. Under the direction of Corporate IT, complete all necessary procedures and paperwork relating to the market’s computer system and be the local eyes and hands for remote IT Help Desk support. Oversee the installation of new equipment and technologies, including the planning and implementation of upgrades to existing systems. Work with the Director of Engineering and market Operations Manager to manage capital projects and implement corporate initiatives. Maintain minimal downtime of broadcast, audio and computer systems, including emergency repairs, but also planning and advocating for any necessary improvements to all systems. Provide technical support and expertise, as needed, to other departments in planning and executing initiatives. Clear, professional, and productive communication with employees who do not have technical or programming backgrounds, as well as subcontractors and vendors. Develop clear instructions relating to simple tasks for non-technical employees to understand and perform. Maintain an accurate equipment inventory, maintenance logs, and technical schematics. This includes the preparation of reports relating to asset additions/disposals and technical issues and solutions. Requirements of this position include the following: A minimum of 1-3 years audio engineering, Radio/TV broadcast engineering and/or IT experience. Knowledge of FCC Regulations. Availability to travel to multiple market locations and transmitter sites. Familiarity with, or willingness to learn about, broadcast automation and centralized audio routing systems. Basic knowledge of, or willingness to learn about, computer networks, STL systems, RF & landline, including analog, digital, and IP. A flexible self-manager with the ability to prioritize tasks and shift priorities as needed. This position requires a fully insured personal vehicle and a valid driver’s license. The candidate is required to provide a safe driving record covering the past three years. Must be able to develop collaborative and productive relationships with market employees, so market staff can help troubleshoot effectively when the engineer is off-site. On call availability for transmitter, studio, and remote broadcast technical issues, remote alarm calls, emergencies, and be proactive about coverage when unavailable. ​

Preferred Qualifications

Military or Post-Secondary electronics training. SBE Certification.

Experience

with Axia LiveWire routing. Demonstrated Project Management skills.​

job.title: Street Team & Board Operator (Part-Time)
job.description:
Connoisseur Media – Amarillo, TX Love live events, great music, sports, and radio? Want to be part of the team behind some of Amarillo's most recognized radio brands? Connoisseur Media Amarillo is looking for an energetic, dependable, and enthusiastic Part-Time Street Team & Board Operator to help bring our stations to life both on the air and in the community. Represent KGNC 97.9 (KGNC-FM), 100.9 The Eagle (KXGL-FM), 102.9 The Rattler (KVWE-FM), and NewsTalk 710 & 97.5 KGNC (KGNC-AM) at concerts, festivals, live broadcasts, sporting events, and community appearances while also helping keep our stations sounding their best behind the scenes. No two days are the same! One day you could be hosting games and giveaways at a concert, and the next you could be running a live sports broadcast or operating the control board during a live show. If you're outgoing, love working with people, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and have a passion for radio and live entertainment, we'd love to meet you!

What You'll Do

Represent our stations at live broadcasts, concerts, festivals, sporting events, and community events. Set up and tear down promotional equipment, including tents, banners, sound systems, tables, and displays. Engage listeners through contests, prize wheels, games, giveaways, and on-site promotions. Make announcements using microphones and PA systems while creating an exciting event atmosphere. Drive station vehicles and transport promotional equipment to and from events. Operate the on-air control board for live and syndicated programming. Run live sports broadcasts, programming, commercials, and station breaks with accuracy. Monitor automation systems, transmitters, and studio equipment to ensure smooth broadcasts. Maintain broadcast logs and accurately report discrepancies. Follow FCC regulations, EAS procedures, and station operating standards. Communicate effectively with station management regarding technical or programming concerns. Work collaboratively with promotions, programming, sales, and engineering teams. Perform other duties as assigned. What We're Looking For Positive, energetic personality with excellent customer service skills. Strong communication skills and the confidence to interact with listeners, clients, and coworkers. Reliable, self-motivated, and able to work independently or as part of a team. Comfortable working outdoors and in varying weather conditions. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and assist with event setup and teardown. Ability to work evenings, weekends, holidays, and occasional last-minute shifts. Valid driver's license and current auto insurance. Must be able to drive a company vehicle. Must be at least 18 years old (21+ preferred for events where alcohol is served).

Preferred Qualifications

Previous

experience

in radio, promotions, live events, sports broadcasting, or media.

Experience

operating radio automation systems such as Marketron or similar software. Familiarity with FCC rules and EAS requirements.

Experience

with social media platforms, WordPress, or digital content creation. Passion for music, sports, entertainment, and connecting with the local community. This is a part-time position averaging 10–15 hours per week, with additional hours available during busy event seasons and special programming opportunities. If you're looking for a fun, hands-on opportunity to break into broadcasting while representing some of Amarillo's favorite radio stations, we encourage you to apply!
