job.title: CDL Driver - Yard Spotter / Maintenance Tech
job.description: Primary responsibility will be serving as the semi-tractor driver for hauling trailers and containers within the Studio grounds and between our local off-site storage facilities.  This includes coordinating DOT inspections and maintenance with various vendors. Will also work with domestic and international transportation department coordinators and on-site security personnel regarding logistics and storage of trailers. When there are times that there’s no activity related to trailer movement, this position will assume Studio operations duties as directed by manager as a secondary responsibility.   This position will require periods of night and week-end over-time duties.

job.title: Accounting Manager
job.description:
Overview of the Firm 

FGS Global helps the world's most influential leaders move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments.

We work as one team across geographies and disciplines - bringing together specialists with backgrounds in communications, finance, law, government, journalism, data science, and digital. Whatever the moment demands, we combine multidimensional perspectives to help leaders anticipate what's next, engage the stakeholders who matter, and drive meaningful outcomes.

Across 31 global offices, we draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust. This collaborative approach has established FGS as a market leader: we are consistently ranked Band 1 for Crisis & Risk Management and Litigation Support by Chambers and Partners, and were ranked the #1 Global M&A PR firm by deal value and deal count for four consecutive years (Mergermarket, 2025).

 

The Role

We are seeking an experienced and hands-on Accounting Manager to join our Asia finance team in Hong Kong. Reporting to the Head of Finance, Asia, and working closely with the Finance Operations Senior Manager, this role plays a key part in the accounting operations of the firm across the Hong Kong, Singapore, and China entities, with key responsibility for the month-end close, financial reporting, and tax compliance, as well as supporting the statutory and group audits. The role places a strong focus on income statement analysis to provide insight into revenue and cost performance.

The ideal candidate will be a qualified accountant who combines strong technical knowledge with a hands-on approach, takes accountability for their deliverables, and communicates clearly with senior internal and external stakeholders. They will be comfortable operating in a fast-paced professional services environment and contributing to continuous improvement in processes and controls. Experience with VAT/GST filing across Singapore and China jurisdictions will be highly regarded.

 

Responsibilities

  • Work closely with the Finance Operations Senior Manager on month-end close, audits, and process improvements, ensuring alignment across the Asia finance function.
  • Act as a key member to perform the month-end closing, including revenue recognition, accruals, and balance sheet reconciliations, ensuring accurate and compliant accounting treatment.
  • Perform detailed monthly income statement analysis, explaining revenue and cost movements against prior periods, budget and forecast, and identifying trends, anomalies and risks.
  • Ensure departmental costs are accurately recorded, coded, and allocated to the correct cost centres, reviewing cost reports and resolving variances with budget holders on a timely basis.
  • Review and deliver monthly, quarterly, and annual financial and management reports, providing analysis and commentary on key variances to the Head of Finance and regional leadership.
  • Support the statutory and group audit processes together with Finance Operations Senior Manager.
  • Manage tax filing obligations across Hong Kong, Singapore, and China, including GST/VAT compliance, corporate income tax, and withholding tax matters, and liaise with external tax advisers.
  • Partner with operational teams on cost budgeting and reforecasting to support business to drive cost control.
  • Proactively identify opportunities to drive cost optimisation, analysing spending trends and recommending practical cost-saving initiatives to the Head of Finance and business leaders.
  • Partner with global finance teams and external service providers on group reporting, intercompany, and consolidation matters.
  • Maintain and strengthen internal controls and accounting policies, and drive process and system improvements to enhance efficiency in the Asia finance function.
  • Support ad hoc finance projects as required.

 

Desired Skills & Qualities

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or a related discipline from a recognised university.
  • A recognised professional accounting qualification (e.g. HKICPA, ACCA, CPA) is required.
  • Over 10 years of relevant accounting experience, preferably in a professional services or multinational environment. Audit firm experience is an advantage.
  • Solid technical accounting knowledge, with experience applying US GAAP and/or IFRS/HKFRS.
  • Strong analytical skills with a proven track record in income statement analysis, able to translate financial results into clear, actionable insights for business leaders.
  • Proven experience supporting statutory audits and managing tax filings across multiple jurisdictions; familiarity with Singapore GST and China VAT filing will be highly considered.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel; experience with ERP or accounting systems such as NetSuite is strongly preferred.
  • Strong team player, with the ability to guide and support junior team members.
  • Hands-on, highly organised, and able to manage competing priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced and dynamic working environment.
  • Treasury experience is a plus but it is NOT a must.
  • Proactive, with excellent interpersonal and communication skills and the confidence to engage senior stakeholders, auditors, and advisers.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English and Cantonese is preferred; Mandarin proficiency is an advantage.

job.title: Associate Director / Director, Strategy & Reputation, Energy & Sustainability (12-Month Fixed-Term Contract)
job.description:
Associate Director / Director, Strategy & Reputation, Energy & Sustainability (12-Month Fixed-Term Contract)

About the Role

The Strategy & Reputation team works across the full breadth of corporate communications - from campaign strategy and issues management to corporate narrative, stakeholder engagement and sustainability communications. We deliver multi-channel, multi-stakeholder programmes for some of the world's leading companies, working fluidly with colleagues across public affairs, digital, crisis, financial communications and research. Our Energy & Sustainability capability is one of the fastest-growing areas of the practice – advising leading philanthropic groups, coalitions, start-ups and major businesses.

We are seeking an Associate Director or Director to join our London team on a 12-month fixed-term contract, covering a period of parental leave. The successful candidate will be an energetic, delivery-focused S&R generalist - ideally with some energy or sustainability experience - who can integrate quickly into an active team, hold accounts confidently and bring a campaigner's mindset to their work. The role also includes support for senior team members, and offers genuine exposure across a broad range of clients and issues.

Seniority level: Associate Director or Director (approximately 5-9 years' experience)
Contract type: 12-month fixed-term contract
Location: London

What You'll Do

Client Delivery

  • Manage / support a portfolio of client accounts on a day-to-day basis, working closely with senior and junior colleagues - including clients operating in energy, sustainability and regulated industries
  • Development and delivery of communications strategies across a range of issue types - campaign planning, corporate reputation, stakeholder engagement, and issues management
  • Develop high-quality client materials - strategy documents, messaging frameworks, briefing notes, reactive lines, sustainability narratives and stakeholder communications
  • Influence the conversations clients care about through the media, online and through partnerships with think tanks, influencers etc.
  • Monitor and interpret the media, policy and regulatory environment for clients - particularly across the energy transition, net zero and sustainability agenda - flagging relevant developments and helping shape client responses
  • Build and maintain strong media relationships across relevant beats, including energy, environment, business and policy, and proactively identify opportunities for clients

Business Development

  • Contribute to, and where appropriate lead, new business pitches and proposals, bringing sector knowledge and fresh thinking
  • Build your network proactively - with media, intermediaries and potential clients - with an eye on longer-term business development

Team and Culture

  • Mentor and help develop more junior colleagues on a day-to-day basis
  • Contribute to team culture - sharing ideas, insights and enthusiasm for the work
  • Engage with team initiatives on diversity, inclusion and belonging

What We're Looking For

Essential

  • Solid experience in a corporate communications or S&R consultancy environment, with confidence managing accounts and client relationships
  • Strong generalist communications skills - able to move fluidly between corporate narrative, issues management, stakeholder engagement and campaign strategy
  • Exposure to energy, climate or sustainability-related communications briefs - whether in agency, in-house or on specific campaign mandates
  • A campaigner's mindset: experience developing and delivering communications campaigns across multiple channels and stakeholder groups
  • Strong writing skills - clear, precise and adaptable across different formats and audiences, including on technical or policy-heavy subjects
  • An ability to get up to speed quickly, work independently and integrate into an established team without a long runway
  • Proactive approach to media - with developing relationships across relevant beats, including energy, environment and business, and an instinct for creating opportunities

Preferred

  • Familiarity with the policy and regulatory landscape around net zero, the energy transition or environmental reporting
  • Experience supporting business development activity within a team
  • Genuine curiosity about energy, sustainability and the policy environment surrounding the energy transition - and comfort engaging with complex, multi-stakeholder briefs in this space

About FGS Global

FGS Global is the strategic leadership advisory for a complex world. With expertise in strategic and financial communications, policy and public affairs, and data-driven digital engagement, we help leaders align and activate stakeholders, shape and safeguard reputations, and succeed in critical moments. Across 31 global offices, our partners draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary (pro-rated for contract duration)
  • Private medical insurance and life assurance
  • Pension contributions
  • 26 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro-rated)
  • Access to firm-wide professional development programmes

Professional Development

We are committed to the professional growth of everyone who joins us, including on fixed-term contracts. You will have access to structured learning opportunities and development support throughout your time with us.

FGS Global is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds.

job.title: Associate Global Public Affairs
job.description:
Associate Global Public Affairs (all genders)

FGS Global berät die einflussreichsten Entscheider:innen der Welt, genau dort, wo Wirtschaft, Politik und öffentliche Meinung aufeinandertreffen. Wir unterstützen CEOs, Aufsichtsräte und Führungsteams in den entscheidenden Momenten: bei Transaktionen, Krisen, Transformationen und komplexen regulatorischen Herausforderungen. 

Unsere Expert:innen vereinen Hintergründe aus Kommunikation, Finanzen, Recht, Politik, Journalismus und Datenwissenschaft. Was auch immer der Moment erfordert – wir verbinden unterschiedliche Perspektiven und bringen das richtige Team zusammen, damit Führungskräfte die nächsten Schritte antizipieren, die relevanten Stakeholder einbinden und greifbare Ergebnisse erzielen können. Dabei arbeiten wir als ein Team – über Grenzen und Disziplinen hinweg. 

Mit 31 Büros weltweit nutzen wir die gesamte Expertise unserer globalen Teams – von Berlin, Frankfurt, Düsseldorf und München bis New York, London, Singapur und Tokio – damit unsere Mandant:innen mit Klarheit handeln, mit Zuversicht entscheiden und mit Vertrauen führen können. Wir sind vier Jahre in Folge die weltweit führende M&A-PR-Beratung nach Deal-Wert und Deal-Anzahl (Mergermarket, 2025) und werden von Chambers und Partners in der höchsten Kategorie für Crisis & Risk Management und Litigation Support geführt. 

Verstärke unser Team am Standort Berlin ab Januar 2027 als Associate Global Public Affairs (all genders)

Deine Aufgaben 

  • Gemeinsam mit den Projektteams entwickelst Du nicht nur Kommunikationsstrategien für nationale und internationale Kunden, sondern setzt diese auch um - vor allem im Rahmen von Legislativprozessen, Unternehmenspositionierungen, strategischen Neuausrichtungen und M&A-Transaktionen.
  • Du berätst unserer Kunden bei der Public-Affairs-Arbeit und erstellst relevante Dokumente für die politische Kommunikation unserer Mandanten.
  • Du übernimmst eigenständig das Monitoring und die Analyse des gesellschafts- und wirtschaftspolitischen Umfelds unserer Kunden und leitest kundenrelevante Implikationen und Empfehlungen ab.
  • Du analysierst die Wahrnehmung des Mandanten im politisch-gesellschaftlichen Umfeld und entwickelst Maßnahmen zur strategischen Positionierung von Unternehmen und Unternehmensvorständen.
  • Du nimmst an ausgewählten Anhörungen und Konferenzen teil und bereitest die Ergebnisse vor.

Was Du mitbringen solltest 

  • Du hast Dein Hochschulstudium mit sehr gutem Ergebnis erfolgreich abgeschlossen oder stehst kurz vor Deinem Abschluss – dabei ist die Fachrichtung weniger entscheidend als Deine Begeisterung für Kommunikation.
  • Du hast studienbegleitend bereits verschiedene praktische Erfahrungen gesammelt, zum Beispiel in den Bereichen Politik, Regulierung und/oder Public Affairs in Unternehmen, Verbänden und/oder in der Beratung.
  • Du kommunizierst verhandlungssicher in der deutschen und sehr gut in der englischen Sprache – hast idealerweise auch einen Auslandsaufenthalt im englischsprachigen Ausland gemacht.
  • Du hast ein ausgeprägtes Verständnis für Wirtschaftszusammenhänge. Themen im Spannungsfeld von Wirtschaft, Politik und Gesellschaft begeistern Dich.
    Beim Verfassen von Texten für verschiedene Anspruchsgruppen blühst Du auf.
  • Du liebst die Abwechslung und Dein ausgeprägtes Organisationstalent sorgt dafür, dass Du mehrere Bälle gleichzeitig in der Luft halten kannst.

Was wir Dir bieten 

  • Hoch attraktives Einstiegsgehalt.
  • Ein inspirierendes Arbeitsumfeld sowie die Möglichkeit, für eine begrenzte Zeit an einem unserer internationalen Standorte zu arbeiten.
  • Spannende Aufgaben, attraktive Entwicklungsperspektiven und Gestaltungsspielräume.
  • Einarbeitung und individuelle Betreuung durch eine:n erfahrene:n Berater:in.
  • Vertiefung Deiner Expertise im Hinblick auf verschiedene Branchen und Kompetenzbereiche durch die enge Zusammenarbeit unserer integrierten Projektteams über verschiedene Standorte hinweg.
  • Kontinuierliche Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten (FGS Global Academy).
  • Ein engagiertes, kollegiales und wachsendes Team, in welchem gegenseitige Wertschätzung und Teamgeist im Vordergrund stehen.
  • Eine Unternehmenskultur, die Exzellenz mit Herzlichkeit verbindet.
  • Die Möglichkeit, sowohl flexibel in unseren Offices als auch von Zuhause aus zu arbeiten.

Du erfüllst nicht jede einzelne Anforderung? Mach Dir keine Sorgen! Studien haben gezeigt, dass einige Gruppen, wie Frauen oder People of Color, sich seltener auf Stellen bewerben, wenn sie nicht alle Anforderungen erfüllen. Bei FGS Global sind wir bestrebt, ein vielfältiges, integratives und authentisches Arbeitsumfeld zu schaffen. Wenn Du also von dieser Stelle und unserem Unternehmen begeistert bist, Deine bisherige Berufserfahrung aber nicht perfekt mit jeder Qualifikation in der Stellenbeschreibung übereinstimmt, möchten wir Dich ermutigen, Dich trotzdem zu bewerben. Vielleicht bist Du ja genau der/die richtige Kandidat:in für diese oder eine andere Stelle. 

Wir freuen uns auf Deine Bewerbung. Bitte füge ein Anschreiben, einen aktuellen Lebenslauf sowie relevante Abschluss- und Arbeitszeugnisse bei. Du hast noch weitere Fragen zur Tätigkeit, zu FGS Global oder auch darüber hinaus?  

Mehr Informationen findest Du hier: FGS Global

job.title: Associate Global Public Affairs
job.description:
ASSOCIATE GLOBAL PUBLIC AFFAIRS (all genders)  

FGS Global helps the world's most influential leaders move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments.  

We work as one team across geographies and disciplines - bringing together specialists with backgrounds in communications, finance, law, government, journalism, data science, and digital. Whatever the moment demands, we combine multidimensional perspectives to help leaders anticipate what's next, engage the stakeholders who matter, and drive meaningful outcomes. 

Across 31 global offices, we draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust. This collaborative approach has established FGS as a market leader: we are consistently ranked Band 1 for Crisis & Risk Management and Litigation Support by Chambers and Partners, and were ranked the #1 Global M&A PR firm by deal value and deal count for four consecutive years (Mergermarket, 2025). 

Join our team in BRUSSELS as an ASSOCIATE Global Public Affairs.

 

Your responsibilities

  • Working alongside project teams, you will develop and implement communication strategies for national and international clients ; primarily in the context of legislative processes, corporate positioning, strategic realignments, and M&A transactions.
  • You will advise clients on public affairs and produce relevant documents for their political communications.
  • You will independently monitor and analyse the socio-political and economic environment relevant to our clients, and derive client-specific implications and recommendations.
  • You will analyse how clients are perceived in the political and social landscape, and develop measures to strategically position companies and their leadership.
  • You will attend selected hearings and conferences and prepare summaries of the outcomes.

What you should bring

  • You have completed your university degree with excellent results, or are close to graduating ; your field of study matters less than your enthusiasm for communications.
  • You have gained practical experience alongside your studies, for example in politics, regulation, and/or public affairs in companies, associations, and/or consultancies.
  • You communicate with full professional proficiency in English, ideally with experience living or studying in an English-speaking country.
  • You have a strong understanding of economic and business contexts. You are passionate about topics at the intersection of business, politics, and society.
  • You thrive when writing for diverse audiences and stakeholder groups.
  • You love variety, and your strong organizational skills mean you can keep multiple plates spinning at once.

What we offer

  • An inspiring work environment, with the opportunity to work at one of our international offices.
  • Exciting responsibilities, strong development prospects, and room to make an impact.
  • Onboarding and individual mentoring by an experienced consultant.
  • The opportunity to deepen your expertise across various industries and competency areas through close collaboration within our integrated project teams across multiple locations.
  • Continuous learning and development opportunities (FGS Global Academy).
  • A committed, collegial, and growing team where mutual respect and team spirit come first.
  • A company culture that combines excellence with warmth.
  • The flexibility to work both from our offices and from home.

Don't meet every single requirement? Don't worry! Research has shown that some groups, such as women and people of colour, are less likely to apply for roles when they do not meet every requirement. At FGS Global, we are committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. If you are excited about this role and our company but your experience does not perfectly match every qualification listed, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or another position. 

 

We look forward to receiving your application. Please include a cover letter, an up-to-date CV, as well as relevant degree and employment certificates. Do you have further questions about the position, FGS Global, or beyond? 

You can find more information here: FGS Global

job.title: Director / Managing Director, Strategy & Reputation, Campaigns
job.description:
Director / Managing Director, Strategy & Reputation, Campaigns

About the Role

The Strategy & Reputation team works across the full breadth of corporate communications - from campaign strategy and issues management to corporate narrative, stakeholder engagement and sustainability communications. We deliver multi-channel, multi-stakeholder programmes for some of the world's leading companies, working fluidly with colleagues across public affairs, digital, crisis, financial communications and research. Our campaigns capability is a core part of that offer - and an area we are actively growing.

We are seeking a senior campaigns specialist - at Director or Managing Director level depending on experience - to join our London team. The successful candidate will bring integrated campaigns as their primary specialism, the strategic range to operate across corporate reputation, issues and stakeholder engagement, and the commercial instinct to support new business generation. Experience in energy and sustainability communications is a strong advantage. They will work closely with practice leadership to shape the team's campaigns offering and raise its profile in the market.

Seniority level: Director or Managing Director (approximately 8-13 years' experience)
Location: London

What You'll Do

Client Delivery

  • Provide senior counsel on reputation management and multi-stakeholder engagement, drawing on a confident read of the media and policy environment, particularly across corporate affairs, to translate complex situations into actionable advice
  • Develop and lead integrated campaign strategies that span multiple channels and stakeholder audiences, translating complex briefs into executable plans and taking overall responsibility for strategy, execution and outcomes
  • Act as the primary senior relationship holder on a portfolio of key accounts, with direct board-level client exposure
  • Proactively identify media opportunities, leverage an established network of senior contacts to generate high-impact coverage and ensure every account operates with agreed project plans and consistent oversight
  • Lead the production of high-quality strategic outputs - narrative frameworks, campaign plans, stakeholder maps, and executive communications - and deliver research-driven thought leadership proposals that sharpen client positioning

Business Development

  • Identify and convert new business opportunities through a well-developed network of senior client and intermediary contacts
  • Lead or co-lead pitches, bringing intellectual rigour, creative thinking and a commercial perspective - with a strong track record of shaping pitch strategy and winning mandates
  • Build FGS Global's profile in the campaigns and S&R space through thought leadership, speaking opportunities and proactive relationship development
  • Collaborate with colleagues across offices and practice areas to identify cross-sell and referral opportunities

Team and Culture

  • Play a leadership role within the S&R team - setting standards, developing talent and contributing to strategic direction
  • Line-manage and mentor more junior colleagues, with a genuine investment in their growth
  • Champion diversity, inclusion and belonging within the team and in external-facing activities
  • Share knowledge, media intelligence and sector expertise generously across the team and wider firm

What We're Looking For

Essential

  • Substantial experience in a corporate communications role, preferably in an agency environment, with integrated campaigns as a primary specialism
  • Proven ability to design and deliver multi-stakeholder, multi-channel communications campaigns - from strategy through to execution - with clear accountability for outcomes
  • Exceptional written and verbal communications skills, with experience advising at board or C-suite level
  • Demonstrable record of winning and growing client relationships, with existing senior-level contacts in relevant sectors
  • Strong media relationships across corporate, business and policy beats, and a highly proactive approach to media strategy
  • Intellectual curiosity about the world: deeply engaged with geopolitics, business, finance and current affairs - and able to bring that perspective to client briefs
  • Experience leading and developing teams, with a collaborative, generous approach to senior leadership

Preferred

  • Experience working on energy, sustainability or ESG-related communications briefs - whether as a specialism or as a significant element of a broader portfolio
  • Experience building a sub-practice or capability within a firm or team

FGS Global is the strategic leadership advisory for a complex world. With expertise in strategic and financial communications, policy and public affairs, and data-driven digital engagement, we help leaders align and activate stakeholders, shape and safeguard reputations, and succeed in critical moments. Across 31 global offices, our partners draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and discretionary bonus
  • Private medical insurance and life assurance

  • 26 days annual leave plus bank holidays

job.title: Director Global Public Affairs Healthcare (all genders)
job.description:
Director Global Public Affairs, Healthcare (all genders)

FGS Global is the world’s leading stakeholder strategy firm, with approximately 1,400 professionals around the world, advising clients in navigating critical issues and reputational challenges. FGS was formed from the combination of Finsbury, The Glover Park Group, Hering Schuppener and Sard Verbinnen & Co to offer board-level and C-suite counsel in all aspects of stakeholder strategy — including corporate reputation, crisis management, and public affairs and is also the leading force in transaction and financial communications worldwide.  

FGS offers seamless and integrated support with offices in the following locations: Abu Dhabi, Amsterdam, Beijing, Berlin, Boston, Brussels, Calgary, Chicago, Dubai, Dublin, Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, Hong Kong, Houston, Kingston, London, Los Angeles, Munich, Paris, Riyadh, San Francisco, Shanghai, Singapore, South Florida, The Hague, Tokyo, Toronto, Vancouver, Washington, D.C., and Zurich. The firm is headquartered in New York.  

FGS is consistently ranked a Band 1 PR firm for Crisis & Risk Management and for Litigation Support by Chambers and Partners.  For the second year, FGS was ranked #1 Global M&A PR firm by Deal Count and Value in 2024 by Mergermarket. 

Our Global Public Affairs experts advise companies and investors on the impact of political, policy, and regulatory developments on their businesses and strategic positioning. This includes advocacy support, political due diligence, media engagement, and advice on the optimal organization of firms' governmental relations and policy functions. Our Brussels office serves as the EU hub of FGS Global.

We are looking for a Director to join our Global Public Affairs Healthcare team in Brussels. This is a senior role at the intersection of healthcare policy and business strategy - one that spans EU institutions, national markets across Europe, and global mandates. You will work alongside a dedicated Brussels-based healthcare team and collaborate across FGS's European and global network.

 

Join our team in Brussels as Director Global Public Affairs Healthcare (all genders)

 

What tasks can you look forward to?

Client Leadership

  • Client account management: Lead client relationships across European markets and drive cross-sell opportunities across practice areas and geographies. Global mandates will be part of the mix.
  • Policy depth: Serve as the go-to expert on healthcare policy across EU institutions and key European markets. Stay ahead of regulatory and policy shifts to inform client advice and engagement strategies.
  • Policy foresight: Develop and continually refresh relevant, practical, and forward-looking insights - written and oral - for existing clients and in support of new business opportunities.

Team & Practice Development

  • Team management: Guide and develop the Brussels healthcare team - serving as a mentor and day-to-day lead, while remaining hands-on to ensure excellent delivery.
  • Sector group contribution: Contribute actively to FGS's European Healthcare Sector Group - including credentials, thought leadership, event strategy, and internal knowledge-sharing across offices.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Relationship building: Identify, map, and build effective relationships with senior policy, political, and regulatory stakeholders across EU institutions, member states, and relevant international bodies.

New Business

  • Pipeline development: Work hand-in-hand with the firm's Partners to build and grow a pipeline of new clients and projects. Drive pitch preparation and delivery, and bring an entrepreneurial mindset to identifying opportunities across sectors and markets.

What should you bring along?

The ideal candidate is a healthcare policy expert who understands commercial models well enough to translate how policy and regulatory change affects investors and businesses active in Pharma, Medical Devices, Biotech, and Digital Health. You are comfortable working across European markets - including the U.K. and Switzerland - and ideally have exposure to global campaigns or the Washington policy environment.

  • Bachelor's degree plus an MPA, MBA, or similar policy or business-related Master's degree.
  • 7+ years' experience in government, parliament, international organizations, a regulator, trade association, political party, policy-focused public affairs agency, management consultancy, or strategic advisory firm. Candidates with direct policy experience inside a Pharma, MedTech, BioTech, or Digital Health company are equally welcome.
  • Deep knowledge of EU policy-making processes and significant experience advising clients on European healthcare policy, politics, and regulation.
  • Comfort working across multiple European markets simultaneously, with an understanding of how national dynamics interact with EU-level developments.
  • Ability to engage directly with senior policymakers, regulators, and their networks -- often independently and with limited senior support.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide crisp, clear, logical analysis in both written and oral form, adaptable to different audiences.
  • Confidence presenting to, engaging with, and advising senior clients and contacts.
  • Experience managing and developing junior colleagues, with a genuine commitment to their growth.
  • Entrepreneurial approach to building teams and new business pipelines.
  • Excellent project and team management skills.
  • Exposure to Washington, D.C. policy dynamics or experience running global campaigns is a plus but not a requirement.


What we can offer you

  • A senior role within one of the world's leading strategic advisory firms, working on high-profile mandates across EU institutions, national markets, and global clients.
  • The opportunity to contribute to and shape FGS's European Healthcare practice.
  • Exciting mandates and real development prospects across sectors, geographies, and practice areas.
  • An inspiring working environment, with the opportunity to work at one of our international offices for a limited period of time.

job.title: Intern Global Public Affairs (all genders)
job.description:
Intern Global Public Affairs (all genders)

FGS Global is the world’s leading stakeholder strategy firm, with approximately 1,400 professionals around the world, advising clients in navigating critical issues and reputational challenges. FGS was formed from the combination of Finsbury, The Glover Park Group, Hering Schuppener and Sard Verbinnen & Co to offer board-level and C-suite counsel in all aspects of stakeholder strategy — including corporate reputation, crisis management, and public affairs and is also the leading force in transaction and financial communications worldwide.  

FGS offers seamless and integrated support with offices in the following locations: Abu Dhabi, Amsterdam, Beijing, Berlin, Boston, Brussels, Calgary, Chicago, Dubai, Dublin, Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, Hong Kong, Houston, Kingston, London, Los Angeles, Munich, Paris, Riyadh, San Francisco, Shanghai, Singapore, South Florida, The Hague, Tokyo, Toronto, Vancouver, Washington, D.C., and Zurich. The firm is headquartered in New York.  

FGS is consistently ranked a Band 1 PR firm for Crisis & Risk Management and for Litigation Support by Chambers and Partners.  For the second year, FGS was ranked #1 Global M&A PR firm by Deal Count and Value in 2024 by Mergermarket. 

 

Join our team in Brussels starting ASAP as Intern Global Public Affairs (all genders) 

 

Your Responsibilities

job.title: Intern Strategic Corporate & Transaction Communication
job.description:

FGS Global helps the world's most influential leaders move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments. 

We work as one team across geographies and disciplines - bringing together specialists with backgrounds in communications, finance, law, government, journalism, data science, and digital. Whatever the moment demands, we combine multidimensional perspectives to help leaders anticipate what's next, engage the stakeholders who matter, and drive meaningful outcomes.

Across 31 global offices, we draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust. job.title: Stagiair Global Public Affairs – Focus op Nederlandse Politiek
job.description:
Stagiair Global Public Affairs – Focus op Nederlandse Politiek

 

FGS The Hague zoekt een stagiair Global Public Affairs van 1 februari 2027 tot 31 juli 2027.

FGS Global is het toonaangevende stakeholderstrategie-bureau ter wereld, met ongeveer 1.800 professionals wereldwijd, die klanten adviseren bij het navigeren door kritieke vraagstukken en reputatie-uitdagingen. FGS is ontstaan uit de samenvoeging van Finsbury, The Glover Park Group, Hering Schuppener en Sard Verbinnen & Co om advies op bestuursniveau en aan de C-suite te bieden op alle aspecten van stakeholderstrategie — waaronder corporate reputatie, crisismanagement en public affairs — en is tevens de toonaangevende kracht in transactie- en financiële communicatie wereldwijd.

Onze Global Public Affairs experts in Den Haag adviseren bedrijven over de impact van politieke, maatschappelijke en economische ontwikkelingen op hun businessmodel en over hun strategische positionering. Dit omvat ondersteuning bij belangenbehartiging, media-engagement en het schrijven van analyses en aanbevelingen voor een optimale organisatie van Global Public Affairs.

 

Welke taken kun je verwachten?

  • Als stagiair maak je vanaf dag één deel uit van ons team en maak je het dagelijkse werk van een Public Affairs consultant van dichtbij mee. Je bent veel bezig met het monitoren van politieke en maatschappelijke ontwikkelingen in Nederland.
  • Je woont relevante Tweede Kamerdebatten en evenementen bij, en maakt hiervan verslagen. Daarnaast volg je het nieuws op de voet. Je maakt media-analyses over politieke ontwikkelingen en stelt briefings op voor collega’s en klanten.
  • Je ondersteunt collega’s bij de ontwikkeling en uitvoering van strategieën om het Nederlandse publieke beleid en het bijbehorende mediadebat positief te beïnvloeden.
  • Je schrijft briefings over o.a. Kamerleden, ambtenaren, en andere stakeholders.
  • Je leert hoe politieke communicatie werkt en ondersteunt bij het schrijven van persberichten, position papers, en andere stukken.
  • Let op: Voor deze stagepositie ligt de focus op de Nederlandse politiek - nationaal én lokaal. Europese en internationale ontwikkelingen komen aan bod waar ze de nationale agenda raken. Ben je meer geïnteresseerd in buitenlandse/EU politiek, kijk dan ook eens naar vacatures bij ons kantoor in Brussel.

 

Wat breng je mee?

  • Je volgt momenteel een bachelor- en/of masteropleiding – de studierichting is minder belangrijk dan je enthousiasme voor politiek en communicatie;
  • Een achtergrond in bijvoorbeeld Bestuurskunde, Politicologie, (Politieke) Communicatiewetenschap, Economie, Europese en/of Internationale Betrekkingen of een vergelijkbaar vakgebied is een pré.
  • Je spreekt vloeiend Nederlands en hebt een goede beheersing van de Engelse taal;
  • Je bent nieuwsgierig, proactief, zelfstandig en breed geïnteresseerd in de raakvlakken tussen het Nederlandse bedrijfsleven/economie en politiek/maatschappij;
  • Je beschikt over sterke analytische vaardigheden en bent een bewezen teamspeler;
  • Je kunt complexe ideeën effectief overbrengen, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk;

 

Wat bieden wij jou?

  • Kennis van hoe de Nederlandse politiek écht werkt: hoe beleid wordt gevormd en waar de mogelijkheden liggen om daar invloed op uit te oefenen.
  • Inzicht in de activiteiten van een strategisch adviesbureau en in verschillende expertisegebieden als onderdeel van onze geïntegreerde projectteams;
  • Interessante en gevarieerde taken in een internationale en inspirerende werkomgeving;
  • Individuele begeleiding en ondersteuning, evenals gedetailleerde feedback van een ervaren consultant;
  • Een betrokken, collegiaal en groeiend team waarin respect en teamspirit centraal staan;
  • Een bedrijfscultuur die excellentie combineert met vriendelijkheid, en veel gezellige teamactiviteiten in het hart van Den Haag;
  • Je ontvangt een stagevergoeding;
  • Duur: 6 maanden, 40 uur per week.

 

Voldoe je niet aan alle eisen? Geen zorgen! Onderzoek wijst uit dat sommige groepen minder snel solliciteren als ze niet aan alle eisen voldoen. Bij FGS Global streven we naar een divers, inclusief en authentiek werkklimaat. Dus als je enthousiast bent over deze functie en ons bedrijf, maar je eerdere ervaring niet volledig aansluit op elke kwalificatie in de vacature, moedigen we je toch aan om te solliciteren. Misschien ben jij wel de juiste kandidaat voor deze of een andere rol.

We kijken uit naar je sollicitatie. Neem gerust contact op met ons HR-team via careers-eu@fgsglobal.com.

Meer informatie: FGS Global

job.title: Analytics Engineer
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

 

The role

The Analytics Engineer is responsible for bridging the gap between data engineering and data analytics by maintaining and developing scalable data models and solutions that support finance, B2B, and B2C teams. The role plays a key part in delivering value through modern data stack technologies (including dbt), supporting cloud migration efforts, ensuring data quality, and maintaining the performance of analytical data pipelines.

 

Key responsibilities

  • Collaborate with stakeholders across departments to design and implement robust data models and BI solutions.
  • Build, test, and maintain data transformations using dbt (data build tool).
  • Implement software engineering best practices for data, including version control, CI/CD, and automated testing.
  • Deliver day-to-day support and project-related tasks for the data and BI infrastructure.
  • Develop and maintain scalable, maintainable, and well-documented data pipelines.
  • Identify and resolve issues across ETL/ELT processes and data pipelines.

 

Required skills and experience

Essential

  • 3+ years of experience in Analytics Engineering, BI, or Data Engineering roles.
  • Strong proficiency in SQL, including complex queries and performance tuning.
  • Hands-on experience with dbt for data transformation and modeling.
  • Understanding of data migration to cloud platforms such as AWS (Redshift) or GCP (BigQuery).
  • Familiarity with database design, version control (e.g. Git/GitHub), and CI/CD practices.
  • Experience with ETL/ELT tools (e.g. Airflow,DBT).

Personal skills

  • Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
  • Effective communication skills and ability to collaborate across teams.
  • Attention to detail and focus on continuous improvement and data quality.
  • Adaptability to fast-paced environments.

 

Often used technology stacks and tools

  • Databases & Data Warehouses: AWS Redshift, BigQuery, MS SQL Server.
  • Data Transformation: dbt (data build tool).
  • ETL & Data Processing: Airflow.
  • BI & Data Visualization Tools: Looker.
  • Programming & Scripting: SQL, Python.
  • Version Control & DevOps: GitHub, CI/CD pipelines.
  • Cloud Platforms: AWS, GCP.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

  • Annual bonus scheme
  • 25 days paid leave
  • 24/7 Employee Assistance Program
  • Life Insurance
  • Enhanced Parental Leave policy
  • Food Allowance
  • Multisport Card
  • Both in house and external training programs
  • Your own training dedicated budget (for conferences, courses etc.)

 

We currently operate a hybrid model which requires staff to work onsite 50% of the time, subject to role requirements & regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for all roles. We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, building stronger relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning.  We reserve discretion on reasonable notice to change this approach either generally or for specific individuals or teams. 

 

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

 

Further information

At the FT, we embrace innovation and the use of technology and appreciate that individuals may leverage AI tools as part of their job application process. Whilst we are happy for you to use AI to assist with your application, it is essential that all information provided is authentic and accurately represents your skills, experience, and qualifications.

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process may be monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

Please beware of fraudulent job postings and offers claiming to be from the Financial Times. All legitimate opportunities will direct you to apply through the official Financial Times careers site, and the FT will never ask for financial information, payments, or referrals to third parties during the hiring process. If you have any concerns about the legitimacy of a job posting or suspect any scam activity, please contact talent@ft.com.

Interested in the FT but don’t see the right role yet? Join our Talent Community to receive exclusive updates, featured jobs, and insights into working at the FT.

job.title: Application Security Engineer
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide. At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world. In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing. Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere. Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The Role Overview

We’re looking for a Cyber Security Engineer to help improve application security across the FT’s cloud-native technology estate. This is a hands-on role focused on making secure engineering easier for product, platform and software engineering teams.

Application security experience is essential for this role. You’ll help improve developer-friendly security guardrails across GitHub-based CI/CD pipelines, application repositories and engineering workflows. This includes working with SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning, vulnerability management and secure coding guidance so that security findings are clear, actionable and owned by the right teams.

You’ll work closely with engineers to support practical threat modelling, triage application vulnerabilities, improve security playbooks and help teams remediate issues in a pragmatic way. You do not need to be a deep AWS or cloud security specialist, but some exposure to AWS, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security would be useful.

We’re looking for someone with practical AppSec experience who wants to grow their impact - someone who enjoys working with engineers, improving tooling and helping security become part of normal delivery rather than a last-minute checkpoint.

What you’ll bring to the role

Application security experience: practical experience identifying, explaining and helping remediate application security risks in modern engineering environments.

Developer-friendly security mindset: you enjoy working with engineers, explaining risks clearly and helping teams adopt secure practices without unnecessary friction.

Vulnerability management experience: experience triaging and tracking application vulnerabilities from sources such as SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning, penetration tests, bug bounty reports or third-party advisories.

CI/CD and code security awareness: familiarity with security tooling in development workflows, such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning or repository security controls.

Threat modelling awareness: experience participating in, supporting or facilitating lightweight threat-modelling sessions for applications, services or new features.

Automation mindset: ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to reduce manual effort, improve visibility or make security workflows easier.

Cloud security awareness: Some exposure to AWS, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security would be useful, but is not essential.

Growth mindset: willingness to keep developing across application security, cloud security, secure development and modern engineering practices.

Required Experience, Essential

  • Practical experience in application security.
  • Experience working with software engineers to explain and remediate security issues.
  • Familiarity with common web application security risks and secure coding practices.
  • Experience with vulnerability triage, prioritisation and remediation tracking.
  • Experience using or interpreting findings from tools such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning or similar.
  • Experience participating in or supporting threat-modelling activities.
  • Ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to automate tasks or improve visibility.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • Familiarity with Agile or Scrum ways of working.

Desirable

  • Exposure to AWS security, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security.
  • Experience with Terraform or CloudFormation.
  • Experience with container or Kubernetes security.
  • Experience with bug bounty, penetration testing or security testing programmes.
  • Experience with Splunk or similar logging/SIEM platforms.
  • Exposure to AI security, such as LLM-enabled applications, AI-assisted development workflows or prompt/data leakage risks.
  • Experience building dashboards, metrics or reports to support vulnerability management.
  • Relevant security certifications or training, such as AWS security training, secure coding training, GIAC, ISC2, CREST or equivalent practical experience.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

We currently operate a hybrid model which requires staff to work onsite 50% of the time, subject to role requirements & regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for all roles. We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, building stronger relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning.  We reserve discretion on reasonable notice to change this approach either generally or for specific individuals or teams. 

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process may be monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

job.title: Assistant Finance Manager
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion 

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

 Job Purpose

The Assistant Finance Manager is responsible for leading the day-to-day finance operations of FT Japan while supporting assigned finance activities across other Asia entities. The role ensures the delivery of accurate financial reporting, strong financial controls, and full compliance with local statutory requirements and FT Group policies.

Working closely with regional Accounting Services and Finance teams across APAC and the UK, the Assistant Finance Manager serves as a key finance business partner, driving continuous process improvement, promoting strong governance, and supporting efficient finance operations across the assigned areas of responsibility.

Main Duties and Responsibilities

Financial Reporting & Control

  • Lead the month-end, quarter-end and year-end close processes to ensure accurate and timely financial reporting.
  • Prepare and review balance sheet reconciliations and investigate outstanding items to ensure completeness and accuracy.
  • Review financial results, perform variance analysis, and explain key movements.
  • Monitor cash flow requirements to support day-to-day business operations.
  • Ensure compliance with FT Group accounting policies and IFRS.
     

Statutory & Tax Compliance

  • Coordinate statutory reporting requirements and annual external audits.
  • Liaise with external auditors, tax advisers and regulatory authorities.
  • Prepare and review corporate tax, consumption tax and other statutory filings.
  • Monitor changes in Japanese accounting and tax regulations and assess their impact on the business.
  • Ensure timely completion of all statutory and compliance obligations.
     

Compliance & Internal Control

  • Maintain effective financial controls and ensure compliance with FT policies and global standards.
  • Support internal and external audit activities and ensure timely implementation of audit recommendations.
  • Maintain finance procedures, process documentation and control frameworks.
  • Identify opportunities to improve efficiency through process automation and standardisation.
     

Accounting Services Collaboration

  • Act as the primary Finance contact for the regional Accounting Services team.
  • Partner with Accounting Services to ensure the accurate and timely completion of month-end accounting activities.
  • Collaborate with Accounting Services to investigate and resolve accounting issues promptly.
  • Contribute to regular operational meetings with Accounting Services by identifying and resolving operational issues, agreeing action plans, and monitoring progress.
  • Work with regional Finance teams to identify opportunities for process improvements and enhance service delivery.
     

Treasury & Banking

  • Manage banking administration, payment processing, and cash management activities.
  • Ensure timely and accurate execution of supplier, employee, tax, and statutory payments.
  • Maintain appropriate banking controls and payment authorisation procedures.
     

Projects & Continuous Improvement

  • Lead or participate in finance transformation initiatives and regional projects.
  • Support the implementation of new systems, finance processes and policy changes.
  • Drive process improvements to increase efficiency, strengthen controls and reduce operational risk.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify and standardise finance processes across the assigned areas of responsibility.
     

Stakeholder Management

  • Build strong working relationships with Finance teams across APAC and the UK.
  • Collaborate with HR, Legal, Procurement, IT and other business functions.
  • Provide guidance and support to internal stakeholders on finance-related matters.
  • Work effectively with external advisers, banks, auditors and government authorities.
     

Operational Leadership

  • Act as an operational leader within the FT Japan Finance team, fostering collaboration and accountability in day-to-day operations.
  • Coordinate finance activities across multiple stakeholders to ensure the timely delivery of key objectives.
  • Drive the timely resolution of operational issues through effective collaboration with Accounting Services and business teams.
  • Support finance projects and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Promote best practices, share knowledge, and contribute to the development of an effective and high-performing Finance team.
     

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance or a related discipline.
  • CPA or equivalent professional qualification is preferred.

The role 

We are looking for a detail-oriented finance professional to join our Finance team and support a broad range of accounting, supplier management, statutory compliance, audit, and fixed asset activities.

Working closely with the Financial Accountant and wider Finance team, you will help ensure that financial records, transactions, and supporting documentation are accurate, complete, and maintained in line with internal controls and Philippine regulatory requirements. The role will also involve regular coordination with suppliers, internal stakeholders, auditors, banks, and government agencies.

This is a great opportunity for a qualified CPA with audit and accounting experience who is looking to build broader hands-on experience across financial operations, compliance, and reporting within a fast-paced, international organisation.

Key responsibilities

Supplier and Invoice Management

  • Verify vendor onboarding requirements and coordinate the creation or update of vendor records.
  • Prepare Purchase Requisition (PR) and Purchase Order (PO) requests and follow up on pending approvals.
  • Review quotations, supplier invoices, and supporting documents for completeness and compliance with documentation requirements prior to processing.
  • Maintain and monitor the filing of supplier invoices, official receipts, and other related documents.
  • Assist in preparing payment batches, bank instructions, and supporting documents for supplier, payroll, tax, and other disbursements.
  • Coordinate with suppliers and internal stakeholders regarding pending invoices, payment status, and outstanding supporting documentation.
  • Request supplier statements and aging reports and reconcile outstanding balances for review.
  • Prepare BIR Forms 2307 and maintain related supporting records.
  • Assist the Financial Accountant in preparing supplier management and accounts payable-related reports.

Financial Accounting Support

  • Prepare routine journal entry templates and supporting schedules for review and posting.
  • Prepare assigned balance sheet reconciliation schedules and supporting documentation for review.
  • Maintain accounting files, schedules, and records to ensure completeness, accuracy, and proper filing.
  • Assist with month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close activities by preparing supporting schedules, documents, and standard reports.
  • Extract financial data and prepare standard reports and analyses requested by the Finance team.

Tax and Statutory Compliance Support

  • Prepare supporting schedules and documentation required for BIR, PEZA, and other applicable government and regulatory submissions.
  • Assist in the preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual BIR tax returns and supporting schedules for review.
  • Maintain tax compliance files and ensure statutory records and supporting documentation are complete and properly organized.
  • Monitor documentary requirements and compliance deadlines assigned to the role and follow up on outstanding items.
  • Coordinate document requests from government agencies, banks, auditors, and external consultants.

Audit and Internal Control Support

  • Organize audit schedules and supporting documents for internal and external audits.
  • Coordinate routine audit document requests and follow up with relevant stakeholders on outstanding requirements.
  • Ensure accounting records and supporting documentation are complete, properly filed, and readily available for review.
  • Assist in monitoring compliance with internal finance policies, controls, and documentation requirements.
  • Maintain finance process documentation, checklists, and standard operating procedures.

 Administrative and Operational Support

  • Coordinate intercompany documentation, approvals, and filing of supporting records.
  • Assist stakeholders with expenditure coding requests and finance documentation requirements.
  • Track finance-related action items and follow up on outstanding requests with internal and external parties.
  • Support finance system administration by maintaining user records, templates, and standard master data, where applicable.
  • Participate in process improvement initiatives and special projects assigned by the Finance Manager.
  • Perform other finance-related duties as assigned.

Fixed Asset Administration

  • Maintain the Company's Fixed Asset Register and supporting documentation, including records of asset additions, disposals, and transfers.
  • Prepare fixed asset additions, disposals, transfers, and related documentation for review and recording.
  • Prepare PEZA fixed asset reports, applications, and supporting documentation for review and submission within prescribed deadlines.
  • Coordinate with PEZA, suppliers, and internal stakeholders regarding fixed asset documentation and compliance requirements.
  • Conduct periodic physical verification and inventory counts of fixed assets, identify discrepancies, and prepare reconciliation reports for review.
  • Assist in reconciling the Fixed Asset Register against accounting records and physical inventory.
  • Coordinate and perform fixed asset tagging and maintain asset identification records.
  • Maintain fixed asset files, purchase documentation, importation records, and other supporting documents for audit and regulatory purposes.
  • Prepare schedules and supporting documents for fixed asset reviews and audits conducted by internal auditors, external auditors, and government agencies.

Required skills and experience 

  • Bachelor's degree in Accountancy or a related field.
  • Must be a Certified Public Accountant (CPA).
  • Must have 2–5 years of relevant work experience in external or internal audit, preferably with exposure to financial statement audits, accounting processes, and internal controls.
  • Working knowledge of Philippine accounting and regulatory requirements, including applicable BIR, SEC, and PEZA rules and regulations.
  • Experience in general accounting, financial reporting, account reconciliations, and preparation of supporting schedules is preferred.
  • Must have experience using financial accounting software and/or ERP systems.
  • Advanced MS Excel skills
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to review financial information and supporting documentation accurately.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills and the ability to coordinate effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines in a fast-paced finance environment.

The Audience Development Executive plays a crucial role in driving delegate acquisition and audience engagement for high-impact B2B events. Based in Manila, this role supports the FT Live marketing team by researching, qualifying, and managing delegate leads, contributing directly to the success of our client-sponsored and FT-branded events.

  • Create high-quality lead lists based on event-specific briefs (e.g. job title, industry, location, and company).

  • Provide ad hoc reporting and analysis as requested.

  • Attend internal briefing meetings and proactively share research findings, audience trends and potential targeting opportunities.

  • Curiosity and willingness to learn about different industries, companies, markets and business topics.

job.title: Data Journalism Summer Intern
job.description:
About Us 

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading business news organisations, recognised internationally for its authority, integrity, and accuracy.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing. 

The FT has a record paying readership of 1.6 million, more than 1.4 million of which are digital subscriptions. It is part of Nikkei Inc., which provides a broad range of information, news, and services for the global business community. We have offices in more than 35 countries, including London, New York, Hong Kong, Beijing, Manila, Sofia, San Francisco, and Tokyo.

Our Internships

We are looking for passionate and motivated students who are interested in pursuing a career in media to join our team! We expect our interns to be in the office a minimum of three days a week. 

This program offers the opportunity to connect and collaborate across the FT — in the US and globally. You’ll develop ideas that help drive our growth, present your work to US leadership, and gain valuable insights from across the business. Plus, you’ll be paired with a dedicated Buddy to provide mentorship and support throughout your experience.

This internship pays $22 per hour for 40 hours per week and runs from June 7, 2027 - Aug 13, 2027. Before applying, please ensure you will be available on these dates.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the US.

Role Overview

You will work closely with all members of the FT’s US data journalism team. We are a small, interdisciplinary group working across the paper — on data visualisation, data analysis, news writing, enterprise stories, narrative features, interactive features and visual stories. All this work is strung together by our keen interest in the quantitative and the empirical.

Our team fulfils a dual role: enhancing existing reporting with sharp analysis and visualisation, and pitching and producing our own original work. We are looking for candidates with a proven interest in data journalism and some experience with data and data graphics.

Key responsibilities

  • Source, collect and clean data for news stories and other pieces
  • Create data graphics and perform analyses, often on deadline
  • Collaborate with US data team members, and our data colleagues in London, on larger projects
  • Work closely with beat reporters to conceive and create effective graphics
  • Pitch and produce original pieces for editors in New York and London 

Required skills/experience

  • Some experience creating clear and engaging graphics (ie. Flourish, Datawrapper, ggplot2)
  • Some experience analysing datasets in a journalism context 
  • Strong writing and communication skills; experience reporting and writing news is an advantage
  • Familiarity with sources of US data, especially financial, economic and political data
  • Programming fluency, in a language of your choice, is an advantage
  • Specific knowledge of business, economics and financial markets is an advantage

Please submit your application by November 2nd by 5pm Eastern Time and be sure to include the following documents in your application:

  • Resume
  • A cover letter explaining why you would be a good fit, and explaining your interest in joining our team
  • Two relevant clips

Any application submitted after the deadline will not be considered.

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. For this reason, FT editorial staff do not use AI tools to write articles or create reader-facing content.

AI may be used in specific, pre-approved cases to assist with research, such as in data investigations. We expect internship applicants to refrain from using AI in writing tests or written materials submitted during the application process. All submissions must reflect your own knowledge, skills, and experiences.

Candidates may use AI to assist with research and interview preparation. However, the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure fairness and transparency for all applicants.

  • Collaborate closely with reporters, editors and visual journalists across Ignites and BoardIQ.

  • Use public records, databases, APIs, web scraping techniques and proprietary datasets to uncover new reporting opportunities.

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

  • Experience using data, research or quantitative analysis to support decision-making, storytelling or audience engagement.

  • An interest in developing or expanding technical skills in areas such as Python, R, data visualisation, databases or related analytical tools.

  • Knowledge of FT products, audiences, editorial standards or internal workflows that can help accelerate impact in the role.

We welcome applications from colleagues across Editorial, Product & Technology, Audience, Research, Commercial and other FT business areas who can demonstrate transferable analytical, storytelling or data-focused skills.

FT Specialist, a business division of the Financial Times, is seeking a Deputy Editor for Health Payer Specialist, a publication covering one of the most dynamic sectors in the U.S. economy: health insurance.

Published three times a week, Health Payer Specialist delivers essential news and intelligence to insurance companies, helping them grow and stay ahead of industry developments.

This role is ideal for a journalist with strong experience covering the health insurance sector, a proven track record to break news, and a sharp analytical approach. You will produce both fast-turnaround scoops and in-depth trend analysis, while also interpreting sophisticated financial documents such as SEC filings and earnings reports.

As Deputy Editor, you will work closely with the Managing Editor to shape coverage, contribute to editorial strategy, and step in to lead editing when required. As part of a small, high-performing team, you will play a key role in driving editorial output while also having the opportunity to grow into broader leadership responsibilities.

Key responsibilities

  • Report and write about about four articles per week and at times create video content or other formats, when appropriate
  • Show your expertise on the subject matter by writing with clarity, insight and depth
  • Establish and maintain close relationships with insurance executives and their companies
  • Serve as back-up to the Managing Editor, and help to generate story ideas and shape coverage
  • Travel to industry events and meet with prospects to stay on top of the latest industry trends
  • Work with other departments to produce videos, graphics etc. as necessary for editorial coverage
  • On occasion, moderate webcasts or panels at events

Required skills / experience

  • At least five years’ experience in business journalism, ideally covering health insurance or related sectors
  • Experience at a daily or wire publication with a focus on breaking news
  • Strong background of generating scoops and differentiated content for a niche audience
  • Editing experience and ability to refine others’ work
  • Ability to interpret financial information, including SEC filings and earnings reports
  • Strong news judgment, deadline skills, and understanding of audience needs
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to build industry sources
  • High levels of initiative, creativity, and resilience

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location, but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, health coverage, 401k and company match, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

We currently operate a hybrid model which requires staff to work onsite 50% of the time (two to three days onsite), subject to role requirements & regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for all roles. We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, building stronger relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning. We reserve discretion on reasonable notice to change this approach either generally or for specific individuals or teams.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

Further information

This role is covered by the Writers Guild of America East (WGAE) collective bargaining agreement.

A reasonable estimate of the salary range for this role is $99,000–$110,000. To ensure pay fairness, the successful candidate will be offered a salary within the estimated range based on factors including but not limited to skills, experience and training, certifications, and other business and organisational needs. The disclosed range estimate is for our NYC office and has not been adjusted for other locations.

At the FT, we embrace innovation and the use of technology and appreciate that individuals may use AI tools as part of their job application process. Whilst we are happy for you to use AI to assist with your application, it is essential that all information provided is authentic and accurately represents your skills, experience, and qualifications.

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process may be monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

The role

 We are looking for an experienced financial journalist to join our Hong Kong-based team as Deputy Editor. This is primarily a reporting role with additional editing responsibilities, offering a senior reporter the opportunity to focus on producing original journalism while helping shape our daily publication.

 The successful candidate will cover one of Asia's most important financial sectors at a time of significant change. Key responsibilities

  • Cover a beat and produce around four original stories each week.

  • Develop strong sources across the asset management industry.

  • Edit colleagues' copy and help maintain editorial standards.

  • Publish Ignites Asia in the absence of the Managing Editor.

  • Travel occasionally within Asia for reporting assignments.

Required skills and experience
