Junior Broadcast Technician

Melfort, Saskatchewan

After an incredible 51 years of service, our longtime Technical Manager in Melfort has recently retired. Pattison Media is now looking for a Junior Broadcast Technician to join our Technical Services team and help support our two radio stations in Melfort.

This is a great opportunity for someone early in their technical career who enjoys troubleshooting, working with technology and learning how things work. You don't need to arrive knowing everything about broadcast engineering. You'll be supported by Pattison Media's Technical Services team and will work closely with our Technical Services Manager in Prince Albert, who will provide ongoing technical support and mentorship.

If you have a background in electronics, IT, networking, telecommunications or broadcast technology and are interested in building a career in radio broadcast engineering, we'd like to hear from you.

What you’ll do:

  • Help maintain, troubleshoot and repair studio and broadcast equipment.
  • Assist with the operation and maintenance of radio transmission systems.
  • Support computers, servers, network equipment and other technology used by our Melfort stations.
  • Support broadcast systems including WideOrbit automation and other studio, newsroom and audio systems.
  • Assist with the installation and commissioning of new technical equipment and systems.
  • Maintain technical documentation, records and drawings.
  • Help troubleshoot technical issues affecting our on-air and business operations.
  • Work with the Pattison Media Technical Services team on technical projects and upgrades.
  • Provide day-to-day technical assistance to staff at our Melfort stations.

What we’re looking for:

  • A genuine interest in broadcasting, electronics and technology.
  • Education or experience in electronics, electrical technology, IT, networking, telecommunications, broadcast technology or a related technical field.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Basic knowledge of computers and networking.
  • Good organizational skills and an ability to follow tasks through to completion.
  • Comfortable working both independently and as part of a larger technical team.
  • Good communication skills and a willingness to learn.
  • A valid driver’s License.

Broadcast experience is an asset, not a requirement.

Previous experience working in radio or with broadcast equipment would certainly be an asset, but we're also interested in candidates with strong technical aptitude who are willing to learn.

You'll have the support of an experienced Technical Services team and the opportunity to develop hands-on experience with studio technology, radio automation, IT and networking, RF transmission systems and other broadcast infrastructure.

If you're technically curious, enjoy solving problems and are interested in building a career in broadcast technology, we'd like to hear from you.

Please apply below or submit a cover letter, resume and demo along with the completed Pattison Media Self ID Form before Friday, November 27th 2026 to:

Bill Stovold

Director, Technical Services

Pattison Media Ltd.

Bill.stovold@pattisonmedia.com

job.title: Manager, Content Operations
job.description:
Position Title: Manager, Content Operations Department: Distribution Strategy & Operations Corporate Area: Digital & Marketing Status: Regular, Full time Exempt Manager Title: Sr. Manager, Digital Video Operations

Position Overview

The Manager of Content Operations will be responsible for managing the day-to-day delivery, readiness, and availability of PBS general audience video content across PBS owned-and-operated and third-party streaming platforms, including PBS.org, PBS apps, and YouTube. This role will oversee the workflows that move content from producer delivery through quality review, publishing, and ongoing library management, supporting both free and paid streaming experiences. Working alongside the other video operations roles, this role will translate programming schedules, content windowing policies, and platform strategies into reliable operational plans. The Manager will coordinate with PBS Programming, Technology, Digital & Marketing, and content management teams as well as PBS Distribution, and national producers to ensure content and supporting assets are complete, accurate, and available when audiences expect them.

Key responsibilities

will include, but are not limited to: Manage digital video delivery from intake through distribution, establishing schedules, confirming requirements, and coordinating dependencies across internal teams and external partners. Translate approved content windowing and platform plans into publishing requirements, including release dates, expirations, geographic restrictions, and access settings. Resolve discrepancies with the appropriate policy and rights owners. Oversee multiple versions of video assets and supporting materials, including captions, audio tracks, artwork, metadata, and platform-specific edits, ensuring the correct assets reach each destination. Manage operational readiness for premieres, library releases, and new distribution initiatives. Identify delivery risks early, communicate impacts, and coordinate contingency plans. Establish and maintain quality assurance procedures for video, audio, captions, and metadata. Coordinate corrections and verify that published content meets PBS standards and platform requirements. Maintain accurate asset records, delivery tracking, and streaming availability information across content and digital asset management systems. Lead troubleshooting of failed deliveries, publishing errors, and content availability issues. Coordinate resolution across teams, escalate risks, and address recurring causes. Develop and document processes that improve turnaround times, reduce manual work, and clarify

responsibilities

across Video Operations, Programming, Content Packaging, and platform teams. Partner with Technology and Product teams to define operational requirements, test system changes, and support migrations, integrations, and workflow automation. Execute certain job functions outside of general work hours (M-F 9am-5pm) on an as-needed basis to accommodate last minute deliverables ahead of airdate Lead the implementation of new processes and workflows as opportunities arise or circumstances evolve across Digital Video Team, Technology, Media Operations Center, Programming, and others Coordinate operational support for livestreams and near-live releases, including testing, caption readiness, delivery plans, and backup procedures. Additional

responsibilities

as assigned. undefined Requirements for success: Bachelor’s degree in communications, media production, technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Seven or more years of

experience

in digital video operations, media asset management, streaming distribution, or a related field, including responsibility for complex workflows and cross-functional projects.

Experience

with content management and digital asset management systems, including asset ingest, metadata, publishing, and library maintenance. Working knowledge of video formats, encoding and transcoding, captioning, audio specifications, and file delivery methods. Understanding of streaming platforms across web, mobile, and connected television, including YouTube publishing tools and operational requirements.

Experience

applying content rights, windowing restrictions, and platform specifications to distribution workflows. The base pay range for this position at the beginning of employment is expected to be between $80,000/year to $85,000/year. The actual base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position will also include other elements for eligible employees, including: (i) eligibility for discretionary bonuses; (ii) various insurance options, including medical, dental, vision, hearing, life, accidental death and dismemberment, short-term and long-term disability, and business travel accident insurance; (iii) identity protection program; (iv) employee assistance program; (v) financial and retirement savings

benefits

including the PBS Retirement Plan 403(b); (vi) paid time off (17 days per year), paid sick time

benefits

(12 days per year), paid parental leave (60 days / 12 weeks ), and paid holidays (12 days per year). Details of these benefit plans will be provided upon request. The application window for this position is expected to close on 11/2/2026. If hired, the employee will be in an “at-will position,” and the Company reserves the right to modify the base hourly rate/salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors. PBS is an

Equal Opportunity Employer

in accordance with the EEOC and the Commonwealth of Virginia. POLITICO is in search of an Advertising Operations Specialist who will work closely with the Media Business team to ensure successful activation and fulfillment of advertising campaigns. The ideal candidate will be agile and work well in a fast-paced environment. 


Who You Are:

  • A detail-driven problem solver who thrives in fast-paced, deadline-oriented environments.
  • A collaborative communicator with a knack for translating data into actionable insights.
  • A tech-savvy professional fluent in ad operations tools, creative platforms, and web languages.
  • A dependable team player who takes initiative and embraces leadership opportunities.
  • A strategic thinker who values integrity, innovation, and contributing to a mission-driven culture.

job.title: Assistant Editor, Central Desk
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking an Assistant Editor to join its Central Editing Desk, the newsroom’s general-assignment editing team. Central editors support a daily flow of stories through editing and publication while also deploying to individual teams during major news events or to fill temporary staffing needs. 


This is an opportunity to develop an expansive view of POLITICO’s journalism while also building expertise in particular coverage areas. You will touch some of our most impactful work and collaborate with journalists throughout our fast-moving newsroom. Assistant Editors work alongside Editors and Senior Editors to support the daily second-editing workflow as they build their editing skills.


The Assistant Editor will work M-TH 4pm-12am and F 1pm-9pm. The desk is staffed 7 days per week, 6 a.m. to midnight on weekdays, with hours subject to change. We're looking for candidates who can work from one of our offices: Arlington, VA, New York, NY or Sacramento, CA.


Who You Are: 

  • You are curious about the full breadth of POLITICO’s news coverage and want to work across beats, products and platforms 
  • You are already an editor, or a reporter or producer who has developed strong editing skills and is eager to make editing a larger part of your career 
  • You enjoy moving between the big picture and the details that make an individual story stronger 
  • You can quickly learn the priorities and working styles of different teams while developing deeper expertise in particular coverage areas 
  • You find satisfaction in helping a newsroom respond effectively when priorities change or coverage intensifies 

 

What You’ll Do: 

  • Edit a wide range of content for POLITICO’s consumer and Pro subscriber audiences, including breaking news stories, live blogs, quick-turn enterprise pieces, daily newsletters and long-form deep dives across all our digital platforms, applying consistent high standards while understanding the needs of each platform 
  • Edit articles in our content management system for accuracy and clarity, as well as fact-check and copy edit, ensuring articles adhere to POLITICO standards and style 
  • Optimize content for digital platforms and search, review choice of photos and other multimedia, and assist in writing and reviewing headlines, decks and photo captions 
  • Collaborate with reporters, editors and multimedia teams to ensure smooth and speedy publishing 
  • Deploy flexibly to teams that need additional editing capacity because of breaking news, major events, special projects or temporary staffing gaps 

 

What You’ll Need: 

  • Demonstrated editing ability, whether developed in a formal editing role or through substantial experience editing colleagues’ work, producing coverage, shaping stories or collaborating closely on publication 
  • Strong news judgment and a rigorous commitment to fair-minded, nonpartisan journalism  
  • Excellent organization and communication skills and an ability to quickly adapt to changing priorities and juggle multiple tasks in a fast-paced newsroom 
  • Flexibility to work varying shifts and support different projects and teams, depending on need 
  • Experience in digital publishing and content management systems 
  • Working knowledge of AP Style 

Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter under the Resume/CV section of the application.

 

COMPENSATION: 

Assistant Editor: $78,000-$85,000 Annual Base. 


The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.title: Senior Manager, Customer Success
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO's mission from the very beginning was to win the audience. We dedicate ourselves to providing accurate, non-partisan, impactful information to the right people at the right time so that they can act with confidence and speed. We experiment to avoid being disrupted and we have fun disrupting others. And we are not afraid to risk failure if it means being the best at what we do.


POLITICO is looking for a Senior Manager, Customer Success to lead the US Customer Engagement Specialist team and develop scalable customer engagement practices that drive product adoption, customer value, Wallet Retention Rate, and retention rate across the US Professional Subscriptions business.


Overall Mission: The Senior Manager, Customer Success is responsible for leading, developing, and evolving the US Customer Engagement Specialist team. In partnership with the Managing Director, Customer Success, this role builds and executes the US CES strategy, with a focus on scalable proactive and reactive customer engagement, product adoption, customer support, and account health. The Senior Manager serves as a leader in developing consistent Customer Success processes and practices across the CES team.


What You’ll Do:

  • Lead and develop all US Customer Engagement Specialists.
  • Build and execute the US CES strategy in partnership with the Managing Director, Customer Success.
  • Establish team goals, priorities, processes, and performance expectations that drive product adoption, customer engagement, Wallet Retention Rate, and retention rate.
  • Own the US CES team’s contribution to Wallet Retention Rate and retention rate within the US Professional Subscriptions business.
  • Drive scalable proactive and reactive Customer Success processes across the CES team.
  • Improve and innovate practices related to customer onboarding, engagement, adoption, support, training, and account health.
  • Coach and develop CES team members through regular feedback, skill building, and career development.
  • Partner with Account Management and CSM leadership to identify customer needs, coordinate engagement opportunities, and support account-level strategies.
  • Use customer health, usage, and engagement data to identify opportunities for proactive service and intervention.
  • Champion customer feedback and ensure insights from the CES team are shared with Product, Marketing, Technology, Data, and other internal partners.

What You’ll Need:

  • Significant experience in Customer Success, customer engagement, client services, account management, support, or a related function, preferably within a SaaS, subscription, information services, or media business.
  • Experience managing and developing customer-facing professionals.
  • Proven ability to build scalable processes and programs that improve customer engagement, adoption, and retention.
  • Strong understanding of proactive service, customer onboarding, product adoption, support, and customer health practices.
  • Excellent coaching, communication, and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong analytical problem-solving skills and comfort using customer data to identify opportunities and risks.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate with Sales, Product, Marketing, Technology, Data, and other internal partners.
  • Strong product knowledge or the ability to quickly learn complex products and customer use cases.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

COMPENSATION: $85,000 - $100,000 annual salary. This role is also eligible to participate in POLITICO’s commission plan, with a target incentive opportunity of $35,000 - $50,000, resulting in an on-target earnings (OTE) potential of approximately $120,000 - $150,000. Commission payments are variable and are based on achievement against applicable performance goals and the terms of the commission plan. Actual compensation will depend on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, and other job-related considerations.

job.title: Senior Newsroom Developer
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a Sr. Newsroom Developer (Machine Learning) to help build the next generation of AI-powered newsroom and product capabilities. As we expand into new sector products, new professional audiences and new geographies, POLITICO is investing in machine learning systems that go beyond simply integrating foundation models. This role will work alongside software engineers, product managers, journalists and editorial leadership to develop models, evaluation frameworks and data pipelines that apply POLITICO's editorial expertise across AI-powered tools and improve newsroom and product workflows.


The ideal candidate is excited about applying machine learning in support of journalism. You'll work closely with software engineers, journalists and product teams to develop AI-powered tools and data products that strengthen reporting, improve newsroom workflows and help bring POLITICO's editorial expertise to a broader audience.


What You'll Do:

  • Design, build and deploy production machine learning systems that support newsroom, editorial and new-audience initiatives.
  • Develop classification, prediction and ranking models using proprietary newsroom data and editorial expertise — a modeling foundation that extends across new products rather than requiring a bespoke build per vertical.
  • Build datasets, feature engineering pipelines and evaluation frameworks to improve AI system performance.
  • Experiment with prompting, retrieval, fine-tuning and other model adaptation techniques to solve journalism-specific problems.
  • Partner closely with journalists and editors to translate editorial knowledge into machine learning features, labels and evaluation criteria.
  • Collaborate with software engineers to integrate machine learning capabilities into production applications.
  • Measure and improve model quality using rigorous evaluation methodologies that balance accuracy, editorial standards and operational performance.
  • Evaluate new AI technologies while considering performance, cost, maintainability and long-term flexibility.

Example Projects:

You may work on initiatives such as:

  • Building systems that classify the newsworthiness of stories using editorial judgment.
  • Developing prediction models that combine public information with POLITICO's proprietary reporting expertise.
  • Improving AI-assisted editing by helping models better understand and apply POLITICO's editorial style guide.
  • Creating proprietary classifiers that enrich public datasets with editorial intelligence, extendable to new sector products as they launch.
  • Designing evaluation frameworks to measure AI quality before newsroom deployment.
  • Optimizing AI workflows to improve performance while reducing inference costs.
  • Supporting investigative and enterprise reporting through machine-learning-assisted analysis of complex datasets.

What You'll Need:

Required

  • 5+ years of professional experience building or deploying machine learning systems.
  • Strong software engineering skills, preferably in Python.
  • Experience with machine learning fundamentals including supervised learning, feature engineering, model evaluation and experimentation.
  • Experience with modern machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
  • Familiarity with large language models, embeddings or natural language processing techniques.
  • Experience working with structured and unstructured data.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate with engineers, product managers and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred

  • Experience adapting or fine-tuning foundation models.
  • Experience building NLP, information retrieval, classification or ranking systems.
  • Familiarity with model evaluation frameworks, experiment tracking or MLOps practices.
  • Experience deploying machine learning models to cloud infrastructure.
  • Interest in journalism, media, public policy or knowledge-intensive domains.

What Success Looks Like in the First Year:

  • Improve the accuracy and reliability of AI systems used by POLITICO's newsroom.
  • Build evaluation frameworks that help teams confidently assess AI quality and editorial alignment.
  • Contribute to proprietary classifiers, prediction systems and editorial intelligence capabilities that differentiate a named initiative.
  • Partner effectively with software engineers, product teams and newsroom stakeholders to bring machine learning solutions into production.
  • Help establish a strong technical foundation for future AI initiatives across the newsroom and our new lines of business.

COMPENSATION: $175,000 - $225,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.title: Senior Research Analyst, Food Regulatory Policy
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a Senior Research Analyst to help lead part of its regulatory intelligence and information services product, AgencyIQ. Since its founding in early 2020, AgencyIQ has quickly become the premier source of regulatory intelligence and analysis for professionals working in the life sciences and food industries.


Our written research and analysis are relied upon by many top companies, trade groups, law firms and advocacy groups to help them understand breaking news, identify emerging trends, predict future action and prepare for seismic shifts in regulatory policy.


The Senior Research Analyst will serve as a subject matter specialist in the regulation of food by U.S. regulatory agencies like the FDA on a variety of topics including labeling, ingredients, packaging, nutrition, safety, and compliance. The role will be responsible for analyzing the relevance of regulatory changes and developments across both the federal and state policy landscape, articulating the type and degree of impact on food companies, and providing context to an audience of knowledgeable regulatory professionals.

Reporting to the Director of Food and Chemicals Research in POLITICO’s Arlington, Virginia offices, the Senior Research Analyst will join a team of experienced researchers responsible for producing a mix of daily written content, in-depth written research, weekly insights, directed deliverables and presentations.


Expected areas of subject matter coverage will include regulations, guidance, legislation, announcements, and industry developments.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Produce daily (3-4 per week) topical intelligence articles and other content for our subscribers based on emerging regulatory and legislative developments related to food regulatory topics
  • Serve as a subject matter specialist on several food topics for AgencyIQ (e.g., labeling, packaging, nutrition, ingredients, safety, compliance, etc.)
  • Lead or participate in the development and delivery of in-depth analysis, deep-dive research, webinars and email newsletters
  • Collaborate with other members of the AgencyIQ research team focused on chemical, food and life sciences regulation
  • Participate in subscriber- and prospect-facing events, briefings, and business development activities

 

What You’ll Need

Required

  • At least 4 years’ experience analyzing U.S. food regulatory policy at a consulting company, think tank, trade association, government agency, or company
  • A strong affinity for writing – efficiently and effectively, and for a business or policy audience – paired with a knowledge of (and passion for) regulation and regulatory policy
  • Experience and comfort working in fast-paced, research-driven environments in which daily delivery of regulatory analyses is the norm
  • An excellent working knowledge of the food regulatory process (and in particular the FDA) capable of delivering expert insights to our knowledgeable subscribers

 

Preferred

  • Have an advanced degree or certification related to food science, law or policy (i.e., a JD, PhD, or relevant master’s degree); or
  • Have prior experience working in media, including as a journalist or writing a product widely read by others (i.e., a business intelligence product or internal newsletter).
  • Experience presenting on regulatory topics to a variety of different audience types (small groups, large groups) in different environments (virtual and in-person)

COMPENSATION: $100,000 - 125,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.title: Social Media Editor
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a social media editor to play a key role in our North American social media team — to help expand the reach of our journalism and connect with new audiences across a variety of formats and platforms. 


This role is focused on off-platform growth. The ideal candidate will play a crucial role in growing our social audiences in strategic ways that drive our business goals, helping determine how our reporting reaches audiences on platforms including Instagram, TikTok, X, LinkedIn and emerging channels. They will also assist in the development and execution of social-first video projects, working closely with visual journalists to bring our journalism to life.


Who You Are:

We're looking for someone who understands both the demands of a fast-moving newsroom and the realities of modern social platforms. The ideal candidate is a strong editorial thinker who knows what works on social and understands how to bring a multimedia newsroom to life. 

 

What You’ll Do:

  • Publish to and manage our social accounts including Instagram, TikTok, X, LinkedIn and emerging channels.
  • Implement social strategies and playbooks for breaking news, key policy coverage areas, enterprise projects, etc.  
  • Work with newsroom leaders, reporters and producers on social best practices
  • Work closely with product & tech teams to identify & implement social workflow improvements and tools across our website and app 
  • Regularly share insights and takeaways with data and audience teams  
  • Participate in daily coverage planning and be a voice for our audience 
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to analyze audience data, identify trends, and provide timely recommendations that contribute to informed journalistic decisions 
  • Maintain off-platform standards and journalistic independence  
  • Proactively identify opportunities for improvement in content creation, delivery, and audience engagement based on data analysis. 
  • Stay aware of social media trends, innovations, and best practices and incorporate them into the newsroom's workflow. 

 

What You’ll Need:

  • 2-3 years of experience in social media, newsroom experience is required  
  • Experience identifying, analyzing, and using data to independently test theories, confirm assumptions, and measure success via iteration and with attention to detail.   
  • Strong writing skills, and experience drafting compelling headlines and polished copy across a variety of formats. 
  • Excellent news judgment: This candidate will have to respond in breaking and fast-moving scenarios and cover a wide-variety of subject matters responsibly and fairly. 
  • Knowledge of politics and policy news. Fluency is a major plus.
  • Experience editing and creating social video is not necessary, but is a major plus. 
  • NOTE: This role may require a schedule outside normal working hours. 


COMPENSATION: $75,000 - $85,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.title: Technical Product Manager, AgencyIQ by POLITICO
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking an experienced Technical Product Manager to design and deliver new tools and features for  AgencyIQ by POLITICO, a policy-driven product for regulatory professionals in the life sciences, food, and chemicals sectors.

 

AgencyIQ combines expert research, data, and software tools for regulatory professionals in the life sciences, food, and chemicals industries. This Technical Product Manager will shape AgencyIQ’s roadmap and help the product team move from customer insight to working solutions faster. The role spans product innovation (including the development and roll-out of AI-driven tools), commercial strategy, and technology execution—driving measurable growth in subscriber acquisition, engagement, and retention across both product lines.

 

The ideal candidate combines strong technical capabilities with a proven ability to translate subscriber insights into product roadmaps that deliver commercial results, partnering closely with research, editorial, technology, data, and commercial teams.

Who You Are

 

  • You are a highly user-centric product manager with a strong track record of translating research, data, and market insight into clear roadmaps and measurable business impact.
  • You are comfortable with both customer discovery and hands-on technical work. You can test an idea with users, understand how it fits into a subscription product, and collaborate with engineers on APIs, data flows, security, and deployment.
  • You enjoy enabling others by creating repeatable processes that make the whole team more effective.

 

What You’ll Do


Product Strategy & Roadmap

  • Own and prioritize a roadmap for AgencyIQ features and workflows, balancing customer value, commercial impact, technical feasibility, and engineering capacity.
  • Interview customers and prospects; analyze usage, feedback, market developments, and competitors; turn findings into clear product requirements, experiments, and defined KPIs.
  • Partner with research, commercial, design, and engineering teams to improve acquisition, engagement, expansion, and retention of customers across the market segments we serve.

 

AI-Assisted Prototyping and Technical Enablement

  • Design and roll out a repeatable workflow that lets nontechnical product managers use approved AI coding tools, such as Codex or Claude Code, to build and test feature prototypes and data collection tools.
  • Work with POLITICO’s engineering and design teams to create reusable templates and documentation that adhere to company standards and connect to POLITICO systems through approved access paths.
  • Align new templates and workflows with the tooling, policies, and procedures established by POLITICO’s engineering and operations teams.
  • Define how prototypes are evaluated with users, reviewed by engineers, and either hardened for release or retired.
  • Build representative prototypes yourself and coach other product managers through the workflow, and improve it based on where they get stuck and what engineers need for an efficient handoff.
  • Create reusable evals for prototypes and AI-enabled features, using representative regulatory tasks, expected results, and clear quality thresholds. Run them as designs change and use the results to guide engineering review and release decisions.

 

Regulatory Data and Delivery

  • Scope and prototype reliable ways to collect public data from government sources in the United States, Europe, Japan, and other global jurisdictions using official APIs or structured feeds where available and compliant scraping where appropriate.
  • Partner with research and engineering on source provenance, data quality, parsing, change detection, monitoring, and maintainability so promising data prototypes can become dependable product capabilities.
  • Write clear specifications, make trade-offs visible, coordinate delivery to make the most of limited engineering capacity, and measure whether shipped features improve customer outcomes.

What You'll Need

 

  • 3+ years of product management experience delivering B2B software or data products, with evidence of strong product judgment and measurable customer or business results.
  • Hands-on ability to prototype with modern AI coding tools and enough working knowledge of code, APIs, databases, and software delivery to assess output and collaborate credibly with engineers.
  • Experience designing usable product workflows from interviews, usability tests, feedback, and behavioral data; fluency in product metrics and prioritization.
  • Experience working with engineering on technical requirements, integrations, testing, and release processes; sound judgment about security, data access, and where human review is necessary.
  • Ability to teach technical practices to colleagues with different backgrounds and to communicate decisions clearly to commercial, research, technology, and senior leadership teams.
  • Familiarity with Python or JavaScript, SQL, web data collection, cloud development environments, CI/CD, and API-based integrations.

Preferred Experience

 

  • Experience in information services, regulatory intelligence, or another B2B subscription business that combines expert content, structured data, and software.
  • Knowledge of public regulatory sources or the needs of regulatory affairs, policy, legal, or scientific users.
  • Knowledge of the U.S. capital markets—namely public equities and the institutions that trade them

COMPENSATION: $125,000 - 135,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.


We value our people. Click here for more on what we offer and what it’s like to work for POLITICO. 


Let’s keep in touch. You can view our list of open positions here and email us careers@politico.com. We hope to see your application soon! 


About Us. 

POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital. 


Cabinet secretaries and Ministers start their mornings with our analysis. CEOs shape strategy around our reporting. Advocacy leaders rely on our insights to move policy. We deliver the straightforward facts and clear-eyed analysis they need to navigate the most complex political landscape of our lifetimes. 


Our 1,100+ publishing professionals across the world's key democratic capitals—Washington, Brussels, London, Paris, Berlin, Sacramento, and New York—form the world's premier politics and policy newsroom. We tell the story of how power really works by explaining who wields it and how they plan to exercise it, connecting dots others miss and delivering scoops from sources others don't even know exist. 


Innovation has always been a core tenet of our story. At launch, we bet that depth would trump scale, that talent would trump traffic, and that politics would become central to modern life. In 2011, we made another bet and launched POLITICO Pro to help decision-makers understand the business of government, transforming both how they shape government action and the business of journalism itself. 


These bets have made POLITICO the most successful digital news startup of its generation and the indispensable resource for leaders who shape the future. Today, we are a rarity in media: a growing, profitable, and sustainable news organization. 


POLITICO is a subsidiary of Axel Springer SE, a family-owned transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York. Axel Springer is dedicated to shaping the future of journalism in the free world, believing that a free and informed society is essential to democracy. The company’s guiding principles - first articulated as  The Essentials by founder Axel Springer in the aftermath of World War II - remain a cornerstone of the company’s foundation today. Learn more about Axel Springer.

  • As a Talent Acquisition Partner, you’ll help QVC Group teams hire the talent they need by managing recruiting from intake through offer acceptance.
  • You will build trusted relationships with hiring managers and bring talent-market insight into search decisions.
  • You will go beyond reviewing applicants. Through proactive sourcing, thoughtful candidate engagement, and structured hiring practices, you’ll connect people with opportunities and help hiring teams make informed decisions.
  • You will support frontline recruiting with operational forecasts for high-volume recruiting, ongoing pipelines, as well as ongoing pipelines for professional recruiting that calls for deeper market research, passive-candidate outreach, and building external partnerships.

Where You'll Work

  • This role is onsite and requires you to work daily from our Ontario, California Fulfillment Center location.
  • Relocation assistance is not available for this role.

What You'll Do

  • Manage full-cycle recruiting for assigned roles, from intake and sourcing through offer acceptance.
  • Lead structured intake conversations, using labor-market insights to align on requirements, candidate availability, and search approach.
  • Find and engage candidates through inbound applications, Boolean search, direct outreach, pipelining, and other relevant channels.
  • Partner with hiring managers to build structured interview processes, clarify evaluation criteria, and deliver timely, thoughtful candidate communication.
  • Use market insights and recruiting data to share search updates, support equitable offer development, maintain accurate ATS records, and recommend process improvements.
  • Support high-volume frontline fulfillment center hiring by aligning recruiting activity with workforce forecasts, training class start dates, seasonal demand, and operational priorities.
  • Build relationships with external partners and community organizations to strengthen local talent pipelines, increase awareness of QVC Group career opportunities, and support community engagement.

What You'll Bring

  • 3 to 5 years of full-cycle recruiting experience and high-volume recruiting; in-house corporate recruiting experience is strongly preferred.
  • Experience building hiring-manager partnerships and managing searches from intake through offer acceptance.
  • Ability to source candidates proactively, including using Boolean search and direct outreach to engage passive talent.
  • Skill in using talent-market information to calibrate role requirements, explain candidate availability, and shape search plans.
  • Clear, timely communication and a commitment to a respectful, inclusive candidate experience.
  • Ability to manage priorities, maintain accurate ATS records, and use recruiting information to provide useful updates.
  • For frontline portfolios, ability to connect operational hiring forecasts with pipeline and recruiting plans; for professional portfolios, ability to conduct deeper market research and build passive-candidate relationships.



Salary: $75,000.00 - $90,000.00

Our Total Rewards package includes benefits you’ll love such as competitive compensation, paid time off, an employee assistance program, parental leave, paid volunteer hours, and amazing company discounts! In our US market, you can also expect health care benefits starting on day 1, 401(k), and tuition reimbursement benefits.

QVC Group is committed to inclusion and belonging for all and ensuring that our workplace provides equal employment opportunities for all team members and candidates and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. As an equal opportunity employer, QVC Group is committed to a barrier-free employment process. If you need reasonable accommodations/support throughout, please contact us at workwithus@qvcgrp.com for assistance.

If provided, salary ranges are a general guideline only, and actual salaries will vary and are based on factors such as a candidate's qualifications, skills, experience, and geographic location as well as business and market conditions.

Job Summary:

Real Chemistry is looking for a Account Director to join our growing team!

21GRAMS, a Real Chemistry subsidiary is an advertising agency born to make healthcare more human. Not just in our work, but in the way we conduct business, approach client relationships, and treat each other. It’s a place where people subscribe to the adage, “Be good to each other, but hard on the work.” A place where people are not just in it for the paycheck, but to make a dent in the universe. Sound like you?

21GRAMS is in search of an Account Director. In addition to being the diplomatic face of the brand, both internally and externally, they accept the role of manager, liaison, thinker, and problem-solver. The Account Director leads broad-based, complex work-streams, is critical to the smooth running of Accounts, is a credible advisor and has very strong marketing communications experience.

The Account Director has mastered communications, project management, and has a strong point of view on the pharmaceutical side. This person should be able to confidently lead client projects and internal teams, encouraging smart, effective and integrated solutions, and always deliver results and client satisfaction. This position offers the opportunity to become an internal leader while developing strong relationships with clients.

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Carmel, Lambertville or San Francisco—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

What you'll do:

  • Establish and maintain productive working relationships to drive agency success
  • Demonstrate understanding and knowledge of key messages/message platform, data, and promotional story for brand and competition
  • Develop and align on key agency/client documents that drive success (e.g., Project and Creative Briefs)
  • Read and interpret analytics around programming, tactics, and overall brand performance (e.g., metrics, KPIs, goals)
  • Negotiate, when necessary, to meet and deliver on client needs while managing agency resources and projects effectively
  • Continuously identify new opportunities to make recommendations based on customers, markets, and competitive environments, including corresponding rationales
  • Lead by example: exhibit professional conduct while providing ongoing leadership as a role model for the team
  • Demonstrate a solutions-oriented approach and collaborate across teams to drive success
  • Pursue business objectives, while developing talent and preserving the 21GRAMS culture
  • Supervise, train, and mentor team members to develop the skills and careers of others by providing guidance

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • Our Company values, Best Together, Impact Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always, and Accountability with an "I", genuinely resonate with how you work and lead.
  • You demonstrate the Real Chemistry Can mindset by approaching challenges with optimism, accountability, creativity, and a solutions-oriented attitude, always looking for ways to make a meaningful impact for our clients, colleagues, and communities.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and comfortable adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment. As our business grows and changes, so do we.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful, with strong prioritization skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to leverage data to inform decisions and drive outcomes.
  • You are energized by innovation and the transformative potential of AI, actively exploring new technologies, identifying opportunities to work smarter, and championing practical, responsible AI adoption that drives meaningful business impact.

What you should have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing or a related field or equivalent
    experience is required
  • 5-7 years marketing experience, agency environment preferred.
  • Strong ability to multi-task and manage multiple projects with strong organizational
    skills.
  • Excellent business communication skills
  • Strong written and oral communication and presentations skills
  • Experience working on Therapeutic brands a plus
  • Previous experience managing junior staff preferred

job.title: 21GRAMS- Director, Product Design (UI)
job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

21GRAMS, a Real Chemistry subsidiary, is an advertising agency born to make healthcare more human. Not just in our work, but in how we conduct business, approach client relationships, and treat each other. We believe in being good to each other and hard on the work, and in creating work that makes a meaningful difference for patients, caregivers, healthcare professionals, and brands.

Job Summary

The Director, Product Design is a senior design leader responsible for setting the product design vision, raising the quality of the work, and building the conditions for teams to deliver cohesive, accessible, and effective digital experiences. This role leads complex engagements across websites, platforms, products, services, and connected ecosystems, translating user needs, brand strategy, business goals, technology constraints, and healthcare requirements into clear experience direction.

This is not solely an execution role. The Director is accountable for design strategy, client leadership, team development, resourcing, design operations, and measurable experience outcomes. They remain close enough to the work to guide critical decisions, facilitate discovery, critique design, and step into high-impact moments while enabling senior designers to lead day to day.

What You Will Do

Design Vision and Product Strategy

  • Own the product design vision and experience strategy across a portfolio of complex client engagements, connecting user needs, brand intent, business objectives, and technical feasibility.
  • Partner with Experience Strategy, UX, Product Management, Creative, Technology, Data, Medical, Strategy, and Account leadership to frame opportunities, define roadmaps, and establish measurable outcomes.
  • Lead discovery and definition activities, including stakeholder alignment, experience principles, journey framing, service blueprints, value propositions, prioritization, and product or platform planning.
  • Identify opportunities that extend beyond the immediate brief and turn them into clear, decision-ready recommendations for clients and agency leadership.

Design Excellence and Delivery

  • Set and uphold a high bar for interaction design, visual design, responsive behavior, content hierarchy, prototyping, motion, and end-to-end experience coherence.
  • Guide teams from early concepts through detailed design, validation, launch, and optimization, ensuring that strategic intent is maintained through implementation.
  • Oversee scalable design systems, component libraries, pattern governance, and documentation in Figma, working with engineering partners to improve quality and delivery efficiency.
  • Build accessibility into the work from the start, applying WCAG 2.2 AA principles and inclusive design practices rather than treating compliance as a final review step.
  • Use qualitative research, analytics, usability findings, and business measures to evaluate design decisions and recommend iteration.

Client and Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Act as a trusted senior design partner to clients, clearly articulating experience strategy, design rationale, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations to executive and working teams.
  • Lead high-stakes presentations, workshops, critiques, and decision-making sessions, creating alignment across internal and external stakeholders.
  • Partner with project and account leadership on scope, staffing, schedules, assumptions, and change management; surface delivery risks early and propose practical solutions.
  • Represent Product Design in new-business opportunities, estimates, proposals, capability presentations, and pitch work.

People Leadership and Practice Development

  • Manage, coach, and develop product designers across levels through clear expectations, actionable feedback, growth plans, and regular career conversations.
  • Create an environment where designers can do their best work, with strong critique, psychological safety, accountability, and thoughtful delegation.
  • Partner with Experience leadership on hiring, staffing, performance management, succession planning, and capability development.
  • Improve the Product Design practice through reusable methods, templates, standards, training, and responsible adoption of emerging tools, including AI-enabled workflows.
  • Contribute to a culture of collaboration across Product Design, UX, Creative, Technology, and Strategy, reducing silos and improving continuity from concept through launch.

What Success Looks Like

  • Clients see Product Design as a strategic partner, not only a production capability.
  • Teams have clear experience direction, decision criteria, and an appropriate level of design leadership from discovery through delivery.
  • Creates a more consistent, accessible, and high-quality experience across the portfolio.
  • Designers receive strong coaching, understand what is expected of them, and demonstrate measurable growth.
  • The practice becomes more scalable through better systems, methods, staffing decisions, and cross-functional ways of working.
  • Experience recommendations connect to defined user, client, and business outcomes.

What You Should Have

  • 10+ years of experience in product design, experience design, interaction design, or a related discipline, including 3+ years managing and developing designers.
  • A portfolio demonstrating leadership across complex, multi-channel digital products or platforms, from strategy and concept through detailed design and launch.
  • Experience leading multiple workstreams or a portfolio of client engagements in an agency, consultancy, product organization, or similarly complex environment.
  • Deep fluency in human-centered design, interaction design, visual systems, prototyping, responsive design, information architecture, and design systems.
  • Strong working knowledge of Figma and modern collaborative design workflows; familiarity with Adobe Creative Cloud and prototyping or motion tools is helpful.
  • Practical knowledge of accessibility standards, including WCAG 2.2 AA, and the ability to guide teams in designing inclusive experiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to partner with engineering, product, research, content, analytics, strategy, creative, and account teams.
  • Excellent executive communication, facilitation, storytelling, critique, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Experience defining design outcomes and using research, usability testing, analytics, and performance data to improve experiences.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity, making informed trade-offs, and balancing strategic leadership with hands-on guidance when the work requires it.

This Position Is a Strong Fit If

  • You can move between the 30,000-foot view and the detail that determines whether an experience actually works.
  • You are direct, low-ego, generous with feedback, and able to challenge the work while supporting the people doing it.
  • You bring structure to ambiguity, anticipate needs, and help teams make better decisions faster.
  • You care about craft, but judge success by the quality, usefulness, accessibility, and impact of the experience.
  • Our Company values – Best Together, Impact-Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always and Accountability with an “I” – really speak to you. 
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving. 
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data. 
  • You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines. 

Preferred Experience

  • Healthcare, pharmaceutical, patient support, medical technology, or other regulated-industry experience.
  • Experience with privacy, consent, regulated content, and design considerations for patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals.
  • Experience supporting business development, scoping, estimating, and presenting capabilities or pitch work.
  • Experience leading enterprise websites, authenticated platforms, service ecosystems, omnichannel programs, or AI-enabled experiences.

 

Pay Range: $140,000 - $155,000
This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting.  Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

Job Summary:

Real Chemistry is looking for a Medical Copywriter to join our growing team!

21GRAMS, part of Real Chemistry, is a full-service healthcare advertising agency built on the belief that healthcare should feel more human. We combine bold creativity, strategic rigor, and deep scientific understanding to create work that changes behavior, improves outcomes, and makes a meaningful impact on people's lives. Our culture is grounded in collaboration, curiosity, and a shared commitment to doing exceptional work. We believe in being good to each other while pushing ourselves to deliver ideas that move audiences, brands, and healthcare forward.

We’re looking for a Medical Copywriter who can bring together scientific fluency and creative instinct — someone who knows how to turn complex clinical information into clear, compelling, brand-building copy. This is not a traditional medical writer role. We’re looking for someone with healthcare advertising experience who can concept, collaborate, and write across a range of promotional and scientific materials while maintaining accuracy, compliance, and brand voice.

The Medical Copywriter is responsible for developing medically sound, strategically sharp, and emotionally resonant copy across healthcare/pharma campaigns. This person will partner closely with Creative, Strategy, Account, Project Management, Editorial, and medical teams to bring ideas to life across multiple channels and deliverables.

The ideal candidate understands how to translate science into stories, can move fluidly between promotional copy and scientific content, and has experience working in an agency environment where deadlines are fast, standards are high, and collaboration is key.

This is a great opportunity for a writer who loves the challenge of making complex science feel human, relevant, and creatively powerful. You’ll work at the intersection of medical rigor and brand storytelling, helping shape work that is strategically grounded, emotionally intelligent, and deeply impactful.

This role can be remote within the United States or based in any of our U.S. office locations, including New York City, San Francisco, Boston, Chicago, Lambertville or Carmel.

 

What you’ll do:

  • Write for healthcare/pharma advertising campaigns across HCP, patient, caregiver, and DTC audiences 
  • Translate complex clinical data, mechanism of action, and product information into clear, engaging, on-brand messaging 
  • Develop copy for a wide range of deliverables, including websites, digital banners, emails, sales materials, patient education, videos, social, and other omnichannel assets 
  • Partner with an Art Director and broader creative team to develop integrated campaign concepts and executions 
  • Ensure all copy aligns with brand strategy, marketing objectives, tone of voice, and audience needs 
  • Work closely with Medical/Scientific leadership to ensure content is accurate, balanced, and compliant 
  • Participate in strategic planning, internal brainstorms, and client meetings as needed 
  • Present concepts internally and incorporate feedback thoughtfully and efficiently 
  • Review and refine copy throughout the agency process for clarity, grammar, consistency, and accuracy 
  • Collaborate with Editorial to resolve stylistic or grammatical concerns 
  • Build a strong understanding of assigned brands, disease states, competitors, and the evolving market landscape 
  • Proactively identify relevant medical, competitive, or regulatory updates that may impact messaging or tactical development
  • Bring a solutions-oriented mindset to projects and contribute to the overall quality of the work 

 

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • Our Company values, Best Together, Impact Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always, and Accountability with an "I", genuinely resonate with how you work and lead.
  • You demonstrate the Real Chemistry Can mindset by approaching challenges with optimism, accountability, creativity, and a solutions-oriented attitude, always looking for ways to make a meaningful impact for our clients, colleagues, and communities.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and comfortable adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment. As our business grows and changes, so do we.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful, with strong prioritization skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to leverage data to inform decisions and drive outcomes.
  • You are energized by innovation and the transformative potential of AI, actively exploring new technologies, identifying opportunities to work smarter, and championing practical, responsible AI adoption that drives meaningful business impact.

 

What you should have:

  • 2–4+ years of experience in healthcare/pharma advertising, medical communications, or a closely related agency environment 
  • Experience writing within regulated categories, ideally with exposure to HCP and/or DTC promotional work 
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating conceptual thinking, copywriting craft, and brand voice development 
  • Ability to balance creativity and scientific accuracy 
  • Comfortable partnering with cross-functional teams including Creative, Account, PM, Editorial, and Medical 
  • Strong verbal communication and presentation skills 
  • Excellent attention to detail and ability to manage multiple assignments in a fast-paced environment 
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and common research tools/platforms 
  • Knowledge of or strong interest in science, medicine, and healthcare marketing 
  • Experience working across multiple products or disease states 
  • Familiarity with MLR/regulatory review processes 
  • Ability to contribute to both promotional initiatives and scientific communications 
  • Curiosity about innovation in healthcare, audience behavior, and emerging creative formats 

 

Pay Range: $90,000 - $110,000

job.description:

Job Summary:

Real Chemistry is looking for a New Business Lead to join our growing team!

Real Chemistry seeks an accomplished and strategically minded Head of New Business to lead the agency’s growth function and drive best-in-class business development for 21GRAMS. In this role, you will establish and refine new business processes, develop a high-performing growth team, and serve as a trusted strategic partner to senior leadership, directly impacting pipeline development, win rates, and revenue growth.

This position is integral to 21GRAMS, part of Real Chemistry, a healthcare advertising and communications firm dedicated to making healthcare more human through innovative, client-centered work conducted with integrity and excellence. You will lead all aspects of new business development, from opportunity identification through pitch execution. You will ensure every team member involved in the pitch process has a seamless, organized experience, fostering collaboration, efficiency and confidence at every stage.

Additionally, you will help own the new client onboarding process, ensuring that day-to-day brand teams are fully equipped with the insights, timelines, and resources needed to service each brand from day one. This critical handoff function bridges the gap between winning the business and delivering exceptional work, setting the foundation for long-term client partnerships.

This role can be remote within the United States or based in any of our U.S. office locations, including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Lambertville, NJ, San Francisco, or Carmel, IN.

What you’ll do:

New Business Process Development

  • Establish, refine, and enforce new business processes and standards across the agency
  • Create repeatable frameworks for how opportunities are evaluated, pursued, and executed

Growth Team Leadership

  • Lead and develop a high-performing new business team
  • Ensure every team member involved in the pitch process has a seamless, organized, and collaborative experience

Pipeline Management

  • Identify and qualify new business opportunities 
  • Manage the full pipeline from initial opportunity through close 
  • Track and report on win rates, pipeline health, Saleforce integration, and revenue impact 

Pitch Leadership

  • Lead and support pitch efforts across the agency and with Real Chemistry Partners
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams through the pitch process 
  • Foster confidence and collaboration at every stage of the pursuit

Strategic Partnership with Senior Leadership

  • Serve as a trusted strategic partner to agency leadership on all growth matters 
  • Inform and influence go-to-market strategy across therapeutic areas including launch planning

New Client Onboarding

  • Help own the end-to-end onboarding process for all newly won clients 
  • Ensure day-to-day account teams are fully equipped with the insights, context, and resources needed to service each brand from day one 
  • Bridge the gap between winning the business and delivering exceptional work

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • Our Company values, Best Together, Impact Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always, and Accountability with an "I", genuinely resonate with how you work and lead.
  • You demonstrate the Real Chemistry Can mindset by approaching challenges with optimism, accountability, creativity, and a solutions-oriented attitude, always looking for ways to make a meaningful impact for our clients, colleagues, and communities.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and comfortable adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment. As our business grows and changes, so do we.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful, with strong prioritization skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to leverage data to inform decisions and drive outcomes.
  • You are energized by innovation and the transformative potential of AI, actively exploring new technologies, identifying opportunities to work smarter, and championing practical, responsible AI adoption that drives meaningful business impact.

What you should have:

  • Bachelor's Degree from an accredited institution
  • 12+ years of new business, account management, or project management experience in a healthcare advertising setting
  • Minimum 5+ years in a leadership or supervisory capacity managing high-performing, cross-functional teams in high-pressure environments
  • Demonstrated expertise in pharmaceutical advertising, healthcare communications, or life sciences agency environment with hands-on experience managing teams and new business opportunities
  • Strong understanding of pharmaceutical promotion standards, FDA/OPDP guidance, and healthcare communications
  • Demonstrated ability in data analysis, reporting, and translating metrics into actionable business insights
  • Working knowledge of project management methodologies including Waterfall, Agile, and Hybrid approaches, with ability to select appropriate methodology for each pitch opportunity
  • Proven track record of leading, developing, and motivating teams to high performance
  • Executive-level communication skills—ability to present complex information clearly to C-suite audiences, stakeholders, and clients
  • Strong written and verbal communication with ability to adapt messages for diverse audiences
  • Strategic thinking and sound judgment, with demonstrated ability to solve complex problems, make decisions under uncertainty, and balance competing priorities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Deep expertise in pharmaceutical advertising and healthcare communications, particularly with experience in oncology, rare disease, specialty pharmaceuticals, or other complex therapeutic areas
  • Demonstrated results from process improvement initiatives with measurable impact on efficiency gains, cost reduction, or quality improvement
  • Client relationship management experience at a senior level, including presenting to pharmaceutical and biotech executives

CORE COMPETENCIES & ATTRIBUTES

Professional Competencies

  • Strategic Business Leadership: Setting vision and direction; aligning operations with business objectives; thinking beyond immediate execution to organizational capability building
  • Process Excellence: Designing, implementing, and continuously improving standardized processes and workflows that scale across new business
  • Stakeholder Management: Building and maintaining effective relationships with executives, clients, cross-functional partners, and team members; navigating competing interests
  • Organizational Development: Building high-performing teams, developing talent, creating culture, and leading organizational change

Required Leadership Attributes

  • Change-Positive, Growth-Oriented

You actively seek smarter, faster, and more effective ways to operate. You are not threatened by AI, innovation, new tools, or new ways of working—you're energized by them. You challenge legacy thinking thoughtfully, experiment with confidence, and view change as an advantage rather than a disruption. You don't defend the status quo because "it works"; you see every process, system, and methodology as a candidate for improvement. You are quick to spot opportunities to expand how we operate collectively and you bring others along on that journey. You stay current with emerging PM tools and methodologies because you're genuinely curious about better ways forward, not because compliance requires it.

  • Commercially and Market Aware

You operate beyond internal agency mechanics and understand the bigger picture. You know your clients' business contexts, therapeutic landscapes, and commercial realities well enough to make informed decisions, ask smarter questions, and connect execution to real-world impact. You don't need to be a medical expert, but you are an industry-savvy operator who understands pharma economics, launch timelines, competitive dynamics, and patient access challenges. You ask "why does this matter commercially?" and "what does success look like for the client?" regularly. This commercial acumen informs how you scope projects, allocate resources, and prioritize decisions. You help your team see beyond deliverables to outcomes.

  • Confident Driver of Progress

You embrace being a driver, not just a facilitator or administrator. You create momentum, push for clarity and decisions when you see ambiguity, hold teams accountable constructively without micromanaging, and move work forward even when information is imperfect or circumstances are complicated. You don't wait for consensus to take action; you make smart calls and bring people along. You recognize that indecision is a decision, and you're willing to take that on. You drive toward clear wins and celebrate progress, which energizes your teams and builds confidence across the organization.

  • Steward of Team Balance and Performance

You actively shape the health of the system, not just the output. You recognize burnout early—in individuals and in teams—and you recalibrate workload, expectations, or resources proactively before people break. You also recognize underperformance with equal clarity and you raise the bar constructively, providing support and accountability. You design operating rhythms, sprint cycles, and governance structures that support both sustainable, high performance and uncompromising standards. You understand that how people feel about their work is as important as what they produce, and that sustainable excellence requires both.

  • Ownership Mindset and Creative Agency

You do not wait for permission to elevate the work. You bring forward ideas on how to operate better, propose smarter ways of organizing projects, design stronger plans, and take responsibility for improving outcomes beyond your assigned scope. You see gaps and fill them. You spot inefficiencies and fix them. You don't assume "that's someone else's problem"—you own the enterprise. This doesn't mean doing everything yourself; it means taking initiative to identify what needs to change and driving toward solutions. Your ownership extends to your team's success, your clients' outcomes, and the health of the broader organization.

  • Strong Judgment and Prioritization Instincts

You consistently make good calls under pressure and constraint. You distinguish signal from noise in a sea of competing demands. You make smart trade-offs between speed, quality, and risk with sound instinct—not by formula. You prioritize effectively, recognizing what matters most and what can wait. You have good instincts about people, situations, and strategic priorities, and you trust those instincts while remaining open to new information. When you have to move fast, you do. When you need to be deliberate, you are. You know the difference, and you rarely get it wrong.

  • Courage and Comfort with Productive Discomfort

You are willing to push when it's uncomfortable and challenge constructively when you see a better path. You hold tension without smoothing it away prematurely; you recognize that some of the best solutions come from sitting with uncomfortable questions rather than resolving them quickly. You make difficult calls when needed—hard conversations, tough decisions, unpopular stands—with confidence rather than approval-seeking. You bring backup (data, reasoning, alternatives) to every discussion. You operate with the confidence of someone who takes responsibility for their decisions and is willing to defend them, but you're also genuinely open to being wrong and course-correcting when new information warrants it.

Pay Range: $250,000-$290,000

job.description:

Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed.
