job.title: Assistant Professor of Sports Media and Communication
job.description:
Department Summary:

Drake University is a forward-thinking community of scholars with a focus on active, collaborative learning and applied scholarship. Drake is in Des Moines, Iowa—a vibrant city that is nationally recognized for its quality of life and a wealth of opportunities for professional, social and civic engagement.


A Drake education couples hands-on training in professional skills with a strong liberal arts education. We strive to create a community of scholars that represents the complexity of the human experience in regards to race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, economic status, gender identification, religion, age and physical abilities. We are committed to creating a welcoming and supportive environment for all our faculty, staff, students and visitors.


We develop and offer innovative programming serving a variety of audiences, including high school, undergraduate, and graduate students, as well as community members, industry professionals, and retirees. The successful applicant will join a collegial, welcoming, energetic and supportive community. Visit our website (drake.edu/sjmc) to learn more.


Job Summary:

The Drake School of Journalism and Mass Communication invites applications for a nine-month, consecutive term appointment of an assistant professor of sports media and communication, beginning in fall semester 2027. Drake’s School of Journalism and Mass Communication is accredited by ACEJMC and offers seven award-winning undergraduate majors: advertising, content strategy and publishing, digital media production, multimedia journalism, public relations, sports media and communication, and strategic political communication. The School also has a successful online Master of Arts in Communication with tracks in brand communication, communication leadership, and public policy and advocacy. The successful applicant will join a collegial, welcoming and supportive community of 14 full-time faculty and staff, and approximately 350 undergraduate and graduate students. We are looking for an innovative colleague who embraces cutting-edge technologies and who can help lead our School in preparing our students for the rapidly changing media landscape.

Professional experience working in sports media is required. Ideally the candidate will have experience in sports production and live broadcasts. Candidates may also bring front-of-camera experience to the role. A portfolio of work is expected. Evidence of teaching effectiveness is preferred. Master’s degree is preferred, but we are open to hiring an experienced professional with a bachelor’s degree for this consecutive-term appointment. Qualified candidates will have a demonstrated ability to train and mentor students and a history of early adoption of new technologies. The ability to work with colleagues across disciplines to lead students in conceiving, creating, delivering, and promoting rich multimedia content packages for all platforms, and for all types of media outlets, is essential. Depending on skills and interest, teaching assignments may include these undergraduate courses, both on campus and online: Sports Writing, Sports Production, Reporting and Writing Principles, Multimedia Lab, Multimedia Sound Design, Electronic Field Production, Reporting for Television and the Web, and special topics courses focused on interactive reality, data visualization, and emerging technologies. The qualified candidate may also teach online graduate classes in Digital Media Strategies, Emerging Media, and Multimedia Storytelling. Course load is seven courses (4/3) over the academic year. Duties also include academic and career mentoring for students, advising a student media organization or student sports production, and service to the University and community.


The search committee is particularly interested in candidates who, through their teaching, scholarship/creative activity, and service, will contribute to the diversity and excellence of the academic community.


Minimum Qualifications:

● An advanced degree (MA, MS) in Communication, Media, Journalism or a related field or equivalent professional experience, which SJMC defines as “at least three to five years of broad and deep experience in real-world situations relevant to the discipline in which the faculty member would be teaching.”

● Potential for successful teaching of undergraduate courses in sports media production

● Production experience directly related to sports media, media production, television production, news production or related fields

● Record of professional achievement related to sports media production

● Excellent written communication skills

● Expressed desire to provide equal opportunity for all students

Preferred Qualifications:

While not everyone may meet all preferred qualifications, the ideal candidate will bring many of the following:

● Experience teaching at the college or university level

● Successful experience in the following:

- working collaboratively with others (e.g., committee service, being part of

a production team, co-teaching);

- working independently (e.g., supervising a production, course

development)

● Experience in Live Sports Productions as any of the following:

- Producer

- Director

- Technical Director

- Replay Operator

- Audio Operator

- Camera Operator

- Graphics Operator

- Talent (Play-By-Play/Analyst)

● Experience in Sports Newsrooms/Departments as any of the following:

- Anchor

- Reporter (MMJ)

- Videographer

- Editor

- Producer

- Director

● Demonstrated successful experience teaching undergraduate media production courses

● Experience connecting and collaborating with media industry professionals on the local, regional, and/or national levels

● Effective interpersonal communication skills

● Effective oral communication skills

● Effective classroom management skills

● Expressed commitment to Drake University’s mission and values.

● Terminal degree in communication, media or related field (MFA, PhD)

‌

Special Instructions to Applicants:

Please complete the online application and attach (1) a letter of interest, (2) CV/Resume, (3) a statement about your experience in supporting the success of students from diverse backgrounds, and (4) the contact details for three references, including one for teaching (if a teaching position).

Please do not attach additional documents at this time. Supplemental documents may be requested or required of semi-finalists and finalists.


For full consideration, apply by November 9, 2026. The position will remain posted until filled.


Questions about this position can be directed to the search chair: Dr. Kelly Bruhn, dean of the School of Journalism and Mass Communication, kelly.bruhn@drake.edu

Questions about the application process, working at Drake, spouse/partner support, reasonable accommodations, benefits, or additional information about Drake or Des Moines, Iowa, may be directed to Drake Human Resources at jobs@drake.edu.

All job offers are contingent upon satisfactory completion of a background check, satisfactory reference checks, and proof of authorization to work in the United States.

Salary is competitive with peer schools and will be commensurate with qualifications and experience of the selected candidate.

At Drake, we are proud to offer our employees, their spouses, and eligible dependents a comprehensive benefits package, which includes a wide range of core benefits, perks, and discounts. If you are exploring a job with Drake University, we invite you to spend a little time with our digital benefits guide: Benefits Overview | Drake University.

One of our very popular policies provides a tuition waiver for Drake employees, their spouses, and eligible dependents. Drake also participates in not one, but two tuition exchange programs available to dependent children. You can learn about both the tuition waiver policy and tuition exchange programs here: Benefits Overview | Drake University.


For faculty positions, selection will depend on the receipt of recommendation confirming the candidate's scholarly achievements and teaching abilities and/or on the candidate's satisfactory passing of a teaching demonstration if selected for an on-campus interview. For staff positions, selection will depend upon careful review of each applicant’s references, education, and, if applicable, experience.

About Drake:


Drake University is recognized as a top private university in the Midwest. Drake is a midsize university in Des Moines, Iowa, with an increasingly diverse student body. We are deeply committed to equity and inclusion and creating a sense of belonging for all members of the campus community—faculty, staff, and students alike. More than 900 faculty and staff are part of the Bulldog pack, a close-knit group of colleagues enthusiastic about preparing students to be global citizens and leaders, challenging assumptions. Drake University is not only an outstanding institution of higher learning, it is also a wonderful place to work. We are enthusiastically committed to welcoming new ideas and people into the fold, and to retaining and rewarding stellar employees.


All positions at Drake provide opportunities to contribute to Drake University’s core mission of creating of creating an exceptional learning environment that prepares students of all backgrounds for meaningful lives and professional accomplishments.


STRONG COMMITMENT TO A DIVERSE AND INCLUSIVE COMMUNITY

At Drake University, we don’t just accept differences—we celebrate them, we support them, and we thrive on them for the benefit of our students, our employees, and our community. Drake University is proud to support an equal opportunity, diverse, inclusive, and welcoming workplace. Learn more about why Drake is an exceptional place to work: An Exceptional Working Environment | Drake University

Drake University is committed to providing access and reasonable accommodations in its services, programs, activities, education, and employment for individuals with disabilities. If you would benefit from an accommodation at any point in the recruitment process (including using our online application process), please contact Drake Human Resources (ph: 515.271.3133; email: jobs@drake.edu) and let us know how we can assist you.

At Drake University, we highly value a diverse, inclusive workforce. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We stand firmly against discrimination including on the basis of race, color, national origin, creed, religion, age, disability, sex, pregnancy, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, veteran status, or any characteristic protected by law.

job.title: Bilingual Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) / News Reporter
job.description:
Telemundo Nebraska | Flood Communications

Position Overview

Telemundo Nebraska is seeking a motivated, creative, and passionate

Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) / News Reporter to join our growing news team!

As Nebraska's local Spanish-language television news station, Telemundo Nebraska is committed to delivering accurate, timely, and meaningful news coverage that informs, connects, and serves our communities.


We are looking for a versatile storyteller who thrives in a fast-paced newsroom, takes initiative, and is excited to cover the people, issues, and events that matter most to Nebraska viewers.

This is a hands-on journalism position where you will pitch, research, shoot, write, edit, produce, and report original news stories for television, digital, and social media platforms. Opportunities for anchoring and live reporting may also be available.

The ideal candidate is a self-starter with strong journalistic instincts, excellent storytelling abilities, and a passion for community-focused reporting.


Key Responsibilities

  • Multimedia Reporting: Research, develop, and report compelling local news stories, breaking news, community events, and human-interest features.
  • Video Production: Independently shoot, edit, and produce broadcast-quality video packages using professional cameras and editing software.
  • News Writing: Write clear, accurate, engaging scripts and digital news content in Spanish, with English proficiency for research and newsroom collaboration.
  • On-Air Reporting: Deliver professional, credible, and engaging on-camera reports, standups, and live coverage as assigned.
  • Story Development: Generate original story ideas, identify newsworthy topics, and develop sources throughout Nebraska's communities.
  • Interviews: Conduct interviews with community members, public officials, business leaders, and other newsmakers.
  • Breaking News Coverage: Respond quickly to developing stories and changing newsroom priorities while maintaining accuracy and journalistic integrity.
  • Digital & Social Media: Create and publish engaging content across the station's website, streaming, and social media platforms.
  • Community Engagement: Build meaningful relationships with viewers and community organizations to identify stories that matter.
  • Newsroom Collaboration: Work closely with anchors, producers, editors, and other journalists to deliver high-quality news coverage.
  • Journalistic Standards: Maintain the highest standards of accuracy, fairness, ethics, and professionalism.
  • Additional Opportunities: Participate in special programming, live events, and sports coverage when appropriate.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Broadcast Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred.
  • Previous television news reporting, multimedia journalism, or video production experience preferred. Recent graduates with strong demo reels are encouraged to apply.
  • Bilingual proficiency in Spanish and English required, including strong Spanish-language writing and on-air communication skills.
  • Ability to independently shoot, write, edit, and produce news stories from concept to completion.
  • Strong on-camera presence and effective storytelling skills.
  • Excellent news judgment with commitment to accuracy, fairness, and community-focused journalism.
  • Experience with video cameras, audio equipment, and nonlinear editing software preferred.
  • Understanding of digital journalism, social media, and multiplatform content distribution.
  • Strong time management and organizational skills with the ability to meet tight deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Willingness to travel for news coverage and work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed.
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel to reporting assignments.


What We Offer

  • Competitive salary based on experience and qualifications.
  • Comprehensive benefits package for eligible full-time employees.
  • Opportunities for professional growth and career advancement.
  • Hands-on experience across television, digital, and social media platforms.
  • Opportunities to develop your own stories, build your portfolio, and expand your on-air experience.
  • A collaborative, creative, and community-focused newsroom.
  • The opportunity to make a meaningful impact through local journalism serving Nebraska's Hispanic communities.


How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit the following:

  • Current resume
  • Demo reel or examples of reporting and video production work
  • Brief cover letter outlining relevant experience and interest in the position

Send applications to: kwilson@floodcomm.com

Subject Line: Telemundo Nebraska – MMJ News Reporter Application

Join Telemundo Nebraska and help tell stories that inform, connect, and strengthen our communities!


Equal Opportunity Employer

Flood Digital Networks, LLC, Flood Communications LLC, and their subsidiaries are Equal Opportunity Employers. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. Women, minorities, and individuals from diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

job.title: Executive Producer
job.description:
EXECUTIVE PRODUCER

SilverLoch Media · Stuart, Florida · On-site · Full-time · $95,000 – $130,000

The Company

SilverLoch Media is the production company founded by Dan and Paula Bongino, producing The Dan Bongino Show and a slate of daily news and commentary programming distributed across [Rumble, podcast platforms, and national radio syndication].

We operate from a purpose-built broadcast facility on Florida's Treasure Coast, where a deliberately lean team delivers live daily programming to a national audience. There is no soft launch here. Every show is live, every day.

The Position

SilverLoch Media seeks an Executive Producer to assume complete ownership of production, from concept through delivery.

The Executive Producer ensures that every program airs on time and to standard, and builds the operational systems that make that outcome dependable. The role carries authority over the production team, the schedule, the technical environment, and the editorial bar.

The Executive Producer works directly with on-air talent, syndication partners, and the digital team.


Core Responsibilities

Daily Delivery. Ensure every live episode is produced as the best possible product and airs on time.

Editorial Oversight. Approve scripts, rundowns, and program concepts. Direct episode planning and story development in alignment with the company's editorial standards and audience.

Team Leadership. Manage and mentor production staff. Own assignments, workflow, performance management, and professional development.

Program Construction. Direct run of show, segment planning, timing, guest coordination, and preparation materials for talent.

Studio and Control Room Operations. Oversee the live switching environment, equipment readiness, sponsor relationships, and a maintenance schedule that prevents a failed component from becoming a dark show.

Post-Production and Distribution. Supervise episode edits, clip production, and podcast versions, delivered on schedule to every platform on which we publish.

Publishing Standards. Verify titles, descriptions, air times, and links prior to release. Accuracy in publication carries the same weight as accuracy on air.

Performance and Growth. Review audience metrics and feedback, and apply them to sharpen content strategy and support audience growth.

Multi-Program Coordination. Allocate studio time, crew, and equipment across a concurrent slate without conflict.

Required Qualifications

  • Five or more years producing live or daily programming in broadcast, radio, podcast, or digital media. Daily cadence is essential.
  • Demonstrated experience leading a production team, rather than producing individual segments alone.
  • Command of a live control room environment. TriCaster and Wirecast experience strongly preferred.
  • Working fluency in post-production workflows — Adobe Premiere or equivalent.
  • Practical understanding of podcast and radio distribution: feed management, syndication requirements, platform specifications, and analytics.
  • Sound editorial judgment, including script and rundown review, story development, and the capacity to decide quickly under pressure.
  • Composure under live conditions and a solutions-oriented approach to failure.
  • Exacting attention to detail. The successful candidate verifies the link, re-reads the description, and catches the incorrect time zone before the audience does.
  • Working knowledge of current events, politics, and the conservative media audience.
  • Availability for the full SilverLoch Media lineup, including early mornings and any afternoon pre-recording requirements.
  • Bachelor's degree in media, communications, journalism, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Background in news or political programming.
  • Familiarity with Rumble, YouTube, Spotify, and the major podcast platforms.
  • Experience working alongside national radio syndication partners.
  • Experience with major social media platforms.

Compensation and Benefits

  • $95,000 – $130,000, commensurate with experience
  • Competitive paid time off, paid holidays, and 401(k)
  • Florida levies no state income tax, and cost of living on the Treasure Coast sits well below that of every major media market. Compensation here carries considerably further than an equivalent figure in New York, Washington, or Los Angeles.
  • A senior position with genuine authority over the operation

Application

Submit your resume to jasmine@bongino.com, accompanied by a brief statement describing a live production for which you were responsible and your experience.

SilverLoch Media is an equal opportunity employer.

job.title: Executive Producer - Daily Show
job.description:
Executive Producer, New Daily Show

KNKX | Full-time onsite in Tacoma, Washington

Salary Range: $90,000 - $110,000 annually, depending on experience



About the Opportunity

Pacific Public Media/KNKX has a strong history of creating memorable, award-winning content. From long-form documentaries to reporting, the station has always valued creativity and digging deep into the topics that matter to Western Washington.


Now, KNKX is launching something new: a daily, one-hour news, interview and storytelling program that will serve listeners from Bellingham to Castlerock, and Seattle to Aberdeen. The show will cover the news of the day while saving space for arts, culture, and the stories that surprise and inspire.


We’re hiring for an Executive Producer onsite in Tacoma, WA. This is a rare opportunity to build a show from the ground up at a station that is investing and growing. In a media landscape where newsrooms are contracting, KNKX is creating something, and the right person gets to shape what it becomes.


Why This Role Stands Out

  • You get to create a show from scratch and define its voice, identity, and editorial direction.
  • You will build your own team: partner in hiring the Host, Co-Host, Producers, and Digital Producer who will bring the show to life.
  • Fill a real need: this show is part of KNKX's commitment to serving the community.



The Role

As Executive Producer, you will be the creative and operational leader behind this new program. Working in close partnership with the News Director, you will shape the daily editorial vision and sound of the show, lead a 6-person production team, and help set the standard for what local public media can be.

This is not a role where you step into an existing show with established workflows. The first months will be about building: developing the show's identity, hiring the team, integrating with the newsroom, and getting a new program on the air. Once the show launches, you will be responsible for the consistency, quality, and growth of the product across broadcast, podcast, digital, and social platforms.



Key Responsibilities

  • Help build the show from the ground up in partnership with KNKX senior leadership, including hiring the production team.
  • Shape the daily editorial direction and sound of the program, balancing news of the day with arts, culture, and storytelling.
  • Manage, develop, and lead a 5-person production team (Host, Co-Host, 2 Producers, Digital Producer) to deliver compelling daily content.
  • Pitch and produce engaging segments alongside the team, leading by example on deadline.
  • Work closely with the KNKX newsroom to share content, develop story leads, and coordinate regional coverage.
  • Champion a multi-platform approach, ensuring the show reaches audiences as a broadcast, podcast, in digital stories, on social media, and through a weekly newsletter.
  • Handle administrative responsibilities including scheduling, time management, and planning for coverage across the team.



What We're Looking For

Must-Haves

  • 5+ years of experience managing people and leading a collaborative production team. This is the top priority. You have inspired and guided different personalities, navigated tough conversations, and managed, supported, and held your team accountable.
  • 7+ years of deep experience with daily production and deadlines. You know what it takes to put out a show every day, whether that has been in radio, television, or podcasting.
  • On-air experience. With a 6-person team, coverage gaps happen. We need you to be comfortable stepping in front of the microphone when the situation calls for it.
  • A demonstrated understanding of public media values and sound. You do not have to come from public radio, but you need to get what makes it different.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred
  • This position is based in KNKX’s Tacoma, WA studios 5 days a week



Sets You Apart

  • Experience building or creating a show or program from scratch. If you have launched something new and it stuck, that puts you in the top tier for this role.
  • Connections to Western Washington's news, civic, cultural, and political landscape. Local knowledge is not required, but it strengthens your candidacy.
  • A flexible, audience-first mindset. You think about what listeners want and need.



About us

At KNKX we work hard to create a culture where employees feel valued and respected, are trusted and encouraged to be a part of improvements that impact their work, create value, and help build trust in public media. KNKX’s vision is to grow and become a more inclusive organization that brings joy, meaning and understanding into people’s lives. We value diverse perspectives and an array of life experiences.


KNKX is a Western Washington public media company, dedicated to bringing jazz, blues, regional news, and NPR programs to the Northwest and beyond. As an independent dual-format station, KNKX employees are energized in their mission to provide the very best music and news content to an audience of more than 400,000 weekly.



How to Apply

Apply here: https://knkx.bamboohr.com/careers/66?source=aWQ9NjE%3D

Submit your:

  • Resume
  • Link to a daily show or podcast you have produced that you are proud of

If selected to continue, we will ask for additional work samples (at least two produced shows/podcast samples and an on-air sample) before the panel interview stage.



Compensation and Benefits

Salary: $90,000 - $110,000 annually, depending on experience

KNKX offers a strong benefits package, including:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage with FSA option
  • PTO and holidays, including the full week between Christmas and New Year's
  • 401(k) with generous company match
  • Disability, life, and AD&D insurance options
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)



Interview Process

  • Phone screening with the myHR Partner hiring team
  • Work sample collection (produced show/podcast samples and on-air sample)
  • Panel interview with the hiring committee
  • Final onsite interview


Our hiring management partner is myHR Partner. myHR Partner is not a staffing service or recruiter. All resumes/applications will be reviewed for this position and only for our organization.


Thank you for considering us as a potential employer!


Additional Information and Conditions of Employment:

Prior to hire, references and a background check including criminal record history will be conducted. Information from the background check will not necessarily preclude employment but will be considered in determining the applicant’s suitability and competence to perform in the position.


KNKX is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, sex (including gender identity), marital status, sexual orientation, race, creed, color, national origin, veteran or military status, or the presence of any sensory, mental, or physical disability or the use of a trained dog guide or service animal by a person with a disability. You are welcome to include the name and pronoun you would like to be referred to in your materials and we will honor it. Persons requiring accommodation in the application process, during the recruitment process, or who need this job announcement in an alternative format, may contact the Human Resources Office at knkxhr@myhrpartner.com.

job.title: Field Producer
job.description:
Rossen Reports is looking for an experienced freelance producer to work closely with Jeff Rossen on retail and shopping videos filmed inside major retailers. This is an editorial position. Research and storytelling are at the heart of what we do. Rossen Reports reach more than 4 million subscribers and followers across our digital platforms, helping consumers save money and shop smarter. We’re looking for a resourceful, organized producer who loves retail, shopping, and consumer content. You must also be comfortable filming content on small cameras, including iPhones.


As we grow, this could evolve into a full-time role for the right candidate.


What you’ll do

  • Research assigned retail stories, including products, deals, price comparisons, and what’s worth buying—or skipping.
  • Verify prices, product details, availability, and other facts before filming.
  • Prepare research notes and organize the products and information needed for each shoot.
  • Work directly with Jeff Rossen in the field, filming on an iPhone and helping bring each story to life.
  • Capture product shots, price tags, demonstrations, and other supporting footage.
  • Coordinate with our production and editing team to deliver organized footage and accurate story notes.


What we’re looking for

  • Prior experience in producing, digital content creation, television, or consumer-focused video.
  • Strong research skills and attention to detail.
  • Comfort filming on an iPhone, with an eye for framing and clean audio.
  • A real interest in retail, shopping, lifestyle, and helping people save money.
  • The ability to move quickly, meet deadlines, and work independently.
  • A collaborative approach and comfort working closely with on-camera talent.


Location and availability

This is a freelance opportunity requiring in-person shoots in South Florida, ideally based near Boca Raton. Candidates must be able to travel to local retail locations.


To apply

Please send a DM. Plus, email your résumé, and a brief note about your producing and shooting experience, location, and availability.


Company Description Rossen Media is the parent company of Rossen Reports, a nationally recognized consumer journalism franchise focused on helping audiences save money, avoid scams, and navigate complex systems. With more than 4 million subscribers across digital platforms and a national broadcast presence, Rossen Media delivers smart, practical, and investigative consumer content to a broad audience. The company is built on credibility, innovation, and strong audience loyalty, making it a trusted source for consumer information. As Rossen Media expands its digital footprint and develops new programming, it is building a next-generation media brand centered on empowering consumers everywhere. Team members join a mission-driven organization that values impactful storytelling and journalistic integrity.

job.title: Producer
job.description:
Carousel's Producer will require outstanding organization, communication, budgeting, negotiating, and leadership skills along with a positive, motivated and entrepreneurial attitude. This role is full-time, on-site in San Diego, with options for hybrid work opportunities.


Our ideal candidate will bring deep experience and creative prowess across pre-production, production and post-production of long-form and short-form brand content, broadcast and commercial work. Carousel is looking for a talented producer who will work quickly and nimbly alongside a growing team to drive projects forward. Your dynamic professionalism, effortless adaptability and easy-going personality will make you an irreplaceable member of the Carousel team.

Owner of multiple workstreams through planning, resourcing and scheduling – keeping projects flowing with ease on time and on budget. Most critically, our Producers simply find a way to make things happen while maintaining healthy, high-quality relationships with our world-class clientele. This integral role is key to the creation of top tier work that Carousel is known for.


  • Organization - outstanding organizational skills keeping projects, timelines, notes, and files clean.
  • Communication - refined communication skills with internal and external teams.
  • Coordination - strong coordination skills getting teams to align on key topics and objectives.
  • Negotiation - excellent negotiation skills and relationship building with internal and external partners.
  • Prioritization - ability to help identify challenges and prioritize solutions in a fast-paced environment.
  • Adaptation - ability to adapt effortlessly to ambiguity and change throughout projects.
  • Solution - ability to approach challenges with optimism to find optimal solutions.


Qualification:


  • Four Year Degree Preferred, not required.
  • 5-10 Years Professional Experience - Production, Studio, Brand, Creative, Advertising Agency preferred.
  • Experience working with Google Workplace, Dropbox, Monday, Slack, Adobe and Wrapbook.
  • High attention to detail required to work on industry-leading work for world-class clients.
  • Growth mindset and desire to learn and challenge yourself in new ways.


Compensation:


  • Annual Salary (1st and 15th)
  • 100% Employee Medical, Dental, Vision Benefits
  • 10 Days Paid Vacation, 5 Paid Sick Days, 6 Paid Holidays
  • Discretionary Performance Bonus
  • 401k Retirement Plan
  • 5% Retirement Employer Contribution (After 90 Days of Employment)


Carousel is a strategic creative + content studio based in San Diego, California. Our office is located in Ocean Beach, two blocks from the ocean. We provide a welcoming work environment with highly talented team, world-class clients, top-notch benefits and outstanding opportunities for all.

job.title: Producer, Media Services - HYBRID Chicago, IL or Carmel, IN
job.description:
CNO Financial Group, Inc. (NYSE: CNO) is a leading insurance and financial services company focused on securing the future of middle‑income America. Through brands such as Bankers Life, Colonial Penn, and Washington National, CNO delivers life and health insurance, annuities, financial services, and workforce benefits to more than 3.3 million policyholders, supported by $38.3 billion in total assets.


With a strong financial foundation, national presence, and a culture rooted in integrity, excellence, and people‑first values, CNO offers meaningful opportunities for professional growth and impact across its U.S. locations, including its headquarters in Carmel, Indiana.


This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.


CNO Financial Group is hiring a Producer, Media Services who is accountable for the full production lifecycle, from strategy to execution, for the audio/visual presentation elements of in-person and virtual broadcast events. The role partners with event planners, internal clients and external vendors to plan, design, and produce audio/visual presentations, staged and virtual broadcast events for the Company. Events include in-person meetings and seminars, internal Town Halls and external corporate briefings, and internal speaker events over Zoom, Teams and other platforms.


This role collaborates with IT, Field Sales, Corporate Communications, Investor Relations, Marketing and senior leadership to recommend and implement scalable, in-house solutions that reduce cost and vendor dependence—often setting new standards for internal production capabilities. The role is responsible for bridging gaps between technical teams and creative vision.


Core responsibilities and deliverables:

Virtual & In-Person Event Support

  • Own the design and execution of the audio/visual elements of staged in-person events including but not limited to business sessions, awards galas, and entertainment staging in collaboration with meeting planners, executive and senior leadership clients.
  • Creates detailed room layouts using room layout software to ensure optimal spatial planning for all events; recommends venue viability and event success by translating complex production requirements into precise, actionable diagrams.
  • Creates cost estimates/budgets and procures necessary A/V needs, including contracting vendors and broadcast production partners.
  • Serve as lead audio/visual producer/director for in-person events readying presentations, videos, cameras, audio and video cues.
  • Provide guidance on production design and equipment needs in support of executing events.
  • Serve as Producer for both live in-person events and virtual broadcast events, which includes calling the show, running graphics and videos, and audio 2 engineer.
  • Manage internal and external resources delegating roles to different internal/external teams including: Event Marketing, Communications, and Learning Media, managing rehearsals and providing post event feedback to ensure ongoing improvements.
  • Optimize presenter audio/video quality within environmental limitations, lead rehearsals; provide live support and troubleshooting during events, escalating issues as needed.
  • Collaborate with meeting planners and client leads in review and approve technical specifications and space requirements of on-location events.


Creative Production

  • Produce promotional events videos, large field meeting openers, and recognition of top branch sales producers
  • Create concepts, scripts, production plans, cost estimates and talent reviews; procure and managing crew, crew travel and on-site schedules.
  • Direct video production; perform post-shoot editing; produce and edit design graphics and musical accompaniments as directed from clients and brand teams.

Technology & Equipment

  • Provide in-depth knowledge and training on software, technology, and A/V equipment.
  • Research and recommend streaming or videoconferencing platforms/methods; oversee setup ensure presenters and team members are prepared and comfortable with the technology
  • Execute videoconference stream support including call set-up, end user training, troubleshooting, and escalation follow-through.
  • Determine equipment needs, oversee rental agreements and vendor management for audio, visual and lighting needs.
  • Onboard and train internal/external resources on equipment, technology and production best practices; Management of all A/V equipment
  • Research and create solutions that reduce hardware or software costs and continually search for new technologies that optimize production


What you need (Minimum requirements):

  • Associates Degree in Communications, TV/Radio production, Marketing, or related discipline, or equivalent experience in lieu of degree.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in supporting meetings including designing, staging and execution of audio / visual presentations and configuration & installation of audio visual systems.
  • Able to work in a hybrid capacity from our Chicago, IL or Carmel, IN corporate office, and travel ~40-60 days of the year for events, with some trips up to 10 days in length. Some international travel required.
  • Must be able to perform the physical demands of the role, including pushing carts over 100 lbs., lifting and carrying up to 50 lbs., working on ladders, and standing or walking for extended periods with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • In-depth knowledge of AV system support: operation, installation, and configuration of projectors, amplifiers, AV matrix routers, control systems and touch panels; SDI, DVI, HDMI video/audio installation and cabling including termination
  • Proficient in Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Keynote, PowerPoint, Excel, and Word.
  • Expertise in video mixing software including Vmix, OBS, NDI, and Bitfocus Companion or related software.


What will set you apart (Preferred experience):

  • 5-7 years of experience years of experience with a track record of broad and growing responsibilities related to the execution of virtual events, live productions, staging, video engineering for large scale events and programs.
  • Solid tact and good judgment in communicating with representatives from external organizations, and vendors.
  • Strong ability to work with associates with all levels of the organization on system functionality, project issues, and planning.
  • Solid problem escalation support and issue resolution; follows-up on service challenges and works with the clients to take corrective action.


CNO Financial Group offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • Performance-based bonus or sales incentive
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match
  • Short-term & long-term disability insurance
  • Paid time off and 10 corporate holidays
  • Paid parental leave
  • Company-paid life insurance
  • Mental & Financial Well-Being resources


Click on this link for additional information.


CNO supports a flexible work environment and encourages Associates to work where they are most productive. This position may work in a hybrid model from our Carmel, IN or Chicago, IL office. Outside of work-related travel, all work must be performed within the United States, and occasional travel to corporate offices may be required.

job.title: Promotions Director – Portland Media Group
job.description:
Looking for your next career move?

We’re Portland Media Group, and we’re hiring a Promotions Director to lead the promotions department for our eight radio brands.

This is a leadership role for someone who’s creative, highly organized and ready to turn ideas into events people remember. You’ll run every on-air and on-site promotion across our brands, from contests and remotes to concerts, community events and sponsor activations, taking each one from first idea to final recap.

You’ll work closely with our sales team to build promotions that deliver real results for clients and open doors with the business owners and decision makers they want to meet. If you enjoy big projects, tight deadlines and being part of a team that helps businesses succeed, you’ll thrive here.

You’ll work alongside our Director of Sales, Sales and Promotions Assistant and our Directors of Content from each radio brand to keep us front and center in the community. Our live events draw thousands of fans each year to raise money for local nonprofits and charities.

We’re what we call a Click, Visit, Call and Search media company. Our mission is simple: help our clients Get Wanted, Get Found and Get Chosen!

What we’re looking for:

3+ years in promotions, event marketing or a similar role; radio experience preferred but not necessary.

Strong planning and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple events and deadlines.

Proficiency with WordPress, website management, Photoshop and Illustrator or comparable tools.

Experience running targeted social media campaigns.

Excellent communication and customer fulfillment skills.

Familiarity with vCreative, vPromotions and Aptivada/Audience is a plus.

A love of live and recorded music.

Availability for evenings and weekends as events may require, a valid driver’s license and the ability to lift 50 lbs.

What you’ll do:

  • Plan and run radio brand promotions, contests, remotes and live events from start to finish.
  • Build sponsor packages with sales team and deliver what was promised on air, on site and online.
  • Host client events such as business breakfasts, VIP nights and concert hospitality that bring our sales team face to face with decision makers.
  • Keep brand websites current in WordPress and create graphics in Photoshop and Illustrator.
  • Run targeted social media campaigns for our brands and sponsors.
  • Write contest rules and ensure FCC, sweepstakes and brand policy compliance.
  • Manage prizes and fulfillment, the street team and the promotions vehicle.
  • Deliver sponsor recaps with photos, attendance and results.
  • Manage promotions budgets and vendor relationships.

What you’ll get:

  • $49,000–$54,000 annual salary, based on experience.
  • Health benefits, PTO, 401K and ongoing training.
  • A creative role at the center of our brands’ concerts, contests and community events.
  • A supportive team that wants to see you succeed.
  • Career growth opportunities within Portland Media Group.

Every day is different, every event is unique, and this is a place that invests in its people. We’re committed to your growth, and if that sounds like your kind of opportunity, let’s talk.

Send your resume and a quick note to Barry Gabloff, General Manager at talent@portlandmediagrp.com. We can’t wait to meet you!

Portland Media Group is a division of Saga Communications and an Equal Opportunity Employer.

job.title: Account Executive, WCPO
job.description:
Are you ready to help local businesses thrive while building your own successful sales career?  WCPO, the E.W. Scripps affiliate in Cincinnati, Ohio, is seeking a dynamic Account Executive who will help local businesses realize growth opportunities by reaching customers through compelling multi-platform advertising solutions. You'll be at the forefront of the evolving media landscape, offering everything from traditional broadcast television to cutting-edge digital marketing solutions.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 

  • Sell advertising solutions to local and regional businesses and advertising agencies.
  • Apply the Scripps Sales Process (SSP) to analyze current and prospective customer needs and apply customized advertising solutions that provide return on their investment.
  • In addition to television commercial airtime sales, facilitate the customer’s ability to take advantage of the full array of digital marketing options available.
  • Independently prospect, secure appointments, perform needs analysis, develop customized solutions, present and close sales to develop and maintain new business from traditional and non-traditional advertisers.
  • Use ratings data, qualitative information, and market trends to negotiate program ratings and advertising rates with advertising agencies in order to maximize revenue as well as develop custom solutions for new advertisers.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor with new and existing clients, provide best-in-class customer service, grow accounts, and gain additional business from referrals.
  • Perform client services, including but not limited to media avail negotiations, presentation preparation delivery and execution, copy writing, credit applications, and collection of revenue due.
  • Effectively and proactively manage a sales funnel by way of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems, monitoring and achieving key performance indicators and expected activity levels.
  • Contribute to the creative development of campaigns through client communication and needs analysis, storyboard and concept creation, and assistance in production aspects.
  • Build and maintain strong client relationships, which may include entertaining prospective and existing clients.
  • Perform routine administrative functions of a media salesperson including makegood resolution, continuous update of CRM system with activity, account information and pending revenue, and communication with sales leadership regarding the status of accounts
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
     

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

 

  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred or equivalent years of experience
  • Generally, 2+ years of proven sales success preferred
  • Experience in strategic account management, broadcast ratings and digital execution preferred

 

WHAT YOU’LL BRING:

 

  • Highly self-motivated and goal focused
  • Highly creative and innovative thinker
  • Strong influencing, selling and upselling skills
  • Effective teamwork and collaboration skills
  • Very strong analysis and data interpretation - able to translate needs and research data into sound marketing proposals
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills
  • Outstanding presentation abilities (in person/virtual, small/large groups, all levels)
  • Strong time management and organizational skills
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint)
  • Working knowledge of Google Office (Sheets, Docs, Slides) and virtual conferencing platforms (E.g. Skype, WebEx, Zoom or MS Teams etc.)
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

 

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY:

 

Cincinnati offers an incredible blend of Midwestern charm and big-city amenities, making it one of the most livable cities in America. Known for its rich history, world-class museums, and vibrant arts scene, Cincinnati is home to the renowned Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra, Cincinnati Ballet, and the contemporary arts scene in Over-the-Rhine. The city boasts an amazing culinary landscape, from famous Cincinnati chili to craft breweries and farm-to-table restaurants.

 

Sports fans will love cheering on the Cincinnati Bengals, Cincinnati Reds, and FC Cincinnati. The city's beautiful riverfront along the Ohio River provides stunning views and recreational opportunities, while nearby parks and trails offer endless outdoor adventures. With affordable housing, excellent neighborhoods like Hyde Park, Mount Adams, and the trendy Over-the-Rhine district, Cincinnati provides the perfect backdrop for both career growth and quality of life.

job.title: Assistant News Director, WEWS
job.description:
WEWS, The E.W. Scripps Company ABC affiliate in Cleveland, Ohio, is looking for an experienced and collaborative Assistant News Director to help lead one of the market's most trusted news operations. Working alongside the News Director, you will help oversee all news broadcasts and online content — shaping editorial direction, driving cross-platform audience strategies, and developing the talented team that keeps Cleveland informed. From planning landmark coverage of elections and major local events to managing the budgetary and operational heartbeat of the newsroom, your leadership will have a real and lasting impact. If you're a seasoned news leader who thrives under pressure and is passionate about delivering journalism that matters, WEWS wants to hear from you.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Assist news director with supervisory responsibility for all news broadcasts and online content.
  • Involved in hiring and performance management of direct reports.
  • Assist news director in the on-going evaluation of personnel.
  • Create tactics and strategies to increase demos performance in key target areas for multiple platforms.
  • Implement and have working knowledge of federal, state and local laws impacting operations.
  • Ability to manage cross platform content creation and distribution.
  • Write copy and edit scripts for air and web.
  • Knowledge of and proficiency in posting content to station websites.
  • Schedule anchors and multi-media journalists.
  • Lead coverage planning of major events, i. e. elections, special events.
  • Proactively communicate news initiatives across departments.
  • Evaluate workflow efficiencies.
  • Assist news director in managing the budgetary aspects of newsroom operations.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • BS/BA in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 7+ years of experience in related field preferred
  • Prior managerial experience preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Advanced oral and written communication skills
  • Advanced computer skills including Microsoft Office
  • Broad understanding of newsroom operations and equipment
  • Proven ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast paced environment

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Cleveland, Ohio is a city on the rise, sitting on the southern shore of Lake Erie with a rich cultural heritage and a passionate, proud community. Home to the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, the Cleveland Museum of Art, and the world-renowned Cleveland Orchestra at Severance Music Center, the city offers an exceptional arts and culture scene. The vibrant neighborhoods of Ohio City, Tremont, and Little Italy are filled with acclaimed restaurants, craft breweries, and independent boutiques that give Cleveland its distinctive, welcoming character.


Sports are woven into the fabric of life here. Cheer on the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field, rally behind the Cleveland Cavaliers at Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse, or soak in the electric atmosphere of a Cleveland Browns game at Huntington Bank Field. Cleveland's passionate fan base and storied sports history make it one of the most spirited towns in the country.


Beyond downtown, Greater Cleveland delivers outstanding outdoor recreation along the shores of Lake Erie, with stunning Metroparks, world-class kayaking, and easy access to Cuyahoga Valley National Park — Ohio's only national park. With a cost of living well below most major markets, a booming food-and-drink scene, and a community that is warm and genuine, Cleveland is a place where your career and your life outside of work will both truly thrive.

job.title: Community Connections Coordinator, WEWS
job.description:
WEWS, The E.W. Scripps Company ABC affiliate in Cleveland, Ohio, is searching for a Community Connections Coordinator. We're looking for a driven, people-first professional to join our team and serve as the vital link between our newsroom and the communities we cover. In this role, you'll cultivate meaningful relationships, surface credible story leads, coordinate community events and listening sessions, and help our journalists connect with the trusted local voices that make our coverage matter. Whether you're in the field building source networks, managing audience tips, or supporting breaking news coverage, your work will directly shape how WEWS serves the people of Greater Cleveland every day.


Application Review: Applications received by 11/04 will receive priority consideration. Applications received after this date may continue to be reviewed as needed.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Build and maintain relationships with community organizations, residents, leaders, and trusted sources to gather community insights and identify emerging issues, events, and story opportunities.
  • Monitor, track, and route audience tips, questions, and leads from community channels, ensuring timely communication and escalation to newsroom teams.
  • Support newsroom listening efforts, community conversations, and source development by connecting journalists with credible and diverse community voices.
  • Assist with breaking and developing news coverage by gathering community context, maintaining source networks, and providing timely intelligence to newsroom staff.
  • Serve as a responsive point of contact for community organizations and residents, fostering positive relationships and trust.
  • Coordinate outreach, maintain partner and contact records, and represent the station at community meetings, events, and activities.
  • Support newsroom talent by coordinating interviews, identifying community contacts, gathering background information, and facilitating community appearances.
  • Coordinate logistics and execution for community conversations, listening sessions, public programs, newsroom events, special coverage initiatives, and station appearances.
  • Manage event-related activities including outreach, scheduling, partner coordination, participant communications, on-site support, and post-event follow-up.
  • Support audience engagement across digital and in-person channels, including live discussions, community groups, neighborhood platforms, and other audience interaction opportunities.
  • Maintain community calendars, project plans, contact databases, and engagement records to support execution of the market community strategy.
  • Track community insights, engagement outcomes, story leads, and best practices, preparing summaries and reports that help inform newsroom and community engagement priorities.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • Associates degree in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 5+ years of experience in journalism, communications, community engagement, nonprofit work, events, public relations or related fields

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Strong listening, relationship-building and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to establish rapport with diverse community members and organizations
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent organization, follow-through and attention to detail
  • Ability to identify and communicate relevant community information quickly and accurately
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with journalists and station teams
  • Comfort working independently in the community and adapting to newsroom needs
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, CRM/contact systems, social platforms and collaboration tools
  • Solid news judgment, comfort with newsroom urgency, ability to verify and relay information quickly, and understanding of how community tips can develop into stories
  • Ability to communicate clearly and accurately across digital platforms, maintain professionalism in public-facing conversations and collaborate closely with reporters, producers, anchors, meteorologists and newsroom leaders

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Cleveland is a city of neighborhoods, grit, and genuine heart — and it's having a moment. Situated on the southern shore of Lake Erie, Cleveland combines a rich cultural heritage with a revitalized downtown and a food and arts scene that consistently surprises newcomers. The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, the world-class Cleveland Museum of Art (with free general admission), and Playhouse Square — the largest performing arts center in the U.S. outside of New York City — give the city a cultural depth that is hard to match. Walkable neighborhoods like Ohio City, Tremont, and Little Italy each bring their own distinctive character, cuisine, and community.


Sports are woven into the fabric of Cleveland life. Cheer on the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field, follow the Cleveland Cavaliers at Rocket Arena, and join the passionate faithful who rally behind the Cleveland Browns every season. The sense of community pride around Cleveland's teams is infectious, and game days turn the city into one big celebration.


The outdoors are never far away. Cuyahoga Valley National Park — the only national park in Ohio — sits just south of the city, offering miles of hiking, biking, waterfalls, and scenic railroad excursions. Cleveland Metroparks wraps the city in a beloved "Emerald Necklace" of parks and trails, and Lake Erie's shoreline provides year-round recreation from sailing to fishing. With a lower cost of living than many comparable metros, a growing tech and healthcare economy, and a community-first spirit you can feel on every block, Cleveland is a fantastic place to build a career and a life.

job.title: Director of Engineering, WTXL
job.description:
WTXL, the ABC affiliate in Tallahassee, Florida, owned by The E.W. Scripps Company, is searching for its next Director of Engineering. This is your opportunity to lead the technology that keeps a local television station connected, innovative, and ready to serve its community every day. You’ll guide the station’s technical operations, lead engineering initiatives, and collaborate across teams to keep critical systems performing at their best. Bring your technical expertise, leadership, and problem-solving mindset to a role where what you do behind the scenes makes an impact on everything we deliver to our audiences.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Model and lead a culture of empathy, customer service and leadership.
  • Lead the research, design, installation and repair of all television, digital, OTT, Internet Systems, high power RF systems, production environments and all associated equipment using current platforms and protocols. 
  • Manage building facilities and grounds, including HVAC, power generation and security systems.
  • Partner with the news department to develop, build and support content workflow and support systems including integration and problem-solving software, hardware, networking and infrastructure while facilitating a collaborative environment between newsroom and production control staff.
  • Motivate and manage a staff of professional and technical engineers, operators and IT technicians. Develop and grow staff in technology and Scripps culture to meet the on-going and future technological needs of the station and evaluate staff growth opportunities and assessments.
  • Establish and implement engineering policies and procedures.
  • Evaluate and maintain the spectrum and broadband usage of the facility.
  • Manage projects.
  • Plan, design and document current and future broadcast and digital systems.
  • Collaborate with other departments to determine current and future studio and transmission and workflow needs.
  • Prepare and track capital, expense, repair and maintenance budgets.
  • Use company purchasing management system to purchase and track assets and services as well as replacement cycles.
  • Evaluate equipment solutions.
  • Keep the station compliant with the FCC Rules and Regulations, as well as related local, state, and federal regulations.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • BS/BA in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 10+ years of experience in related field preferred
  • Prior managerial experience preferred
  • Network, SBE and/or Project Management certification preferred

WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • “Customer service first” mindset, ability to deliver a high level of customer service
  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Strategic planning abilities
  • Excellent managerial skills in working with management, users, staff, peers and vendors
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills
  • Ability to relate technical matters to non-technical users
  • Ability to relate business matters to technical staff
  • Team player
  • Self-directed and can work independently
  • Strong project management skills
  • Can manage shifting priorities, demands and timelines smoothly
  • Knowledge of FCC rules
  • Understanding of electronic, electrical, mechanical and information systems
  • Keen interest in emerging broadcast related technologies and how they might be utilized in our business environment
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits

job.title: Executive Reporter, KERO
job.description:
KERO, The E.W. Scripps Company ABC station in Bakersfield, CA, is searching for an Executive Reporter to join our team. In this role, you'll be at the heart of our newsroom, driving a mission to elevate the way we connect with our community through compelling, authentic, and impactful stories. You'll inspire reporters, MMJs, and newsroom staff at every level, bringing your passion and expertise to foster a culture of continuous growth and creative excellence. If you're energized by mentoring talent and shaping the voice of a newsroom, we want to hear from you.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Lead, develop, and enhance the storytelling skill and abilities of all reporters and MMJs in the station.
  • Collaborate with other newsroom leaders to consistently execute the content strategy through authentic, meaningful storytelling.
  • Oversee the writing of stories for all platforms; provide timely feedback to foster continuous improvement.
  • Develop and supervise effective workflow strategies and procedures for multiple news programs and outlets.
  • Ensure that all content adheres to journalistic standards and ethical guidelines.
  • Deliver a vision and create trust among reporters, photographers and newsroom staff.
  • May provide on-air, multi-platform coverage for breaking news as needed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred, or equivalent years of experience
  • Generally, 7+ years of experience in related field preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Demonstrated expertise in storytelling
  • Knowledge and demonstration of editorial judgment, journalistic ethics and libel laws
  • Curiosity for the community, city, state and world we report on daily
  • Deep understanding of the content strategy
  • Ability to work a variety of shifts including nights, weekends, early morning, and holidays

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Bakersfield sits at the southern end of California's San Joaquin Valley, a city with a rich cultural identity and a surprisingly vibrant lifestyle. Known worldwide as the birthplace of the Bakersfield Sound — the country music movement that launched legends like Buck Owens and Merle Haggard — the city wears its roots proudly. The iconic Buck Owens' Crystal Palace keeps that musical spirit alive, while a growing arts scene, local breweries, and a diverse and delicious food culture give the city its own modern energy.


The great outdoors is practically at your doorstep. The Kern River draws whitewater rafting enthusiasts, anglers, and hikers year-round, while Lake Isabella offers boating and camping under wide-open skies. Sequoia National Park and Kings Canyon National Park — home to some of the tallest trees on Earth — are just a couple of hours away, making weekend adventures a genuine California experience.


Bakersfield offers a quality of life that's hard to beat for the price. With a significantly lower cost of living than Los Angeles (just about two hours south), you'll find spacious housing, short commutes, and a strong sense of community. From Friday night high school football to the Bakersfield Condors hockey games at Mechanics Bank Arena, this is a city where people show up for each other — and for the stories that deserve to be told.

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the narrative of our community while mentoring talented reporters and MMJs to reach their full potential.

  • Lead, develop, and enhance the storytelling skill and abilities of all reporters and MMJs in the station.
  • Collaborate with other newsroom leaders to consistently execute the content strategy through authentic, meaningful storytelling.
  • Oversee the writing of stories for all platforms; provide timely feedback to foster continuous improvement.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY:

Denver, Colorado, combines big-market journalism opportunities with an unmatched outdoor lifestyle. As the Mile High City, Denver is one of the fastest-growing and most dynamic metropolitan areas in the country, offering journalists the chance to cover everything from rapid economic growth and innovation to government, transportation, education, public safety, and environmental issues that shape the future of the American West.


Situated at the foot of the Rocky Mountains, Denver provides year-round access to world-class skiing, hiking, mountain biking, camping, and countless outdoor adventures. The city features a thriving arts and culture scene, professional sports teams including the Broncos, Nuggets, Rockies, Avalanche, and Rapids, award-winning restaurants, and vibrant neighborhoods filled with unique stories and diverse perspectives.


KMGH is a trusted news leader serving one of the nation's most competitive and exciting media markets. With breathtaking scenery, an exceptional quality of life, and a community that values strong local journalism, Denver offers a remarkable place to build a meaningful career while making a lasting impact through storytelling.

job.title: Executive Reporter, KTNV
job.description:
Scripps-owned KTNV, the ABC affiliate in Las Vegas, is looking for a Executive Reporter who believes great journalism starts with great storytelling. In this leadership role, you’ll help elevate the craft across the newsroom, working alongside reporters and MMJs to create authentic, meaningful stories that connect with the Las Vegas community.


You’ll bring a sharp editorial eye, a passion for developing people, and the ability to turn everyday assignments into memorable journalism. You’ll also partner with newsroom leaders to bring our content strategy to life across platforms while maintaining the highest journalistic standards. If you’re an accomplished storyteller who gets energized by helping other journalists grow, this is an opportunity to make an impact both inside the newsroom and throughout the community we serve.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Lead the development and enhancement of storytelling skills for reporters and MMJs across the newsroom.
  • Coach and mentor journalists at all experience levels, helping them discover creative ways to strengthen their reporting, writing, and storytelling.
  • Collaborate with newsroom leaders to consistently execute the station’s content strategy through authentic, meaningful journalism.
  • Oversee story writing and development across platforms, providing timely and actionable feedback that encourages continuous improvement.
  • Develop and supervise effective workflows, strategies, and procedures supporting multiple news programs and platforms.
  • Ensure content consistently meets journalistic standards and ethical guidelines.
  • Create and communicate a clear storytelling vision that builds trust among reporters, photographers, and other newsroom colleagues.
  • Contribute on-air and multi-platform coverage during breaking news when needed.
  • Support evolving newsroom priorities and perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related discipline preferred, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Generally 7+ years of experience in journalism, news, storytelling, or a related field preferred.
  • A valid driver’s license and ability to meet applicable driving requirements for the role.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Demonstrated expertise in compelling, community-focused storytelling.
  • Strong editorial judgment and a thorough understanding of journalistic ethics and libel laws.
  • Genuine curiosity about the people, issues, and events shaping Las Vegas, Nevada, and the world.
  • A deep understanding of content strategy and how strong storytelling can serve audiences across platforms.
  • A coaching mindset and a passion for helping journalists develop their craft and reach their potential.
  • The ability to collaborate, communicate a creative vision, and establish trust across a newsroom.
  • Sound judgment and composure in a fast-moving news environment where priorities and deadlines can change quickly.
  • Flexibility to work a variety of shifts, including nights, weekends, early mornings, and holidays.
  • Ability and willingness to work onsite and drive as required to fulfill job responsibilities.

OUR TEAM:

At KTNV, you’ll join a newsroom united by curiosity, creativity, and a commitment to serving the community through meaningful journalism. Our team brings different backgrounds, experiences, interests, and perspectives to the stories we tell. We value collaboration, thoughtful feedback, strong editorial standards, and the willingness to keep improving our craft. As Executive Reporter, you’ll play an important role in creating an environment where journalists learn from one another, take creative approaches to storytelling, and do work that matters to the people of Las Vegas.


WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Las Vegas offers much more than its world-famous entertainment corridor. The region combines big-city energy with distinctive neighborhoods, a thriving food and entertainment scene, and countless opportunities to discover the people and stories that make Southern Nevada unique. For a curious journalist, it’s a dynamic community with no shortage of stories to tell.


Outside of work, Las Vegas puts the outdoors within easy reach, from desert landscapes and hiking to nearby recreation and scenic escapes. It’s a place where entertainment, culture, community, and the natural beauty of the Southwest come together, giving you plenty to explore when you’re off the clock.

job.title: Local Sales Manager, KTVH
job.description:
Are you a proven media sales leader ready to inspire a high-performing team and make a measurable impact in your market? KTVH is looking for a Local Sales Manager who will champion the growth of local businesses through innovative, multi-platform advertising solutions. From broadcast television to Over The Top (OTT) video, SEO/SEM, social media, digital display and email targeting, you'll guide a talented team of Account Executives in connecting clients with the audiences that matter most — all while driving the station's revenue forward and developing the next generation of Scripps sales talent.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Collaborate with DOS and other sales managers and departments to accomplish the objectives of the station.
  • Organize, direct and manage the execution and performance of a team of local sales Account Executives.
  • Negotiate ratings, rates and budgets.
  • Develop new business for station utilizing and maximizing all station platforms including but not limited to broadcast, digital and mobile.
  • Develop working knowledge of Scripps Sales Process (SSP) and coach Account Executives regarding SSP in the field.
  • Utilize SSP, resources and tools provided to build effective sales strategies.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Sales and Sales Managers to train, develop and motivate the local sales team so that revenue goals are achieved.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Sales and Sales Managers to foster career growth and development of the local sales team so that a pipeline of talent for future Scripps sales management openings is ready.
  • Maintain positive working relationships with outside vendors.
  • Interface with traffic systems and personnel to ensure efficient management of airtime inventory.
  • Oversee accounts receivable and credit policies.
  • Develop and implement pricing and packaging to fill needs of both client and station.
  • Know the strengths and weaknesses of the competing stations, other advertising mediums and position the station accordingly.
  • Effectively forecast sales revenue and manage department expenses so that financial goals are achieved.
  • Other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Bachelor's degree in business or related field or equivalent experience preferred
  • Generally, 7+ years proven success in media sales
  • Experience in agency and direct strategic account management, broadcast inventory and digital/video capabilities required
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Demonstrated aptitude for informal leadership and mentoring; fosters open dialogue, empowers others, addresses conflict quickly and directly
  • Strong coaching and feedback skills
  • Strong ability to motivate others toward team goals
  • Able to foster an environment that enables creative and innovative thinking
  • Strong influencing, selling and upselling skills
  • Effective teamwork and collaboration skills
  • Very strong analysis and data interpretation - able to help others translate needs and research data into sound marketing proposals
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills
  • Outstanding presentation abilities (in person/virtual, small/large groups, all levels)
  • Strong time management and organization skills
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and PowerPoint)
  • Working knowledge of Google Office (Sheets, Docs, Slides) and virtual conferencing platforms (E.g. Skype, WebEx, Zoom or MS Teams etc.)
  • Proven ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
  • May require some travel

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Live in the center of adventure. Helena is the capital of Montana and is centrally located near the continental divide and at the halfway point between two of America's premier national parks: Yellowstone and Glacier. The city's history lies in the search for gold in the west. Prospectors descended on Last Chance Gulch in the mid-1800s and struck gold, transforming a small camp into a frontier town. You will find history across the city. Tour the quiet mansion district's leafed streets in the summer, walk the beautiful campus of Carroll College, or stop at the stately Capitol building to visit the summer farmer's market. If you want to stretch your legs a bit, hop on your mountain bike after work and hit one of Mount Helena's many trails. The Mount Helena city park encompasses an entire mountain and is just minutes from the television station and downtown. Helena is surrounded by the Lewis and Clark National Forest. The forest is home to some of the best hunting, fishing and outdoor recreation opportunities in the state. Blue ribbon trout fisheries that include the mighty Missouri River and the Little Blackfoot are less than an hour's drive from downtown. In the winter, there are ample trails for cross-country or downhill skiing at Great Divide, which is famous for being the first Montana ski hill to open and the last to close each season.
