job.title: Sr. Specialist, Programmatic Operations
job.description:
TelevisaUnivision Management Company in Miami, FL seeks a full-time Sr. Specialist, Programmatic Operations to define innovative solutions to complex programmatic business problems. Analyze partner performance and provide recommendations on programmatic advertising revenue improvement while working together with Product Management, Yield, and Sales Teams. Collect and analyze data on customer demographics, preferences, needs, and buying habits to identify potential markets and factors affecting product demand. Conduct research on consumer opinions and marketing strategies, collaborating with marketing professionals, statisticians, pollsters, and other professionals. Translate marketing briefs into programmatic strategies that align with brand goals, target audience segments, and KPIs. Create effective programmatic advertising strategies using automated workflow to effectively deliver ads to target audience. Monitor campaign pacing, budget allocation, and performance metrics, making real-time optimizations to improve results. Work with data to build custom audience segments using DMPs (Data Management Platforms) and CRM data integrations. Leverage analytics platforms to generate performance reports. Support troubleshooting of monetization and campaign delivery issues such as under pacing, reporting, discrepancies, ad architecture, and technical issues. Create innovative programmatic solutions across Audio, Streaming Video (CTV/OTT), display, video, and native. Create external technical and support documentation across all platforms.

 

Master’s degree or equivalent in Marketing, Advertising, or related field plus 1 year of experience in the occupation or as a digital advertising operations specialist or manager. Will also accept a Bachelor’s degree or the equivalent in Marketing, Advertising, or related field plus 5 years of experience in the occupation or as a digital advertising operations specialist or manager. Employer is willing to accept any suitable combination of work experience education, and training.

 

Must have knowledge of programmatic advertising, digital advertising, analytics, and optimization tools. Must have experience creating complex data modeling, predictive targeting, and cross-platform strategy.

 

This is a Telecommuting/Remote position.

 

Apply on-line at TelevisaUnivision’s career page: https://corporate.televisaunivision.com/careers/

The Media Systems Support team at TelevisaUnivision is looking for a Systems Engineer to join our team!

The Systems Engineer is a hands-on Systems Support position responsible for all aspects of the infrastructure support team and the implementation and maintenance of current and future technologies used to support 24x7x365 News, Sports and/or Entertainment Production Environments. In this role, the hired individual will maintain broadcast-related IT Infrastructure systems and help to identify new technologies and tools to support and improve operations. He or she will provide technical assistance for daily operations of mission-critical systems.

 

The Systems Engineer works closely with the Media Systems Support group on all aspects related to their assigned area of responsibility.

 

ABOUT YOU:

You are an innovative individual that enjoys pushing the limits of technology. job.title: Unreal Engine Artist
job.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM:

TelevisaUnivision’s Art & Design department is looking for a highly skilled Unreal Engine Artist / Developer to join our Augmented and Mixed Reality team supporting our Broadcast and Streaming News operations.

This is a creative and highly technical role focused on developing innovative real-time AR, VR, and virtual production solutions for both live and pre-recorded programming. The ideal candidate combines strong Unreal Engine development skills with a sophisticated understanding of design, visual storytelling, spatial composition, and broadcast production.

Reporting to the Sr. Manager of Graphics Technology, you will collaborate closely with artists, designers, producers, directors, and technical teams in a fast-paced, deadline-driven news environment.

You are a collaborative, detail-oriented problem solver with a strong understanding of scale, space, lighting, architecture, and visual realism. You enjoy building immersive environments and real-time graphics while finding creative and technical solutions to complex production challenges.

 

YOUR DAY-DAY: (aka Responsibilities)

  • Collaborate with the Sr. Manager of Graphics Technology and the Art & Design team to support multiple live and pre-recorded news programs.
  • Take ownership of Unreal Engine projects from concept and development through implementation and on-air delivery.
  • Design and develop innovative AR, VR, and real-time graphics solutions for daily programming, breaking news, and special events.
  • Build, integrate, and optimize 3D environments, assets, animations, materials, and real-time graphics for broadcast.
  • Work closely with producers, directors, designers, and other stakeholders to translate creative concepts into technically viable on-air experiences.
  • Follow established brand, editorial, and technical standards while continuously exploring new creative and technological possibilities.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues related to Unreal Engine, real-time rendering, tracking, camera systems, and virtual production workflows.
  • Help develop and improve Unreal Engine workflows, tools, templates, and production pipelines.
  • Optimize projects for performance, stability, and reliability in demanding live broadcast environments.
  • Stay current with emerging Unreal Engine, AR/XR, virtual production, and real-time graphics technologies.

 

 

YOU HAVE: (aka Qualifications)

 

  • Advanced experience with Unreal Engine / Unreal Editor in professional production environments.
  • Strong proficiency with Blueprints, Sequencer, Materials/Shaders, LiveLink, nDisplay, and DMX.
  • Strong programming experience with C++ and Unreal Engine Blueprints, including the ability to write, maintain, debug, and optimize code.
  • Experience developing real-time systems and interactive functionality within Unreal Engine.
  • Understanding of technical areas such as rendering pipelines, physics, AI systems, procedural workflows, and networking/multiplayer concepts.
  • Strong understanding of 3D environments, spatial design, architectural visualization, lighting, animation, materials, and look development.
  • Experience working with live camera tracking, virtual cameras, data capture, and in-camera VFX (ICVFX).
  • Experience creating data-driven visuals and real-time rendered graphics.
  • Proven ability to optimize Unreal Engine projects and pipelines for live broadcast, virtual production, and linear content.
  • Strong understanding of scale, perspective, composition, and spatial relationships when creating virtual environments.
  • Ability to integrate architectural realism and logical spatial design into immersive virtual environments.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical partners, including producers, directors, and production managers.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced production environment.

·         A creative, collaborative, and solution-oriented mindset with a passion for emerging media and technology.

 

OUR BENEFITS:

At TelevisaUnivision, we prioritize the well-being of our team. Our benefits include:

  • Paid time off (PTO)
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Wellness and employee support programs
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Comprehensive health insurance (medical, dental, vision)
  • Life and other insurance coverage options

job.title: Photo Editor - U.K.
job.description:
General Info:

  • The job will be Sunday-Thursday
  • Hours: 40 hours per week
  • Hours approximately:
    • Sunday: 12pm - 8pm GMT
    • Monday - Thursday: 8am - 4pm GMT

Join The Daily Beast as our Photo Editor for the London Bureau. The Daily Beast is a leading digital news site known for its fearless and incisive reporting. We cover breaking news, politics, pop culture, and more with a distinctive voice that engages a dedicated audience.

About the Role:

The Daily Beast’s London bureau is growing and we’re seeking a creative, witty, and enthusiastic photo editor to help curate the aesthetic of the site. The ideal candidate will have a deep understanding of American culture and politics, a background in both journalism and photo-editing/illustrating, have a keen eye for compelling and impactful visuals, and the ability to work quickly and under tight deadlines. The role is essential in ensuring that our visual content is as engaging and impactful as our reporting.

Key Responsibilities:

  • (Photo)Illustrate: Create inventive and witty illustrations – whether using photo collages or original drawing – that capture the story and engage prospective readers

  • Photo Research: Source, edit, and optimize images for daily stories and features across the site

  • Infographics: Design and produce infographics, charts, maps, and timelines that bring dynamism to stories and help readers understand complex topics

  • Rights Management: Obtain and ensure all images used on the site comply with copyright laws and licensing agreements, and secure permissions when necessary

  • Quality Control: Maintain visual consistency and high standards by ensuring all are properly credited, captioned, and formatted

  • Collaboration: Work closely with other members of the visuals department as well as editors, reporters, and the social media team to develop creative ways to tell stories

Qualifications:

  • Minimum 4 years experience in photo editing in a digital media environment

  • Expertise in Adobe Photoshop, with a proficiency in other Adobe Creative Cloud and supplemental photo-editing software

  • Strong visual literacy and an eye for detail, composition, and color

  • Ability to work under tight deadlines and to manage multiple projects simultaneously

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and ability to work collaboratively both in-office and remote

  • Familiarity with current events, pop culture, news media, and American and global politics

  • Understanding of journalistic ethics and standards

Why Join Us?

  • Be a part of a respected and influential news organization

  • Engage with a dedicated audience passionate about political news

  • Enjoy a collaborative and fast-paced work environment

  • Opportunities for career growth and development

Pay Range Salary

The pay range for this position is $50,000 USD to $60,000 USD, which is approximately £37,000 to £45,000.

Start date: January 4, 2027.

We are recruiting one full-time Photo Editor, Sunday—Thursday, however, some flexibility may be required.

This is a permanent role in a contractor position. You must be based outside of the U.S. to apply. The role is work from home but may change as the Beast expands operations. You do not have to be based in London for the role. Finalists will be required to undertake an edit test. Please submit examples of published work in your application.

Additional Information

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Don’t meet every single requirement listed here? We are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace, so if you’re interested in joining the Beast but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with this job description, we encourage you to give it a shot all the same.

job.title: Account Executive
job.description:
Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism, and holds power to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial professionals, and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We offer a challenging and exciting environment for career development, with a focus on training, growth and fostering an inclusive culture.

We’re looking for an Account Executive to join our award winning advertising team.

Account Executives provide sales support to our advertising team, across all advertising products (print, digital and podcast), to enable them to spend more time with customers.  As you will have the opportunity to support the team across the entire sales process, this is the perfect opportunity to learn the foundations of how to sell, from how to prepare material for pitches to writing and presenting campaign management reports. 

About the role

  • Administration of various processes related to the sales teams activities
  • Coordinating briefing meetings and advertising bookings
  • Researching the media marketplace reading trade press and relevant business press to increase your understanding
  • Analysing market data to provide competitive insight to arm the sales team with a view on the market 
  • Reporting, produce a monthly analysis with insight and commentary showing what our competitors are doing well and where there are opportunities for us
  • Identifying leads and sharing with the sales team insight into where our customers are advertising across competitor titles
  • Presenting pitches and Post Campaign Analysis to smaller clients with support from the Sales Support Lead. 

 

About You

  • Enjoys learning new skills and working in a fast paced environment
  • Interested in advertising and the media industry and keen to learn more
  • Loves working in an environment that is values driven and customer focused
  • Strong administrative skills and attention to detail
  • Able to multitask and work to tight deadlines, often with short lead times
  • Adaptability and flexibility
  • Good numerical skills and comfortable working with data
  • Responsible, accountable, acts with integrity
  • Proactive, able to work on own initiative whilst being a strong team player

 

The starting salary for this role is £30,000 per annum.

We value and respect all differences (seen and unseen) in all people at the Guardian. We aspire to have inclusive working experiences and an environment that reflects the audience we serve, where our people have equal access to career development opportunities, their voices are heard and can contribute to our future. We actively encourage applications from BAME candidates and those from other groups traditionally underrepresented in the UK media. At the Guardian, many of our staff work flexibly and we will consider all requests for flexible working arrangements.

How to Apply

Please upload a copy of your latest CV. 

The closing date for applications is 6pm, Thursday 5th November 2025.

All roles at the Guardian are open for everybody to apply. It is important to us that you feel supported and comfortable throughout your recruitment process, in order to perform your best. Please let us know if there are any changes we could make to help your application, this includes providing documents in accessible formats or personalising the process to better support your needs. Please contact Karen on karen.walter@theguardian.com to discuss further so we can work with you to support you through your application.

 

Benefits at the Guardian

You'll have 30 days of annual leave per year (plus bank holidays) with the option to purchase an additional 5 days. Our pension scheme is generous; if you contribute 5% then we will contribute 8-12% (depending on your age). We believe in giving back, which is why employees are given 2 volunteering days annually and the option of payroll giving. Season ticket loans are also available.

You are entitled to private healthcare, life cover, income protection, and eye tests. You can also opt in to dental insurance.

We have enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave policies in place. We also support our employees by offering an IVF, menopause, baby loss, and trans equality policy.

Culture and Wellbeing

We want everyone to feel like they belong at the Guardian and we champion diversity of thought. Our various employee forums provide a platform to use their voice to foster an inclusive workplace. We became the first major media organisation to achieve B Corp status.

We offer tools to help you prioritise your wellbeing including access to our employee benefits platform which provides tailored support for health and wellbeing. In addition, we also offer free yoga and Pilates classes. These run alongside our corporate gym membership and cycle to work scheme.

Our canteen has views overlooking the Regents Canal and caters for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

Learning and Development

We encourage personal and professional growth. Employees have access to a broad range of tools and solutions, and we are happy to support the pursuit of professional qualifications through vocational courses and apprenticeships.

job.title: Arts and Culture Correspondent
job.description:
Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism and holds power to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial professionals and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. You’ll generate exclusives, break major stories, identify the trends everyone will be talking about, and produce ambitious features spanning the full breadth of arts and culture. From interviewing the artists shaping the moment to investigating the forces transforming the creative industries, you’ll deliver original journalism that informs, surprises and sets the agenda.

job.title: Assistant Europe Editor
job.description:
Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism, and holds power to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial professionals, and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We offer a challenging and exciting environment for career development, with a focus on training, growth and fostering an inclusive culture.

 

We are looking for an assistant Europe editor to plan, commission and edit for Guardian Europe. 

 

Our Europe coverage delivers fearless, incisive journalism that connects European politics, economics, culture, and ideas to an engaged global readership. 

 

This is a permanent NUJ contract.

 

About the role

  • Generate opinion pieces, columns, first-person essays and other forms of original journalism from and about Europe to engage the global audience 
  • Identify great Europe-based thinkers and writers and find exciting new voices 
  • Work closely with both established Europe columnists and new contributors, usually writing in English as a second language, to shape copy and test arguments
  • Edit to ensure pieces are factual, relevant, lively and engaging; liaising with the legal department on accuracy and with production editors through to publication

job.title: News producer
job.description:
Guardian Australia is part of Guardian News & Media (GNM), publisher of theguardian.com. As a leading global media organisation, we are renowned for our pioneering independent journalism and our award-winning digital products.

 

We are seeking for a news producer to be responsible for a full range of production tasks for Guardian Australia, including subediting and publishing stories, displaying them on the website and disseminating through social media.

 

This role is being offered on a full-time 12 month contract, working on a seven-day roster with early starts or late finishes, including one weekend day each week. This role is open to candidates in both 
Sydney and Melbourne.

 

In this role you will…

 

  • Edit copy for online content including articles, blogs, videos, galleries, interactives, podcasts and social media posts, correcting grammar and spelling, consistent with Guardian style
  • Ensure accuracy of what we publish
  • Write page furniture, assign tags
  • Add pictures and multimedia elements 
  • Write engaging and SEO-friendly web headlines
  • Add internal and external web links and cross-references
  • Create and/or edit picture galleries, polls and quizzes, video and audio pages
  • Display stories on the Guardian Australia website effectively and imaginatively 
  • Work on social media promotion of stories as required
  • Cover for the deputy production editor/production editor and news desk editors as required
  • Retrieve wire stories and use them to create articles
  • Liaise with reporters on story progress and to resolve any issues with filed stories
  • Liaise with lawyers, as needed, to resolve any outstanding issues before publication
     

You’ll bring….

 

Knowledge and experience

  • Subbing and production experience – ideally both online and print
  • Expertise in using web tools for editing and layout
  • Interest in and wide knowledge of the output of Guardian Australia
  • Demonstrable enthusiasm for and interest in web and print journalism
  • Understanding the editorial aims and values of the Guardian
  • Awareness of the needs and interests of the Guardian’s readers/audiences
  • Appreciation of Guardian history 
     

Skills and behaviours

  • Excellent writing and communication skills
  • Excellent production skills
  • Meticulous eye for detail, grammar and spelling
  • Ability to handle writers’ copy sensitively
  • Ability to learn and apply new skills quickly and thoroughly
  • Willingness to take responsibility for editing decisions, in collaboration with the news desk
  • Excellent planning and organisational skills 
  • Ability to edit copy quickly and accurately under pressure
  • Flair for writing headlines and other page furniture
  • Team player, enthusiastic with strong interpersonal skills
  • Logical, imaginative, adaptable and flexible
  • Ability to accept constructive criticism
  • A passion for independent journalism and an understanding of our editorial code and values


About working at Guardian Australia… 
 

  • Hybrid working 
  • Employee assistance program (EAP) to support employee wellbeing
  • Paid volunteer leave
  • Dedicated diversity and inclusion employee groups, action plans (including our Reconciliation Action Plan) and cultural competency training
  • Guardian digital subscription
     

For more information please view the full job description here.

 

This role is being offered on a full-time 12 month contract, working on a seven-day roster with early starts or late finishes, including one weekend day each week. This role is open to candidates in both 
Sydney and Melbourne.

 

To apply for this position, please apply online and upload your résumé (maximum three pages) plus covering letter. In your covering letter please outline your motivation for applying for the role and why you think you are suitable.

 

Closing date for applications: 3 November 2026

 

If you have application questions or if you require an adjustment to be made during the recruitment process, please email australia.hr@theguardian.com

 

GNM Australia Limited (Guardian Australia) is proud to be a fair and ethical employer. Australian editorial minimum rates of pay by band and grade are outlined in the Journalists (GNM Australia Pty Ltd) Enterprise Agreement 2024 for roles that fall under its coverage. 

 

We believe that our role in the Australian media is to give a voice to the most marginalised people in society and value and respect all differences in all people — including people of colour, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people from different social classes, people with diverse gender and sexual identities, and people with disabilities (seen and unseen). We believe that these communities must be centred in the work we do, bringing a new perspective and a diversity of thought. We also encourage flexible working and aim to create a work environment where all employees feel respected.

job.title: Temp-to-Perm Finance Analyst
job.description:
About the Guardian

The Guardian is a global news organization that delivers fearless, independent journalism. From breaking news and award-winning investigations to in-depth coverage of technology, sports, film, culture, and lifestyle, the Guardian offers a global view that deepens our audiences' understanding of America and the world.

Headquartered in New York City, Guardian US is an entirely digital operation that seeks to engage US readers by combining the Guardian's international coverage with US voices and expertise. Core coverage areas include US politics, technology, the climate emergency, economic and racial inequality, health, sports, culture, and more. Guardian US launched in 2011 and has bureaus in New York, Washington DC, New Orleans, and Los Angeles. The Guardian is an independently owned, mission-driven organization funded by readers around the globe.

It's the talent, energy, and commitment our people bring to The Guardian that makes us who we are. Across our business, we have some of the most creative thinkers in media and beyond, award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial teams, digital talent, and more.

About the role

We are seeking a highly analytical and detail-oriented Temp-to-Perm Finance Analyst to support the Finance function through financial reporting, planning, analysis, and business partnership. This role will play a key part in delivering accurate and timely P&L reporting, financial analysis, ad hoc reporting, and management insights, while partnering closely with teams across the organization.

 

The ideal candidate is highly proficient in Hyperion, Microsoft Excel, and Google Workspace, with strong financial acumen and the ability to translate financial data into meaningful insights. This individual will be comfortable working independently, managing multiple priorities, and collaborating cross-functionally to support business objectives and improve financial performance.

 

Department: Finance
Reports to: Interim Head of Finance, US
Location: New York, New York

Hybrid/Remote/In-Person: Hybrid, 3 days 
Terms and conditions: Full-time, Temp to Perm (Temporary duration: 6 months)

Annual Salary: $110-120k

 

Key responsibilities

Financial Reporting & P&L Management

  • Own and support monthly P&L reporting, including preparation, analysis, variance explanations, and identification of key business drivers.
  • Prepare recurring and ad hoc financial reports and analyses for Finance leadership and cross-functional business partners.
  • Support the preparation of presentations and financial insights for Finance leadership and business stakeholders.

Financial Analysis & Strategic Planning

  • Analyze actual results against budget, forecast, and prior periods, identifying trends, risks, opportunities, and actionable insights.
  • Investigate variances and financial trends, working with relevant stakeholders to understand root causes and communicate findings.
  • Support the broader Finance function across forecasting, budgeting, reporting, planning, and other strategic and operational initiatives.
  • Assist with special projects and other ad hoc analyses as needed to support evolving business and Finance priorities.

Systems, Modeling & Process Improvement

  • Leverage Hyperion to support financial reporting, data analysis, forecasting, budgeting, and financial planning processes.
  • Develop and maintain sophisticated Excel-based financial models, reporting tools, and analyses to support decision-making.
  • Utilize Google Workspace, including Google Sheets, and Google Slides, to facilitate reporting, analysis, presentations, and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Develop and improve reporting processes, templates, and analytical tools to increase efficiency, accuracy, and visibility into financial performance.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Collaboration

  • Partner with other Finance team members to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of financial reporting.
  • Collaborate closely with cross-functional stakeholders to understand business performance, gather financial inputs, resolve discrepancies, and provide financial guidance.
  • Serve as a trusted financial partner to cross-functional teams, helping stakeholders understand financial results and make informed business decisions.

 

About you

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of relevant financial analysis or FP&A experience.
  • Strong experience with P&L reporting, financial analysis, budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including complex formulas, financial modeling, data analysis, and reporting.
  • Hands-on experience with Hyperion or a comparable enterprise financial planning and reporting system.
  • Strong proficiency with Google Workspace, particularly Google Sheets, Slides, and Drive.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and deliver both recurring and ad hoc financial reporting.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Ability to communicate financial information clearly to both Finance and non-Finance stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and business partnering skills.

 

How to apply

We know there are great candidates who might not check all these boxes or who possess important skills we haven’t thought of. If that’s you, we encourage you to apply and tell us about yourself.

All candidates interested in applying should upload a resume and cover letter.  

 

All roles at the Guardian are open for everybody to apply. It is important to us that you feel supported and comfortable throughout your recruitment process, in order to perform your best. Please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it easier and more comfortable for you. Please email the recruiter listed on the job posting or at recruitment.us@theguardian.com to discuss further so we can work with you to support you through your application.

 

Compensation and benefits

  • 20 days of vacation leave in addition to 12 company holidays and 2 personal days
  • Unlimited sick time
  • Employee Assistance Programs
  • 401(k) Match
  • Subsidized healthcare coverage including medical, vision, and dental
  • Medical and Dependent Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Generous parental leave with 100% pay
  • Long Term and Short Term Disability insurance 
  • Life insurance 
  • Commuter benefits 
  • Wellhub
  • Work/Life balance: Flexible hybrid schedule 

 

Culture & wellbeing

We want everyone to feel like they belong at the Guardian and we champion diversity of thought. You will also have the opportunity to hear unique insight from our journalists in our morning conference, a live discussion on the news story of the day. 

We offer great tools to help you prioritize your wellbeing including access to Employee Assistance Programs. 

Learning & development

We encourage personal and professional growth. Employees have access to a broad range of tools and solutions, and we are happy to support the pursuit of professional qualifications through vocational courses and apprenticeships.

Sustainability

Our goal is to become an environmentally regenerative company and we have signed up to a sustainability vision and strategy to reach it. Find more information about sustainability at GNM here.

***

The Guardian is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, color, national origin, ethnic origin, citizenship status, disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law in its employment policies. In addition, the Guardian will provide reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities.

 

We value and respect all differences (seen and unseen) in all people at the Guardian. We aspire to have inclusive working experiences and an environment that reflects the audience we serve, where our people have equal access to career development opportunities, their voices are heard and can contribute to our future.

job.title: Ad Solutions Producer
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Job Description

The New York Times' Advertising team is looking for an Ads Solutions Producer. You are eager to join this great team of experts critical to NYT's success at creating and QA’ing compelling responsive ad units for our advertising clients. As an Ads Solutions Producer, you will oversee the daily coordination, management, production and deployment of all custom creative HTML5 display ads.

In addition to the production of display ads, you will help oversee the production of the audio advertising spots. Podcasts are a fast-growing and important part of NYT's product offering and the Ad Solutions team plays a necessary role in moving this business forward. 

This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Senior Manager, Ad Solutions. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

About the Role

As an Ad Solutions Producer, you will build and launch our premium advertising products using custom templates in Google Ad Manager. In this role, you will collaborate closely with Advertising Operations, Sales, Creative Technology, Ad Acceptability, Ad Mission, and external vendors, while liaising directly with high-profile clients. We are looking for a strong communicator who can translate complex technical concepts for non-technical partners and stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage all daily production responsibilities and with high client satisfaction including but not limited to, leading kick off calls with advertising clients and our Sales team, communicating creative specifications, managing timelines, and coordinating production with Campaign Management to meet deployment of campaigns and flight starts.
  • Use CSS to build NYT proprietary responsive within HTML templates
  • Follow rich media best practices and production processes as established by Ad Solutions Manager
  • Play a critical role to enforce and refine processes with Sales Planning, Campaign Management, Sales, and external clients
  • Be the internal and external promoter for your product offering, occasionally work with the sales channel and important customers
  • Coordinate with Campaign Management team for podcast script collection, and engage voice actors for tailored recordings on time and within budget
  • Manage the vendor mixing process of raw recordings for final QA
  • Be the escalation point for live advertising-related issues. Use a tracking system for live site issues and use the issues log to assess vendor partnerships and QA process
  • Work with our established custom unit vendor partners to improve ad production, shepherding best practices for working with those vendors from pre­ to post­-sale teams
  • Work with CreativeTech by documenting and communicating critical production challenges and client custom requests to establish the best technical requirements, release date/schedules, and refine technical product documentation
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • BA/BS or equivalent experience
  • 3+ years of experience working as a producer or related account management working in Rich Media and Creative Solutions, Ad Operations, or related area
  • Knowledge of Web technologies such as HTML, JavaScript, XML, and cookies
  • We ask that you have experience with HTML, CSS, experience using programs such as Adobe Creative Suite, and project management tools like Monday.com and Jira

Preferred Qualifications:

  • You have experience with digital advertising and web design technologies
  • You are comfortable coordinating between technical and non-technical groups
  • You are comfortable handling client kickoff meetings regarding production
  • You are a proactive communicator, able to independently manage and follow up on multiple concurrent tasks
  • An understanding of the evolving media landscape, specifically around advertising
  • Familiarity with The New York Times brand and sub-brands

The New York Times' Advertising team is looking for an Analyst, Measurements and Insights who is experienced in analysis of campaign performance data and campaign stories for clients advertising. You will support the Measurement team within The New York Times Advertising. You will turn campaign results into applicable findings for clients by using first- and third-party campaign metrics. You will help identify opportunities, bring the strategy and ongoing output of insights, innovate processes, methodologies, and reporting, directly affecting future business.
This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Manager, Insights and Analytics. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

About the Role:

You will evolve how we measure media and creative across a portfolio of diverse clients. This collaborative and strategic role will work with top tier advertising clients. You will also work with multiple teams, including Sales, Sales Planning, Ad Product, Audience Insights, Product Marketing, and Strategy teams. This collaboration ensures success with strengthening partnerships with marketers and increasing ad revenue.

Responsibilities:

  • Build holistic narratives from large, integrated data sets using data visualization and analytics platforms
  • Work with 3rd party vendors in the setup and delivery of campaign effectiveness reports, such as Brand Lift Studies, Attribution and Sales Lift.
  • Develop expertise in the full suite of NYT research capabilities and measurement products that deliver main performance metrics across the full marketing funnel, to current and potential clients.
  • Collaborate with Strategy to ensure initial campaign goals and client's desired outcomes are incorporated into all post-campaign outputs.
  • Identify and recommend ad products to advertiser goals and KPIs based on relevant performance data.
  • Be a subject matter expert and provide a high level of service when coordinating and communicating in-depth reporting to clients.

  • Socialize industry-level measurement findings across all partners
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • Bachelor's degree in statistics, engineering, economics, or related subject
  • 3-5 years of insights / analyst experience at a publisher or media/research agency managing advertiser-facing products including ad performance tracking, marketing or digital analytics
  • Understanding of ad operations, digital buying and trafficking, and the digital media landscape required.

  • Experience diplomatically navigating complex team member relationships

job.title: Analyst, Technical Trainer
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The New York Times is looking for an analyst who is passionate about promoting security and technology awareness across our newsroom, engineering, and business departments. You will help design technical training and communications throughout the organization, striving to cultivate a company-wide security culture where all employees share responsibility for safeguarding and protecting us.

Based in New York City, this hybrid role involves regular in-person office visits to host group training sessions and individual meetings with staff.

Who are we?

Enterprise Technology enables the people, platforms, and practices that support The New York Times' journalism and business operations. We partner with departments across the company to help employees work securely,, and productively through thoughtful technology solutions. We support the systems and capabilities that keep us running while looking for new ways to reduce friction and improve the daily experience of our workforce.

The Education team's mission is to help our technical and non-technical workforce adopt secure, technology practices through data-driven insights, training, and specialized programming that inspire meaningful behavior change.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Partner with staff throughout the company to lead personal and group security and technology education sessions.
  • Coordinate and lead workshops, events, and training projects focused on information security and IT topics and initiatives.
  • Deliver high-touch technical support and 1:1 briefings for all staff, including the newsroom, providing hands-on guidance on digital hygiene, device hardening, and secure communication workflows.
  • Craft and distribute routine security updates for specific teams or the entire organization in collaboration with corporate communications.
  • Produce instructional resources, including user guides, manuals, video content, and online modules.
  • Support user requests and participate in an on-call rotation to address urgent security inquiries.
  • Design and implement internal phishing simulation campaigns and remediation programs.
  • Manage the logistical and administrative tasks required to schedule and track training projects.
  • Report on security engagement metrics from direct interactions, identifying trends to help refine support strategies and harden newsroom defenses.
  • Visit several bureaus and office sites to deliver training; expected travel is approximately 10% annually.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Manager, Information Security

Basic Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience training on topics related to information security (phishing, account security, data security, secure communications) in person and virtually
  • Familiarity with basic cybersecurity concepts, including social engineering, common tactics, techniques, and procedures.
  • Experience helping people build and understand threat models for themselves and their function or role within an organization.
  • Experience with breaking down complex topics to different audiences, including technical and non-technical partners.
  • Comfortable with public speaking and adjusting content based on audience response.
  • understanding of the audience to produce engaging materials in multiple formats and media, user guides, and gamification elements.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with phishing platforms.
  • Experience with Zendesk or working in a support environment.
  • Experience with learning, creating, and integrating new digital technology such as audio, video, social media, and other web-based technologies.
  • Experience working with journalists or other high-risk groups.
  • Experience working with leadership and management.
  • Knowledge of networking basics, including VPNs, travel routers, and secure Wi-Fi configurations.
  • Interest in or experience with specialized security hardware (e.g., YubiKeys, encrypted storage).
  • Basic data analytics skills.

Job Description

The New York Times Advertising is hiring for an Art Director to join our T Brand Studio. As an Art Director, you will lead the visual execution of assigned projects. Art Directors do the following: they imagine ways to tell stories visually. They present visual ideas and recommendations internally and to our clients. They find visual reference, specifically relevant to each idea, project, and opportunity. They contribute to and oversee the creation of great mood boards, inspired type treatments, exceptional color palettes, and page layouts.

About the Role

You will oversee the design of presentations which enhance our work, the assembly of excellent paid posts in webflow, the design of impactful print ads, and work with developers internal and external on complex custom projects. You will mentor Designers and Senior Designers, and collaborate with external partners, building relationships and guiding them through insightful feedback to create their best work. This is a hybrid role, reporting to the Director, Design. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Contribute to and oversee excellent design work on client and internal projects, with guidance from Design Directors, and Creative Directors.
  • Translate conceptual and strategic ideas into impactful visual solutions.
  • Contribute creative concepts to client and internal projects, brainstorming with other teams.
  • Design iteratively with an easy command of typography, composition, messaging hierarchy, layout, and other fundamental principles of graphic design, and give pointed feedback to designers which directly improves their work.
  • Research and oversee selection of visual reference that inspires (Design, Page Animation, Illustration, and Photography), and build a mental reference library of styles, approaches, creators, and projects.
  • Manage Designers, delegate work to resourced Designers and Senior Designers based on workload, capabilities, and experience. Contribute to the professional growth of direct reports through mentorship, and feedback.
  • Select, brief, and direct outside collaborators to create their best work.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of professional work experience in the art industry
  • 5+ years of experience with Adobe Creative Cloud (InDesign, Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma) and modern digital publishing platforms such as Webflow.
  • An experienced creative portfolio demonstrating mastery of design principles - specifically typography, grid systems, layout hierarchy, color theory, and art direction for both digital and print media
  • Experienced managing designers including delegating tasks, giving constructive feedback, and overseeing visual quality.
  • Experience commissioning and directing external creative partners including photographers, illustrators, animators and external development teams
  • Experience presenting visual strategies and creative direction to executive-level clients and company partners.
  • Visual research skills, with a rich, active mental library of contemporary and historical art, design, photography, and interactive digital trends.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Working knowledge of front-end web technologies (HTML/CSS) and an understanding of dynamic layout capabilities, responsive design, and digital motion/animation principles.
  • Experience in luxury, editorial, or prestige brand storytelling, with a deep appreciation for high-end aesthetic stewardship and cultural context.
  • Experience prioritizing competing programs, responsibilities, and projects

About the Role:

The New York Times is looking for a creative and collaborative Art Director to join our award-winning Opinion Design team. Partnering closely with Opinion Print Editors, you will reimagine our daily pages to establish a distinct visual identity separate from the newsroom. You will demonstrate your talent to organize complex information and create engaging designs. As a story-first editorial partner, you will combine sophisticated typography, photography, data visualization, and commissioned artwork, or create real-time illustration when needed, to push the boundaries of print layouts. You are passionate about print and interested in generating innovative ways to present and adapt digital-first content. You will bring advanced editorial design experience, strong project management skills to support daily deadline pressure, a deep passion for journalism, and a portfolio demonstrating versatile, high-impact narrative storytelling.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceptualize and execute design solutions from initial concept through publication across print and digital platforms
  • Partner with editors, photo editors, and key stakeholders to align visual vision, define story approach, and translate complex interactive/video journalism into print formats
  • Commission and art direct illustrations, growing a deep network of creative talent to elevate storytelling
  • Push layout boundaries through sophisticated art placement, structure, and illustration integration
  • Craft display copy and edit text independently to improve layout flow
  • Manage full project lifecycles within proprietary publishing systems, meeting tight daily deadlines in a fast-paced constantly evolving news environment
  • Provide flexible coverage for the Sunday section when schedules require
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Design Director, Opinion.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of print and digital design experience leading editorial projects, product launches, and redesigns alongside senior leadership
  • Proven art direction and visual editing skills, including commissioning talent, curating photo assets, and illustrating directly under tight timelines
  • Mastery of design tools (Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, pagination software) and pre-press production, including color correction and print-ready prep

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong communicator capable of managing a high-intensity, news-driven schedule, including nights and weekends
  • Experience in a newsroom or media environment with a strong visual judgment of illustration and photography trends
  • Passion for off-platform visual storytelling and strong knowledge of domestic and international competitors
  • Experience optimizing design workflows to support editorial deadlines and team efficiency managing multiple stakeholder feedback

job.description:

And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

 

 

The Data Journalism team is looking for an experienced journalist with editing, management and data analysis skills to serve as an assistant editor. You'll help to run a group of data journalists who collaborate across the newsroom. You'll also advise on analyses conducted elsewhere in the newsroom.

You should be obsessed with detail and rigor, display a knack for lifting stories to the next level and care deeply about developing your colleagues' talents. Collaboration is at the heart of this role; the Data Journalism team works with virtually every other desk in the newsroom. We'll expect you to deftly navigate these partnerships, which require crisp communication, a problem-solving attitude and a dash of diplomacy.

This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days a week. We have a preference for candidates who will work in New York City, with a secondary preference for Washington, DC.

Important application requirement: Please submit a cover letter that describes your qualifications in the context of three stories (or projects) you helped to shape. For each, please provide a link to the work and describe your contributions in one to three paragraphs. Your cover letter should not exceed four pages in total. Within that limit, you are also welcome to provide a more traditional (but brief) description of your career and talents.

Responsibilities:

  • Help to lead the Data Journalism team

  • Directly supervise several data reporters on the team

  • Shepherd, shape and stress-test the team's data analyses

  • Consult on data analyses conducted by reporters outside the Data Journalism team

  • Be comfortable working on an unpredictable mix of short, medium and long deadlines

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Data Editor, who is based in New York City.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of data journalism experience

  • Proficiency working with data in Python and/or R, spreadsheets and relational databases

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of leadership, editing and/or mentorship experience

  • Experience leading a data journalism team

  • Experience with, and a preference for, working collaboratively on multidisciplinary teams

  • Experience data-editing in response to major news cycles

  • Comfort with command-line tooling, version control, working with large language models and other key technical skills

job.title: Assistant Editor, Fine Arts
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times Culture desk covers the arts and culture to help people understand the world. Through our reporting, criticism and service journalism, we provide trusted guidance to help people live fuller, more considered lives.

We are seeking an Assistant Editor, Fine Arts to help shape and elevate our coverage of visual art, architecture and design; museums and other art institutions; and auctions, with an eye toward ambitious, distinctive journalism that reaches a broad, curious audience. You should have expertise that will produce stories that lead readers into the boardrooms and the studios of today's cultural influencers and will also develop stories about the intersection of art and new media, including artificial intelligence.

You will work closely with the art discipline editor, critics and reporters to determine coverage, assign, edit and second edit news, features, reviews and visual story forms.

You'll also manage a critic and assign and oversee the work of freelancers. You should have a deep understanding of fine arts and art institutions, strong editing skills across formats and platforms and a track record of guiding world-class journalism.

This is a hybrid position, based in New York City, and includes regular attendance in the office at least four days each week.

Responsibilities:

  • Help identify and prioritize key fine-arts storylines, from breaking news to longer-term investigations, profiles and criticism that illuminate how the arts intersect with politics, power and the broader culture
  • Assign, shape and edit daily art stories, including news, features, criticism, service pieces, visual pieces and enterprise projects
  • Assign and edit news of institutions, including museums, art galleries, auction houses and non-profits, throughout the U.S. and Europe
  • Respond to news events in the art world by assigning and editing timely stories, explainers and off-the-news pieces that give readers essential context and insight
  • Plan and assign advance obituary coverage of notables in art
  • Coordinate with our European cultural editor on coverage of major events including biennales and museum openings
  • Manage and direct the work of at least one critic
  • Assign, schedule and edit freelance reviews for Weekend Arts, including the weekly Galleries section
  • Identify and shape features and profiles for the weekly Arts & Leisure page
  • Collaborate with photo, design, visual and video editors on stories across a variety of formats
  • Help foster a collaborative, inclusive culture on the desk, modeling clear communication, constructive feedback and high editorial standards
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Art Editor

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7–10 years of editing experience, ideally as an editor in a newsroom
  • Knowledge of and curiosity about visual art
  • A track record of editing a variety of story forms and formats
  • Ability to meet deadlines, juggle multiple stories at once and make sound editorial decisions under pressure
  • Excellent communication and organizational skills, including the ability to manage complex workflows and coordinate across multiple teams

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supervising or mentoring journalists, including guiding reporters from pitch through publication
  • Experience working closely with visual, audio and video teams on digital storytelling, and a willingness to experiment with new formats
  • Familiarity with Times style, standards and journalistic independence, and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • A demonstrated ability to collaborate across desks and disciplines, building strong working relationships in a large, complex newsroom
  • A passion for expanding the audience for arts coverage and making our journalism accessible, surprising and indispensable to a global readership

job.title: Assistant Editor, Visuals
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

We’re looking for a senior editor to lead our visual journalism across Asia, driving the execution of new forms of storytelling and overseeing a team of graphics and multimedia journalists. This role is based in the Times’ Seoul newsroom. 

Visual journalists at The Times have investigated how China built a great wall of villages along its frontier and strong-armed its way into dominating the South China Sea, documented the Myanmar military’s campaign of terror against its own people and Taliban rule in Afghanistan, and reconstructed South Korean president’s botched martial law bid. They have revealed how drones have transformed the war in Ukraine. They have also devised ambitious multimedia approaches to explain the far-reaching impact of the Iran war, air pollution in India and American households’ reliance on Chinese goods.

We want to do more of these kinds of stories. And we want to continue to transform how we work to bring visual reporting and editing into the core of how we show readers the world and hold power accountable. We will do this through compelling graphical explanations; urgent, immersive field reporting in photography and video; sharp visual news coverage; and investigations driven by deep reporting on imagery and data.

This role reports to the assistant international editor for visuals in New York and collaborates with the Asia editor to help drive coverage of Asia. You will work closely with the lead video producer and photo editor in Seoul, the senior editor for visuals in London, and counterparts in photo, video, graphics and news design.

This is an in-office position based in Seoul,  and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Main responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with international editors to drive visual coverage of Asia. 
  • Coordinate, lead and edit the work of correspondents and visual journalists on visual stories.
  • Serve as the leader of a small group of graphics/multimedia reporters focused on Asia, helping to create, design and edit multimedia coverage. 
  • In collaboration with the deputy International editor for visuals, plan and execute stories that use data analysis and visualization, photography, imagery analysis, open source investigation and other reporting techniques.
  • Work with desk leaders to shape and execute our broader editorial strategy for visual journalism, including how we should work with partners in photo, video, graphics and news design.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the assistant international editor for visuals.

Basic qualifications:

  • Strong news judgment.
  • Ability to identify and conceive ambitious stories, spot visual opportunities in reporting and develop them into a range of compelling visual forms.
  • Skill pulling multiple visual disciplines together into multimedia projects, with an emphasis on visualization, explanatory visuals, digital design, use of video and other visual forms. 
  • A record of clear communication and strong collaboration with colleagues.
  • The ability to write clearly, work on tight deadlines and edit to sharpen the relationship between visuals and copy.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams to create ambitious multimedia news stories, including interactive visuals, and help them develop as journalists. . 
  • Strong portfolio in one or more of these areas: data visualization, mapping, explanatory writing, news illustration, digital design, interactive development and explanatory multimedia or video.

In order to be considered for this role, please submit the link to your portfolio/clips.

job.title: Assistant White House Editor
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Assistant White House Editor will play a central role in shaping the Washington Bureau report, supporting the White House editor and collaborating with other teams as news requires. This editor will manage reporters, help launch and edit news and enterprise stories focused on the President, and will help coordinate coverage across platforms. Operating in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment, this editor will help monitor ongoing developments on multiple fronts, and assist the White House editor in planning, making assignments, editing stories and thinking creatively about how to advance our report to serve our audiences.

The Assistant White House Editor also collaborates with other newsroom departments and stakeholders, monitoring daily and weekly priorities, helping to manage daily story planning and budgeting, getting reporters launched on stories and doing first or second-editing. This editor will manage the team when the White House editor is absent and shares responsibility for managing coverage of events on nights and weekends.

At a time when the news priorities can shift rapidly, this editor will sometimes be deployed to jump on other developments, work with other teams and support live coverage.

This editor should be able to move quickly across storylines without sacrificing accuracy and tone. Experience managing reporters or other editors is essential, as is a demonstrated ability to make thoughtful news judgements under pressure. Experience with White House coverage is a plus.

This position is based in Washington, D.C. and may include night and weekend coverage. It includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

You will report to the White House editor.

Responsibilities:

  • You will serve as a deputy first editor for the White House team, stepping in to support the White House editor. You will assign and cover first edits for breaking, live news and some enterprise stories, ensuring continuity of coverage and clear direction for reporters across beats.
  • You will handle edits of all sorts, including quick cuts, write-throughs, live stories, dailies and lead-alls as needed.
  • You will help set up weekend and off‑peak Washington coverage for these teams, including assigning, editing and coordinating with the News Director, editors managing live and breaking news stories as well as staff editors on key stories and providing additional support for stories that move or break at night, on weekends or holidays.
  • You will be nimble and flexible about being directed to other news developments and coverage teams as necessary and to work across platforms.
  • You will support live and alternative formats, helping decide when developments should go into live files versus traditional stories, and partnering with other news editors as needed.
  • You will be organized and work in close partnership with other editors on the bureau to build out the day's budget and update the week's budget, anticipating news needs and planning future coverage.
  • You will be skilled at anticipating potential problems, addressing unexpected issues and finding solutions.
  • You will help identify potential stories, including non-traditional story formats, visual stories, service and explanatory pieces.
  • You will coordinate with editors and the audience team on story publication and promotion plans and foster group headline brainstorming and promotion planning.
  • You will work in close partnership with the Weekend Editor on planning handoffs at the start and mid-points of the week so we have clarity and continuity in our storylines and with other editors on the team to help identify potential stories, assign and edit the daily report.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years' experience at a journalism or media company or other relevant organization
  • Editing skills that demonstrate mastery of journalistic style and standards, including ethical standards.
  • Proven news judgment.
  • Previous experience managing and editing reporters.
  • Previous experience juggling multiple storylines with rigor and judgment.
  • Experience with coverage of some combination of government, policy and politics.
  • Openness to and comfort with new story forms, live coverage and adopting new ways of working as the newsroom's needs evolve.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • People management experience
  • A willingness to be nimble and flexible in anticipating potential problems, addressing unexpected issues and finding solutions.
  • A strong understanding of Times style and standards
  • A willingness to collaborate and the ability to partner with colleagues across The New York Times newsroom.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive coverage across multiple topics.

Additional Compensation and Benefits:

For roles in the U.S., dependent on your role, you may be eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. Benefits may include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs.

job.title: Associate Creative Director, Earned Marketing (Temporary)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. In service of that mission, we have a journalism operation that includes thousands of people reporting on the ground from most countries around the world, producing journalism with the independence, accuracy, depth and authority for which The Times is famous.

Marketing plays a key part in extending this journalistic legacy into the future. Our job is to answer the question, “Why is quality journalism worth paying for?” We create award-winning marketing that builds our brand and deepens affinity for our journalistic offering. Above all, we strive to be timely, straightforward and relevant — illustrating in new and creative ways how The New York Times can enrich the lives of our readers.

We are seeking an Associate Creative Director, Earned Activations (Contract) to lead the creative vision for our specific “earned” marketing initiatives. This is a critical leadership role for a creative strategist who can move beyond traditional advertising to produce culturally resonant work that drives organic press and social conversation.

Reporting to the Creative Director, Design, with a dotted line to the Executive Director, Brand Marketing, you will serve as a creative partner to our marketing, editorial, comms, commerce, photo, external agency partners, Games and The Athletic creative teams. You will be responsible for dreaming up and executing ideas that turn the value of our world-class journalism and lifestyle products into shareable experiences. You will focus exclusively on creating a cohesive but distinct earned lens for our core products: News, The Athletic, Games, and Cooking.

We will look to you to bring unexpected, deeply resonant thinking to how we market our journalism, championing creative ideas that can break through the noise of the modern media landscape.

This is a temporary hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters, reporting to the the Creative Director, Design. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Concept and lead the development of brand-building activations, partnerships, and communications content designed specifically to generate earned media and social sharing.

  • Direct the day-to-day work of a Senior Designer, Earned providing clear conceptual vision to guide projects from strategy to launch. You will oversee the translation of earned media concepts into high-quality design solutions, ensuring that every deliverable—from seeding kits to social assets—upholds The New York Times's rigorous brand standards.

  • Translate marketing strategies into clear, provocative creative directives that excite internal teams and external partners.

  • Develop creative ideas tailored to the unique audiences of our core products, ensuring a cohesive visual and conceptual narrative for News, The Athletic, Games, and Cooking.

  • Create work that natively integrates celebrities, influencers, and culturally noteworthy subscribers to amplify our mission in ways that feel authentic and newsworthy.

  • Guide the creation of "social-first" activations designed to thrive on digital platforms and spark community engagement without relying solely on paid media or editorially motivated social media handles.

  • In partnership with the Director, Creative Strategy and Earned Production and Director, Brand Earned Activations, guide external agency relationships to ensure top-notch quality and brand/product standards are enforced.

  • Work closely with the Executive Director of Brand Activations and Talent to ensure earned ideas align with broader business goals.

  • Act as an ambassador for earned thinking across the organization, engaging the right stakeholders in productive conversations to build alignment.

  • Execute high-concept ideas, balancing quality with the demands of the news cycle.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience in creative leadership, with a heavy focus on earned media, PR-led activations, or non-traditional advertising.

  • A portfolio that demonstrates “work the world talked about”—campaigns that broke through via PR, social trends, or cultural moments.

  • Deep understanding of how to leverage Social, Celebrity, and Influencer ecosystems to drive brand discovery.

  • Experience translating marketing strategies, product roadmaps, and the news cycle into clear creative directives.

  • Service diverse categories across the NYT portfolio, from the rigor of News to the fandom of The Athletic and the community-driven spaces of Games and Cooking.

  • Cultivate trusted relationships across the organization and navigate complex stakeholder dynamics.

  • Operational agility to navigate the time sensitive requirements of earned media while maintaining high standards of craft.
