job.title: Editor, Weekend Audience
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for an editor to help lead our teams across our flagship social accounts and search, with a focus on weekend programming. A successful candidate for this role will bring expertise in all things audience growth off-platform, including search and social platforms as well as emerging ones, a strong sense of news judgment and audience signals, as well as a keen eye for off-platform photos, graphics and videos.

The editor will help establish a vision for shaping and targeting our journalism for different platforms to ensure that the full breadth of Times journalism finds audiences on weekends. This role bridges tactical execution and high-level strategy. Leading the work of a small team of off-platform editors during the weekends, you will work story by story — including helping to program our social accounts — and think more broadly about the mix of our off-platform social report, and how it should or should not differ from the weekday to the weekends. You will also have a hands-on role in ensuring our journalism appears across high-demand topics for users who seek news, but haven't yet made The Times their destination for news.

This person will work Wednesday through Sunday.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Play a lead role in shaping our weekend social report off-platform. This will include leading the work of social editors to develop effective ways to share Times journalism off-platform, as well as helping to execute those strategies day to day and week to week

  • Conduct daily performance tracking and detailed analysis to identify immediate content opportunities and necessary optimizations.

  • Systematically translate complex changes and day-to-day observations into clear, timely, and actionable editorial SEO recommendations and best practices for various newsroom teams.

  • Help to lead our weekend report off-platform, ensuring that priorities are shared on key platforms where they are most likely to find audiences and helping to organize broader plans for signature enterprise stories and other priority projects.

  • Monitor on-site and off-platform conversations and signals for story ideas.

  • Developing, refining and upholding the voice of The Times on all of our off-platform channels, exhibiting excellent news judgment and audience-sensitive framing.

  • Interpreting data and signals to know what pieces are the right fit for what audiences both on and off our platforms.

  • Working with journalists in the newsroom on best social media and SEO practices, including framing pieces for specific audiences.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Audience Deputy, Off-Platform.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of experience in social media, SEO or digital journalism for a news organization

  • Excellent news and editorial judgment and exceptional editing skills

  • Proven track record of identifying real time coverage opportunities using internal data and external audience signals

  • Consistent record running social accounts and/or search optimization for major news outlets, both in a hands-on way as an editor and in a supervisory role

  • Strong writing and editing skills, and knowledge of Times style or the ability to absorb and apply it quickly

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience managing direct and dotted line reports

  • Experience with social video, and video-first platforms

  • Passion for The New York Times mission and commitment to be part of our innovation and growth

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

Analytics Data Products (ADP) is an enablement team in the Data Platform mission. We support Product Engineering teams across The Times in creating, operating, and stewarding data products by providing onboarding workflows, developer experience, modeling expertise, and data-lifecycle standards. We also build shared behavioral data products, such as Pageviews, Sessions, and client-side Interactions, so core reader behaviors can be measured consistently across missions and standalone experiences. Mission teams remain accountable for their domain data while we work alongside them as a forward-deployed team to help them onboard and publish. You will report to the Senior Director of Data Platform.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can expect to come into the office 3+ days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Hire, develop, and lead a high-performing engineering team, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and high productivity
  • Own developer experience and tooling (onboarding, CLI, templates, validation, automation) and define and track success metrics such as producer adoption and data reliability
  • Oversee roadmap execution, architectural guidance, technical decisions
  • Develop and maintain budgets, forecasts and a cost attribution model for your team's cloud solutions
  • Partner with product managers and stakeholders to define requirements and manage change while systematically retiring legacy systems.
  • Develop and maintain budgets, forecasts and a cost attribution model for your team's cloud solutions
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of formal people management experience
  • 4+ years building and supporting production data pipelines
  • Demonstrated experience managing or leading technical teams with diverse skill sets and backgrounds
  • Experience enabling successful collaborations across engineering teams and have a knack for bringing engineers together to achieve shared goals
  • Ability to jump in as needed to assist technically with code reviews, design discussions, and analysis
  • Experience using SQL to transform data and a working knowledge of at least one of: Python, Java or Go
  • Knowledge of relational, columnar, and key-value storage technologies as well as data modeling for analytics
  • Passion for the Times' mission and desire to join us at a moment in history where our data has the power to transform every aspect of creation and practice of journalism

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience building developer tooling, onboarding workflows, or internal platforms that other engineering teams adopt
  • Experience with distributed systems and event-driven architectures and event instrumentation

And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.

The New York Times is looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the Compute and Storage team in the Data Platform mission. We build, run and scale the shared compute engines, lakehouse storage and connective infrastructure that power our data platform at The Times. Our work enables teams across the company to publish and own data products without managing the infrastructure underneath. You will report to the Senior Engineering Manager of Data Platforms.

  • Oversee roadmap execution for our compute, streaming, orchestration and lakehouse storage platforms. 
  • Guide architecture and technical decisions. Set standards for shared platform code and engine integrations so our systems stay secure, reliable and scalable.
  • Define and track service goals for availability, provisioning speed, pipeline success and query performance. 
  • Build strong practices for on-call, automation, SLAs and escalation paths.
  • Partner with the product and engineering teams that build on our platform to turn their needs into self-service capabilities.
  • Develop and maintain budgets, forecasts and a cost attribution model. 
  • Support our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • 5+ years of software or data infrastructure engineering experience building scalable and distributed systems.
  • Experience running production cloud infrastructure on Kubernetes.
  • Skilled in defining SLOs and SLAs, monitoring and alerting, incident management and operational automation.
  • Strong technical fluency. Comfortable guiding architecture discussions and reviewing code alongside engineers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with data processing engines and runtimes such as Spark, Trino, Flink, Kafka, Airflow.
  • Experience leading platform migrations, system deprecations, and vendor evaluations.

job.title: Executive Assistant, Newsroom - Masthead
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The New York Times is seeking an experienced, highly organized and proactive executive assistant to support the newsroom masthead, including the masthead editor overseeing newsroom strategy, operations and finance as well as one additional masthead editor.

This is a critical role at the center of the Newsroom's leadership and administrative operations. The executive assistant will manage complex scheduling and logistics, organize priorities and follow-through, coordinate across senior leaders and departments, draft correspondence, support projects with research and project management, and serve as a trusted representative of the masthead leader's office.

The ideal candidate exercises sophisticated judgment, anticipates needs, communicates with discretion and professionalism, and is comfortable working in a fast-paced, highly collaborative newsroom environment. They should be able to manage shifting priorities while maintaining strong attention to detail and confidentiality.

This position will report directly to the assistant managing editor for strategy, operations and finance.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide a wide range of operational and administrative support with organization, proactivity and discretion

  • Manage a complex, fast-changing calendar by prioritizing requests, resolving conflicts, and safeguarding focus time

  • Track executive priorities, direct report updates, and newsroom initiatives by preparing agendas, briefing packs, and action trackers to ensure prompt decision follow-through

  • Anticipate needs by proactively flagging relevant information, risks, and opportunities

  • Draft and edit executive correspondence using strong judgment and discretion

  • Process expense reports, reconcile receipts, and ensure timely reimbursement

  • Serve as a professional liaison to newsroom leaders, department heads and external partners

  • Coordinate domestic and international travel, including detailed itineraries, logistics and alignment with security and operations teams

  • Work primarily on-site (4–5 days per week) to provide direct, real-time newsroom support

  • Provide support as needed for the teams overseen by the leaders you support

job.title: Executive Producer, The Interview
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Over the past two years, “The Interview” has made itself a trustworthy New York Times brand and a destination, where artists (Mick Jagger, Nicolas Cage, Charlize Theron), politicians (Zohran Mamdani, Chuck Schumer), athletes (Karl-Anthony Towns), influential figures in the media (Megyn Kelly, Andrew Schulz, Tucker Carlson), at the center of a story (Scott Pelley, Gisele Pelicot) and beyond sit down for thoughtful, wide-ranging, challenging, fun, news-making conversations about their lives and ideas. And now we are looking for the next Executive Producer to lead the show.

We're looking for a senior editorial leader with strong, relevant experience running a video show, working with hosts (we have two great ones: Lulu Garcia-Navarro and David Marchese) and leading show teams made up of talented staffers with audio and video backgrounds. You will drive the show's creative and editorial direction, and work to grow The Interview's already considerable audience across Times-owned platforms, YouTube and social media. You will be responsible for setting the editorial priorities, managing the production team that delivers the show each week and communicating with stakeholders across the newsroom on timely, impactful conversations. Because you will work closely with the staff of the New York Times Magazine, having experience in an ideas-driven magazine environment is a plus.

You are a curious, creative thinker, a stylish editor, a decisive and compassionate manager, and an excellent communicator. You should be comfortable working in video, excited by an evolving media landscape and motivated by booking big guests in important moments, whether that's the the definitive conversation with a Hollywood icon, a rising political star or a newsmaker at the center of a breaking story. You should be a fan of what The Interview has built, and excited to keep building and growing and evolving the show. You will report to the editor-in-chief of the New York Times Magazine.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the overall editorial and creative strategy for The Interview, setting the editorial goals and guiding the coverage for the show

  • Oversee the editorial quality of each episode, ensuring strong structure, pacing, framing and tone that aligns with the overall strategic goals of the franchise and the standards of the Times

  • Oversee workflow to ensure that several episodes at various stages of production are being made in the smartest, most efficient and sustainable way possible

  • Work closely with the hosts, booker and editor to solicit and field pitches and book a compelling mix of guests

  • Own all expressions of the show, including onsite and off-platform, all mediums (video, audio, digital), episode packaging, titles and thumbnails, in coordination with the Audience team

  • Collaborate with video operations and the Shows team to shape the visual identity of The Interview, including set design, camera approach, clips and other media to enhance each episode

  • Collaborate with the Magazine's photo, fact-checking and copy departments

  • Cultivate relationships with Times journalists across the newsroom whose valuable perspectives can be invaluable during the prep phase for any given interview

  • Lead communication with and seek feedback from the masthead on high-profile interviews

  • Manage and mentor a team of producers (some with audio backgrounds, some with video backgrounds), setting clear expectations, supporting their growth, assessing performance and providing regular feedback

  • Work with the audience team to understand audience trends and performance analysis, translating insights into recommendations

  • Create a culture of productive experimentation, because the show should never get stuck in its ways and the environment we are publishing into is always changing

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand

Basic Qualifications:

  • 15 years of experience leading editorial teams, including significant experience running a host-driven conversational audio or video show

  • Strong experience working on high profile interviews in culture and politics

  • Highly skilled at every aspect of editing at the show level, from structuring episodes (both before and after the interview) and pacing to line editing and reviewing cuts

  • Experience managing and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, including hosts, audio or video producers, audience strategists and others

  • Comfortable interpreting platform analytics and audience insights to inform editorial decisions

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong organization and communication skills, with the ability to make decisions and set priorities in a fast-moving news environment

  • Belief in The New York Times's mission and dedication to being part of our innovation and growth

job.title: Fact Checker, Shows
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times Shows department is hiring a staff editor to fact check episodes of Hard Fork, both in video and audio formats.

You will work with producers and editors to check facts and assertions, with extra attention to the tone and context in which they're delivered.

You are comfortable working in print, audio and video mediums in a fast-paced news environment. We're looking for exceptional news judgment, an investigator's mind and the ability to dive into unfamiliar material on deadline. And while we value deliberate, careful checking, speed is also important. The fact checker will be part of a small group of producers and editors, so collegiality, diplomacy and a collaborative spirit are a must.

This is a part-time role for 20 hours a week to start. It could scale up over time. You will report to the Executive Producer of Hard Fork.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Check factual assertions in podcast and video episodes to determine veracity and correctness on deadline
  • Check prep documents and listen during live recordings to track facts and assertions to be verified
  • Listen to drafts, checking all facts, noting attribution, and providing guidance on editing or adjusting material as needed
  • Conduct quick and accurate research to gather and verify facts in collaboration with producers, editors and hosts
  • Work to ensure fairness and accuracy; correct contradictions and omissions in consultation with producers, editors and hosts; correct spelling and grammar
  • Check episode descriptions and other copy for video and audio assets. Adjust show print excerpts, transcripts and captions for factual accuracy
  • Check video episode's visuals for factual accuracy and context
  • Exercise news judgment
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 or more years of fact-checking experience
  • Available to work evenings as needed

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Exercise news judgment
  • Quickly identify facts to be checked in a podcast episode transcript
  • Communicate notes & feedback clearly
  • Superb research skills
  • Use data to inform decisions
  • Manage deadlines simultaneously
  • Well-developed and adaptive cultural competence and emotional intelligence
  • Experience in a deadline-driven environment
  • Experience fact checking audio or video products
  • Experience working with talent
  • Uphold the existing editorial standards of The Times

job.title: Fellow, A.I. Initiatives
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as an A.I. Initiatives fellow in New York.

We are looking for a fellow who will bring a mix of machine-learning and journalism experience to newsroom reporting projects. You will work with journalists across departments to identify, develop and execute projects that use the power of artificial intelligence, machine learning and data science techniques to address investigative challenges. You will be part of the A.I. Initiatives team, which includes editors, engineers and a product designer.

This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed.

Responsibilities: 

  • Collaborate with investigative reporters to support projects that benefit from A.I., including large-scale research, transcription, translation, document search, language analysis and computer vision tasks
  • Identify opportunities and experiment with responsible A.I. tools to empower the newsroom
  • Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional experience in journalism and/or machine learning
  • Technical proficiency and experience analyzing data, developing applications and conducting research with machine-learning models
  • Editorial experience, such as interning in a newsroom or working on a college newspaper
  • Engineering skills and experience with APIs, front-end web applications and databases
  • Recent experience working with LLMs and other machine-learning models
  • Interest in the intersection of journalism and artificial intelligence
  • Understanding of ethical considerations surrounding the use of A.I. in journalism

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Record of multiple news or opinion journalism internships, or equivalent experience
  • Work demonstrating experience applying A.I. to real-world problems
  • Experience working with large datasets and cloud computing platforms
  • Experience working with Svelte or similar front-end frameworks

To apply, upload a résumé and cover letter. The application will prompt you when to upload materials. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered.

You must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor work visas for the fellowship, but we will consider applicants with valid work authorization or a valid student visa that can be extended with Optional Practical Training.

You may apply to only one fellowship position per year. For instance, if you apply as an A.I. Initiatives fellow, you should not apply for any other positions in the fellowship. Duplicate applications will be discarded.

The Times Fellowship generates a high level of interest, so we cannot acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process, which can take eight weeks or more. The fellowship will be divided into rotations with the departments that make up the Audience team:

  • Off platform: You will develop social strategy, visual, copy/framing and news-judgment skills. You will help track trends, shape live coverage on breaking storylines, and optimize headlines and links. 
  • On platform: You will engage readers on our owned surfaces, contributing to our expanding community efforts, as well as through home screen and email engagement.
  • Data and audience insights: You will gain an understanding of our analytics and our audience — whom we reach and whom we need to engage. You also will learn data-literacy skills and work to help desks optimize coverage.


This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed.

  • Write social copy and help shape how we share our journalism on social, analyze our presence and strategy on existing platforms, and evaluate opportunities on new social platforms
  • Interpret data and signals to shape how we present stories on and off our platforms
  • Optimize stories for search, and identify trending topics and competitive trends 
  • Work on projects to deepen engagement on our owned surfaces, including the home screen, push alerts, email and community products
  • Partner with the newsroom audience analytics team on deep and actionable analysis
  • Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship
  • Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional journalism experience, excluding internships
  • Experience writing in an engaging, smart tone that feels native to social media and is consistent with the values of independent journalism
  • Experience looking at and interpreting data

  • Record of multiple news internships or equivalent experience
  • An understanding of all mainstream and some emerging social channels, and a willingness to learn about new platforms
  • Comfort with data and testing, and with iterating to find what resonates with different audiences

You will be part of the Election Analytics team, which produces The New York Times/Siena University Poll, the live election-night forecast known as The Needle and our polling tracker, in addition to stories that explore voter decisions and analyze past elections.

Election Analytics is an interdisciplinary team of reporters, editors, developers and statisticians. You should have experience working in one of these areas and be excited to learn about the others. You will use your knowledge of elections and voting to contribute to stories, graphics and our longer-term projects.

The exact form of this role will depend on your background. Perhaps you are more comfortable writing than coding and want to deepen your technical skills to more easily answer questions yourself. Or perhaps you bring a background as a developer or statistician and want to work on your ability to communicate your ideas in words.

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional journalism experience, excluding internships
  • A deep and demonstrated understanding of American elections
  • Experience working with data
  • Expertise in at least one of the team’s focus areas: 
    • Data-driven reporting, including reporting clips or blog posts that demonstrate analytical findings meant for a broad audience 
    • Statistics, including experience developing statistical models in R or Python
    • Development, including proficiency in R or Python, experience working with cloud computing providers and experience building productionized web applications

Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as a copy editor for the Opinion section in New York.

Copy editors are the last line of defense before publication of Opinion columnists, contributors and guest essayists. Basic duties include checking writers’ grammar, spelling and adherence to style and standards. An exceptional copy editor will also serve as an advocate for readers, ensuring that a story’s argument, logic, style and tone are sound. Opinion copy editors must balance enforcement of the standards of The Times with preserving a writer’s distinct viewpoint and voice. 

You have experience with copy editing and making editorial judgment calls. You can work collaboratively with story editors and fact-checkers. You are experienced digitally and enthusiastic about Opinion’s daily report — and open to working on stories from all points of view. You are platform agnostic and interested in working on copy for any medium. You are comfortable raising potential problems concerning standards and taste, and have good radar for when to push back on edits made by more senior colleagues.

The Opinion department is separate from the newsroom. This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed.

Finalists will be required to take an editing test.

Responsibilities:

  • Copy edit story text, headlines, captions and other display copy, elevating articles on the sentence level for clarity 
  • Ensure accuracy and consistency across a range of content, including editorials, guest essays and columns
  • Polish, format and quality-check podcast transcripts, graphics and video elements
  • Respond to changing priorities and demands based on department needs and the news cycle
  • Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional journalism experience, excluding internships
  • Experience editing articles, essays or scripts for publication
  • Experience working on firm deadlines

  • Comfort with a wide range of subject matter, from politics to science and culture
  • Familiarity with content management systems and transcription tools

Our photographers bear witness to events around the world, and our Photo department is one of the treasures of our newsroom.

As a fellow, you will work with Times photo editors, shooting daily news and enterprise assignments for many sections. The goal is to give you exposure to news and feature photography, and the opportunity to learn about news judgment, editing choices, video journalism, building visual narratives, lighting techniques and aesthetic direction. Working with photo editors, you will also initiate enterprise projects.

You should be open to learning from others, and inclusive, generous and empathetic toward our colleagues, our audience, and the communities we cover.

You will work out of either our New York headquarters, where you will cover a mix of assignments, or our Washington bureau, where you will mainly cover Capitol Hill and the White House.

  • A portfolio of work demonstrating excellence in visual storytelling

  • Some experience with videography or an interest in learning video
  • Knowledge of photographic equipment, Photoshop, Photo Mechanic, Premiere and/or other photo- and video-editing software

Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as a print news designer in New York.

The Times is a recognized leader in print design and has been named World’s Best Designed Newspaper multiple times by the Society for News Design. You will work with art directors and designers across news and feature sections to creative engaging layouts, reimagining digital-first content for a print audience.

You should have a portfolio that shows a talent in narrative and visual storytelling using typography, photography, illustration and page architecture. You are a problem-solver and quick learner with an interest in journalism across all subject matters. You can communicate and collaborate well with editors, photo editors and fellow designers.

This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed.

Responsibilities:

  • Edit, design and produce impactful, functional newspaper pages that ensure the accuracy and clarity of our journalism in the print newspaper
  • Create print versions of digitally native multimedia stories, like interactive graphics and video-driven investigations 
  • Use editorial and visual judgment to ensure that impact is commensurate with editorial value
  • Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship
  • Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional photojournalism experience, excluding internships
  • Visual judgment and design competency — typography, layout, photo editing, color, and reader behavior
  • Experience with Adobe Creative Suite and/or Figma

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working in a collaborative environment and articulating the reasons behind design decisions
  • Ability to meet deadlines and adapt to change in an unpredictable news and production environment
  • Curiosity and interest in the news, and in finding innovative approaches to telling stories
  • Record of multiple news or visual internships or equivalent experience

To apply, upload a résumé and cover letter. You should also include a link to a portfolio demonstrating your design work. The Upshot is a small, versatile team that publishes analytical and explanatory journalism, often on policy and politics. And we often use data, visuals and interactivity to explain the world in new ways.

As a fellow, you will pitch your own ideas and contribute to group projects in various forms. That work may mean visualizing the Caitlin Clark effect, showing political polarization in action, finding possible insider trading or tracking data centers from the sky.

We are open to proposals on a range of roles. Typically, our fellows come with at least a year of reporting experience (or equivalent), along with technical or domain knowledge — in politics or policy, statistics or data analysis, information graphics, or web development. You don’t need to be an expert with data or technology, but you should be comfortable with it. And you don’t need to be a seasoned beat reporter, but you should be ready to pitch, report and write on complicated topics.

Much of our best work involves working as a team. You should be excited about collaborating with other members of the Upshot and colleagues across the newsroom.

Finally, we want you to know the Upshot and our work. Why do you want to work on this desk, as opposed to a different one? job.title: FOIA Editor
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for a FOIA editor to oversee and guide our strategy of using the Freedom of Information Act and other local, state and federal public records laws to obtain information from governmental and public entities.

You will serve as a hub for the newsroom’s public records requests, helping provide resources and guidance to journalists across The Times about how to maximize our ability to obtain information in the public’s interest. You will serve as a consultant to teams on effective tactics, working with reporters and editors at the inception of stories and projects to help integrate FOIA requests early in the process. You will also be responsible for developing story ideas and original coverage through the FOIA process, identifying opportunities to obtain public records that will generate news. You are excited to experiment with new technology and formats and collaborate with our data, visual and product teams to tell stories that resonate with our audience.

You will help track and expedite public records requests by maintaining a centralized database of FOIA requests and appeals, and will work closely with the Legal department to identify efforts that merit litigation support.

This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office each week. The person will also work closely with our bureau in Washington and make periodic visits there. 

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and refine FOIA requests in partnership with internal stakeholders for submission

  • Serve as a consultant for teams as they design public records requests to bolster their reporting, with a priority on integrating such requests early into the process of developing stories.

  • Propose and drive story ideas based on FOIA requests and coordinate coverage across multiple desks 

  • Consult with desks to understand when and how to augment ongoing themes with FOIA requests

  • Advise journalists across the newsroom about the most effective approaches to obtain information through public records laws.

  • Develop and maintain training materials and deliver training about what information can be obtained through the federal Freedom of Information Act and similar state and local statutes.

  • Coordinate, track and help expedite public records requests by maintaining a centralized database of FOIA requests and appeals.

  • Partner with the Legal department in identifying efforts to seek public information that merit litigation support.

  • Represent the Newsroom in partnership with Legal on FOIA matters

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the enterprise OR news research team.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years’ experience at a journalism or media company or other relevant organization.

  • Demonstrated success navigating and resolving legal issues related to public records laws. 

  • A record of collaborating and partnering with colleagues to find innovative storytelling approaches through the use of public records and other legal strategies. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience in shaping the public records strategy of a news organization.

  • Conversant in local and state public records laws and practices in addition to the federal statute.

  • Deep familiarity with media law or a law degree 

  • A record of adjusting to the evolving and changing needs of a newsroom 

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

job.title: Front-End Web Engineer - T Brand
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

T Brand is a growing team of editors, designers, strategists, and more who create branded content across the gamut of The New York Times's advertisers. Our work takes many forms — reported articles, documentary videos, animations, photo essays, social posts, podcasts, interactive data visualizations, event activations and Newsroom sponsorships.

The Studio is looking for a junior web engineer. As a Front-End Web Engineer, you will contribute to the development of our front-end products, including Paid Posts, the Flex Suite, and custom interactive applications. Working with senior engineers and your manager, you will implement responsive features, building modular components, and writing clean, maintainable, readable, and reusable code across our advertising templates. You will collaborate with the broader creative team, participates in code reviews, and grows their technical skillset across our modern front-end stack.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City Headquarters. You will report to the Director of Design.

Responsibilities:

  • Build features using modern technologies, and frameworks (e.g., React, Astro) to support product capabilities and performance.
  • Create fluid animations and interactive visual elements using CSS and web animation libraries (such as GreenSock/GSAP).
  • Implement front-end development for web products, including advertising templates and interactive single-page applications under technical guidance.
  • Follow established coding standards, design patterns, and best practices, producing clean, modular, and reusable HTML, JavaScript/TypeScript, and CSS (SASS).
  • Participate in regular code reviews, receiving constructive feedback and applying team design principles to improve code quality.
  • Receive mentorship from Web Engineers, Senior Web Engineers, and Lead Engineers, participating in team learning projects and technical growth.
  • Collaborate with partners (Design, Product, and Editorial) to translate creative mockups and requirements into functional web experiences.
  • Support front-end performance, cross-browser compatibility, and accessibility best practices across all developed features.
  • Help resolve technical debt, fix bugs, and maintain clear project documentation and detailed work tickets (e.g., in Jira).
  • Integrate AI-assisted workflows and modern developer tools to improve code production, improve, and boost development efficiency.
  • Implement best practices in version control using Git and GitHub, managing repositories, branching strategies, and collaborative code reviews.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Director of Design.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience in front-end web development.
  • Experience with foundational web technologies: HTML5, CSS3/SASS, JavaScript (ES6+), and basic TypeScript.
  • Familiarity or eagerness to learn modern front-end frameworks, specifically Astro and Svelte.
  • Knowledge of responsive web design principles, cross-browser compatibility, and web accessibility standards.
  • Basic familiarity with version control workflows using Git.
  • Careful eye for detail when debugging and troubleshooting front-end code.
  • Clear communication, excellent interpersonal skills, with a collaborative mindset when working with designers and project managers.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Exposure to web animation libraries like GreenSock (GSAP) or CSS animation techniques.
  • Exposure to Google Ad Manager (GAM) or ad technology integration patterns.

Applications without a digital portfolio will not be considered.

job.title: Graphics Multimedia Editor, Shows
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The New York Times' Motion Graphics team focuses on elevating how animated graphics and motion design are used in our video journalism. Working in close collaboration with Video, Shows and Graphics, the team responds to the demands of stories and formats across the newsroom—from news explainers and visual investigations to enterprise series and shows.

As a member of Digital News Design's Motion Graphics team, you will focus on work for Shows, a department created to expand the reach of The Times's audio and video shows. You will collaborate with reporters, editors, producers, art directors and show hosts to craft motion assets and visuals for our expanding roster of shows across a range of formats and platforms.

You will be responsible for identifying creative needs and producing a range of design assets, including motion graphics, typography, animations, and MOGRT templates. In consultation with editors and other newsroom leaders, you'll exercise journalistic judgment and visual creativity to innovate and ensure accuracy, clarity, and validity of the content presented. Design team members are expected not only to make exceptional contributions to our journalism, but also to engage with others to foster an environment of learning and constructive dialogue about our work.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Create original designs and craft video toolkits for a range of shows and show formats.
  • Work collaboratively with show producers, and editors to create engaging and informative videos.
  • Convey visual story ideas and complex information in engaging video sequences and animation.
  • Work alongside other Times design teams to ensure consistent visual languages, and develop best practices.
  • Be a pragmatic innovator whose solutions elicit responses that justify the effort and investment.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Motion Graphics Editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of motion design experience. Expertise with After Effects, designing for motion and animation is essential.
  • Expertise with Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator and Adobe Creative Suite.
  • Strong portfolio of design work.
  • Solid understanding of layout, typography, and storytelling techniques.
  • Experience creating visual presentations that intelligently incorporate audio, video, still images and text.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Enthusiasm for designing and making great animations and design for storytelling to cover current events for The New York Times.
  • Experience making quick decisions under deadlines and a high-pressure newsroom environment.
  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a multidisciplinary team.
  • Experience meeting deadlines and to adapt to change in a daily, unpredictable news and production environment
  • Open to working a flexible schedule.

job.title: Graphics/Multimedia Editor, Elections Data Developer (Election Analytics)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Election Analytics team produces flagship, standard-setting elections coverage, including the live, election night statistical model known as the Needle and The New York Times/Siena Poll. The department is looking to hire an experienced data developer to contribute to data creation, management and architecture across our products.

Underneath our poll and the Needle are massive amounts of data. This includes the voter file, as well as demographics for different localities, hundreds of scrapers collecting precinct data and countless pipelines for processing and cleaning data. Our understanding of the electorate is only as good as the data we have access to, including the data we create to test our systems and the election night model itself.

You will have a central role in creating and cleaning these data sources for use in our products. You will help knit together data from different sections of the team to build our understanding of what may happen on election night throughout the year. And you will ensure we have proper observability into how data is being used.

Election Analytics is a multidisciplinary team of reporters, developers, statisticians and modelers who work on written coverage, graphics, our polls and the election-night model. This is a highly collaborative role that will involve working with colleagues from Election Analytics, the Graphics department and Interactive News.

This is an in-office position in New York City or Washington, D.C., and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

To apply, you MUST include a cover letter of no more than 300 words that…

  • Explains how you approached a specific instance where you had to balance engineering principles with the need to meet a deadline; and

  • Explains specifically why you are interested in covering elections

Responsibilities:

  • Create test data for the election-night mathematical model and for live election-night Graphics

  • Build and improve pipelines for ingesting, processing, and displaying large data sets, precinct data or absentee files.

  • Build and maintain observability tools for the model that allow for fast debugging on election night and clear monitoring of precinct data entering the model

  • Work with stakeholders to understand the data needs and schema requirements

  • Develop and maintain libraries in R that form the basis of our apps

  • Balance engineering principles with the need to move at the speed of news

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • You will report to the Director of Election Analytics

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of relevant experience

  • Familiarity working with large datasets and with best practices in data management

  • Experience working with data-oriented programming languages, such as R or Python

  • Experience working with cloud computing providers such as Google Cloud Platform or Amazon Web Services

  • Experience working collaboratively with people of different skills and backgrounds

  • Willingness to work a flexible schedule as needed to support coverage of elections and polls

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working with election data

  • Experience developing ETL pipelines, working with orchestration tooling, and ensuring reliability and observability

  • Experience with Google BigQuery or other OLAP databases

  • Experience building productionized apps

job.title: Graphics/Multimedia Editor, News
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Graphics department at The New York Times is looking for a versatile, experienced visual journalist to report, design and create graphics and multimedia stories, with a primary focus on breaking news and fast-turn news response.

You will execute visual coverage on major breaking stories, producing maps, charts, diagrams and interactive graphics on deadline. Your work may also include statistical visualizations, video, photography and animation. You will identify visual story angles, analyze data, and collaborate closely with Graphics colleagues and newsroom journalists across desks. This role combines quick-turn breaking news execution with high-impact journalism. You may also be required to work weekends.

The Graphics department is a diverse group of journalists and visual thinkers with creative backgrounds ranging from architecture to cartography to computer science. We are curious about all kinds of things and seek to find individuals who bring their own curiosity to bear in creative approaches to storytelling.

This is an in-office position based in New York City, and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week.

Applications should include links to a portfolio or work samples to demonstrate the creation of visual journalism. Please feel free to describe your role in specific projects in your cover letter.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceive, report, design, and publish breaking news graphics and multimedia stories using a variety of visual forms.
  • Design and build interactive and static visualizations.
  • Collaborate with Graphics staff and journalists from other newsroom desks on major breaking news events.
  • Conceptualize new lines of reporting and analyze data to discover visual stories with accuracy, clarity, and impact.
  • Share responsibility for regular weekend news graphics coverage, ensuring prompt, high-quality visual response to breaking news.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the news editor on the Graphics team.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of professional experience producing, reporting, or editing visual journalism or news graphics.
  • Proven track record of identifying visual opportunities quickly and delivering effective graphics in a fast-paced breaking news environment.
  • Expertise in visual software (Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, Figma) and front-end web development tools (HTML, CSS, JavaScript).
  • Demonstrated experience with data reporting, interface design, and information graphics design.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Excellent news judgment, strong written and oral communication skills, and ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.
  • Familiarity with interactive web frameworks (such as Svelte), web mapping/GIS tools, and tools like ai2html.
  • Experience integrating multimedia elements such as video, photography, and animation into news coverage.
  • Experience prioritizing, organizing, and managing multiple fast-moving visual projects under tight deadlines.
  • Flexibility to work a schedule that includes regular weekend shifts.

job.title: Graphics/Multimedia Editor, Publishing and Storytelling Tools
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Graphics department at The New York Times is looking to hire an experienced engineer to build interactive applications, infrastructure, and tools that power our visual journalism. Our most ambitious data-driven projects rely on bespoke systems to publish multimedia stories to our readers at scale. As part of a multidisciplinary team, you will architect, build, and maintain the cloud infrastructure that powers those stories.

You have demonstrated experience creating visually-compelling interactive experiences, and have expertise creating tooling and systems to build web-based features. Here are some examples of the types of projects you might help build or power with the tools you create:

  • The New York Times 2024 Election Results 
  • The Needle: Live 2024 Presidential Election Forecast
  • President Trump’s Approval Ratings: Latest Polls
  • Track Covid-19 in the U.S.
  • What It Was Like Inside Syria’s Most Fearsome Prison
  • The Complex Deportation Network Behind Trump’s Immigration Crackdown

The Graphics department is a group of journalists and visual thinkers with creative backgrounds ranging from architecture to cartography to computer science. We are curious about all kinds of things and seek to find individuals who bring their own curiosity to bear in creative approaches to storytelling.

Applications should include links to a portfolio or code repositories to demonstrate the creation of interactive applications and web sites from concept to launch. Please include a cover letter describing your role in specific projects, with details about software tools and systems you have created.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and maintain software used by graphics developers to render and publish visual journalism.
  • Build and improve pipelines for ingesting, processing, and displaying large data sets like national election results and statistical models.
  • Facilitate and guide contributions from other developers to our core software libraries.
  • Maintain automatic cloud tooling to support high-frequency publishing, data ingestion and data analysis.
  • Sketch and quickly build prototypes of interactive applications, graphics and other types of multimedia story forms.
  • Ensure compliance with web performance and accessibility standards.
  • Collaborate on news deadlines with a multidisciplinary team.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Director of Interactive Platforms

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of relevant experience
  • Expertise in development of interactive graphics, data dashboards and Web sites, including HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • Expertise in building software and tooling for the development and publication of web sites and interactive applications
  • Demonstrated experience working with Svelte or other modern web technologies
  • Expertise in managing applications in complex cloud computing environments

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proven experience meeting deadlines and adapting to change in a daily, unpredictable news production environment
  • Skill in interface design and information graphic design
  • Curiosity and interest in the news, and in finding innovative approaches to telling stories
  • Experience creating news graphics in a variety of formats and timeframes

job.title: HR Generalist
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

We are looking for a dynamic and hands-on HR Generalist to partner directly with our Advertising, Marketing, Communications, Licensing, Partnerships, Wirecutter, and Events departments and HRBP team. Reporting to the Senior Manager, HR Business Partner you will be a primary contact for daily operational HR issues, processes, and coordinating projects for our client groups.

You will balance business-aligned strategic support with rigorous operational execution. You will manage critical operational transactions—including Workday data integrity, position management, auditing, and reporting—to ensure seamless HR operations across all assigned departments. Additionally, you will partner with leadership and HR Centers of Excellence (COEs) on core talent programs. You will operate on a hybrid model requiring 3 days per week in our New York City office.

Responsibilities:

  • Partner with HRBPs, business leadership, cross-functional partners, and COEs (Total Rewards, Talent Acquisition, Talent Management, ER, Legal, and Labor) to support various people initiatives, e.g. end-to-end performance management, goal setting, and annual compensation cycles.
  • Provide direct guidance to employees and line managers on HR policy interpretation, performance and employee relations inquiries, and everyday workplace solutions.
  • Manage position opening and reconciliation against department hiring forecasts in collaboration with hiring managers, Finance, and Talent Acquisition.
  • Maintain strict data integrity within Workday by processing transactions (promotions, manager changes, cost center updates, work location changes) and conducting regular audits.
  • Pull reports and reconcile data sets as requested (rosters, anniversaries, attendance), shout outs.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 2 or more years of experience as an HR Generalist supporting matrixed departments.
  • Technical proficiency in using a cloud-based HRIS such as Workday (position management, transactions, and reporting).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree and professional HR accreditation (e.g., Society for Human Resource Management Certified Professional, Professional in Human Resources).
  • Outstanding capabilities in project management and organizational planning.
  • Demonstrated history of establishing relationships and offering practical, solutions-focused guidance.

job.title: HRIS Analyst II - Workday Performance
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The HRIS Analyst II reports directly to the HRIS Senior Manager and is important for optimizing and supporting Workday Performance, Core HCM, Compensation, HR reporting, and related areas. Primary responsibilities include system configuration, issue troubleshooting, data analysis, testing, production support, and creating mid-level reports. Working with senior HRIS analysts, the HR operations team, and partners, you will guide enhancements to provide HR technology solutions.

This is a hybrid role based in our Norfolk, VA office. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Be a primary technical contact for the Workday Performance module, while providing functional support for Core HCM, Compensation, Payroll, and Time/Absence domains.

  • Accomplish end-to-end system configuration to support global performance evaluation cycles.

  • Be a primary contact for performance workflow design and resolution of technical issues.

  • Deliver technical and user support for Workday, handling questions, troubleshooting, and resolving issues across supported modules.

  • Execute assigned production support tickets and project tasks with high accuracy and within target deadlines.

  • Maintain HCM production support processes, encompassing monitoring, detailed analysis, and issue resolution.

  • Define, refine, and maintain business process configurations.

  • Configure, schedule, and oversee automated mass actions and system alert notifications.

  • Participate in Workday's biannual feature update cycles.

  • Collaborate with the Workday Security team to configure and maintain domain and business process security policies.

job.title: Journalist, Graphics Intensive
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The Graphics Intensive is a unique opportunity for mission-driven students and early career professionals with visual skills to work alongside journalists for a 12-week, full-time program. We seek individuals who bring their own inquisitive nature to develop creative approaches to storytelling, including those who may not have previously considered working in an independent newsroom. Prior journalism experience isn't required — many of our team members have embraced journalism's core fundamentals while at The Times — but you must have a desire to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

The Graphics desk at The New York Times is composed of visual journalists from diverse creative backgrounds, including architecture, cartography, and computer science. We cover all topics across the news cycle, motivated by a shared curiosity. This position is designed to cultivate skills and judgment in the creation of visual stories, including training and regular feedback from team members. Many of our projects are a collective effort, so you will work with a range of people and skill sets.

We are interested in applicants who want to learn how to apply creative and technical skills to a range of journalistic and storytelling assignments. Do you know how to write code to analyze data and produce visualizations? Are you a mapmaker or satellite imagery analyst? Do you use design and illustration to clearly convey complex information? These are the types of people that we seek to develop as potential graphics journalists.

The graphics intensive position is available throughout the year, including winter, spring, summer and fall openings. This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Under close guidance and supervision of a senior editor, produce visual and data-based multimedia journalism in response to breaking or as ongoing news coverage
  • Design and build graphics and other visual forms using web-based markup and coding languages with guidance from senior editors
  • Participate in training sessions
  • Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom
  • Complete work assignments based on team needs and news demands
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a Deputy Editor, Graphics.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 1+ year of demonstrated strong performance toward an undergraduate degree, or relevant professional experience
  • 2+ years of experience working with graphics tools and software, like D3.js, R, JavaScript, Python, HTML/CSS, GIS, and 3-D modeling software
  • Interest in data visualization, cartography or other forms of visual journalism and the skills to start producing work in these areas
  • Skill in interface design and information graphic design
  • Experience with Adobe Creative Suite, especially Illustrator, or with design tools like Figma
  • A portfolio demonstrating experience with news graphics or interactive visualizations

Preferred Qualifications:

  • News or visual internships or equivalent experience
  • Curiosity and interest in the news, and in finding innovative approaches to telling stories
  • Experience working independently, meet deadlines, and being attentive to detail in an unpredictable news cycle and a high-pressure newsroom environment
  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a team with diverse creative skills
  • Available to work some nights, weekends and holidays as the news cycle demands
  • Experience multitasking, prioritizing, and balancing multiple projects in a dynamic work environment
  • Interest in professional growth and openness to professional feedback

Applications should include links to a portfolio or work samples to demonstrate your skills and experience. Please attach a cover letter describing your role in specific projects and which periods of time you will be available for the Graphics intensive. Your cover letter should include any periods when you will be able to work full time in New York, such as, “Available: Winter (2026-27), Spring, Summer or Fall” — or any combination of these.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

job.title: Lead Product Designer, Search
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Mission Overview & Responsibilities: 

The New York Times is looking for a Lead Product Designer to help us design and prototype compelling A.I. experiences that help curious people understand and engage with the world.

We are looking for a Lead Product Designer to shape how readers search for information and understand the world through New York Times products — someone with a passion for design, journalism, and technology, as well as experience delivering A.I.-enabled consumer experiences at scale.

The New A.I. Products and Platforms mission is a critical, company-wide initiative tasked with building the next generation of A.I.-powered products to accelerate The New York Times's essential subscription strategy.

The Times operates in a hybrid model, with those based in NYC working in-office two days per week. We plan to speak with all candidates about where they're based and how they work in a hybrid environment.

As a Lead Product Designer, you'll identify opportunities to use A.I. to address news and information needs through our products' search feature. You'll use your interaction design and coded prototyping skills to build functional prototypes that gain alignment and drive work forward. You'll validate that these prototypes meet users' informational needs and align with our brand and journalistic standards. You'll collaborate with product managers, engineers, user researchers, and editorial partners to ship excellent and performant experiences to the world.

We value an environment of learning and collaboration. You'll play a leadership role to grow and support more junior design team members. You'll help promote a "make to think" design culture. You'll participate in regular design rituals to give and receive critique.

Responsibilities:

  • Create sketches, mockups, user journeys and other UX artifacts to rapidly explore a range of editorial and consumer scenarios and identify promising concepts.

  • Frame different approaches and describe tradeoffs.

  • Create functional coded prototypes of A.I.-powered experiences.

  • Give input to product strategy and concept development.

  • Lead conversations and help make decisions with the cross-functional team.

  • Contribute to the development of design standards and systems around A.I.

  • Represent your work to leadership within the company.

  • Improve the people and process around you by shaping and participating in team and Product Design rituals.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Deputy Head of Product Design.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of experience as a product designer, with recent experience creating coded prototypes using AI-enabled tools and workflows.

  • 7+ years of experience with interaction design and prototyping, including a portfolio showing a deep care for micro-interactions, motion, and accessibility best practices.

  • 7+ years of experience collaborating, building alignment and communicating clearly.

  • 7+ years of experience working with user research and data analysis teams to inform product and UX decisions.

  • 3+ years of creating functional prototypes.

  • Experience designing features that use generative A.I. to deliver end-user experiences.

  • Experience refining A.I.'s tone, format, and behavior to align with brand guidelines, product goals, and quality standards.

  • A portfolio of shipped work demonstrating experience working in 0-to-1 environments.

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Experience with media production workflows.

  • Experience designing or conceptualize large solutions while also aligning user and and business goals.

  • Experience balancing multiple goals to achieve an excellent outcome.

  • Strong ability to show design decisions and impact.

  • Experience working with senior stakeholders.
