job.title: Local Investigations Fellow
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Times is looking for reporters with a local story idea who want to investigate it under the editing guidance of Dean Baquet, The Times’s former executive editor, and a group of veteran investigative editors.

The goal of the Local Investigative Fellowship is to provide fellows the opportunity to learn the ways and means of investigative reporting from some of the best in the business. Our fellows will be based in the communities where they are reporting and make periodic trips to The Times’s offices for training and support.

This one year program is for reporters in local newsrooms or freelancers.

Responsibilities:

  • Spend a year producing signature investigative work focused on your state or region that will be published by The Times.
  • Under the guidance of Mr. Baquet and a handpicked group of veteran editors, you will receive the rare opportunity to learn the judgment, skills and techniques needed to excel at investigative journalism from the best in the business.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet
  • You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue
  • Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here. 

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered. 

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  1. What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  2. Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  3. Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  4. What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  5. What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  6. Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor new work visas for the fellowship, but we may consider you if you have an existing work visa or a valid student visa that can be extended via Optional Practical Training

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis. 

Keep in mind that the fellowships are very competitive and generate a high level of interest. We won’t be able to accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. Nor will we acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

These positions are represented by the NewsGuild of NY

job.title: Manager, AI Strategy & Enablement
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Manager, AI Strategy & Enablement will help execute Marketing's AI strategy by turning approved priorities into tools and workflows that teams can use. You will identify opportunities where AI can improve work, recommend whether AI, process changes, or conventional software are the better approach, and build and configure solutions directly.

Quality, business impact, adoption, and time saved will determine how we measure success, not the number of tools used or launched.

You will sit on the Marketing team and report to the Managing Director, MarTech & AI. You will work across Marketing and regularly collaborate with Enterprise IT, Product, Data, Information Security, Legal, Privacy, and Procurement teams. This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can expect to come into the office three days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Identify opportunities to automate or improve Marketing work and translate ambiguous business problems into practical use cases.

  • Recommend whether AI, process changes, or conventional software are the best approach to each problem.

  • Lead assigned AI projects from discovery through rollout and ongoing improvement, managing requirements, timelines, owners, dependencies, risks, and success measures.

  • Build, configure, test, and improve AI tools and workflows using approved enterprise, low-code, and development tools.

  • Apply established standards for instructions, reference materials, data, permissions, testing, monitoring, human oversight, and failure handling.

  • Partner with technical teams when solutions require production engineering, data access, integrations, or complex system architecture.

  • Create role-specific documentation and enablement, track adoption and impact, and use the results to improve tools, workflows, and training.

  • Evaluate AI tools and vendors for business fit, quality, integration requirements, risk, and cost. Work with governance partners to ensure solutions meet established legal, privacy, security, data, and AI oversight requirements.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience in product or program management, digital transformation, marketing technology, automation, enablement, or a related field.

  • 2+ years of experience applying generative AI tools to business problems and workflows.

  • Working knowledge of AI agents and related concepts, with experience building or configuring agents, automations, retrieval systems, or AI-enabled workflows.

  • Experience leading cross-functional work from discovery and prototyping through implementation and adoption.

  • Experience translating ambiguous business problems into requirements, implementation plans, and measurable outcomes.

  • Experience evaluating AI quality, privacy, security, data governance, legal risk, and AI-human workflows, and explaining technical concepts to non-technical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience creating evaluation methods for AI outputs and using the results to improve instructions, context, tools, or workflow design.

  • Experience with AI-enabled productivity, knowledge, automation, and development tools such as Notion, Glean, Gemini Notebook, Make, Replit, or Cursor.

  • Experience in Marketing, Marketing Operations, or MarTech, with familiarity in vendor assessment, procurement, contracts, and enterprise technology governance.

Our mission in BOE is to provide the best experience to our internal and external clients.

You will report to the Sr. Director, BOE and partner with the Executive Director, BOE. This is a hybrid role based in the NYC office.

  • You will lead a team of client coordinators, developing skills, managing capacity planning, staffing, coverage.

job.description:

It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Job Description

The New York Times' Marketing team is looking for a Manager, Event Campaign Production to be the operational engine of the event marketing campaign and production assets. You will oversee the daily creative workflow — from receiving direction from the Director to ensuring the Creative team delivers the right assets, on brief, on brand, and on time. They are the connective tissue between strategy and execution, translating campaign priorities into clear assignments and keeping every moving part accountable. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Director, Event Campaign Strategy and Production. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

About the Role

You will be hands-on, someone who excels at process and clarity. As the Manager, Event Campaign Production, you do not attend external or client-facing partner meetings independently, but operate with authority within the production workflow. You will direct creative output, managing vendor relationships daily, and overseeing the project management infrastructure that keeps the campaign on track.

Responsibilities:

  • Be the primary daily point of direction for the Creative team — assigning work, setting task-level priorities, and reviewing output against the brief and brand standards.
  • Translate campaign direction from the Director into clear, applicable briefs and assignments for the Creative team and external vendors.
  • Build the Marketing Notion Board — the central project management tool tracking all creative tasks, owners, statuses, and deadlines across every active campaign.
  • Manage the creative production timeline for each event, from initial brief through final asset delivery.
  • Coordinate daily workflow across internal creative teams, external vendors, and agency partners to keep production moving without bottlenecks.
  • Brief the NYT Communications Systems team on landing page and event page updates and manage the production timeline for those deliverables.
  • Be the primary daily contact for external creative vendors and production agencies, under the strategic direction of the Director and Production Lead.
  • Manage the review and approval workflow for all campaign assets — scheduling reviews, coordinating stakeholder feedback, and tracking revisions to completion.
  • Manage the timeline, asset coordination, and deliverable tracking for the post-event sizzle reel in collaboration with the Copywriter and Director.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience in creative production, project management, or campaign operations
  • 3+ years of experience coordinating review and approval workflows across multiple company partners
  • Track record managing complex multi-asset campaigns with many simultaneous moving parts
  • Experience briefing and managing external vendors and creative agencies daily
  • Process-minded with the instinct to create structure where it is missing
  • Working knowledge of the full marketing asset landscape: digital, print, video, social, email, and experiential

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Exposure to live event or in-show production
  • Experience with events, media, or a marketing environment
  • Proficiency with project management tools — Monday.com

job.title: Manager, Measurement Analytics
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Job Description

The New York Times advertising department is looking for a Manager of Measurement Analytics. As a strategic and data-driven individual, you will transform our vast data resources into compelling narratives. These narratives will explain the unique value of our platform and products, focused on campaign performance. You will be a central hub of knowledge, applying deep analysis of our audience and ad products to empower our Sales, Strategy and Product teams. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Senior Director, Measurements, Audience and Insights. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

You will evolve how we measure and increase media and creative across a portfolio of diverse clients. This collaborative and strategic role will work with top tier advertising clients. You will also work with Sales, Sales Planning, Ad Product, Audience Insights, and Strategy teams. The goal is to achieve results to promote relationships with marketers and increase ad revenue. Furthermore, You will work with our Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Product Marketing teams to create and validate measurement solutions supporting new lower funnel advertising solutions.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop expertise in the full suite of NYT research capabilities and measurement products that deliver important performance metrics across the full marketing funnel, to current and potential clients.
  • Lead meta-analyses that merge different first-party and third-party data sources to create unified, powerful narratives about The New York Times advertising platform and its audience.
  • Monitor key datasets to identify latest trends, package them into applicable insights, and communicate findings to support go-to-market strategies and client conversations.
  • Translate complex analytical findings into clear insights and present for both technical and non-technical partners, including senior leadership.
  • Perform ad hoc analysis using data tools and 3rd party datasets to answer critical business questions from Sales, Strategy, and Measurement teams.
  • Be an important consultative partner to Analytics teams, providing expert user feedback to guide the design of our first-party data dashboards and tools.
  • Contribute to the development of new measurement capabilities, metrics, and frameworks that measure the value of our evolving suite of advertising products.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in data analytics, media insights, ad tech, or a related quantitative field.
  • Experience fielding measurement analysis, and an understanding of solutions that help report on performance from Awareness to Conversions (e.g., Brand Lift studies, Content Evaluation, Sales Lift, Incrementality, MTA etc.) with vendors such as Kantar, Brand Metrics, ABCS Insights, Lucid, Nielsen etc.
  • Experience working with data clean room solutions (e.g., LiveRamp, Snowflake) for measurement and audience activation
  • Experience translating complex data into applicable insights for non-technical audiences.
  • Experience with SQL
  • Experience working directly with sales or client-facing teams.

job.description:

The New York Times is looking for an experienced journalist to helm the Mid-Atlantic Region as its bureau chief.

You understand the issues that are playing out across the coverage zone — which includes DC, Delaware, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, Ohio and Kentucky. You see news moments as opportunities to show off your expertise through clear and vivid writing.

As the authority on your region and a leader among peers, you will conceive and direct coverage plans and identify revelatory follows and deeper work on breaking news.

You will come brimming with ideas for engaging stories in many formats that help to explain and visualize the region for our readers, driving the conversation on topics of import to the region and the country.

You must be able to write quickly, clearly and accurately on deadline. Willingness to embrace a variety of formats and embracing new forms of storytelling is essential. You must be collaborative with colleagues.

This position may be based in-office in Washington D.C or remote in the region, pending business needs. In-office would include regular attendance in the office, four days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • You will drive a sense of what is coming next, both by watching themes in their region and a calendar of what news and events are coming.
  • You will oversee what is happening in your region on a constant basis, by scanning competition and guiding editors on the relevance of stories coming from their region.
  • You will be the Times' ambassador to your region or bureau; demonstrate and share your authority and expertise with colleagues looking for knowledge on your region. Be a leader to fellow regional reporters with questions.
  • You will cultivate a deep source network of authorities, politicians, sheriffs, union reps, cultural figures, law enforcement, agency representatives and beyond – positioning yourself to tap a source in a given news moment, from scoops to interviews and real-time updates. Discern which stories to write to further develop and engage your sources.

The Science desk of the New York Times is looking for a creative, energetic reporter to cover the world of space exploration. We’re looking for a heartbeat of stories that capture the wonder, the successes and failures, the big dreams and big personalities of the space world, whether at private space companies like SpaceX or in the orbit of NASA. The ideal candidate will be an accomplished multimedia journalist who can report and produce both text and video. You are adept at moving quickly on breaking news including launch coverage and other fixtures of the daily beat, but also able to identify stories with visual potential and eager to pursue a wide array of types of stories, including developing ambitious visual enterprise stories.

This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in a New York Times bureau four days each week. There may also be flexibility to work remotely per departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Pitch, report and produce news, enterprise and explanatory stories in both text and video, including on-camera reporting.

  • Contribute to live and developing-news coverage, including launches, mission milestones, anomalies and breaking developments.

  • Help to develop well-structured scripts for linear videos and combine text and visuals in multimedia formats.

  • Monitor wires, local and regional outlets, social media feeds and other sources for developing storylines and reporting opportunities that help explain the beat and advance ongoing storylines, keeping us ahead of national competitors.

  • Cultivate existing sources and develop new ones to land exclusive stories to cover this beat authoritatively.

  • Work collaboratively across the newsroom including with editors, video producers, video and photo editors and motion graphics colleagues to develop stories from pitch through publication.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • 5+ years of experience covering space or science-related topics 

  • Experience covering complex subjects with elegance, sensitivity and fairness

  • A portfolio that demonstrates you are well-versed in a range of topics, and have a growing circle of sources across storylines

  • Demonstrated understanding of the video production process and creative instincts that go beyond traditional text formats

  • A willingness to be flexible as the news demands and the newsroom's needs evolve

  • An openness to trying new storytelling approaches, and a demonstrated ability to communicate clearly

job.title: Newsroom Operations Manager
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Role

The New York Times is looking for an operational owner and highly organized self-starter to join our Newsroom Operations team as an Operations Manager. You will provide hands-on support and oversight of numerous logistics involved in the smooth daily operation of several assigned department(s) – News Platforms and Data, T Magazine and others.

We are looking for a quick learner and creative problem solver who is capable of handling the ever-changing demands of a fast-paced newsroom environment. You will guide tasks across the finish line for the desks in the newsroom. Key to this will be supporting members of our masthead and our journalists with a variety of daily responsibilities and short- and long-term projects. This includes being at the center of on-the-ground coordination of both in-office and offsite events, ensuring execution of on-site logistics and meals for key news coverage events, ensuring that administrative operational tasks are completed by internal deadlines so that operations on the desk run continually and uninterrupted. You will report directly to a Senior Manager of Newsroom Operations.

This role will be Hybrid, with a required in-office presence of 4 days a week. The schedule of these 4 days can fluctuate based on the needs of the desks, and during some peak news cycles, you may be required to be on site for 5 days during those weeks.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the primary, accountable operational contact for members of the masthead, department heads, and journalists, resolving operational roadblocks independently.
  • Responsible for on-site setup of various in-office events including mock elections, team all hands gatherings of staff from around the country, team lunches and various similar events, and also serving as a production coordinator for all such events. including live coverage setups, catering logistics, seating arrangements, and equipment deployment during breaking news cycles.
  • Oversee complex equipment setups for assigned desks, special coverage teams, and events, ensuring that all hardware, workstation, and specialized technical configurations in real-time to ensure journalists have fully functioning tools.
  • Work with the Newsroom Finance team to help create annual budgets and provide oversight of those budgets, including monthly closes, supplying additional financial reports.
  • Manage work and vacation schedules and maintain accurate time banks in Workday, and work with Payroll to verify time banks for transfers, departures, and annual payouts.
  • Manage a travel calendar and be sure anyone traveling on assignment is properly set up on the company's business travel accident insurance.
  • Approve expenses and travel costs in Workday.
  • Manage and process freelancers and vendors' payments, working with the Contracts Manager
  • Oversee accounts payable and accounts receivable for assigned departments
  • Work with HR and recruiting teams to assist with position management transactions
  • Facilitate Workday management, including onboarding new employees and helping them to get the training, equipment, and information they need
  • Keep staffing lists, org charts, and various email distribution lists up to date with any staffing changes in the department
  • Purchase supplies and equipment, keep track of all departmental expenses, including capital spending and outside vendor spending
  • Work in Zip for independent contractor onboarding, sourcing events and purchasing
  • Be available for a variety of tasks that come up, often urgently, including troubleshooting, assisting writers and editors,with on-site and off-site needs, etc.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in an operational or administrative role
  • Ability to drive projects forward
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Experience dealing with detailed and confidential and private concerns
  • You can work and keep an optimistic attitude while maintaining a keen sense of urgency
  • Be accessible after hours or on weekends when circumstances require
  • Impeccable organizational and time management skills; ability to multitask, prioritize and work under deadline pressure
  • Ability to work with all levels of management and staff and manage the needs of a team of 100+ employees and leaders

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of training and experience
  • Able to research resources, troubleshoot, and solve problems
  • Workday experience

You will manage the Politics news report during the evening, coordinating with leadership and the subject matter and live editors, serving as the primary liaison. You will edit a wide range of copy including major enterprise pieces and breaking news. You will launch reporters on breaking stories and start live blogs with speed and good judgement when the news rises. You are curious and passionate about meeting our audience needs. You are excited to collaborate with departments across the newsroom, experimenting with different storytelling formats to find the best ways to connect our journalism with audiences around the world. This is a collaborative desk; you must be able to navigate input from colleagues across the newsroom and develop superb relationships with the news desk, live, audience, video, photo and print teams, among other collaborators. 

You are currently expected to work weekdays, from afternoon through evening, and must be capable of stepping in at all stages of the editing process, from a story’s conception through its publication. 

This is an in-office position, based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

job.title: Open Source Reporting, Graphics (Graphics Multimedia Editor)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times Graphics team is looking for a reporter with extensive open-source and investigative reporting skills to turn raw evidence into impactful visual stories. You have a track record for uncovering exclusive information off the news.

The Graphics team is a leader in using spatial and visual techniques on investigative stories, and we're looking for someone who is passionate about accountability journalism using cutting-edge reporting techniques.

Below are a few examples of the kinds of stories that you will be a part of:
  • An exclusive look at the failed columns of the Midtown Manhattan near-collapse
  • A 3-D analysis of why firefighters' lines of sight were limited in the deadly LaGuardia Crash
  • An investigation into the mass graves in Syria
  • An investigation into the causes of a Miami building collapse
  • A spatial investigation into a deadly fire in the Bronx
  • A forensic analysis of an apartment building collapse in the Turkey earthquake
Working with journalists on the Graphics team and across the newsroom, you will play an important role in shaping visual reconstructions and investigations that rely on spatial analysis or use 3-D modeling. You will gather and analyze evidence for stories across a wide range of topics for both quick-turn stories as well as longer-term enterprise.

You will be expected to take the initiative in leading major storylines, with the goal of uncovering new or exclusive findings across multiple visual story formats. You should be curious and driven, and be comfortable with moving between solo deep dives and fast-paced, cross-desk collaborations.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days a week.

Responsibilities:
  • Bring core OSINT fluency to the desk's coverage: geolocation, chronolocation, satellite/aerial imagery analysis, audio-video research, and more.
  • Analyze a variety of data sources, including satellite and aerial imagery, flight/vessel tracking data, social media platforms and radio scanner data.
  • Vet and build relationships with a network of sources on stories.
  • Generate ideas that help the team develop custom tooling to automate open-source reporting for analyzing and visualizing evidence.
  • Find new ways to report beyond the standard OSINT toolkit, by using computational techniques, including through machine learning, computer vision and approved AI tools.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to an Assistant Editor on the Graphics desk.
Basic Qualifications:
  • 5+ years of relevant experience as an investigative reporter, open-source researcher or forensic expert.
  • Proven experience conducting open-source investigations by sourcing audio and visual evidence across a variety of platforms.
  • Experience producing accountability journalism, with a strong portfolio.
  • Experience producing clear copy about the visual evidence on tight deadlines.
  • Experience verifying user-generated content from social media for authenticity.
  • Skilled in building timelines using a variety of sources, including official statements and metadata from user-generated content.
  • Familiarity with open-source intelligence tools and techniques like Google Earth, satellite imagery platforms, scanner audio data, flight or vessel tracking, or similar.
Preferred Qualifications:
  • Experience working both independently and collaboratively while managing multiple research threads.
  • Experience with advanced tools for reporting, such as QGIS, Blender for 3-D scene reconstructions, data analysis methods, audio and image forensics tools.
  • Adept at creating clear, visual explainers piecing together complex findings.
  • Familiarity with programming and custom tool development.
  • Familiarity with Adobe Suite and Figma.
  • Experience with web scraping tools and working with APIs.
  • Experience using command line tools.
  • Willingness and flexibility to work evenings and weekends as needed.
This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.   REQ-020693

job.title: Operations & Engagement Coordinator, Agency Development & Sales Strategy
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Job Description

About the Team

The mission of the Agency Development & Sales Strategy team is to leverage agencies as our next big source of incremental revenue growth. Our strategy is to create the conditions for our Sales Organization to drive more revenue from agency partners. Our approach is threefold: drive demand by changing perceptions; enable commerce by reducing friction and creating incentives; and standardize ways of working in order to scale. As a small but growing team, we have outsized impact by leveraging other internal teams, including Industry Marketing, Sales, Revenue Operations, and Programmatic Ops.

About the Role

You will report to the Associate Director, Agency Development & Sales Strategy. This role is based in our New York office and follows a hybrid work schedule.

As the Operations & Engagement Coordinator, you will support the operational core of the team. You will help execute day-to-day processes, coordinate projects, and manage logistics that enable successful, long-term partnerships with advertising agencies, with a particular focus on agency-facing activations. You will ensure that information, timelines and logistics stay aligned. You will assist in setting up and maintaining internal systems and workflows that translate strategy into successful agency partnership.

This role is ideal for a highly organized professional with strong project coordination skills, attention to detail, and an interest in agency partnerships, engagements, and media. Success in this role is defined by reliable execution, clear communication, and the smooth, scalable operation of our processes.

Responsibilities

Change agency perceptions of The Times

Agency Engagements: Support the planning and coordination of agency-specific engagements (e.g., Lunch & Learns, leadership gatherings, summits); managing logistics, invitations, venue and vendor coordination, materials preparation, and day-of execution

Scheduling: Maintain an event calendar, track deadlines, manage checklists, coordinate internal stakeholders (Sales, Marketing, Research, Creative), and ensure follow-up actions and reporting are completed on time

Outbound Communications: Help create external-facing materials – such as competitive reports and presentation decks – to strengthen agency relationships

Enable commerce by reducing friction and creating incentives

Agency Partnerships: Support the development and execution of revenue-generating deals with agency partners (e.g., tracking deliverables, updating status docs, coordinating approvals)

Strategic Implementation: Support the roadmapping, scoping and executing of strategic initiatives and work streams aligned with team goals

Prioritization and Planning: Coordinate with Sales, Revenue Operations, and Programmatic teams to identify opportunities, propose priorities, and ensure alignment on agency engagement strategies

Standardize ways of working in order to scale

Workflows: Help design and refine workflows and processes that streamline repeated tasks and external-facing materials, using AI-driven tools and automations where possible

Industry Research: Monitor industry trends and agency needs, collaborating with Sales Ops and Measurement teams to generate insights that enhance The Times' value proposition.

Lifecycle Support: Support the lifecycle of projects by helping to organize information, schedule meetings, capture notes and action items, and follow up with stakeholders to keep work moving

Accountability: Use and help maintain tools and processes (e.g., CRM and reporting dashboards) required to associate our engagement efforts with real traction with agencies (e.g., RFPs, IOs)

Basic Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of experience in operations or project coordination, event planning, business strategy support, business development support, or a related field.

  • Experience coordinating events or programs (professional, academic, or extracurricular), including logistics and communication with participants

  • Experience working collaboratively across teams and build positive working relationships

  • High attention to detail and willingness to roll up your sleeves on both administrative and project-based work

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of experience in Media, Advertising, Media Agencies, or Tech

  • 1+ years experience with project management software tools (e.g., Monday.com, Coda)

  • Comfort working with data in spreadsheets and basic reporting tools; familiarity with CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce)

job.title: Operations Manager
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Role:

The New York Times is looking for someone to join our Newsroom Operations team. We are looking for someone who can handle the demands of a fast-paced news environment and can work under sometimes ambiguous circumstances. 

The Operations Manager will work with Shows and Visuals, but also assist other departments at the center of visual journalism at The Times. The work of these journalists — along with visual efforts across the newsroom — is a pillar of our reporting that has a large and engaged audience. You will help support these journalists with a variety of daily responsibilities and short- and long-term projects and coordinate with this group's other operations managers. You will be responsible for ensuring that day-to-day on-site operational tasks are completed in a timely manner to support the needs of department managers and staff.

The Operations Manager's work is critical in supporting the journalism produced at The New York Times and all tasks, whether daily, weekly or one-off are greatly valued. You will report to a senior manager of Newsroom Operations.

This role will be Hybrid, with a required in-office presence of 4 days a week. The schedule of these 4 days can fluctuate based on the needs of the desks, and during some peak news cycles, you may be required to be on site for 5 days during those weeks.

Responsibilities:

  • Support editors during breaking news and timely news events, ensuring that our journalists have what they need to work
  • Coordinate, and help plan and execute culture-building activities for the departments held both on and off site
  • Manage and approve staff expenses in Workday, communicating and observing policy limits, correcting categorizations and cost centers
  • Manage work and vacation schedules, maintain accurate time banks in Workday and work with Payroll to verify timebanks for transfers, departures and annual payouts
  • Oversee accounts payable and account receivable for the department
  • Be a move coordinator, working with Facilities and other departments on internal desk moves/assignments
  • Work with HR and Recruiting teams to assist with position management transactions
  • Facilitate Workday management, including onboarding new employees and helping them to get the training, equipment and information they need
  • Purchase supplies and equipment, keep track of all departmental expenses, including capital spending and outside vendor spending
  • Work in Zip for independent contractor onboarding, sourcing events and purchasing
  • Manage and pay freelancers and vendors
  • Hands-on management of a variety of tasks that come up: troubleshooting, assisting producers, visuals teams and editors
  • Manage set up of departmental special events, and on-site tasks to ensure events are set up properly
  • You will organize, prioritize, multitask and work under deadline pressure
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience in an operational or administrative role
  • Work under deadline pressure and be accessible after hours or weekends as breaking news demands
  • Professional judgment with respect to detail and confidentiality
  • High energy working style and optimistic attitude, with a keen sense of urgency
  • Able to work with all levels of management and staff in a highly professional manner; ability to manage the various needs of a team of 100+ employees and leaders

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree, or equivalent combination of training and experience
  • Experience with Workday, Zip and the freelance payment system
  • Experience with G-Suite
  • Willingness to learn and support the team across all tasks.
  • Able to research resources, troubleshoot and solve problems
  • Calm under pressure
  • Patience and a sense of humor

job.title: Paperhandler (Casual)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

#LI-Onsite 

The New York Times is an international brand that prints nine daily newspapers. These are printed at our Print Plant in College Point, Queens, and distributed to the New York Metropolitan area and the Eastern Seaboard. Our daily work is guided by our mission and values. 

We are looking for a part-time casual Paperhandler with in-depth knowledge of all Paperhandler equipment and multiple newsprint roll types for commercial printing. You will undergo a training period, after which you will read work orders or receive instructions to determine work assignments, material, and equipment requirements. You will be reporting to the Deputy Plant Manager and you will report to work onsite at our Printing facility in College Point, Queens, New York. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Ensure that all paper rolls for the nine daily newspapers are handled and transported safely. 
  • Work in a Union production environment with deadlines on a daily basis. 
  • Take inventory of paper rolls and prepare them for use in the printing facility. 
  • Ensure that all paper rolls are stacked according to safety regulations. 
  • Operate Paperhandler equipment safely while working with extreme care and caution. 
  • You must maintain a clean environment in the paper storage area. 
  • You must follow all safety guidelines and report any accidents or incidents to the supervisor. 

Basic Qualifications: 

  • Must be willing to work flexible hours in a Union production environment on a daily basis. 
  • Must have a high school diploma or equivalent. 
  • Can stand and walk for 8-10 hours per shift and lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Must be willing to undergo a background check. 

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • 1+ year of experience in a production environment. 
  • The ability to work with different types of paperhandler equipment. 
  • The ability to work in a team environment. 

This role is a union role represented by the Paperhandlers and Straighteners Union.

job.title: Product Marketing Manager, News
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for a motivated, collaborative, creative, analytical, and user-centric product marketer to help deepen audience engagement with our News product, with a particular focus on community and sharing features in the core Times app.

Reporting to the Director of Product Marketing, News, you will be embedded within the Community News Product team as the dedicated product marketing lead. You will partner closely with product, design, and newsroom stakeholders to leverage our community and sharing experiences to drive daily habit and new audience growth.

Your core focus will be the Community News Product team, with opportunities to support other editorially driven News product teams as priorities require. You will combine strategic leadership with hands-on execution: helping shape the product roadmap, developing go-to-market strategies, leading cross-functional launches, and creating lifecycle marketing programs that help our readers feel connected to our journalism, our newsroom, and each other.

This role is a hybrid position, where you'll be in the office three times per week in our NYC Headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Act as the embedded product marketing lead for the Community News Product team, partnering with product, design, and newsroom stakeholders to define the role of commenting, community features, and sharing in the News product experience.

  • Partner with editors, reporters, and newsroom leadership to increase journalist participation in comments and community spaces, ensuring those interactions align with editorial values while deepening trust and engagement among readers.

  • Validate unique market and audience opportunities within News community and sharing experiences by gathering insight into reader and reporter perspectives, creating audience segmentation frameworks and personas that build empathy for how people participate in and benefit from community features and C2C sharing.

  • Craft positioning and messaging and develop go-to-market strategies for evolving community and sharing features, such as commenting improvements, reporter-led interactions, and sharing prompts. Use market and customer insights to design campaigns and in-product programs that increase engagement, repeat visits, and new audience growth.

  • Create and increase habitual product usage and retention by monitoring KPIs, conducting message tests and experiments, and supplementing quantitative data with qualitative feedback from readers and newsroom partners.

  • Collaborate with other News product teams. Lead and influence cross-functional teams without formal authority, helping stakeholders align on shared goals and balance growth, user experience, and editorial integrity.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Director of Product Marketing, News.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of related experience in marketing, product marketing, or product management, including at least 2 years of insights-driven go-to-market experience.

  • Experience with the product development lifecycle and operating within product-led teams; experience driving successful go-to-market strategies for product and feature launches, aligning product marketing and messaging to a larger brand narrative, and translating brand strategy into product marketing output.

  • Experience working in newsroom or editorial environments, driving audience and engagement with journalism or community features.

  • Demonstrated experience partnering with editorial or audience teams to design and promote community or social experiences (comments, reactions, forums) that deepen engagement.

  • Lead teams without formal authority, collaborating across product, newsroom, marketing, and data disciplines to achieve shared outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Digital subscription, content, newsletter, or mobile app experience.

  • Experience with referral programs, C2C community management, or two-sided marketplaces.

  • Distill essential insights from research and create clear and thoughtful market requirement documents and creative briefs.

  • Balance creative, conceptual thinking with data-driven projects; excel in creative and analytical environments; identify and assess success metrics.

  • Capacity for, and interest in, flexing across both planning and execution, shifting between strategic direction-setting and hands-on go-to-market work as needed.

  • Demonstrated collaboration with different disciplines; build trust and relationships quickly, with empathy for customers and expertise in understanding user experience.

  • Experience working on products where brand and editorial integrity are competitive advantages, maintaining trust while experimenting with new community formats and engagement tactics.

job.title: Reporter Fellow, Local Investigations - Mississippi, Louisiana, & Arkansas
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The Times is looking for reporters with a local story idea who want to investigate it under the editing guidance of Dean Baquet, The Times’s former executive editor, and a group of veteran investigative editors.

The goal of the Local Investigative Fellowship is to provide fellows the opportunity to learn the ways and means of investigative reporting from some of the best in the business. Our fellows will be based in the communities where they are reporting and make periodic trips to The Times’s offices for training and support.

This one year program is for reporters who have a local investigative story idea rooted in Louisiana, Mississippi, or Arkansas.  

This is a NY Guild role based in Louisiana, Mississippi, or Arkansas.

Responsibilities:

  • Spend a year producing signature investigative work focused on your state or region that will be published by The Times.
  • Under the guidance of Mr. Baquet and a handpicked group of veteran editors, you will receive the rare opportunity to learn the judgment, skills and techniques needed to excel at investigative journalism from the best in the business.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet
  • You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue
  • Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here. 

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered. 

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  • What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  • Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  • Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  • What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  • What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  • Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor new work visas for the fellowship, but we may consider you if you have an existing work visa or a valid student visa that can be extended via Optional Practical Training

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis. 

Keep in mind that the fellowships are very competitive and generate a high level of interest. We won’t be able to accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. Nor will we acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

These positions are represented by the NewsGuild of NY

job.title: Reporting Fellow
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as a reporter.

The Times is looking for fellows who have strong writing and reporting fundamentals, and who are eager to learn and work with others. The program is an opportunity to stretch your journalistic skills alongside the world’s best editors and reporters. You would be assigned to a news or features department, and directly report to editors on your desk. 

Many of your stories may take the form of traditional reported articles. But you could also write live updates and explainers, as well as pieces that put visuals first. You should be eager to participate in these different kinds of storytelling and to engage with readers in a variety of ways.

The most competitive candidates will be those who submit a variety of published clips that show excellence — in breaking news, high-impact news stories, features and/or thoughtful, reported analytical pieces. 

These are in-office positions and include regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed.

Responsibilities: 

  • Deliver a mix of breaking news and enterprise assignments
  • Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship
  • Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional journalism experience, excluding internships
  • Can demonstrate clear prose, evocative writing, and original and impactful reporting

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Record of multiple news internships or equivalent news experience

To apply, upload a résumé, cover letter and five published clips. Include the full text of your clips, not just the links. The application will prompt you when to upload your materials. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or do not follow these instructions will not be considered. 

In your cover letter, briefly indicate what desks you are most interested in working on. While we take note of preferences, we determine assignments based on need and skillset. 

You may apply to only one fellowship position per year. For instance, if you apply as a reporter, you should not apply for any other positions in the fellowship. Duplicate applications will be discarded.

You must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor work visas for the fellowship, but we will consider applicants with valid work authorization or a valid student visa that can be extended with Optional Practical Training.

The application deadline is 5 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on Nov. 20.

The Times Fellowship generates a high level of interest, so we cannot acknowledge the status of applications upon receipt or during the vetting process, which can take eight weeks or more. We cannot accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

Reporting fellows may be placed in one of the following areas of coverage. All fellows, including the International reporting fellow, are based in New York unless otherwise noted: 

  • Business
  • Climate
  • Culture
  • Express (breaking news and trends)
  • International
  • Investigations
  • Metro
  • National (one National fellow will focus on disability issues)
  • Obituaries
  • Politics
  • Science
  • Technology (based in San Francisco)
  • Washington (based in Washington)
  • Well

The Business reporter will serve as the David Carr Fellow in honor of the late David Carr, a groundbreaking voice in journalism and media at The Times who was also a passionate advocate for early-career writers.

The Washington reporter will serve as the David E. Rosenbaum Fellow in honor of the late David E. Rosenbaum, a prize-winning Times reporter known for his illuminating coverage of Washington and politics who was a role model for countless journalists.

The fellowship program will begin on or about June 7, 2027, and end on May 26, 2028, subject to satisfactory performance. There is no guarantee of a full-time position upon completion of the program. 

For more information about the Times Fellowship, visit here.

job.title: Research Director, Audience Insights, Content Insights
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Research Director, Content Insights will have a critical role informing the creation, iteration and measurement of video and video products at the New York Times. You will lead all video measurement research to inform our understanding of how video content performs across platforms, surfaces, and audience segments. You will oversee the end-to-end measurement of video effectiveness, from individual videos to longer-form recurring concepts, and translate data into relevant strategies that inform production, distribution, and editorial decisions. You will also work with product, design, and editorial teams to improve on-platform video experiences.

You will report to the Managing Director, News Products on the Audience Insights Team and will collaborate with partners across the Newsroom. You understand how to blend market research and user research methods and practices into actionable insights for an entire mission.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop audience research to support the creation and growth of video franchises and recurring shows. Drawing on research methods used by production studios and streaming networks, you'll conduct research that can inform greenlight decisions — including concept testing, pilot testing, audience appetite studies, and competitive landscape analysis.
  • Partner with video leadership to evaluate whether a format, host, or editorial premise has the demand to sustain an audience over time. For existing shows, help build longitudinal tracking that monitors audience health: loyalty, satisfaction, and reasons for churn.
  • Help build a video performance tracking program grounded in survey-based measurement, tracking metrics like awareness, recall, engagement, and sentiment among defined audience segments over time.
  • Working alongside analytics teams, you'll help establish benchmarks, monitor performance across all surfaces where video is published (owned and operated, social, streaming), and develop a consistent cadence of reporting that gives editorial, product, and business stakeholders a reliable read on how our videos are landing with audiences.
  • Lead quantitative and qualitative research among target audiences to support video strategy and format development (e.g., format preference studies, thumbnail and title concept tests, viewer satisfaction studies). Partner with video producers and editors to understand their needs and scope appropriate methodologies, from brief development through questionnaire design, survey launch, and insight delivery.
  • Manage multiple research projects and ad-hoc requests simultaneously, developing timelines and planning resources.
  • Partner or lead research on other editorial projects and franchises, such as newsletters, podcasts, or other emerging products
  • Collaborate with research partners, analytics teams, and company partners.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the quality, speed, and effect of video measurement, including recommending new vendors, tools, and methodologies.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in market research, user research, or consumer insights, with an emphasis on multimodal and product research.
  • Proficiency in both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies and experience with continuous improvement and new ideas.
  • Experience leading all facets of a tracking program, including vendor relationships, questionnaire development, data mining, and reporting.
  • Fluency in analyzing large datasets, identifying insights, and creating clear reports.
  • Experience developing timelines across multiple projects, applying project management skills.
  • Experience managing external research partners/vendors.
  • Experience with visualization tools and creating compelling presentations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • B.A./B.S. degree.

job.title: Research Lead, New AI Products & Platforms
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Mission Overview & Responsibilities: 

We are looking for a Research Lead with a passion for ensuring that reader-centric insights are at the heart of the product development process. You will lead a variety of end-to-end research projects that drive strategy for the New A.I. Products and Platforms (NAPP) Mission. You will work with a cross-functional digital product team, including Product, Design, Editorial, Engineering and Marketing. You will report to the Managing Director of News Products and Audience Insights at The New York Times.

The mission of the New York Times Audience Insights team is to help The Times grow by understanding our audience. The Audience Insights team is centralized team of researchers working with teams across The New York Times. We utilize product, human-centered design, innovation, market and UX research, and we draw from principles in the social sciences (Psychology, Anthropology, Sociology and Behavioral Economics).

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City office.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead a human-centered design approach for products teams, inspiring colleagues to build innovative product features grounded in user needs to drive NAPP and company goals.

  • Use research-based insights and GenAI tools for rapid prototype iteration.

  • Own evaluation for quality and editorial integrity: Create frameworks to assess the success of A.I. prototypes and products.

  • Build innovative solutions using AI tools to support certain parts of the research process.

  • Champion A.I. innovation and ethics: Stay up to date with industry trends, new research methodologies, LLM advancements, and emerging technologies. Champion the ethical and responsible use of AI, ensuring our tools uphold our standards of accuracy and objectivity.

  • Complement research with behavioral data, proprietary and industry research, and A/B testing results to provide a holistic view of our users.

  • Work with Audience Insights researchers across News Product, Marketing, Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic and Games to identify opportunities to collaborate and avoid duplicative product work.

  • Manage external research vendors to support moderation, fieldwork, and analysis, ensuring high-quality and efficient project execution.

  • Contribute to the collaborative culture of Audience Insights and the NAPP Mission; help The New York Times understand, and build empathy for, our audiences.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications: 

  • 8+ years of research and insights experience.

  • Experience researching chat interfaces or GenAI search tools and using a range of GenAI tools and features in your work.

  • Experience moderating qualitative research and facilitating brainstorms and workshops with cross-functional partners.

  • Mastery of a range of research methods . These methods include participatory design, in-person and remote interviews, ethnographies, co-creation, and user-initiated feedback tools. Additionally, surveys, card-sorting, and usability studies are also part of the range.

  • Experience executing qualitative and quantitative research and selecting the right approach based on the problem to be solved.

  • Experience synthesizing complex findings into compelling narratives and visualize insights for diverse audiences.

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Experience conducting research for early-stage 0-1 product development, helping teams identify opportunities, validate concepts, and shape new product experiences.

  • Experience working in rapid prototyping environments, using research to inform iterative product development and experimentation.

  • Experience building alignment among cross-functional stakeholders, including Product, Design, Engineering, Editorial, and Marketing partners.

  • Experience presenting to stakeholders, senior management, and fellow researchers.

  • A deep curiosity about the role of AI in shaping the future of information, media, and journalism.

We are looking for a Research Lead with experience ensuring that shopping-centric insights are at the heart of product development. You will lead a variety of end-to-end research projects that inform Wirecutter's strategy. Your projects will focus on helping connect our visitors to Wirecutter across the full shopping experience. Your research will inform audience strategy, content prioritization, and the Wirecutter Store, amongst other areas. You will be an important partner with Design, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Data, Editorial, guiding decision-making and informing the teams' strategies.

We at The New York Times seek the truth and help people understand the world. This mission is rooted in our belief that great journalism has the power to make each reader's life richer and more fulfilling, and all of society stronger and more just.

The mission of the New York Times Audience Insights team is to help The Times grow by understanding our audience. The Audience Insights team is a team of researchers that employ tools, methods and approaches across a wide variety of research domains, including product, human-centered design, innovation, market and UX research, and we draw from principles in the social sciences (Psychology, Anthropology, Sociology and Behavioral Economics). We believe that the best work is achieved when we support healthy work-life balance. We support people in managing their workload and encourage team members to take all of their personal and vacation time each year.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead research through a human-centered design approach to identify opportunity areas, alongside Product, Design, and Editorial teams
  • Test prototypes, create surveys, and run alpha and beta programs
  • Evaluate impact on trust and relationships with Wirecutter
  • Complement research with behavioral data, proprietary and industry research, and A/B testing results to provide a holistic view of our users.
  • Be a resource and partner to researchers across Marketing, Cooking, News Product, The Athletic and Games to identify opportunities to collaborate and avoid duplicative product work.
  • Manage external research vendors to support moderation, fieldwork, and analysis, ensuring high-quality and efficient project execution.
  • Contribute to the collaborative culture of Audience Insights and Wirecutter; help The New York Times understand, and build empathy for, our audiences.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Managing Director, Games and Wirecutter Audience Insights

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor of Arts/Bachelor of Science in a relevant field
  • 8+ years of research and insights experience.
  • 8+ years of experience implementing a range of research methods (qualitative and quantitative) and design thinking techniques based on the problem to be solved
  • 3+ years of experience in the e-commerce industry, or shopping experiences.
  • 3+ years of experience moderating qualitative research and facilitating brainstorms and workshops with partners.
  • 3+ years of experience summarizing complex findings into compelling narratives and visualize insights for diverse audiences with actionable insights.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience in the e-commerce industry, or shopping experiences
  • 2+ years of experience working on a product with a subscription-based model
  • 2+ years of experience using behavioral data alongside research (either qualitative or quantitative) to provide a holistic picture
  • Experience creating buy-in with cross-functional partners
  • 1+ years understanding the role of AI within the shopping experience

It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the role

As the Senior Analyst, Total Rewards (Data Insights & Modeling), you will be a strategic partner reporting directly to the SVP, Total Rewards. You will bridge the gap between complex data science and talent strategy, serving as a lead architect for our global compensation structures. You will go beyond traditional reporting to build and maintain the predictive models that forecast salary market movement, simulate compensation cycles, and drive pay equity outcomes. This position is pivotal in ensuring our compensation practices remain fair, equitable, and market-relevant, directly supporting our ability to attract and retain the world-class talent necessary to sustain The New York Times’s journalistic mission. 

Responsibilities

  • Strategize design and maintenance of global compensation structures using advanced data science and predictive analytics.
  • Develop sophisticated models for variable pay (AIP/LTI) and annual merit/bonus cycles under various business performance scenarios.
  • Build predictive models to forecast salary market movement and internal budget requirements.
  • Conduct statistically significant pay equity analyses to identify and remediate gaps across demographics.
  • Build and maintain automated Total Rewards benchmarking tools and executive dashboards.
  • Lead the advancement of data insight capabilities to support compensation analytics for the New York Times workforce.
  • Manage participation in external compensation surveys, including job matching and data validation.

Basic Qualifications

  • 5–8+ years of experience in Compensation or Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), with at least 3 years focused on advanced modeling.
  • Proficiency in statistical analysis (correlation and regression) and experience with HCM systems (e.g., Workday).
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel (VBA, Power Query, Complex Nested Formulas) and data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI, or Visier).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Human Resources or related field
  • Experience with SQL, Python, or R.
  • CCP (Certified Compensation Professional) or GRP certification.
