job.title: Senior Community Editor
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Every week, The New York Times hosts hundreds of conversations in our comments sections across a wide variety of topics and types of articles — from investigations and breaking news to features and service journalism. We are seeking a Senior Editor to work directly with reporters, writers and editors to build this community.

This role is designed for an editor who thrives in fast-paced environments, possesses sharp news judgment, and loves finding creative ways to bring reader voices into our journalism. You will be collaborating with editors and reporters to identify opportunities for them to participate in comments, editing posts for length, clarity and accessibility and finding appropriate places to embed conversations in our journalism. You will also work closely with the wider community team to ensure our editorial approach and workflow fits into evolving moderation and policy guidelines.

The ideal candidate is eager to experiment with new approaches to reader engagement, be comfortable training creative teams on technical concepts and is brimming with ideas for how to build and support online communities.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Identify articles and storylines that would benefit from journalist participation in the comments, and reach out to editors and reporters in advance of publication.
  • Edit posts for length, clarity and tone, helping to grow the number of journalists who are independently posting in creative ways that align with our style.
  • Collect high quality examples of reporter participation and help train the global newsroom on best practices.
  • Make Community team initiatives more visible and useful to the wider newsroom and enterprise by writing regular internal updates.
  • Build pathways to community surfaces by embedding comments across the report and help track their effectiveness.
  • Pitch and execute on community-first initiatives that deepen reader-reporter relationships, e.g. AMAs, UGC roundups
  • Collaborate with cross-functional partners to build and improve tools that make journalist participation easy and intuitive.
  • Help to develop guardrails and approaches for staff to participate in conversations about hot-button topics across the report.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Community Editorial Lead.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of editorial experience with news organizations or media companies
  • Excellent editorial judgment and project management skills
  • Demonstrated interest in the online community ecosystem
  • Passion for The New York Times mission and commitment to be part of our innovation and growth

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience training reporters and editors on digital tools and editorial approaches.
  • A proven ability to meet deadlines in a fast-paced news environment.
  • Editing samples of work you have assigned or played a significant role in shaping.

Wirecutter, a New York Times company, is the premier product recommendation service dedicated to rigorously testing and reviewing products to help readers make the best decisions for their lives. Building on our mission of trust and utility, the Wirecutter Store (wirecutterstore.nytimes.com) is our dedicated e-commerce destination, offering our audience for purchase a highly-curated selection of the exceptional products we recommend.

 

As we approach our busiest time of the year (Q4/Holiday Season), we are looking for two experienced Senior Temporary Customer Service Agents to join our team. You will be the customer-facing voice of the Wirecutter Store. You will ensure that our customers receive the same level of care, clarity, and reliability that they expect from Wirecutter's editorial recommendations.

 

You will report directly to the Ecommerce Operations Director. You will work with our Customer Experience Manager to resolve inquiries, refine support processes, and improve our helpdesk operations during the peak holiday shopping rush.

 

Schedule and Hours:

  • Base Hours: Up to 40 hours per business week.

  • Peak Season: An additional 10 hours on weekends during peak periods.

  • Available Shifts (subject to change):

    • Shift A: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM

    • Shift B: 1:00 PM – 5:00 PM

  • You will provide customer support across our primary communication channels: email and chat.

  • You will manage inquiries coming through our email and AI chat systems, providing rapid, real-time responses to customers and take over complex issues that require a human touch.

  • You will resolve inquiries regarding order status, product information, shipping, and returns.

  • You will process returns using Loop Returns, ensuring accurate refunds and inventory tracking.

  • You will guide communication between the store and our external supply partners, investigating and escalating complex fulfillment, shipping, or product inquiries to ensure rapid resolution for the customer.

  • You will navigate and use our ecommerce tech platforms at an expert level, specifically Shopify, Gorgias (including live chat and AI automation features), and Loop Returns.

  • You will collaborate with the Customer Experience Manager to identify trending customer issues and suggest operational improvements.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • Technical Expertise: at least 2 years of experience with Shopify, Gorgias, and Loop Returns.

  • AI Chat & System Optimization: at least 1 year of experience working with AI chat tools, managing live chat queues, creating macros, configuring auto-responses, and performing advanced administrative tasks within Gorgias.

  • Work Environment: at least 3 years of experience in a high-volume retail environment, meeting strict response time expectations during peak season.

job.title: Senior DevSecOps Engineer, Cybersecurity
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Senior Engineer, Cybersecurity is a hands-on contributor who designs, builds, and operates security controls and services that protect The Times' systems, data, and users. As a member of the Security Architecture team, you will own complex initiatives end-to-end, drive measurable risk reduction, and collaborate across product engineering and enterprise technology with technical depth, operational rigor, and clear communication aligned with business outcomes.

Who are we?

Cybersecurity helps prevent The Times from becoming news. Our teams work to protect the news makers, their support staff, the platforms they rely on every day, as well as all of The Times' products and services, and our readers who consume them.

This role reports to the Director of Engineering, Cybersecurity.

Responsibilities:

  • Create an environment that favors context, not control. Empower product engineers and ensure they have the relevant information and tools to deliver secure products and services.
  • Design, implement, and operate security controls and services (e.g., identity and access management, secrets management, endpoint/agent hardening, network segmentation, detection, and response automation) that meet reliability, security, scalability, and observability standards.
  • Partner with product and platform teams to integrate security into architecture and developer workflows while articulating business impact and tradeoffs.
  • Perform security reviews, threat modeling, and risk assessments (code, design, 3rd-party apps).
  • Investigate and resolve urgent and/or complex security issues, triaging effectively and driving architectural changes that prevent recurrence.
  • Participate via RFCs, community of practices, and other internal knowledge sharing channels to share learnings, align on standards, and influence secure patterns across areas; model The Times' core values in cross-functional collaboration.
  • Support team growth through peer design/code review, pairing, and clear feedback; on security engineering practices across the department.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in software engineering and security engineering space.
  • Understanding of security controls across a variety of security domains, including access management, encryption, vulnerability management, AI security, network security, authentication/authorization.
  • Knowledge of one or more Cloud platforms (AWS, GCP) and best practices for architecting and securing.
  • Experience with software engineering practices (CI/CD, GitOps, IaC, etc.) and related security practices (SAST, SCA, secure by design, shift left, etc.).
  • Programming skills in at least one language (Go, Python).
  • Experience with containerization and orchestration platforms.
  • A bias towards helping people. Many teams will rely on you to help build their systems.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Security/Compliance or DevOps certifications
  • Experience with Kubernetes
  • Experience with Terraform and Packer
  • Experience with HashCorp Vault

This role may require limited on-call hours. An on-call schedule will be determined when you join, based on team size and other factors.

This is a hybrid remote/in-office role.

The Senior Director, Global Benefits will be responsible for the strategic design, operational excellence, and holistic governance of all benefits and perquisites for The New York Times on a global scale. Reporting to the SVP, Total Rewards, this leader will architect a robust benefits strategy that attracts, engages, and retains top talent and ensures fiscal sustainability. This role is also responsible for leading the Benefits operations function to deliver a superior employee experience through resource optimization and cost-efficient best practices. Beyond design and administration, the incumbent will partner with Corporate Communications and Culture to drive an engaging communications strategy, ensuring our diverse and complex population understands the full value of their benefits package. 

This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement a global benefits strategy that aligns with our goals, ensuring equity and relevance in local markets across the US and internationally.
  • Oversee the design and execution of all benefits programs, ensuring they are competitive, comprehensive, and compliant with local, federal, and international regulations (e.g., ERISA, ACA, GDPR).
  • Lead the Global Benefits Operations department, overseeing a team of benefits administrators to deliver a high-quality employee experience.
  • Be the primary benefits subject matter expert for the Labor Relations team, providing strategic modeling and direct support during collective bargaining negotiations regarding welfare and retirement provisions.
  • Source technologies and administrative best practices, while managing operational costs to increase efficiency and fiscal discipline.
  • Monitor market trends, benchmarks and best practices to lead innovation in plan design, ensuring The New York Times remains relevant with market peers.
  • Oversee relationships with third-party vendors, carriers, and consultants to ensure high service levels, compliance, and return on investment.
  • Collaborate with Legal counsel to review plan documents and summary plan descriptions, ensuring all programs meet legal requirements and minimize liability.
  • Ensure that benefit plans for unionized employees are administered following collective bargaining agreements.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in benefits design and administration, and leadership experience managing Global Benefits.
  • Experience working with a unionized workforce and supporting labor negotiations.
  • Expertise in US regulations (ERISA, COBRA, HIPAA, FMLA) and a working knowledge of international social security systems and statutory requirements.
  • Experience translating complex benefits concepts into clear, accessible language for executive partners and employees.

job.title: Senior Editor, Style, NYT Wirecutter
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

Wirecutter is seeking a visionary senior editor to oversee our style team.

As Wirecutter's senior style editor, you'll be responsible for guiding and expanding our style and accessories coverage to become an indispensable destination for readers looking for straightforward, engaging, and smart advice to help them develop their personal style. You will lead a team of writers and work closely with the photo and video team, audience development team, and lifestyle writers and editors to make sure our coverage is helpful, engaging, and up-to-date. We ask that you have writing, editing, and management skills, as well as subject-matter expertise.

You have sharp editing skills and a firm grasp of all categories of style, including clothing basics, fashion accessories, bags and carrying items, shoes, and more. You have a strong knowledge of the style landscape, whether menswear or womenswear. You're a fashion expert who knows brands and trends as well as how to apply a skeptic's eye to the industry's claims at large. You know that when it comes to personal style, there's no such thing as the best product for everyone, but you understand how Wirecutter's method of rigorous testing, thorough reporting, and deep beat expertise can help readers find the perfect option that fits their needs. You also understand the importance of journalistic standards and integrity, and you're passionate about cutting through the clutter to provide inclusive recommendations at any budget.

A successful person in this role will be comfortable creating an exciting guide-based coverage plan while managing a team and collaborating with colleagues across Wirecutter's newsroom. You have a solid network of fashion freelancers, publicists, and sources, and an instinct for what makes a good style story. As a Wirecutter journalist, you'll also recognize the importance of considering those with different needs and diverse perspectives.

This is a hybrid position, based out of our LIC office in NYC and includes regular attendance in the office.

Responsibilities:

  • Plan coverage for style and accessories guides and projects over the course of the year
  • With the editorial director, execute strategy for our coverage and manage a team of writers in execution of dynamic style content, including guides, short-form, and multi-platform coverage
  • Assign projects to freelance and staff writers as needed, and manage them on a per-project basis
  • Manage editors and writers as direct reports, set clear expectations, facilitate performance feedback, and support learning and development
  • Manage editorial process and serve as top or lead editor for guides, short-form journalism, and other projects that fall under your area of coverage
  • Approve ideas from your team and use data to support pitches and to monitor performance
  • Contribute original ideas to test planning, suggest creative reporting strategies, challenge writers' assumptions
  • Interact with our reader community through multiple channels, including social, comments, and through our community team
  • May be required to attend trade shows and product news events as needed
  • Perform related work as assigned
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the editorial director of lifestyle

Basic Qualifications:

  • Minimum 5 years of professional editing experience and at least two years managing editors and/or writers, with a proven ability to effectively manage projects and direct reports
  • The ability to write clearly and accessibly about topics for lay audiences, and edit with an eye for helping others do the same
  • Deep knowledge of fashion subject matter and clear sense of good aesthetic taste

 Preferred Qualifications:

  • Excellent communication and people management skills
  • An effective organizational system with the ability to manage multiple projects at various stages in the publication process
  • A commitment to high standards of reporting and accuracy
  • An understanding of how to use web analytics data to make editorial decisions

Please include a cover letter and your résumé/CV.

We’re now expanding into more AI-assisted developer workflows using tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot to support debugging, migrations, test generation, and everyday development in a safe, measurable way.

This role sits in Developer Platforms and reports to the Engineering Manager of the DevEx Platforms team.

As a Senior Software Engineer on DevEx Platforms, you’ll build GenAI-augmented developer experiences and platform capabilities used across all of The New York Times.

Your work will help teams ship faster and more safely, pay down technical debt through structured migrations and platform modernization, and turn effective internal practices into reusable tools and agents.

  • Design and build GenAI-powered developer tooling: prompts, IDE integrations, Cursor/Claude rules, and telemetry to understand how they’re used.

  • Work closely with engineers and managers across Product Engineering to understand how they build software today and to design solutions that actually fit the way they work.

  • This role includes limited on-call responsibilities; the schedule will be set when you join.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • 2+ years of experience improving developer experience through workflows, documentation, and capabilities of the internal platform

job.title: Senior Manager, Lifecycle Marketing (Temporary)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About New York Times Games

The New York Times is looking for a Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager to join the New York Times Games team, reporting to the Executive Director of Marketing, Games.

In 2025, players completed more than 11 billion games across our portfolio, led by hits like Wordle and Connections, alongside the iconic New York Times Crossword, which has existed in print since 1942.

Games is one of the largest and fastest-growing businesses among our portfolio of products, including Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic and News.

About the Role

We need a senior lifecycle marketer to lead how we keep Games players engaged over time across email, push (app and desktop), display and other channels. You will focus on deepening engagement with our existing players (non sub + sub)  and reducing churn. 

You will lead the end-to-end marketing lifecycle strategy for Games players, from onboarding and activation through ongoing engagement, win-back and reactivation. You will design and run cross-channel programs that create timely, relevant, and personalized experiences for our players, grounded in data and insight. You will work closely with product, growth marketing, product marketing, data and creative partners to bring these programs to life.

This is a temporary hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters, reporting to the Executive Director, Marketing, Games. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities

Lifecycle Strategy and Planning

  • Define the lifecycle marketing strategy for Games, including goals for activation, engagement, retention and reactivation.
  • Map player journeys and identify key moments where lifecycle programs can deepen engagement and reduce churn.
  • Partner with product and product marketing to ensure lifecycle programs align with feature launches, game updates and the broader Games roadmap.

Channel Execution and Optimization

  • Lead the planning and execution of lifecycle campaigns and automations across email, push, display and other channels, from brief through launch, in partnership with channel owners. 
  • Work with channel owners to build, test and optimize always-on programs (onboarding flows, engagement nudges, winback journeys) that drive meaningful changes in player behavior.

Data, Measurement and Insights

  • Own key lifecycle metrics for Games, including retention, reactivation, engagement and churn, and build reporting that gives the team a clear view of performance.
  • Partner with analytics and data science teams to use segmentation, cohort analysis and predictive signals to inform targeting and personalization of lifecycle programs.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Build strong relationships with product, product marketing, growth marketing, media team and channel owners, audience insights, data analytics, engineering and creative to align on shared goals, design and launch lifecycle programs.

Player Experience and Brand Stewardship

  • Champion the perspective of our players, bringing research and behavior insights into planning and creative development.
  • Balance performance goals with a thoughtful, respectful approach to frequency, personalization and offers. 

Basic Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in lifecycle marketing, CRM, retention marketing or related fields, with a track record of driving measurable improvements in engagement and retention.
  • Experience owning cross-channel lifecycle programs (email, push, and at least one additional channel such as display or in-app messaging) for consumer products or subscription services.
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort working with data to build hypotheses, design tests and interpret results.
  • Operate in cross-functional environments and collaborating with product, analytics, media partners and creative teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with cohort and funnel analysis.
  • Interest in The New York Times and New York Times Games; prior experience with digital subscription, content, or mobile app products.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate both autonomously and collaboratively, with curiosity about identifying and forging new opportunities.

About New York Times Games

The New York Times is looking for a Product Marketing Manager to join the New York Times Games team, reporting to the Executive Director of Marketing, Games.

In 2025, players completed more than 11 billion games across our portfolio, led by hits like Wordle and Connections, alongside the iconic New York Times Crossword, which has existed in print since 1942.

Games is one of the largest and fastest-growing businesses among our portfolio of products, including Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic and News.

About the Role

You will work cross-functionally to develop strategies and projects that support player understanding and product adoption of new and evolving New York Times Games product experiences (new games and features), with a focus on building product awareness, launch success, and deepening usage among new and existing audiences. 

As a product marketer, you will sit at the intersection of messaging strategy and product experience, collaborating across departments to support go-to-market planning and launch for new games and features, feature discovery, launch, adoption and usage. You will bring digital product marketing knowledge, experience working with product teams on go-to-market plans, and an understanding of how brand strategy informs positioning for new product experiences. 

You will help unlock the impact of product marketing by:

  • Providing insights and guidance on important product features and suggesting future roadmap items with an audience-centric lens, with a particular focus on upcoming games, feature launches and new product experiences.
  • Scaling the product marketing discipline within the Games team and advocating for the PMM discipline.
  • Optimizing our processes and building relationships and trust across departments and teams.
  • Leading product-focused storytelling and product x writing collaboration with partners in product, design, editorial and creative.
  • Independently identifying projects and opportunity areas.

This is a temporary hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters, reporting to the Executive Director, Marketing, Games. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities include:

Product Marketing Strategy

  • Develop ideas and campaigns that help players understand, discover and use key product features.
  • In partnership with the Executive Director of Marketing, Games, build and own go-to-market strategy, from ideation to launch, for new games and features.
  • Partner with product, design, data analytics and user research teams to infuse product development with a data-driven and player-first perspective.
  • Consult on UX research sprints in partnership with product, audience insights and data insights.
  • Understand the competitive landscape and become knowledgeable about the digital games market and broader subscription ecosystem.

Go-to-Market Planning and Optimization

  • Identify which product features merit external marketing messaging and lead marketing strategy (including creative brief writing) and end-to-end execution of campaigns as relevant.
  • Analyze campaign performance and recommend next steps based on results.

Collaboration and Communication

  • Partner with colleagues in marketing and brand strategy, media, product, product design, engineering, creative, audience insights, project management, data analytics and Games editorial.
  • Effectively communicate in any forum — from daily work with core teammates to presentations with Games or marketing leadership — and be a trusted voice for our players as we make product decisions and prioritizations.

Basic Qualifications

  • 7+ years of related experience in marketing, product marketing or product management, including at least 2 years of insights-driven go-to-market experience.
  • Experience driving go-to-market strategies for product and feature launches, with an understanding of how brand strategy connects to product marketing output.
  • Interpret and organize data and identify actionable insights.
  • Familiarity planning and runningA/B tests and drawing key learnings from analytics reports and dashboards.
  • Familiarity with the product-development life cycle and direct experience operating within product-led teams and with technology partners.
  • Proven experience with cross-functional collaboration and working with a diverse array of stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Digital subscription and mobile app experience.
  • Experience conducting competitive and category research to inform positioning and go-to-market plans.
  • Interest in The New York Times and New York Times Games.
  • Operate both autonomously and collaboratively, with curiosity about identifying and forging new opportunities.

As a player-coach role, you will lead a team of analysts and partner closely with Revenue, Product, and Marketing leads to establish KPIs, run conversion experiments, and build attribution frameworks that scale revenue. You will report to the Executive Director, Data Analytics.

Responsibilities

  • You will lead, mentor, and onboard a team of two direct reports, nurturing their career growth
  • You will analyze affiliate revenue drivers (e.g., merchant commissions, EPC, conversion rates, and partner yield) across all content touch points.

  • You will partner with Ad Ops and Advertising teams to track ad yield (RPM, eCPM), fill rates, and ad unit viewability, balancing display and custom content revenue against user experience and page speed
  • You will evaluate trade-offs between affiliate links, ad placements, and Wirecutter Store product placements on site, creating a holistic monetization framework to maximize total revenue per user.
  • You will lead recurring commercial reporting for Wirecutter Leadership, communicating complex multi-channel revenue dynamics, forecasting, and strategic expansion opportunities.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • 2+ years of people management experience
  • 3+ years of experience analyzing diverse revenue models, including affiliate marketing, programmatic/direct digital advertising, and DTC e-commerce operations
  • 3+ years of experience in A/B testing, conversion rate optimization (CRO), and pricing/placement experiments aimed at.
  • Advanced mastery of SQL and experience with BI/data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker) to build end-to-end commercial dashboards and financial reporting models.

To help us do this essential work, The New York Times is hiring a Senior Manager, Strategic Business Communications.

In this role, you'll be part of a team that leads internal communication on the business side of The Times, with a focus on XFun, our cross-functional product development organization. You'll partner closely with XFun leadership, their chiefs of staff, HR, Legal, Labor Relations and other stakeholders across the org — bringing our strategy, priorities and culture to life, and elevating the employee experience for our team. You're comfortable working in a highly matrixed organization, bringing together many voices and priorities in service of The Times's mission, and you take real pride in helping colleagues feel seen, connected and celebrated for their work.

We're looking for someone who can manage several projects at once — some you'll lead, some you'll support — with experience helping executives and leaders accomplish their communication goals, ideally within a tech company or similarly fast-moving environment. You're an impeccable writer and you know how to make communications break through the noise, including through audio, video and other formats. You come with big ideas, the drive to see them through, and a collaborative spirit that puts the team and the work first.

Responsibilities

  • Connect colleagues to strategy and culture through communications, events and experiences.

  • Support communications and planning for All Hands and other internal events for XFun, Wirecutter and The Athletic — including recurring programs like Maker Week (our annual hackathon), EngX (our annual engineering gathering), and Behind the Report (our monthly series designed to connect colleagues with our mission).

  • Develop All hands agendas, prepare presenters, and manage scheduling and event logistics, from invitations and calendars to space bookings and catering.

  • Own communications plans across a range of topics and issues, working closely with leaders to draft communications, facilitate cascades across the organization, and help leaders share timely, aligned updates with their teams in a highly matrixed organization.

  • Own internal communications for external product launches (e.g., Games, Cooking, News), partnering with Product, Marketing, and XFun Ops to ensure employees understand what's launching and why it matters.

  • Own the XFun-all Slack channel, ensuring information inclusive, and aligned with XFun priorities.

  • Experiment with new formats — short-form video, audio/podcast content, interactive posts — to keep communications and events dynamic and engaging.

  • Serve as the central point of contact for XFun managers, owning a yearly engagement plan (including the managers Slack channel and producing recurring manager meetings) and partnering with Labor and Legal on sensitive communications.

  • Elevate XFun's work through 3–4 stories a year with the Storytelling team and segments at company-wide meetings.

  • Own communications for core people programs (the performance cycle, required training, the employee survey and benefits updates), and partner with HR, Legal and leadership on personnel matters such as departures, org changes and executive hires.

  • Champion recognition across XFun, executing on existing plans, finding new ways to celebrate wins big and small, and spotlighting major moments like Publisher Awards and team milestones.

job.title: Senior Manager, UX Writing
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About Us

Marketing plays a key role in extending the journalistic legacy and mission of The Times into the future. Our job is to answer the question: “Why is quality journalism worth paying for?” We create award-winning marketing that builds awareness of our brand and affinity for the breadth of our journalistic offering. Above all, we strive to be timely, straightforward and relevant in our marketing — illustrating in new and creative ways how The New York Times can enrich the lives of our readers.

About The Role

In an ongoing effort to create new and elevated product experiences, we’re looking for a Senior Manager, UX Writing to concept, develop and execute UX writing across The New York Times portfolio, including our core news product and Games, Cooking, Wirecutter and The Athletic.

You will write crisp, clear and engaging copy for customer journeys, partnering with product, design, marketing, engineering, research and editorial teams to create experiences that grow, engage and retain subscribers. You will also manage a small team of freelance UX writers, coordinating resources, assigning projects and developing practical standards and workflows.

We're looking for candidates who can balance the clarity that UX copy demands with the personality and approachability of an engaging brand. We will look to you to help create solutions that inspire and excite others, then present them effectively and enthusiastically. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Associate Creative Director, Writing. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Write clear, accurate and compelling user-interface copy for experiences on nytimes.com, in The New York Times app and more.
  • Manage inbound UX writing requests, prioritizing tasks and assigning overflow projects as needed.
  • Maintain quality and consistency across projects and teams, acting as a brand voice steward to ensure all UX copy meets brand, newsroom and product style guidelines and lives up to the journalism itself.
  • Expertly apply brand voice in wayfinding moments, enhancements, paywalls and payflows, plus new tools and features, adjusting tone as appropriate. Touch points might include push notifications, tooltips, light boxes, bottom sheets, screens for new flows and more.
  • Mentor in-house writers and manage a small team of freelance UX writers.
  • Consider problems from multiple angles while aligning work with overarching business and engagement goals.
  • Use insights, data and strategy to influence product copy.
  • Collaborate with designers, prototypers, marketers and more to create compelling UX solutions.
  • Communicate the strategic intent of your work in meetings, presenting rationale to a broad group of partners, including leadership.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience writing for product, brand and UX across multiple products, teams or surfaces.
  • Experience managing or functionally leading writers.
  • A portfolio that shows ideas expressed clearly across a range of touchpoints.
  • The ability to write clear, succinct and engaging copy while writing for small spaces.
  • The ability to collaborate with multiple partners and adjust copy based on data and input from others.
  • Fluent in branding and UX theory and practice.
  • Proficiency using Figma.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A love of writing and storytelling, with the ability to apply it to systemic thinking.
  • Curiosity about every piece of the customer journey.
  • A belief in the value of journalism to people and society, and genuine curiosity about our work and company. We hope you enjoy reading, watching and listening to New York Times journalism and products.

job.title: Senior Multimedia Producer/ SVJ, Serial
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Serial Productions, in collaboration with The New York Times Metro desk, is launching a new bi-weekly narrative podcast focused on New York City. The podcast will be accompanied by weekly editorial extensions — primarily social video, but also newsletters and live events — that share the sensibility of the show while standing alone as distinctive creative work.

The Senior Multimedia Producer will lead the conception, production and evolution of these extensions, helping invent a distinctive visual language that translates Serial's narrative, character-driven stories about New Yorkers into social-first video and other formats that feel unmistakably of New York City.

This role is a key member of the Serial editorial team and will work closely with Serial producers and editors, New York Times video, social and marketing teams, and freelance collaborators to create fun, experimental and ambitious content that grows and deepens the audience for the show and for Serial more broadly.

This role is based in New York City. The Senior Multimedia Producer is expected to spend significant time in person with Serial, Metro and partner teams, in accordance with New York Times policies, while also doing field and location work across the city as needed.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the editorial vision and production strategy for all extensions to the podcast, including social video, newsletters and live or virtual events.
  • Develop platform-specific social video concepts (for example, TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts) that translate the show's reporting, characters and ideas into compelling visual storytelling.
  • Oversee end-to-end production of social videos, from pitching and scripting through shooting, editing, sound design, approvals and publishing.
  • Be able to independently shoot and edit straightforward social video pieces when needed, while primarily commissioning work from New York Times video teams and freelance collaborators.
  • Work with the Metro desk, Serial producers and reporters to identify stories, moments and themes that lend themselves to extensions, and to ensure alignment with the core podcast.
  • Hire, manage and direct freelance videographers, editors, designers and other collaborators; over time, this role may supervise staff producers or associates.
  • Work with Serial staff to develop newsletters and other written extensions that bring the project's reporting, voice and perspective to readers in distinctive formats.
  • Partner with events and live journalism teams to design and produce live or virtual experiences that reflect Serial's editorial sensibility and can generate compelling audio and video.
  • Work with the NYT Audience team to define success metrics for extensions, track performance across platforms and incorporate data and audience insights into ongoing strategy.
  • Run experiments in format, tone, length and distribution to learn what resonates with different audiences while maintaining Serial's editorial standards.
  • Ensure all extensions adhere to New York Times and Serial guidelines around fairness, accuracy, ethics and visual and audio standards.
  • Help foster an inclusive, collaborative and creatively adventurous culture on the Serial team and across partner desks.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Executive Editor, Serial Productions.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Experience (typically 4+ years) producing digital video, social content and multimedia storytelling, ideally in a news, documentary or narrative audio environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to conceive, produce and deliver compelling and unique social video series or campaigns that grow and engage audiences across platforms.
  • Strong hands-on production skills, including scripting, directing talent, field production and working with editors on visual and audio cuts, as well as the ability to shoot and edit short-form social video.
  • Experience collaborating with editorial, audience, marketing and visual teams on cross-platform projects.
  • Comfort working with analytics and platform tools (such as TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and internal dashboards) to interpret performance and inform decisions.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proven experience managing complex projects with multiple stakeholders, deadlines and deliverables.
  • Experience hiring, directing and giving constructive feedback to freelance and, ideally, staff colleagues.
  • Excellent communication, organization and time-management skills.
  • Deep familiarity with, and enthusiasm for, Serial's work and The New York Times's audio journalism.
  • Experience producing content specifically about New York City and its communities, or in another large metropolitan context with similar complexity.
  • Background in podcast or audio production and comfort working alongside audio-first producers and editors.
  • Experience developing live or virtual events tied to audio or video projects.
  • Familiarity with The New York Times newsroom, standards and workflows, or comparable large news organizations.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

The Video department is looking for a Senior Producer to work on the multi-disciplinary Reporter Video team of video journalists who create powerful videos featuring the expertise of our world-class journalists. Based in London, this role will focus on covering breaking news and major international developments in short-form video, producing a mix of quick-turnaround videos, explanatory and analysis pieces, as well as major enterprise and investigations. 

The Senior Producer will report to a London supervisor and work with the rest of the Reporter Video team in New York and other video hubs, becoming the key manager of the department’s content during the hours that London acts as the main Times hub. 

We are looking for a strong leader who is eager to motivate, inspire teams and innovate. Attention to detail, impeccable organization and effective communication with reporters and editors in the International Desk are a must.

You should also be an excellent storyteller with an eye for visual short-form digital formats, able to work autonomously to identify critical stories outside the U.S. and make sound, quick editorial decisions on world news. You will be expected to produce engaging stories through original reporting, on-the-ground filming, motion graphics and studio-based recordings.

You must have deep experience reporting on stories from Europe, the Middle East and Africa, including managing teams in conflict zones, devising security plans and making risk assessments.

This is a hybrid position based in London and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week.

  • Drive innovative Reporter Video delivering on a range of formats.

  • Build and strengthen relations with colleagues on the International Desk, including mentorship of reporters, photographers and fellow editors on the reporter video storytelling format.

  • Lead story development and story edits.

  • Review, assign and provide feedback on productions.

  • Support and guide script writing and visual approaches for effective short-form video.

  • Oversee production across multiple projects.

  • Guide interviews and shoots as needed, both in studio and field.

  • Foster experiments with new video approaches and editorial strategies.

  • Manage video journalists and video editors in the newsroom and field.

  • Proven experience producing digital news videos.

  • Experience managing video journalists, also during field deployments, including in hostile environments and involving risk assessments.

  • Broad and in depth experience in digital or broadcast news.

  • Proven track record managing direct reports.

  • Demonstrated deep command of a variety of video sources, including wire services, UGC, archival footage, motion graphics, and original footage.

Preferred Requirements:

  • Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.

  • Expert knowledge of current events with advanced-level experience covering breaking news stories in the U.S. and internationally. 

  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a multidisciplinary team.

  • Experience overseeing shoots and interviewing experts on camera.

  • Flexibility to work extended hours.

job.description:

The New York Times is hiring a collaborative Senior Product Marketing Manager for The Athletic. Reporting to the Director of Product Marketing, you will combine strategic product partnership with go-to-market leadership for priority Athletic products, features, and experiences.

In this role, you will bring market insights directly into product development by transforming customer needs, marketplace dynamics, and behavioral data into relevant recommendations. You will partner with product teams from discovery and strategy through launch and measurement, helping the team build experiences that support acquisition, engagement, and retention.

You will also lead go-to-market strategies for major launches and product updates working with Product, Marketing, Research, Editorial, Creative and other teams. You will define positioning, develop messaging, align team members, and ensure launches reach the right audiences with the right value proposition.

This role sits at the intersection of customer insight, product strategy, positioning, launch planning, and performance measurement. You are comfortable operating in ambiguity, influencing without authority, and making complex ideas clear. You are a hands-on builder yourself who enjoys building prototypes to help get your ideas across. You have direct experience scaling adoption and habituation with apps.

Responsibilities:

  • Partner directly with Product teams to represent customer and market perspectives in planning, prioritization, and roadmap decisions.

  • Use research and data to identify customer needs, prioritize use cases, and uncover market opportunities for Athletic products and experiences.

  • Lead end-to-end go-to-market strategy and execute major product launches by defining positioning, messaging, audience strategy, creative briefs, channel plans, and enablement materials.

  • Translate complex product capabilities into compelling customer benefits and clear value propositions tailored for sports fans.

  • Collaborate with Growth Marketing and Product teams to uncover opportunities across the entire user journey (acquisition, activation, onboarding, engagement, conversion, upsell, and retention).

  • Define success metrics, analyze post-launch performance, and establish feedback loops to inform future product and marketing strategy.

  • Build clear narratives, frameworks, and presentations that align partners around customer needs, product strategy, and project impact.

  • Foster trusted relationships across the organization by bringing structure to complex programs, facilitating productive discussions, and sharing best practices to improve product marketing standards.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • Experience using customer research, audience insights, competitive intelligence, and analytics tools to inform positioning, value propositions, and messaging strategies.

  • Experience partnering with Product, Data, Tech, and Research teams to influence roadmap decisions, run test-and-learn agendas, and measure outcomes.

  • Clear and engaging communication, with the ability to tailor complex information to a range of audiences.

job.title: Senior Staff Editor (Temporary)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Washington bureau is seeking a temporary senior staff editor to work on editing Washington news, including stories on the White House, Congress, the military, intelligence agencies, the Justice Department, the State Department, the Supreme Court, health care, economics and more.

You will work on a mix of daily and enterprise stories as well as breaking news and live coverage during weekday evenings, picking up from the dayside team and working alongside other editors in the Washington bureau and on the Live team in New York, as needed. You will also monitor news developments, consult with the Washington Night Editor and bureau leadership about priorities, do first and second reads and make judgments on the length, placement and framing of stories and, at times, assign stories to reporters.

You will need to have familiarity with a wide variety of topics, versatility, speed, proven judgment and the ability to collaborate across desks and platforms.

This is a temporary position based in Washington, D.C., with regular presence in the office, 4 days per week. It includes night and weekend work as newsroom needs require.

Responsibilities:

  • You will work with other editors and reporters to ensure stories are cleanly edited.
  • You will edit a wide range of material for accuracy, grammar, style and readability, including breaking news, live updates, daily news and major enterprise stories.
  • You will provide first and second edits for a variety of stories and topics across the desk.
  • You will manage coverage of breaking news stories, coordinate with other editors on deployment decisions and launch reporters as needed.
  • You may work with reporters on stories from assigning to publication, including framing, shaping and close-in editing.
  • You will monitor wires, social media and other sources for news developments and stay in touch with reporters and editors about advancing running news stories to keep the report fresh and competitive through the evening, with an eye to coverage into the next news cycle.
  • You may manage the Washington live blog, as needed. Be familiar with its workflows and adjust presentation and coverage plans as news developments require.
  • You will work with other editors in the Washington bureau, on the Live team and across the newsroom to collaborate as necessary.
  • You will coordinate with editors and the audience team on story publication and promotion plans as needed.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Washington Night Editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of editing and writing experience at a journalism or media company or other relevant organization
  • Commitment to The New York Times strategy, ethics, standards and mission for themselves, their team, stringers and colleagues
  • A willingness to collaborate and the ability to partner with colleagues across the Washington bureau and The New York Times newsroom
  • Experience working in high-pressure, deadline-driven newsrooms, including breaking-news or live-coverage workflows
  • Writing and editing skills that demonstrate mastery of journalistic style and standards, including ethical and superb news judgment

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A strong understanding of Times style and standards
  • Experience managing or contributing to a live blog, running news report or other continuous coverage format
  • Knowledge of Washington politics, policy and institutions
  • A willingness to be flexible as the bureau and newsroom's needs evolve

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

job.title: Senior Staff Editor, Off Platform Graphics
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The Graphics department at The New York Times seeks to hire an experienced and versatile senior visual editor to manage and execute the presentation of our graphics journalism in formats beyond nytimes.com, including social media, email newsletters and the print newspaper. This is a high-impact role designed for a senior journalist who wants to pioneer best practices and drive our off-platform visual storytelling.

You will guide the adaptation of complex graphics for audiences on social media, including Instagram, Facebook, X and other emerging surfaces. You will be responsible for coordinating strategy with the Social Visuals team and for assigning, editing and in some cases crafting graphics to meet that strategy, and help to do the same for Times newsletters, including The Morning and On Politics. And you will work with the Print Hub to coordinate production and edit graphics for the Times print edition.

You possess impeccable news judgment and have extensive experience creating and editing a wide range of types of information graphics. You operate with autonomy to proactively identify new opportunities to extend the reach of our journalism.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceptualize and execute unified visual styles that can effectively translate complex data, maps and diagrams into digestible, high-impact visual assets to fit a variety of formats.
  • Produce and edit news graphics under tight deadlines during breaking news environments.
  • Guide and edit the work of other visual journalists who translate interactives, spatial models and breaking news graphics into these formats.
  • Expertly and independently carry out all aspects of visual production, serving as the primary leader of all off-platform displays.
  • Work with the Social Visuals and Audience teams to direct the packaging of graphics journalism off-platform.
  • Maintain strong relationships and coordinate across other multidisciplinary desks (Graphics, Design, Video and the Print Hub) to track projects and establish publishing workflows.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a deputy graphics editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of professional experience producing and editing visual journalism or multimedia graphics at a major news organization.
  • Deep familiarity with visual storytelling devices, including a strong portfolio demonstrating hands-on execution of maps, charts, diagrams, 3-D modeling or motion graphics.
  • Expert proficiency with Adobe Creative Suite (specifically Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects) and Figma.
  • Experience with creating, editing or art directing graphics for a print publication.
  • Strong writing and editing skills and experience synthesizing complex information and work on strict deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with reading and editing code (HTML, CSS, JavaScript).
  • Familiarity with tracking off-platform traffic trends and optimizing display assets (headlines, thumbnails, custom visual cards) to maximize audience engagement.
  • Experience managing or guiding visual journalists.

The New York Times Magazine is looking for an experienced Senior Video Editor to edit and publish short- and long-form videos that support the magazine's storytelling. This role is for an editor with a refined understanding of video production and storytelling, including video editing, and creative use of graphics and animation to communicate complex ideas. Ideal candidates should have some journalistic or editorial experience and should know how to translate the unique sensibilities of the magazine into compelling and sophisticated video stories.

In this role, you'll be expected to work with reporters, editors, producers, art directors and designers at the magazine to craft video assets that feature the expertise of our world-class journalists. The work will cover a wide range of subjects including news and enterprise projects and short-form video columns with an eye towards social media platforms.

  • Work collaboratively with writers, editors, and visual journalists at the magazine to create tight, informative and engaging short-form vertical videos.

  • Convey visual story ideas and complex information in engaging video sequences and animation.

  • Be a pragmatic, solutions-based innovator with the ability to complete projects within budget and on deadline.

  • Enthusiasm for developing and innovating video forms that reflect the breadth and voice of The New York Times Magazine.

The Reporter Video team identifies compelling stories and brings the depth and breadth of our news report onto our site and other platforms through video that features the expertise of our world-class journalists.

We are looking for an experienced video editor with a portfolio that demonstrates the ability to deliver engaging work on tight deadlines. You will work across a range of newsroom video coverage focused on vertical video storytelling with The Times' world-class journalists on-camera. You have deep experience in breaking and ongoing news coverage, with a track record of creating digitally compelling short-form video journalism.

Your portfolio and work samples should reveal a strong grasp of modern mobile video storytelling, and it should show that you're a quick learner with creative ideas and the ability to work on small or large teams. You are collaborative and solid technically with a solutions mindset, detail oriented, organized and fast.

Please note we have two positions available in the newsroom. Please speak to your expertise and/or interest(s) in your cover letter:

  • News and Enterprise

  • Culture and Lifestyle (music and film to fashion and real estate)

These are in-office positions based in New York and include regular attendance in the office four days each week. We are open to a Senior Video Editor working out of our LA office for the News and Enterprise role only. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

  • Video editing and color correction of news, culture, enterprise and investigative videos featuring reporters from across the newsroom.

  • Collaborate with video journalists and producers in the pre/post production process, including writing, structure and creative execution. Demonstrate excellent news judgment across projects.

  • Deliver top-notch product under intense deadline pressure, and without the need for direct supervision, continuous editorial guidance, or task management.

  • Work across a range of stories with various newsroom desks including culture and styles, often juggling multiple projects.

  • Work with animators to incorporate animation, motion graphics and house design styles into videos.

  • Experiment with different formats of vertical and mobile visual storytelling.

  • Guide junior staff on edits as needed.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to a Senior Producer based in New York.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of multimedia storytelling, video editing and production experience at a major news video outlet and/or production company. (Minimum 5 years of video editing experience.)

  • Strong digital video editing background.

  • Expertise in Adobe Premiere and Creative Suite.

  • Strong audio editing, mixing and fixing skills for video.

  • Proven ability to craft stories, own video research for a project and edit a video with oversight from managers and senior staff.

  • Thorough knowledge of current events, with experience covering news.

  • The ability to conceive and create fresh original videos related to the news.

  • Must have an impressive portfolio of video editing primarily for digital or broadcast.

  • Experience animating and editing animations in Adobe After Effects.

  • A digital first mindset to editing on-platform and for social media.

The goal is to help readers understand the world through powerful video stories, reaching our core audience as well as new viewers who increasingly consume journalism in video. We will experiment with a mix of direct, immersive vertical video forms that can bring our audience with us on the ground.

You will join a multi-disciplinary team of video journalists that will shape this work. This role is based in our New York office, working remotely with correspondents in the field to produce, edit and publish stories. You should have a refined understanding of video production and storytelling, including video editing, shooting and writing for narration, with a clear sense for how to creatively use graphics and animation to illustrate complex ideas. 

Your news judgement about what makes a good story in video will be crucial, as will creative ideas for how to reenvision the basic elements of foreign correspondence, across news, features and analysis. You must be an effective collaborator and a strong communicator who can work closely with regional editors and video colleagues to shape our approach to this coverage. You are capable of working independently and decisively.

This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week.

  • Write, produce, edit and publish videos with hybrid correspondents, in close partnership with regional editors.

  • Collaborate closely with International editors, correspondents and video colleagues.
  • Guide the work of cinematographers, editors and other collaborators.

  • 8+ years experience producing news video journalism for digital or broadcast news.

  • The ability to edit quickly and accurately with Adobe Premiere.

The New York Times is continuing to expand its video journalism, identifying compelling visual stories across the depth and breadth of our report. We showcase the expertise of Times journalists on-camera, share urgent news updates, produce on-the-ground reporting, pioneering Visual Investigations, and video podcasts. 

We are looking for a temporary Senior Video Journalist who can bring our audio portfolio to mobile, social and digital audiences through horizontal video podcasts and vertical video clips for Popcast which covers the latest in popular music criticism, trends and news.

This is a production-heavy position to oversee and lead the production and post-production of an individual show, and guide the team that executes on it. You have music journalism experience, a well developed sense of pop culture news, and thoughtful story framing and scripting skills, as well as a refined understanding of production and editing techniques in multi-camera environments with a meticulous attention to detail. 

As your primary job is producing—including overseeing the work of cinematographers, editors, and other collaborators—you are fluent in cinematography, including lighting techniques in multi-camera environments, and post-production.

You will work with reporters, editors and external collaborators to establish and execute on a vision for podcast video work that enhances our report. This role is for someone with a deep understanding of social video trends and who takes an innovative and adaptive approach to video formats and techniques.

This is a temporary (12 months)  in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

  • Produce Newsroom podcast videos in horizontal and vertical formats
  • Oversee the work of cinematographers and editors
  • Work closely with newsroom audio editors and producers to uphold standards

  • Pitch and develop different forms of short-form vertical video storytelling that are journalistically powerful and visually transformative
  • Must be able to handle the pressure of newsroom deadlines and juggle multiple projects at any given time
  • Must be open to experimenting with new ideas
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • 8+ years of multimedia storytelling, video editing and production experience at at a major video outlet or production company 
  • Experience creating original videos that incorporate audio, video, still images, graphics and text
  • Familiarity with Adobe Creative Cloud

  • Excellent news judgment and ability to work with colleagues and reporters to synthesize news gathering and investigations into a tight, informative and engaging video
  • Experience working in video podcasts
  • Experience working in newsroom environments

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The News Product team at The New York Times is looking for a Staff iOS Engineer. You will work with our Native squad to lay the foundations for satisfying native app experiences. You will deliver world-class journalism to millions of daily readers in a responsive and performant medium. You will lead efforts to enhance the quality, performance, and long-term maintainability of the News app codebase. You will establishing a technical vision that ensures our native experiences remain responsive and reliable for all readers. As part of the News Product organization, you will work with designers, other mobile engineers, and web engineers, and more on a team.

This is an opportunity to use different tools, ranging from SwiftUI to hybrid web technologies - whatever will best solve the problem at hand. You'll be part of an engineering organization that values transparency and openness, diversity, learning, community, and continuous improvement.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

You express:

  • Belief in our mission: You have passion with the news and for making the Times an indispensable daily destination for our readers.

  • Technical competency: You have knowledge of iOS frameworks and Swift, and keep up to date on changes in the frameworks, language and overall developer community.

  • Code cleanliness: You understand what makes code well structured, maintainable and flexible and aim to create a culture where quality code is valued.

  • User focus: You care about how design, engineering and product decisions help create a seamless, engaging and enjoyable user experience.

Responsibilities:

  • You will lead the design and implementation of core architectures, shared frameworks, and infrastructure using Swift, SwiftUI, and UIKit that accelerate our feature teams.
  • You will work with your team to build solutions that are scalable, maintainable and reliable.
  • You will guide app-wide architectural decisions, shape the long-term technical roadmap, and set engineering standards for the iOS platform.
  • You will lead technical understanding, collaborating with backend engineers, web teams, and other internal dependency owners.
  • You will help promote standards in iOS and Swift delivery, and engage with the community of iOS developers at the Times.
  • You will lead programs to help the quality, performance and maintainability of the News app codebase
  • You will mentor engineers and contribute to/participate in Communities of Practice
  • Where applicable, you will integrate with broader New York Times Swift platform code
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, with 5+ years focused on large-scale iOS applications.
  • Experience setting technical direction, guiding engineering teams, and leading mobile architecture.
  • Deep mastery of iOS runtime mechanics, memory management, advanced design patterns, and Swift Concurrency.
  • Hands-on experience designing complex data persistence layers, advanced networking, and scalable test suites.
  • Expertise in mobile performance engineering, including app launch optimization, binary size reduction, and memory profiling.
  • Experience designing client-side observability infrastructure using Datadog or similar platforms.
  • Experience orchestrating large-scale architectural migrations (e.g., UI framework shifts, monolithic decoupling, automated refactoring).
  • Experience with framework design and modularization, including internal SDK development.
  • Product and Developer Experience (DX) mindset with the vision to translate complex goals and developer friction into scalable code.

job.title: Staff Photo Editor, Business
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

A Photo Editor for The New York Times has a creative eye and an innovative approach to formats and mobile-focused presentations. You should bring sharp technical skills and sound journalistic judgment to join a team creating visual journalism—still and video— for breaking news, features and enterprise stories for on- and off-platform publishing.

The primary duties of the job are to conceptualize and assign photography and video for the New York Times’ Business report, and to select and publish images and video for multiple platforms of The New York Times. You will assign and research a wide array of news and feature photographs and video, working productively with staff photographers, freelance photographers, wire services, agencies and all other sources of pictures, as well as editors, designers, and reporters in the newsroom. You will engage our staff and freelance photographers to identify and develop pitches with strong visual potential, producing strong photographic, video and multimedia displays with an eye toward innovative digital story forms and presentations.

You have a strong demonstrable passion for multimedia, journalism and photography of all kinds, and possess a broad knowledge of the current photographic, video, visual and social media landscape, including digitally innovative formats and mobile-first multimedia presentations. You must be a team player and a good communicator, and must initiate and develop ideas for photographs, short video clips and visual stories in different formats.

This is a hybrid position based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office 4 days each week.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceive of, pitch, develop, edit, pace and build powerful and innovative visual stories with attention to detail in a fast-paced newsroom
  • Maintain the highest standard of photography and multimedia assigning for feature, news and enterprise stories for all platforms including mobile, print and social
  • Identify, vet and onboard new contributing photojournalists as needed. Ensure that new contributors are versed and committed to ethical journalistic rigor, independence and integrity. Build relationships with the photographers you are directing through briefings, regular contact and feedback
  • Collaborate with writers, reporters, editors, visual editors and photographers to shape ideas into visual story opportunities
  • Demonstrate strong editorial judgment, working with Times editors and legal department for all vetting, copyright, legal and ethical questions
  • Focus on working with a diverse range of subjects and photographers, keeping our global and multigenerational audience in mind
  • Coordinate with Business desk editors and security team members to ensure the utmost preparation, training and safety of our photojournalists in the field
  • Maintain and meet your desk’s photo budget, process/approve invoices in a timely fashion
  • Attend photo department meetings to report and share your desk’s visual priorities
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • This role reports to a Deputy Editor of Photography

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience in a newsroom or equivalent
  • Experience assigning and directing photojournalists in a variety of situations
  • Proven deep research skills
  • Expertise in handling electronic images, photographic usage and copyright issues
  • Strong technical skills, including proficiency in digital tools and programs, including content management systems, Photoshop, PhotoMechanic, video editing tools and social media platforms

Preferred Qualifications:

  • An enthusiasm for visual journalism and current events, coupled with keen news judgment and a firm sense of journalistic ethics
  • Strong organizational, communication and collaborative abilities.
  • Knowledge of Adobe Premiere is a plus
  • Experience prioritizing and managing multiple projects in fast-moving environments
  • The initiative to take on and learn new technologies and tasks.
  • Openness to working a flexible schedule as news demands.
