job.title: Director, Privacy and Data Protection
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

Director, Privacy & Data Protection

Job Category: Business & Legal Affairs


How We LEAD:

The Director, Privacy & Data Protection will be an experienced privacy attorney supporting Universal Music Group's global privacy and data protection program. Working closely with the Senior Vice President, Privacy & Data Protection, this role will provide practical, hands-on legal support across privacy contracting, data subject rights, cybersecurity incidents, digital marketing and other matters involving the collection, use, sharing and protection of personal data.


As the world leader in music-based entertainment, UMG operates across a broad range of labels, artist businesses, digital platforms, e-commerce experiences, marketing initiatives and fan-facing services. The Director will work with colleagues across Legal, Information Security, Technology, Digital, Marketing, E-Commerce and the business to help UMG use data responsibly while supporting artists, creators and fans around the world.


The ideal candidate will combine strong privacy law fundamentals with excellent drafting and negotiation skills, sound judgment and a practical, business-oriented approach. This role requires an attorney who is comfortable managing a significant volume of day-to-day matters, can independently handle work within established frameworks, and recognizes when novel, sensitive or higher-risk issues require escalation.


How You'll CREATE:

  • Draft, review and negotiate data protection and privacy terms in commercial agreements, including data processing agreements, data-sharing arrangements, international data transfer provisions, information security terms and other privacy-related contractual provisions.
  • Partner with UMG's Business & Legal Affairs teams on privacy issues arising in artist, vendor, technology, platform, licensing, e-commerce, marketing and other commercial arrangements involving personal data.
  • Handle UMG's day-to-day legal work relating to data subject and consumer privacy rights requests, including assessing request scope and applicable legal requirements, advising on exemptions and response obligations, coordinating with privacy operations and relevant business teams, reviewing and drafting responses, and escalating complex or sensitive matters as appropriate.
  • Support the privacy-law aspects of cybersecurity and data security incidents, working closely with Information Security, Legal and other stakeholders to assess incident facts and affected data, analyze applicable notification and regulatory requirements, document legal assessments, and draft or review incident-related communications.
  • Assist with investigations of potential privacy and data security issues, including gathering relevant facts, evaluating legal obligations and coordinating with outside counsel where appropriate.
  • Advise business and legal teams on privacy requirements affecting UMG's websites, applications, digital platforms, artist and fan experiences, e-commerce operations, advertising and marketing activities.
  • Provide practical guidance on online advertising and tracking technologies, marketing communications, consent and preference management, and related privacy and consumer protection requirements.
  • Advise on compliance with U.S. federal and state privacy laws, GDPR and other applicable international privacy and data protection requirements.
  • Support privacy reviews of new and evolving business initiatives, technologies, vendors, products and uses of data, including privacy impact assessments where appropriate.
  • Assist with third-party privacy and data protection matters, including vendor diligence, data-transfer requirements, privacy questionnaires and remediation of identified issues.
  • Help maintain and improve privacy policies, procedures, templates, playbooks and other resources that support consistent and scalable privacy practices across UMG's labels, territories and business units.
  • Work with privacy operations, Information Security and business teams to identify recurring issues and improve processes for contract review, rights requests, incident response and other recurring privacy matters.
  • Support responses to regulatory inquiries, audits and other privacy or data protection matters as needed.
  • Monitor relevant developments in privacy, data protection, cybersecurity, digital marketing and consumer protection law and provide clear, practical guidance regarding developments relevant to UMG's businesses.
  • Provide privacy guidance and training to Legal, business and operational teams as needed.
  • Support privacy issues arising from emerging technologies and new uses of data as appropriate.
  • Collaborate effectively with colleagues across UMG's labels, business units and territories, handling routine and moderately complex matters independently and escalating novel, sensitive or significant matters as appropriate.

Bring Your VIBE:

  • J.D. from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar.
  • 8+ years of relevant legal experience, with substantial experience in privacy, data protection, cybersecurity, technology transactions or a closely related field, gained at a law firm, in-house legal department or a combination of both.
  • Experience drafting and negotiating data processing agreements and privacy, data use and security provisions in commercial agreements.
  • Strong working knowledge of U.S. federal and state privacy laws, including CCPA/CPRA and other comprehensive state privacy laws, and meaningful familiarity with GDPR and international data protection requirements.
  • Experience advising on data subject and consumer privacy rights requests, including access, deletion, correction and related requests.
  • Experience advising on privacy issues arising from websites, digital advertising, online tracking technologies, e-commerce, marketing and other consumer-facing data practices.
  • Familiarity with consumer protection and marketing requirements relevant to digital and direct-to-consumer activities.
  • Meaningful experience supporting cybersecurity or data security incident response, including familiarity with breach-notification requirements and experience working with information security or technical teams during investigations.
  • Strong legal research, analytical, drafting and negotiation skills, with the ability to identify the issues that matter and provide clear, practical and business-oriented advice.
  • Ability to understand technical and operational facts sufficiently to identify relevant privacy, cybersecurity and digital marketing legal issues.

  • CIPP/US, CIPP/E or another relevant privacy certification preferred.

job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

How you'll LEAD

The Executive Assistant, Finance Centers of Excellence will provide high-caliber executive support to the VP, Finance Intelligence CoE and the VP, Planning & Forecasting CoE.


This role offers a rare opportunity to support two senior Finance executives who are building new global capabilities from the ground up. You will work at the center of a major Finance transformation spanning planning, forecasting, trusted data, Management Reporting, business intelligence, analytics and modern technology. It is an exceptional platform for an Executive Assistant who wants broad exposure, meaningful responsibility and the opportunity to help shape how UMG Finance operates.


This is not a passive administrative role. Core Executive Assistant responsibilities - complex calendars, travel, expenses, meeting logistics, communications, confidentiality and executive prioritization - are table stakes. The person who excels will anticipate needs, create structure from ambiguity, keep information moving and ensure decisions and commitments do not stall. You will be a trusted, action-oriented partner who protects executive capacity, connects the right stakeholders, prepares leaders to make decisions and brings discipline and momentum to two new global Finance organizations.


How you'll CREATE

  • Executive partnership and prioritization: Own two complex executive calendars across functions, geographies and time zones; resolve conflicts proactively; protect focus and preparation time; and align schedules to the highest-value priorities.
  • Meeting and decision enablement: Coordinate leadership meetings, workshops, interviews, vendor sessions and offsites end to end, including agendas, pre-reads, presentations, logistics, actions, decisions and follow-through.
  • Executive communications: Draft, edit and coordinate correspondence, briefing notes, presentations, announcements and follow-up communications with accuracy, discretion and strong executive judgment.
  • Travel, expenses and logistics: Manage complex domestic and international travel, itineraries, contingencies, expenses, purchase requests, invoices and related executive-office administration.
  • Information flow and stakeholder liaison: Act as a central coordination point across Global FP&A, Controllership, FTO, CDO, CIO/CTO, Regional and OpCo Finance, consultants, recruiters, vendors and implementation partners.
  • Transformation and program coordination: Maintain selected milestone plans, action and decision logs, dependency trackers, stakeholder lists and deliverable inventories under the direction of the VPs and designated program leads.
  • Delivery follow-through: Track due dates, missing inputs, open decisions and material dependencies; follow up persistently and diplomatically; and escalate emerging issues with practical options.
  • Vendor and external-partner coordination: Organize meetings, information exchange, onboarding, access requests, deliverables, approvals and invoices; ensure external parties understand objectives, outputs and decision timelines.
  • Document and collaboration management: Support controlled document versioning, review cycles, approvals, distribution and shared-workspace organization so current information is easy to find and use.
  • Team operations: Coordinate leadership cadences, recruiting and onboarding logistics, team events, recognition and learning activities; identify administrative friction and improve how the teams work.
  • Confidentiality and judgment: Handle sensitive organizational, talent, commercial, vendor and transformation matters with exceptional discretion, emotional intelligence and professionalism.
  • Continuous improvement: Look beyond the immediate request, anticipate the next step and simplify routines, meetings and information flows so both VPs and their teams operate more effectively.

Bring your VIBE

  • Significant experience as an Executive Assistant supporting VP, SVP, C-suite or equivalent senior executives in a complex global organization.
  • Demonstrated success supporting two or more senior leaders simultaneously and managing competing priorities with fairness and transparency.
  • Exceptional calendar, meeting, travel and expense-management capability across multiple time zones.
  • Strong project and program coordination skills, including practical experience tracking milestones, actions, decisions, risks, dependencies and stakeholder communications.
  • A proactive, action-oriented style with a record of anticipating needs, solving problems early and closing loops without constant direction.
  • Outstanding organization, attention to detail, written communication and executive presentation skills.
  • Strong executive presence and the ability to work confidently with senior leaders, employees, consultants, vendors and external partners.
  • High emotional intelligence, diplomacy, discretion and sound judgment with sensitive information.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Teams, PowerPoint, Word, Excel and SharePoint; comfort learning project, workflow and knowledge-management tools.
  • Ability to operate calmly and constructively in a fast-moving environment where priorities can change quickly.
  • Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

job.title: IAM Engineer
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

Job Summary 


We are currently seeking an Identity & Access Management Engineer with specialization in Identity Governance & Administration (IGA) to join UMG’s global Tech Security & Identity organization. Reporting to the VP, Tech Security & Identity, this is a hands-on engineering role responsible for designing, implementing, and operating enterprise IGA capabilities across a complex, global environment. 

This engineer will play a critical role in governing digital identities, access entitlements, and lifecycle processes for employees, contractors, and non-employee populations. The role emphasizes strong engineering execution, automation, and operational discipline, partnering closely with security, HR, infrastructure, and application teams to ensure access is provisioned appropriately, reviewed regularly, and removed in a timely manner. The ideal candidate brings deep experience with modern IGA platforms, strong understanding of access governance controls, and the ability to operate at scale in a regulated enterprise. 


Job Functions 


Design, engineer, deploy, and operate Identity Governance & Administration (IGA) solutions across the enterprise. 

Implement and manage identity lifecycle processes including joiner, mover, and leaver (JML) workflows for employees and non-employee identities. 

Engineer and maintain access request, approval, and provisioning workflows integrated with HR systems, directories, and enterprise applications. 

Design and operate access governance controls including role models, entitlement catalogs, access certifications, and periodic access reviews. 

Partner with application owners and platform teams to onboard applications into IGA and remediate access governance gaps. 

Develop and maintain automation and integrations for IGA workflows using scripting, APIs, and infrastructure-as-code approaches (e.g., PowerShell, Python). 

Support segregation of duties (SoD) controls, access policy enforcement, and audit readiness activities. 

Troubleshoot and resolve complex identity lifecycle, provisioning, and access-related issues across integrated systems. 

Collaborate with Security, HR, Compliance, and Infrastructure teams to ensure identity governance controls align with security policies and regulatory requirements. 

Maintain technical documentation, configuration standards, and operational runbooks to support scalable and repeatable IGA operations. 

Continuously identify opportunities to improve access governance maturity, reduce manual effort, and enhance user experience through automation and platform enhancements. 


Job Requirements 


Essential Qualifications 


5+ years of hands-on experience in Identity & Access Management or Security Engineering roles, with a strong focus on Identity Governance & Administration. 

Demonstrated experience implementing and operating enterprise IGA platforms (e.g., Saviynt, SailPoint, or equivalent). 

Strong understanding of identity lifecycle management, access provisioning, role-based access control (RBAC), and entitlement governance. 

Hands-on experience designing and supporting access certification campaigns and remediation processes. 

Experience integrating IGA solutions with HR systems, Active Directory / Entra ID, and enterprise applications. 

Proficiency in scripting and automation using tools such as PowerShell or Python. 

Experience working in hybrid and cloud environments (Azure and/or AWS) with IAM integrations. 

Ability to independently own complex technical deliverables while collaborating effectively within a global organization. 

Strong troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills. 


Desirable Qualifications 


Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Engineering, or a related technical discipline. 

Experience with advanced IGA capabilities such as role mining, access analytics, or policy-based provisioning. 

Familiarity with compliance and audit frameworks such as SOX, ISO 27001, NIST, or similar. 

Professional certifications such as Saviynt Certified Professional, SailPoint Certified IdentityIQ Engineer, Security+, or CISSP. 

Experience operating IAM or identity governance platforms within a large, global, or highly regulated enterprise environment.

job.title: Manager, Artist Relations
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

How We Lead:

CD Baby champions human creativity, providing the technology, guidance, and professional infrastructure artists need to turn creativity and ambition into sustainable success.


We’re looking for an Artist Relations Manager to build and grow relationships with artists and their teams. Your first priority will be managing inbound referrals from our industry network, followed by strengthening relationships with high-value and high-potential artists already using CD Baby and developing targeted outreach to prospective artists. This is a relationship-driven role with a strong commercial and analytical component. You’ll use artist data and industry knowledge to identify opportunities, understand artists’ goals, and connect them with appropriate support.


As an individual contributor reporting to the SVP, Marketing & Revenue, you’ll own day-to-day artist relationships and partner with leadership to develop the processes and systems behind a growing Artist Relations program.

You’ll work closely with Artist Success and Lifecycle Marketing teams to support successful onboarding and ongoing engagement. You’ll remain the relationship lead for assigned artists, helping CD Baby understand and support their evolving needs.



How You’ll Create:

Manage inbound artist opportunities

  • Own referrals from artists, managers, labels, Virgin Music Group colleagues, and other industry partners.
  •  Evaluate opportunities against program criteria and recommend an appropriate level of service.
  • Explain CD Baby’s distribution, support, and additional services clearly, setting clear expectations about available support and how additional opportunities are considered.
  • Lead commercial conversations within approved parameters, partnering with the SVP, Marketing & Revenue and Legal and Business Affairs on negotiations and agreements as needed.
  • Document artist goals, service commitments, release plans, and relevant context for a complete handoff to Artist Success for onboarding and release coordination.
  • Maintain relationships with referral partners and follow through on introductions.

Develop relationships with our current roster

  • Use revenue, streaming, audience, and engagement data to identify existing artists who could benefit from a closer relationship with CD Baby.
  • Build relationships with selected artists and their teams, understanding their goals, upcoming projects, and service needs.
  • Maintain regular, purposeful contact with priority artists, anticipating concerns and identifying useful next steps.
  • Recommend relevant tools, services, and approved promotional opportunities based on each artist’s needs.
  • Identify relationship risks and coordinate internally to address concerns and retain artists’ future business.

Build a targeted artist recruitment pipeline

  • Identify prospective artists through industry data, research, professional relationships, live shows, and local music communities.
  • Develop targeted outreach to artists whose goals and needs align with CD Baby’s offering.
  • Build relationships with industry professionals who can introduce relevant artists.
  • Manage consistent follow-up from initial contact through qualification and conversion.
  • Represent CD Baby at shows, industry events, panels, workshops, and other artist-facing opportunities.

Connect artist relationships with lifecycle marketing

  • Partner with Lifecycle Marketing to identify artist segments and signals that warrant personalized outreach, education, or additional support.
  • Coordinate direct contact with broader marketing communications so artists receive relevant, consistent messages.
  • Help develop approaches for nurturing prospective artists, reengaging existing customers, and introducing appropriate services.
  • Share insights from artist conversations to improve messaging, educational content, and lifecycle journeys.

Help build a disciplined artist relations program

  • Maintain accurate CRM records covering contacts, opportunities, artist goals, service commitments, relationship history, and next actions.
  • Develop and refine repeatable processes for qualification, outreach, follow-up, handoffs, and ongoing relationship management.
  • Work with Artist Success to ensure commitments are understood and operational requirements are considered before they are made.
  • Coordinate with marketing colleagues to assess promotional opportunities and communicate approved support.
  • Track pipeline quality, conversion, artist engagement, retention, and commercial results.
  • Bring recurring artist needs and feedback to Product, Customer Experience, and Marketing.

Bring Your Vibe:

  • Experience in artist relations, artist management, talent partnerships, A&R, business development, or a related music-industry role.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trust with independent artists, managers, and industry partners.
  • Strong commercial judgment and experience helping move opportunities from introduction through agreement.
  • Ability to interpret streaming, revenue, audience, and engagement data to prioritize opportunities.
  • Working knowledge of digital music distribution, DSPs, artist marketing, and editorial pitching.
  • Clear, proactive communication and the ability to set expectations, anticipate concerns, and close the loop.
  • Strong organization and follow-through across multiple relationships and opportunities.
  • A practical, collaborative approach to improving processes and working across teams.
  • Connections within an independent music community and the ability to develop new industry relationships.
  • Comfort representing CD Baby externally with artists and their teams.

Preferred experience

  • Hands-on use of CRM tools to manage contacts, pipelines, follow-up activities, and reporting.
  • Collaboration with lifecycle, customer engagement, or retention marketing teams on segmentation, lead nurturing, or targeted communications.
  • Experience using customer or artist signals to trigger timely outreach and relevant service recommendations.

job.title: Manager, Social Media
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

How we LEAD:


CD Baby is looking for a Social Media Manager to lead our organic social presence as one of the most useful and relevant voices for self-releasing artists.


Our audience spans from artists releasing for the first time to experienced musicians building independent careers. What connects them is their intent: they care about their craft, want to grow, and take their careers seriously. You’ll help them navigate the business of music, make informed decisions, and find tools and opportunities to move their careers forward.


This is a hands-on role spanning strategy, content creation, community engagement, and performance. You’ll turn business priorities and audience needs into a clear social plan, and own its execution.


We’re looking for someone who understands both social and artists: what they care about, what they struggle with, and what earns their attention.


How you'll CREATE:


Own Social Strategy & Growth:

  • Lead organic social strategy across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Reddit, and emerging platforms.
  • Build a prioritized roadmap grounded in audience needs, with clear channel strategies and KPIs tied to artist acquisition and brand authority.
  • Stay close to artist conversations—from release strategy and fan growth to royalties, promotion, touring, and industry shifts.
  • Evaluate trends and cultural moments for artist relevance and business opportunity.
  • Build a distinctive mix of timely content, recurring series, artist stories, education, and entertainment.

Create Great Content:

  • Own the calendar from idea through publication, coordinating production, stakeholder input, approvals, and deadlines.
  • Concept, write, shoot, edit, and publish platform-native content, especially short-form video.
  • Turn artist challenges and complex topics – from royalties to music marketing – into clear, credible, useful content that reflects CD Baby’s expertise.
  • Develop strong hooks and formats that give artists a reason to follow our socials.

Build Artist Community:

  • Lead daily engagement across comments, DMs, mentions, and relevant conversations.
  • Use community insights to shape content and identify opportunities to support and spotlight artists.
  • Build a distinct CD Baby voice that is knowledgeable, approachable, direct, and human.
  • Exercise editorial judgment about when to educate, celebrate, take a point of view, or join the conversation.

Use Social to Drive Growth:

  • Define channel-specific KPIs for audience growth, engagement, traﬃc, artist acquisition,and conversion.
  • Own reporting and analysis, translating insights into recommendations for content, channel strategy, and campaigns.
  • Test formats, messaging, talent, and CTAs; apply learnings and scale what works.
  • Partner with marketing to connect social goals to broader business priorities.
  • Track competitors, platform shifts, creator trends, and music culture to inform strategy.


Bring your VIBE:

  • You bring 5+ years of relevant experience, ideally in music, entertainment, creator platforms, or a community-driven business.
  • You’ve independently owned organic social strategy and execution, with measurable results.
  • You understand creating content for musicians versus marketing to musicians.
  • You know social platforms and internet culture, with strong creative and editorial judgment.
  • You’re hands-on with short-form video, from concept through shooting and editing.
  • You write clearly, with a strong voice, making complex subjects engaging and useful.
  • You’re proficient in social analytics and Google Sheets or Excel and can translate data into strategic recommendations.
  • You’re highly organized and keep multiple priorities moving.
  • You’re collaborative, but don’t wait for a brief to bring ideas and turn them into action.
  • You’re based in the NYC area and plugged into music, emerging artists, and culture.

Why CD Baby:

Independent artists have more ways than ever to release music—and more responsibility for what happens after release day. CD Baby is building for artists who take that opportunity seriously.


For nearly three decades, CD Baby has helped independent artists bring their music to the world. Now, as part of Virgin Music Group and Universal Music Group, we’re building on that history for the next generation.


This role will help define how that next chapter sounds, feels, and shows up every day.

job.title: Manager, Strategic Analytics
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. Universal Music Group is looking for a Manager, Strategic Analytics to join the Strategic Analytics team.


How we LEAD:

The Manager will scope out and execute on projects for Senior Executives, as well as individuals within Business Development, Finance, Communications, Marketing, and UMG’s various label groups. The ideal candidate should have experience conducting complex analyses using large data sets in SQL and Excel, forming strong and commercially impactful insights from these analyses, and communicating the results to decision-makers of a wide range of functions, seniority and technical expertise. Candidates should also demonstrate a solid understanding (or an eagerness to learn) the business models that are currently revolutionizing digital and subscription-based media.


How you’ll CREATE:

  • Work with stakeholders in a consultative fashion to understand their goals and scope out analytical projects to answer their biggest questions
  • Create detailed financial models for scenario analysis on UMG’s biggest licensing negotiations
  • Extract necessary data for projects using complex SQL scripts, employing strict quality control and sense-checks
  • Create executive-level presentations to drive UMG-wide strategy
  • Own complex analytical workstreams from start to finish with minimal technical oversight
  • Sample work may include:
    • Advising stakeholders at UMG responsible for new business on potential market sizes and sources of growth
    • Developing dynamic models to support licensing negotiations (e.g., with Spotify, Apple, YouTube) and help explain market dynamics in partners’ biggest growth areas
    • Creating robust internal methods for forecasting and predicting content performance for newer and older artists
    • Conducting breakeven analyses for major content promotion investment opportunities
    • Collaborating with junior Strategic Analytics team members to complete more extensive/longer-term analytical projects

 

Bring your VIBE:

  • 3-5 years’ experience leading complex, multi-stage strategic projects from start to finish, from data collection and analysis to quality checking and final packaging and presentation
  • 3-5 years’ quantitative experience using SQL and Excel to conduct data analysis
  • Bachelors in Economics, Business Administration, Computer Science or equivalent years of experience
  • 2+ years Experience in consulting, finance, or corporate strategy preferred
  • Experience building flexible financial models to run scenario analyses
  • Experience visualizing data and using PowerPoint to explain complex data concepts to technical and non-technical audiences
  • Experience managing and engaging with clients in a consultative or analytical capacity
  • A track record of solid client and/or stakeholder relationships developed through repeated excellence in delivering their needs
  • Experience building relationships across business units
  • Ability to balance multiple projects and deadlines
  • A thoughtful approach to gen AI: comfortable using LLMs to augment work while thinking critically, independently, and maintaining full ownership of the output
  • Passion and curiosity for music and the data that is used within the industry
  • Ideal candidates will have also have proficiency in common programming languages used in data analytics (Python, R, etc.)
  • This role is located on-site in UMG’s Santa Monica office, with the expectation of at least 3-4 days a week in office.

Preferred experience, but not required:

  • Previous experience in the entertainment or subscription media space
  • Experience in economics research
  • Experience building flexible financial models to run scenario analyses
  • Experience working with data in an integrated cloud environment (e.g, AWS, Google Cloud)

As AI transforms how businesses operate, trusted data products become even more critical. job.title: Senior Manager, Identity Governance
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

Job Summary

As a key member of UMG Global Tech’s Security & Identity organization, the Senior Manager, Identity Governance & Administration leads UMG’s Identity Governance and Administration capability and serves as the enterprise IAM deputy for governance, operating model, roadmap, and execution. This role is accountable for the security, effectiveness, scalability, and continuous improvement of UMG’s IGA processes and platforms, with primary responsibility for Saviynt and related identity-governance capabilities.


This is an identity-security leadership role, not simply an IT operations or account-administration role. The Senior Manager treats identity as a foundational security control and enterprise risk domain. They ensure that identity data, access decisions, entitlements, workflows, lifecycle events, and governance evidence are designed and operated in a way that reduces cyber risk, supports business outcomes, and enables sustainable global operations.


The Senior Manager directly leads the IGA/Saviynt team and mentors leaders and practitioners across UMG’s other identity product functions. The role reports directly to the VP, Security & Identity and works as a peer leader with the Sr. Security & Identity Architect. The Senior Manager owns IGA strategy, operating model, platform outcomes, and control execution, while partnering with the Architect to align IGA capabilities with UMG’s broader identity-security architecture, standards, and technology strategy.


Success requires a balanced business and technical leader who can challenge designs, diagnose complex issues, translate cyber risk into practical decisions, lead through influence, and build trusted relationships with security, technology, business, audit, compliance, HR, application, and regional stakeholders.


What Your Impact Will Be

·   Strengthen UMG’s identity-security foundations by improving the quality, ownership, governance, and reliability of identities, accounts, entitlements, access decisions, and lifecycle processes.

·   Establish and execute a multi-year IGA roadmap while stabilizing near-term control performance, including User Access Reviews, remediation, evidence, data quality, workflow reliability, and ownership accountability.

·   Reduce inappropriate, excessive, stale, orphaned, and otherwise unmanaged access through risk-based governance, automation, clear accountability, and measurable control outcomes.

·   Translate business requirements, cyber risk, audit findings, control objectives, and architectural direction into prioritized capabilities, sustainable operating processes, and measurable results.

·   Improve the experience of business reviewers, application owners, access approvers, and technology partners while maintaining the rigor required for identity security and auditability.

·   Build a high-performing IGA team and strengthen the broader identity organization through mentoring, shared standards, technical leadership, and effective cross-functional partnership.


Job Functions

·   Lead the strategy, operating model, roadmap, governance, and day-to-day execution of UMG’s Identity Governance and Administration program.

·   Serve as the enterprise IAM deputy to the VP, Security & Identity, helping align identity governance, identity engineering, access management, privileged access, authentication, and related identity product functions around common security outcomes and priorities.

·   Directly lead, coach, and develop the IGA/Saviynt team; establish priorities, clarify accountability, remove obstacles, and promote a collaborative, security-minded culture.

·   Partner with the Sr. Security & Identity Architect to evaluate identity-security designs, establish practical standards and patterns, prioritize roadmap investments, and translate architectural direction into sustainable IGA capabilities and operating processes.

·   Serve as the business and governance product owner for Saviynt and related IGA capabilities, working with internal engineering teams, implementation partners, and vendors to define requirements, manage roadmaps, and deliver measurable improvements.

·   Own the end-to-end lifecycle of Saviynt User Access Review campaigns, including scope, population and data validation, reviewer and owner assignment, launch, reminders, escalations, remediation, certification, evidence, and formal closure.

·   Establish and maintain the UAR campaign calendar and readiness process, confirming that application data, entitlements, owners, reviewers, communications, dependencies, and support processes are prepared before launch.

·   Lead the continuous improvement of joiner, mover, and leaver processes, including identity creation, change detection, access updates, termination, deprovisioning, exception handling, and evidence of timely execution.

·   Govern access-request, approval, provisioning, deprovisioning, and recertification processes across applications, infrastructure, cloud platforms, and other enterprise services.

·   Establish effective governance for roles, entitlements, access packages, privileged access relationships, segregation-of-duties policies, high-risk access, service accounts, application accounts, and other non-human identities.

·   Define and improve data ownership models for authoritative identity sources, application accounts, entitlements, organizational attributes, manager relationships, and access metadata.

·   Improve the reliability of data synchronization and reconciliation relationships across HR, directories, identity platforms, applications, cloud services, service-management platforms, and other systems of record.

·   Monitor and improve data quality, connector health, reconciliation, workflow execution, notification, reporting, access-removal, and user-experience performance; identify root causes and coordinate sustainable resolution.

·   Translate policy, control, audit, risk, architecture, and business requirements into functional requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, test plans, implementation plans, operating procedures, and support models.

·   Manage the Saviynt enhancement, defect, integration, and technical-debt backlog; prioritize work using cyber risk, business impact, control effectiveness, operational resilience, user experience, and implementation complexity.

·   Establish appropriate governance for platform releases, configuration changes, workflow changes, integrations, access models, and other changes that may affect identity-security controls.

·   Define and report meaningful metrics, key performance indicators, and risk indicators, including campaign completion and timeliness, exception volume, remediation aging, access-removal effectiveness, data-quality trends, orphaned ownership, workflow and integration health, control performance, and vendor service levels.

·   Provide concise and actionable updates to governance forums and senior leadership on readiness, status, risks, issues, exceptions, remediation progress, decisions required, and the business impact of unresolved identity risks.

·   Partner with application owners, entitlement owners, business reviewers, IAM Engineering, Security Architecture, Security Operations, GRC, Audit, Compliance, HR, Service Management, regional IT teams, and external providers to drive accountability and results.

·   Support internal and external audits, control testing, regulatory inquiries, and risk assessments; respond to findings, develop remediation plans, and track corrective actions through closure.

·   Establish and maintain governance documentation, including standards, procedures, RACI models, data-ownership models, campaign playbooks, workflow documentation, communication templates, issue and decision logs, training materials, and audit evidence.

·   Lead stakeholder adoption and process change, using feedback and operational data to simplify processes without weakening identity-security controls.

·   Provide business and technical consulting on identity governance, helping stakeholders understand the cyber risk, control intent, technical tradeoffs, and practical path forward.

·   Mentor leaders and practitioners across the broader identity product organization, including through shared practices, design reviews, technical coaching, and career development.

·   Manage strategic vendors and service providers; establish expectations for deliverables, quality, service levels, issue resolution, roadmap alignment, and escalation.

·   Balance operational stability, control execution, platform modernization, project delivery, and strategic improvement in a global, fast-paced, and geographically distributed environment.

This role is based in Nashville and requires in-office attendance Tuesday through Thursday.


Job Requirements

Essential

·   Minimum of ten years of progressive experience in Identity and Access Management, Identity Governance and Administration, cybersecurity, technology risk, security architecture, consulting, or a closely related field; equivalent education and experience may be considered.

·   Minimum of five years leading enterprise IAM, IGA, security-governance, product, consulting, or technology-risk programs, including experience leading teams or complex cross-functional workstreams.

·   Demonstrated production experience with Saviynt, SailPoint, or other IGA platforms, including platform administration or configuration, User Access Reviews and access-certification campaigns, workflows, reporting, troubleshooting, integrations, and continuous improvement.

·   Strong practical knowledge of Saviynt or another enterprise IGA platform; experience with both Saviynt and SailPoint is preferred.

·   Deep understanding of identity-governance processes and controls, including joiner-mover-leaver, access requests and approvals, provisioning and deprovisioning, UAR and certifications, roles and entitlements, segregation of duties, least privilege, exception management, auditability, and control evidence.

·   Demonstrated understanding of identity data ownership, authoritative sources, synchronization and reconciliation relationships, data-quality management, and the dependencies between HR, directories, IGA platforms, applications, cloud services, and service-management platforms.

·   Experience governing human and non-human identities, including service accounts, application accounts, shared accounts, technical identities, and other machine-to-machine access.

·   Ability to understand and challenge technical designs, diagnose complex workflow or integration issues, assess tradeoffs, and distinguish sustainable control improvements from short-term operational workarounds.

·   Experience translating business needs, security risks, control requirements, audit findings, and architectural direction into practical roadmaps, functional requirements, operating processes, and measurable outcomes.

·   Demonstrated business and technical consulting experience, preferably across multiple industries, complex enterprises, or geographically distributed and matrixed organizations.

·   Experience partnering with security architects, engineers, application owners, HR, business leaders, audit, compliance, risk, and external vendors.

·   Strong program and product-management skills, with the ability to manage concurrent priorities, dependencies, roadmaps, releases, risks, issues, decisions, and stakeholder expectations.

·   Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical identity issues and cyber risk clearly to business stakeholders, technology teams, executives, auditors, and control owners.

·   Demonstrated leadership and ability to influence without authority, build trusted relationships, resolve conflict, drive accountability, and lead through organizational change.

·   Experience supporting audits, compliance activities, control testing, risk assessments, remediation plans, and evidence requirements within an IAM, IGA, cybersecurity, or technology-risk environment.

·   Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify patterns, evaluate data quality and control performance, determine root cause, and coordinate practical solutions.

·   Exceptional organization, attention to detail, documentation discipline, and follow-through, with the ability to work independently while maintaining a high level of accountability.

Desirable

·   Bachelor’s degree in cybersecurity, information systems, computer science, business, risk management, or a related field, or comparable education and experience.

·   Experience with adjacent identity and security technologies and data sources, including Workday or another HR system, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, ServiceNow, privileged access management, cloud platforms, enterprise directories, and application-integration services.

·   Working knowledge of identity and security protocols and integration patterns such as SAML, SCIM, OAuth, OpenID Connect, LDAP/LDAPS, APIs, and event-driven integrations.

Job Summary:

We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. As a key member of our Global Technical Operations team, you will be responsible for the reliability, scalability, and performance of the critical systems that power a global enterprise. By blending a software engineering mindset with operational expertise, you will engineer solutions that improve system reliability, automate complex processes, and reduce manual toil. You will be an essential partner to our development, infrastructure, and security teams, driving a culture of resilience and continuous improvement across the organization. 

As a Site Reliability Engineer, you won't just be supporting systems; you'll be ensuring the services that connect artists and fans around the globe are always on.

Job Functions:

Key Responsibilities

System Reliability & Performance

  • Design, build, and maintain the availability, scalability, and performance of critical services.
  • Develop and maintain robust monitoring, alerting, and observability systems (e.g., using AWS CloudWatch, Dynatrace) to ensure rapid issue detection and resolution.
  • Monitor infrastructure capacity and performance, providing analysis and suggestions for service delivery improvement.

Automation & Efficiency

  • Drive the automation of repetitive operational tasks, including infrastructure provisioning, deployments, and scaling.
  • Create and maintain scripts and custom code to support and enhance our operational toolset.
  • Support and optimize CI/CD pipelines to improve deployment speed and reliability.

Incident Management & Collaboration

  • Participate in an on-call rotation to troubleshoot and mitigate production incidents.
  • Lead post-incident reviews and root cause analyses to implement lasting solutions.
  • Partner with engineering and IT stakeholders to embed SRE best practices (SLOs, error budgets) into the design and development lifecycle.

Required Experience & Skills:

  • A strong background in systems administration (Linux/Windows) in a large-scale environment.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, Go, Java).
  • Hands-on experience with a major cloud platform (AWS, GCP, or Azure), with a high preference for AWS.
  • Solid understanding of networking, containers (Docker, Kubernetes), and Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, Ansible).
  • Experience with modern monitoring and observability tools (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, Splunk, Dynatrace).
  • Proven analytical and problem-solving abilities with experience in a high-pressure environment.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to foster a collaborative team environment.

Preferred Experience & Skills:

  • Bachelor's degree in an IT-related field.
  • Experience managing large-scale, distributed systems for a global organization.
  • Familiarity with IT governance standards like ITIL.
  • Direct experience with ServiceNow for IT service management.
  • Knowledge of chaos engineering, resilience testing, and advanced capacity planning.

job.title: Technical Operations Center Manager
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

Job Summary:

We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.

 

As a Technical Operations Center (TOC) Manager, you will be one of three global managers operating in a "Follow the Sun" model, ensuring continuous 24/7 coverage and operational excellence across our technical infrastructure. This role is accountable for more than ticket throughput. It turns operational signals into measurable reliability outcomes by strengthening service ownership, leading disciplined incident response, reducing repeat failure and toil, and moving the organization toward proactive, increasingly automated operations. Your leadership will be crucial in facilitating seamless handoffs between shifts, maintaining high performance, and upholding and improving they systems and processes that create operational drag.

 

Job Functions:

Service Reliability & Operational Leadership

·         Lead day-to-day operations for the Technical Operations Center, ensuring critical infrastructure and services are operated safely, reliably and consistently.

·         Establish and maintain a service-centric operating rhythm covering service ownership, criticality, dependencies, SLOs/SLIs, incident trends, capacity, risk and operational readiness.

·         Partner with service owners, engineering, cybersecurity, business technology teams and vendors to identify reliability risks before they become business-impacting incidents.

·         Use observability, telemetry and service health data to improve detection, prioritization and decision-making.

·         Maintain a regular operating review and publish a concise scorecard focused on outcomes rather than activity.

 

Major Incident Management & Swarming

·         Lead or sponsor response to major incidents, acting as Incident Commander or ensuring the appropriate command structure is in place.

·         Establish clear incident roles, escalation triggers, communication standards and decision rights for high-severity events.

·         Make swarming repeatable through shared queues, structured triage-ready information and timely engagement of the right technical and business partners.

·         Coordinate internal teams and third-party providers through restoration, stakeholder communication and service validation.

·         Ensure blameless postmortems convert incident learning into prioritized problem-management, reliability and prevention work.

 

Problem Management, Toil Reduction & Automation

·         Maintain a ranked backlog of repeat incidents, operational toil, alert noise and manual work, with owners and measurable outcomes.

·         Drive the conversion of repeatable procedures into versioned runbooks, scripts, workflows, automation and self-service capabilities.

·         Apply AI-assisted triage and knowledge discovery where appropriate, with human oversight, security controls, auditability and clear escalation paths.

·         Improve the quality, findability and lifecycle management of operational knowledge, including runbooks, known-error records, as-builts and shift documentation.

·         Track automation adoption and toil hours avoided using the results to redirect capacity toward reliability engineering and service improvement.

 

Change, Release & Operational Readiness

·         Strengthen risk-tiered change practices, including pre-checks, peer review, testing evidence, implementation plans, monitoring and rollback readiness.

·         Partner with engineering and delivery teams to shift operational readiness earlier in the lifecycle, including supportability, observability, runbooks and ownership before release.

·         Analyze change-related incidents and failure patterns leading corrective actions that improve change success and reduce recovery time.

·         Support paved-road standards and a transparent exception process for common infrastructure, cloud, identity, network and systems patterns.

 

Global Coordination & Follow-the-Sun Operations

·         Facilitate structured handoffs between global teams, ensuring the incoming shift receives current service health, active incidents, risks, decisions, next actions and escalation needs.

·         Maintain consistent severity, response, handoff, change and review practices across regions while respecting local context and coverage requirements.

·         Build strong working relationships across time zones, technical domains, business units and strategic vendors.

·         Participate in a rotating global coverage and escalation model, including occasional out-of-hours or weekend coverage when required. The schedule should support sustainable coverage rather than routine weekend office attendance.

 

People Leadership & Capability Building

·         Lead, coach and develop Technical Operations Center specialists, creating a culture of accountability, learning, collaboration and continuous improvement.

·         Set clear expectations for performance, incident leadership, documentation, operational discipline and customer experience.

·         Hire, onboard and develop talent while building role-based learning paths and cross-training plans for critical domains.

·         Establish resilient coverage with documented SME and backup relationships, reducing key-person dependency.

 

Job Requirements:

 

Skills/Abilities

·         Deep technical knowledge in infrastructure operations, site reliability, platform operations or related disciplines.

·         Ability to assess impact, prioritize under pressure, communicate clearly and make sound decisions during high-severity events.

·         Experience with service ownership, observability, SLOs/SLIs, operational readiness, runbooks and reliability metrics.

·         Experience reducing operational toil through scripting, workflow automation, self-service or similar engineering practices.

·         Working knowledge of cloud, identity, network, systems and/or enterprise infrastructure operations.

·         Ability to build trust across engineering, security, business technology, vendors and geographically distributed teams.

·         Commitment to blameless learning, continuous improvement and inclusive people leadership.


Experience

·         Eight or more years of progressive experience in infrastructure operations, site reliability, platform operations, IT service management or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

·         Three or more years leading technical teams, major incident response, operational programs or cross-functional reliability initiatives.

·         Demonstrated experience operating mission-critical infrastructure or applications in a complex, globally distributed environment.

·         Strong working knowledge of incident, problem, change, service-level and knowledge-management practices.

·         Experience leading a follow-the-sun operating model or global shift handoff process is preferred.

 

Preferred Qualifications

·         Experience with AI-assisted operations, event correlation, anomaly detection or intelligent triage, with appropriate governance and human review.

·         Experience implementing or improving a service catalog, SLO framework, error-budget practices or reliability scorecard.

·         Experience with ITSM, observability, automation/orchestration and knowledge-management platforms.

·         ITIL, SRE, cloud, automation or related certification.

·         Experience leading a follow-the-sun operating model or global shift handoff process.

 

Education

·         Industry-standard IT certifications are desirable; ITIL, SRE, cloud or automation certifications are a plus.

job.title: Vice President, Finance
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

How we LEAD:


The Vice President, Finance is a senior financial leader responsible for driving profitable growth, financial discipline, and strategic decision-making across a music merchandise and apparel business operating through eCommerce, wholesale, retail, licensing and touring channels.

 

This role will engage in financial planning and forecasting, product and channel profitability, inventory and cost accounting, commercial deal evaluation, and management reporting. The Vice President will partner closely with executive leadership and teams across merchandising, eCommerce, retail sales, touring, licensing, production, supply chain, and operations.

 

The ideal candidate combines deep apparel-industry financial expertise with strong commercial judgment and a practical understanding of the operational complexities associated with inventory, product development, fulfillment, royalties, licensing, and multi-channel distribution.

 

How you'll CREATE:

 

  • Participate in the annual budget, long-range plan and periodic reforecast.
  • Partner with commercial leaders to develop revenue targets, margin goals, expense plans, and performance improvement initiatives.
  • Develop integrated financial plans covering revenue, gross margin, operating expenses, working capital, cash flow, inventory, and capital investment.
  • Provide timely variance analysis of actual results compared to budget, forecast, prior year.
  • Identify key performance drivers, risks, and opportunities and translate them into clear recommendations for senior management.
  • Develop and maintain profitability reporting by artist and business line and evaluate margin performance
  • Support inventory planning, SKU rationalization, markdown strategies and end-of-cycle inventory decisions.
  • Partner with business and legal affairs and senior management in deal structuring and negotiation.
  • Support assortment planning, demand planning, pricing decisions, product launches, artist campaigns, tour planning, retail programs, and customer negotiations.
  • Develop executive dashboards and management reporting that provide clear visibility into revenue, margin, profitability, inventory, cash flow, and operational performance.

 

Bring your VIBE:

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, business administration, or a related discipline.
  • Significant progressive finance experience, including leadership responsibility in FP&A, commercial finance, operational finance, or a related function.
  • Substantial experience in the apparel, fashion, merchandise, footwear, accessories, consumer products, or closely related inventory-based industry.
  • Strong knowledge of apparel economics, including product costing, sourcing, landed cost, inventory management, markdowns, returns, sell-through, and seasonal product lifecycles.
  • Experience leading annual budgets, forecasts, long-range plans, management reporting, and financial performance reviews.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze profitability by product, channel, customer, artist, program, or business unit.
  • Strong understanding of inventory accounting, cost accounting, inventory reserves, purchase commitments, and working-capital management.
  • Experience evaluating commercial deals, investments, guarantees, royalties, licensing arrangements, or strategic partnerships.
  • Familiarity with ERP and warehouse management systems, specifically SAP, BPC, Oracle HFM.
  • Experience with financial planning, business intelligence, reporting, or data-visualization systems.
  • Advanced Excel skills, including complex financial modeling, scenario analysis, large datasets, lookups, pivot tables, and structured reporting.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate financial concepts clearly to creative, commercial, operational, and executive audiences.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial, and deadline-driven environment.

job.title: R1 News Anchor
job.description:
About the Role:

The R1 News Anchor is responsible for anchoring newscasts, news gathering, reporting, content creation, execution, and collaborative strategy on all WIBC/Network Indiana on air, digital and social platforms. The position requires the production and gathering of text, images, audio/video,etc. Video production and posting experience preferred. The ideal candidate will have a knack for social media and possess excellent writing skills and news judgement. Will be responsible for creating on air news packages for use on WIBC and Network Indiana and anchoring newscasts as assigned. This role requires synthesizing complex information into clear, concise narratives that inform and captivate viewers while maintaining journalistic integrity and impartiality. The anchor will collaborate closely with producers, reporters, and technical staff to ensure seamless broadcast execution and adherence to editorial standards. Additionally, the position involves staying current with breaking news, conducting live interviews, and adapting to rapidly changing news environments. Ultimately, the R1 News Anchor plays a critical role in shaping public understanding and trust through professional and compelling news presentation.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Proven experience as a news anchor or reporter with on-air presence in a professional broadcast environment.
  • Exceptional verbal communication skills with the ability to articulate complex information clearly and engagingly.
  • Strong understanding of journalistic ethics, news production processes, and media law.
  • Ability to work under pressure and adapt quickly to breaking news and changing schedules.
  • Experience with digital media platforms and social media engagement to extend news reach.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Communications, Broadcast Media, or a related field.
  • Proficiency in teleprompter operation and familiarity with broadcast studio technology.
  • Experience in investigative journalism or specialized reporting areas such as politics, economics, or science.

Responsibilities:

  • Present daily news broadcasts clearly and confidently, ensuring accuracy and professionalism in delivery.
  • Write report on, write, and edit news stories, scripts, and content for broadcast.
  • Conduct live interviews with guests, experts, and correspondents to provide in-depth coverage and diverse perspectives.
  • Monitor breaking news and update scripts promptly to reflect the latest developments during live broadcasts.
  • Maintain a strong on-air presence by engaging viewers with a balanced tone and clear communication.
  • Participate in editorial meetings to contribute ideas and feedback for improving news coverage and presentation.
  • Adhere to all journalistic ethics, legal standards, and company policies to uphold credibility and trust.

Skills:

The R1 News Anchor utilizes strong communication skills daily to deliver news stories in a clear, engaging, and trustworthy manner, ensuring viewers remain informed and connected. Critical thinking and editorial judgment are essential for selecting relevant news content and responding effectively to live developments. Technical skills and familiarity with broadcast equipment, support smooth and professional on-air presentations. Interpersonal skills facilitate productive collaboration with producers, reporters, and guests, enhancing the quality and depth of news coverage. Additionally, adaptability and composure under pressure enable the anchor to maintain poise during breaking news and live interviews, ensuring consistent broadcast excellence.

job.title: Broadcast Technician - Relocation to Huntsville, ON
job.description:
Reporting to the Director of Technical Operations, the Broadcast Technician is responsible for maintaining Vista Radio’s cluster of stations across our Ontario markets, ensuring reliable broadcast operations and supporting all technical processes related to transmission, studio systems, and content delivery.

This is a permanent, full-time position based in Huntsville, Ontario. Interested candidates must be willing to relocate. Relocation assistance will be provided.

About the Role

The Broadcast Technician plays a critical role in keeping our stations on-air and operating at peak performance. This position supports transmitter sites, studio environments, automation systems, and network infrastructure, while ensuring compliance, uptime, and operational excellence across the cluster.

Responsibilities

Installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of FM/AM broadcast transmitter systems

Diagnose RF and transmission system issues using strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills; assess equipment health onsite and remotely, determine repair options, dismantle components for off-site repair, and complete replacements and installations as required

Installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of radio studio equipment including computers, AXIA IP audio consoles, nodes, processors, analog consoles, mixers, microphones, amplifiers, speakers, and STL systems

Troubleshoot mixed digital and analog broadcast environments

Installation, maintenance, and ongoing troubleshooting of broadcast computers and hardware supporting ENCO Radio automation systems, servers, regulatory audio loggers, IP online streams, and audio distribution systems

Maintain building infrastructure, documentation, and inspection reports; identify current or potential issues and implement preventative maintenance measures to improve uptime

Proactively monitor critical equipment and make necessary adjustments to ensure broadcast continuity and content delivery

Troubleshoot, maintain, and repair radio automation systems and related networks, routers, switches, and wireless access points

Provide remote and hands-on technical support to station staff, including support for remote broadcasts

Liaise with management to address facility issues including HVAC, power outages, generators, internet and phone outages, working toward timely restoration

Maintain accurate and up-to-date technical records and generate reports with findings and recommendations; liaise with community contractors to obtain project costing aligned with departmental budgets

Travel to transmitter sites throughout the province for maintenance, testing, and site upkeep, including vegetation removal near towers and building entrances

Participate in after-hours and on-call rotations as required; respond to emergency and off-air situations. Travel may be required

Qualifications

Minimum three (3) years of recent and direct radio engineering experience in a Broadcast Technician role

Graduate of an electronics technician or technologist program preferred

Strong technical aptitude and hands-on troubleshooting skills

Self-motivated, reliable, and safety-conscious

Detail-oriented, highly organized, and able to prioritize effectively in response to changing needs or critical off-air emergencies

Demonstrated interest in staying current with industry trends and technical standards

Positive attitude with a strong customer service mindset

Demonstrates Vista Radio’s core values: Integrity, Respect, Compassion, Responsibility, and Excellence

Ability and willingness to work in all climates

Valid driver’s license with a clean driving abstract

Proficiency in written and spoken English

Working Conditions

Permanent, full-time position based in Huntsville, Ontario

Relocation required for candidates not currently residing in the area; relocation assistance will be provided

After-hours and on-call work required

Travel within Ontario required

job.title: Chief Engineer - Huntsville, ON
job.description:
Reporting to: Director of Technical OperationsTerm: Permanent, Full-TimeLocation: Huntsville, Ontario

Role Overview

The Chief Engineer is an in-house leadership role responsible for overseeing the technical operations across our Ontario radio markets. This role provides leadership within each cluster, guiding and supporting the technical team while maintaining their own responsibilities. The Chief Engineer will take the lead from the primary technician in each market, supervise project initiatives, and serve as a key support for technical staff. The technical team within each cluster reports into this role, which in turn reports to the Director of Technical Operations.

Responsibilities

Provide technical leadership and support within each cluster, ensuring all technical staff receive guidance and oversight on project initiatives.

Oversee the installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of FM/AM broadcast transmitter systems.

Diagnose and resolve RF and transmission system issues both onsite and remotely, determining repair strategies in the field and offsite as needed.

Supervise the installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of all radio studio equipment, including computers, AXIA IP audio consoles, nodes, processors, analog consoles, mixers, microphones, amps, speakers, and STL systems.

Maintain and troubleshoot mixed digital and analog environments, ensuring seamless integration of broadcast automation systems, servers, regulatory audio loggers, IP streams, and audio distribution systems.

Conduct proactive monitoring of critical broadcast equipment and implement necessary adjustments to maintain uptime.

Manage building infrastructure, maintain documentation and inspection reports, and schedule preventative measures to improve reliability.

Lead the troubleshooting, maintenance, and repair of radio automation systems, network infrastructure, routers, switches, and wireless access points.

Provide both remote and hands-on technical support for station staff, including troubleshooting remote broadcasts.

Act as the primary liaison with management regarding facility issues, such as HVAC, power outages, generator operations, internet, and phone service disruptions, working towards prompt resolution.

Maintain accurate records and generate reports on system health, equipment status, and recommended improvements. Develop costing estimates for projects in alignment with budget expectations.

Travel to transmitter sites for routine maintenance, equipment testing, and site cleanup, including vegetation management around towers and buildings.

Provide emergency after-hours response for critical technical issues and off-air situations, as required.

Qualifications

Minimum of 5 years of recent, direct experience in radio engineering as a Broadcast Technician.

Graduate of an electronics technician or technologist program preferred.

Strong technical skills and problem-solving aptitude.

Proven leadership skills with the ability to supervise and support a team of technicians.
