job.title: Network Architect
job.description:
Network Architect

Position Summary

We are looking for an experienced Network Architect to design, optimize, and oversee our network and firewall infrastructure. This position will be responsible for ensuring our data, cloud, and security systems are scalable, reliable, and secure.

This is the deepest technical seat on the network team. It owns how the network is designed: corporate, data center, cloud, and the media networks that carry live content, and it leads the team that runs it. The lead responsibility is real but informal. There are no direct reports. This role leads through design authority, technical credibility, and follow-through. On a lean team it is also a working role: the architect writes the configs, joins the maintenance window, and handles escalation for any outages or issues, and mentors other engineers.

Depth is the point of this position. It is not a role for a generalist who reviews vendor diagrams. The successful candidate can defend a design decision under questioning, read a packet capture, and troubleshoot a problem at all hours. This role owns the architecture being right and the network staying up.  This position will be the SME for all network and security infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

Network Architecture

  • Plan, design, and own the LAN,WAN,and hybrid onsite/cloud architecture. Provide a roadmap to keep architecture up to date and to encompass new technologies.

  • Produce architect-grade documentation: designs with stated requirements, constraints, alternatives considered, failure modes, and a migration path. Not diagrams alone.

  • Maintain IP/Vlan schemas and configuration standards.

  • Set routing and switching standards — analyze traffic patterns, monitor network performance, and address any latency, network bottlenecks, or bandwidth issues.

  • Design for measurable resilience: no single points of failure on network paths, and a documented, tested behavior for every failure path.

  • Own capacity planning and technology lifecycle across the network; make the buy/refresh case with data.

  • Evaluate platforms and vendors on technical merit and give management a defensible recommendation, including the option not to buy. 

  • Prepare project plans, budget estimates, and resources needed for any infrastructure deployments.

  • Technical peer to partner with other teams for operational or engineering needs.

Network Security Architecture

  • Own Palo Alto firewall architecture: PAN-OS platform design, Panorama management, App-ID/User-ID policy model, decryption strategy, HA design, URL filtering, AI security, and geo-location firewall rules.

  • Own remote access and edge architecture — GlobalProtect, ZTNA/SASE direction, internet edge, and cloud connectivity.

  • Design segmentation and east-west controls, including microsegmentation strategy for the data center.

  • Ensure logging and flow visibility reach network monitoring and security tools.

  • Keep abreast of new URL categories, technologies, and vulnerabilities.  Make recommendations where needed for upgrades, changes, new licenses, or new technologies.

Network Operations Leadership (Soft Lead)

  • Own the operational health of the network day to day: monitoring, alerting, incident queue, change quality, code upgrades, policies, and procedures.

  • Set the engineering standards the team builds to; review every significant change before implementation.

  • Own change planning and maintenance windows in a 24x7 environment — pre-checks, rollback, post-change validation, and coordination with on-air schedules.

  • Serve as the top escalation point for network incidents and lead technical bridge calls.

  • Own the postmortem and drive corrective actions to closure.

  • Mentor engineers and grow the bench so the team is not single-threaded.

  • Coordinate with other business-unit technologists on shared work: agree on outcomes, publish expectations, follow up until closed.

  • Act as the technical delegate in vendor, carrier, and architecture review sessions.

Communication

  • Write clearly. Designs, standards, change records, and incident narratives are deliverables of this role, held to the same standard as the engineering.

  • Present and defend architecture to technical peers, and translate the same decision into cost, risk, and on-air impact for executives.

  • Communicate during incidents on a defined cadence: what is known, what is not, what is being done, when the next update comes.

  • Give management an accurate picture without prompting — what is on track, what is slipping, what needs a decision.

Ownership & Accountability

This is stated explicitly because it is the primary filter for this role. The successful candidate:

  • Owns the design and its consequences. A failure caused by an architecture decision is an architecture problem, not an operations problem.

  • Verifies rather than assume — redundancy is proven by testing the failover, not by reading the diagram.

  • Surfaces bad news early, with a recommendation attached.

  • Does not defer to a vendor SE for a decision this role should be making.

  • Takes responsibility for the team's misses when leading the work, and gives credit for the wins.

  • Do not let something fall because it sat outside the job description.

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years in enterprise network engineering, with 3+ years in an architect or principal-level role.

  • Expert-level routing and switching: BGP, OSPF, VXLAN/EVPN, multicast, QoS, high availability. Design-level, not just configuration level.

  • Deep hands-on experience with Palo Alto (PAN-OS, Panorama) and Cisco platforms (Catalyst, Nexus, ACI, Meraki switches and routers).

  • Demonstrated experience designing and operating networks in a 24x7 environment where downtime is externally visible.

  • Strong troubleshooting discipline: packet capture, flow analysis, and structured fault isolation under pressure.

  • Track record of leading technical work through people who do not report to you.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred

  • CCIE, CCNP, Palo Alto certification, or equivalent depth demonstrated by work history.

  • Familiarity with multicast including protocol implementation and configuration

  • Experience with a data center or facility build, migration, or consolidation.

  • Familiarity with network monitoring and network observability platforms

  • SD-WAN and cloud connectivity design experience (Direct Connect / GCP Interconnect).

  • Automation or scripting for network config and validation (Python or equivalent).

  • AI experience to accelerate troubleshooting and problem resolution, automate repetitive tasks, and increase operational efficiency

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to these characteristics. We are dedicated to providing a workplace free from harassment and discrimination.

job.title: Security Engineer
job.description:
Security Engineer — GRC, Cloud, Workspace & IdAM

Reports to: Director, Systems Operations & Cybersecurity

Location: Atlanta / Hybrid


Position Summary

This role runs programs that most organizations staff separately: governance and compliance, cloud, SaaS, Identity and Access Management security posture, and the assessment cycle that tests them all.

It is an individual contributor role with program ownership. There are no direct reports, and nearly everything that needs to change is owned by someone else — a cloud engineer, an application owner, a business-unit administrator. The work is therefore split between doing (assessing, documenting, evidencing, configuring) and driving (getting findings closed by people who do not report here).

The Director owns policy approval, budget, vendor contracts, and executive reporting. This role owns the programs running, the findings closing, and the evidence being ready before it is asked for.


Key Responsibilities

Governance, Risk & Compliance

  • Maintain the security policy and standards library — drafting, revision cycles, approvals, publication, and attestation tracking.

  • Own the risk register day to day: intake, scoring, treatment plans, owner assignment, and review cadence.

  • Map controls to the applicable framework(s) — NIST CSF / CIS Controls / SOC 2 / PCI DSS.

  • Run exception and risk-acceptance governance: documented, time-bound, owned, and reviewed on expiry rather than renewed by silence.

  • Own third-party and vendor risk reviews, including pre-contract security assessment and periodic reassessment of critical suppliers.

  • Complete customer and partner security questionnaires; assemble evidence packages for audits, insurers, and M&A due diligence.

Identity & Access Management (IdAM)

  • Implement, support, and troubleshoot Identity and Access Management (IdAM) and Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions.

  • Administer and maintain identity security platforms and directories (e.g., Okta, Password Safe).

  • Design and enforce secure remote access.

  • Partner with the identity team on SSO coverage and lifecycle so SaaS access follows the joiner/mover/leaver process rather than around it.

Google Workspace & SaaS Security

  • Own the security configuration of Google Workspace: admin console hardening, context-aware access, 2SV enforcement, Drive external sharing controls, Gmail threat protection and routing rules, DLP policies.

  • Govern third-party OAuth application access — review, approve, restrict, and periodically re-review what has been granted access to corporate data.

  • Monitor Workspace alert center and audit logs; investigate and escalate anomalous access, sharing, and configuration change.

  • Extend the same discipline to the broader SaaS estate: inventory sanctioned applications, review security configuration at onboarding, and identify shadow IT.

Cloud Security

  • Operate the cloud security posture platform (Wiz) across GCP/AWS/Azure: coverage, policy tuning, and triage of misconfigurations, exposed workloads, and toxic combinations.

  • Route findings to the accountable engineering owner with enough context to act, and track them to closure against defined SLAs.

  • Review cloud IdAM configuration — over-permissive roles, standing access, unused credentials, key hygiene.

  • Contribute cloud security requirements to new architecture and provide secure-by-default baselines that teams can adopt without a consultation.

  • Partner with the network and endpoint security functions on shared telemetry, logging coverage, and detection gaps.

Security Assessments

  • Plan and execute recurring internal security assessments against the control framework.

  • Coordinate third-party penetration tests and external audits: scoping, scheduling, access, evidence, and readout.

  • Own the finding lifecycle end to end — validation, owner assignment, remediation tracking, retest, and closure. A finding is not closed because it was assigned.

  • Maintain a single consolidated view of open findings across all sources (pen test, audit, cloud posture, vulnerability scanning, assessments) so remediation is prioritized once, not five times.

  • Support security awareness programs and phishing simulation where they intersect with control requirements.


Communication

  • Write clearly and for the audience. Policy, findings, risk narratives, and evidence summaries are the primary output of this role — writing quality is a core requirement, not a soft skill.

  • Explain a finding in terms of business impact and required action, not tool output. An engineer should be able to read the ticket and act without a meeting.

  • Give the Director an accurate picture without prompting — what is closing, what is stuck, what needs escalation or a risk decision.

  • Present assessment and compliance status to stakeholders across the business units at a defined cadence, showing trend and decision rather than raw counts.


Ownership & Accountability

This is stated explicitly because it is the primary filter for this role. The successful candidate:

  • Owns the outcome, not the ticket. Nearly every fix belongs to someone else — driving it to closure still belongs here.

  • Follows up without being reminded, and escalates with a recommendation when follow-up stops working.

  • Verifies rather than assumes. Remediation is confirmed by retest, not by an email saying it was handled.

  • Keeps the evidence current continuously, so audits and insurance renewals are a retrieval exercise rather than a fire drill.

  • Raises the uncomfortable finding, including when it lands on an internal team or a senior stakeholder.


Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years in information security, with demonstrated ownership of a GRC program or a substantial portion of one.

  • Technical knowledge in designing and implementing Identity & Access Management (IdAM) and Privileged Access Management solutions.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud security posture management (Wiz or comparable tool) and practical understanding of cloud IdAM and misconfiguration risk in at least one major provider.

  • Administration or security-configuration experience with Google Workspace (or comparable enterprise SaaS suite), including sharing controls, DLP, and OAuth app governance.

  • Experience running or supporting security assessments, audits, and penetration tests, including evidence production and remediation tracking.

  • Working knowledge of at least one control framework — NIST CSF, CIS Controls, SOC 2, or PCI DSS — applied in a real environment rather than studied.

  • Demonstrated ability to drive remediation through teams that do not report to you.

  • Strong technical writing. Candidates should expect to provide a writing sample.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.


Preferred

  • CISSP, CISA, CCSK, CISM, or cloud provider security certification.

  • Experience administering and maintaining security platforms such as Okta, Password Safe, Crowdstrike, Wiz, Palo Alto XSIAM, and ExtraHop.

  • Scripting for evidence collection and reporting automation (Python, PowerShell, or equivalent).

  • Experience with cyber insurance underwriting questionnaires or M&A technology due diligence.

  • Experience in media, broadcast, or another 24x7 operational environment.

  • Familiarity with vulnerability management and endpoint security tooling (CrowdStrike) as a consumer of their output.


First-Year Success Measures

Timeframe

Expected Outcome

 

90 days

Policy library and risk register inventoried and current-state assessed; Wiz, Workspace, and IdAM configurations baselined against benchmark; consolidated open-findings view established; relationships built with each remediation owner.

6 months

Control framework crosswalk complete and evidence mapped; exception governance running with dated, owned entries; cloud, Workspace, and identity findings closing against SLA with measurable backlog reduction; third-party risk review process operating at onboarding.

12 months

Audit, questionnaire, and insurance evidence produced on request without a scramble; at least one full internal assessment cycle and one external test completed with findings closed or formally accepted; measurable reduction in external Drive exposure and over-permissive cloud/IdAM roles; risk register reviewed in a standing governance forum with business participation.


Working Conditions

  • Occasional participation in incident response and after-hours escalation.

  • Periods of elevated workload around audit, assessment, and insurance renewal cycles.

  • Occasional travel to sites/facilities.

  • Hybrid/Atlanta office onsite expectations.

job.title: Systems Operations Architect
job.description:
Systems Operations Architect

Reports to: Director, Systems Operations & Cybersecurity 

Direct reports: None. Design authority for the systems estate; works alongside the Lead Systems Engineer and through matrixed engineers in the business units.

Location: Atlanta / Hybrid 

Position Summary

This is the deepest technical seat on the systems team. It owns how the platform estate is designed — directory and identity infrastructure, virtualization and compute, storage and data protection, and the Windows and Linux operating environments — and it owns whether that design holds up when something fails.

The role has no direct reports and no authority over matrixed engineers or application owners. It leads through design authority, technical credibility, and follow-through. On a lean team it is also a working role: the architect builds the proof of concept, writes the automation, joins the maintenance window, and takes the escalation when a recovery is not going as documented.

Depth is the point of this position. It is not a role for a generalist who reviews vendor reference architectures. The successful candidate can defend a design decision under questioning, explain the failure behavior of their own cluster design, and has personally recovered something important under time pressure.

The Director owns budget, vendor contracts, policy, and executive reporting. The Lead Systems Engineer owns day-to-day operational execution and the team queue. This role owns the architecture being right, the recovery actually working, and the estate not accumulating debt faster than it retires it.

Key Responsibilities

Directory & Identity Infrastructure

  • Own Active Directory and Entra ID architecture: forest and domain design, trust model, sites and replication, DNS, and hybrid identity synchronization.

  • Own the tiered administration model — administrative tiering, privileged access workstations, clean-source principle, and the roadmap to eliminate standing domain-level privilege.

  • Own Group Policy and configuration architecture, and the migration path toward modern management where it makes sense.

  • Own certificate services (ADCS) design: hierarchy, templates, autoenrollment, lifecycle, and the plan for what breaks when a CA expires.

  • Design service account and machine identity architecture — gMSAs, credential rotation, and integration with the privileged access management platform tools. 

  • Partner with the identity function on Okta integration, authoritative source of truth, and authentication flow design across on-premises and SaaS.

Virtualization, Compute & Storage

  • Own VMware vSphere/vCenter architecture: cluster and failure-domain design, HA and DRS policy, admission control sizing, host lifecycle, and storage presentation.

  • Own the hypervisor platform strategy, including the Broadcom licensing trajectory. Evaluate alternatives on cost, risk, and migration effort, and give the Director a defensible recommendation — including the option to stay.

  • Design storage architecture for the platform estate — capacity, performance tiering, replication, and the interaction with media storage where they meet.

  • Own capacity planning and hardware refresh cycles; make the buy case with data rather than vendor projections.

  • Design the hybrid and cloud IaaS footprint (GCP, AWS, Azure) — landing zone, connectivity, workload placement criteria, and migration path.

Data Protection & Recovery

  • Own backup and recovery architecture end to end: coverage, immutability, air-gapped or logically isolated copies, retention, and replication topology.

  • Define recovery tiers with real RTO and RPO commitments per workload, agreed with the business rather than assumed by IT.

  • Design and prove the ransomware recovery capability — isolated recovery environment, clean-room restore procedure, and AD forest recovery. Own the runbook and lead the exercise.

  • Establish restore testing as an architectural requirement with published results. A backup platform that has never been restored at scale is an unvalidated assumption.

  • Own disaster recovery design for critical platform services, including dependency mapping so recovery order is known before it is needed.

Operating Environment (Windows & Linux)

  • Own standards, hardening baselines, and golden images across Windows Server, Windows endpoints, and Linux (Ubuntu) distributions (CIS Benchmarks / DISA STIG as the reference).

  • Own patch architecture across both OS platforms — tooling, ring strategy, maintenance window design, exception handling, and emergency patch capability.

  • Own configuration management and infrastructure-as-code direction (Terraform, Ansible, DSC or equivalent) and drive the estate toward declarative, repeatable builds.

  • Own OS lifecycle and end-of-support planning so migrations are scheduled work rather than compliance emergencies.

  • Design provisioning and decommissioning so systems enter and leave the estate with their monitoring, backup, patching, and inventory records correct.


Technical Leadership

  • Set the engineering standards the systems team builds to; review designs and significant changes before they ship.

  • Serve as top technical escalation for platform incidents alongside the Lead Systems Engineer, and lead recovery on the hard ones.

  • Own the postmortem for system architecture-related failures and drive corrective actions to closure.

  • Mentor engineers and grow the bench so the team is not single-threaded — including this role.

  • Coordinate matrixed engineers and application owners on shared work: agree on outcomes, publish expectations, follow up until closed.

  • Act as the Director's technical delegate in vendor and architecture review sessions.

  • Support audits, assessments, and cyber insurance questionnaires with accurate architectural detail and evidence.

Communication

  • Write clearly. Designs, standards, runbooks, and recovery procedures are deliverables of this role, held to the same standard as the engineering.

  • Produce architecture-grade documentation: requirements, constraints, alternatives considered, failure modes, and migration path. Not diagrams alone.

  • Present and defend architecture to technical peers, and translate the same decision into cost, risk, and business impact for executives.

  • Communicate during incidents and recoveries on a defined cadence: what is known, what is not, what is being done, when the next update comes.

  • Give the Director an accurate picture without prompting — what is on track, what is slipping, what needs a decision.

Ownership & Accountability

This is stated explicitly because it is the primary filter for this role. The successful candidate:

  • Owns the design and its consequences. A failure caused by an architecture decision is an architecture problem, not an operations problem.

  • Verifies rather than assumes. Recovery is proven by restoring, redundancy by failing over, and hardening by testing — not by reading the documentation.

  • Surfaces bad news early, with a recommendation attached.

  • Does not defer to a vendor SE for a decision this role should be making.

  • Retires technical debt deliberately rather than documenting it and moving on.

  • Does not let something fall because it sat outside the job description.

Architecture-Grade Depth

Candidates should be prepared to whiteboard, without notes:

  • An AD tiered administration model, and specifically how it interrupts credential theft and lateral movement.

  • A vSphere cluster design with stated failure domains and the admission control math behind the host count.

  • An AD forest recovery from backup — order of operations, what goes wrong, and how long it actually takes.

  • A ransomware recovery design: where the immutable copy lives, how the clean room is built, and how you know the restored data is trustworthy.

  • A patch architecture spanning Windows and Linux with rings, SLAs, and a credible exception process.

  • A hybrid identity design across AD, Okta, Google Workspace and Entra ID — where authority lives and what breaks when the sync stops.

  • A certificate hierarchy and the blast radius when a CA or a widely deployed certificate expires unnoticed.

Depth in several of these with genuine working competence in the rest is acceptable. Surface familiarity across all of them is not.

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years in enterprise systems engineering, with 3+ years in an architect or principal-level role.

  • Expert-level Active Directory: design, hardening, tiering, and remediation at enterprise scale — not administration alone.

  • Deep design and operational experience with VMware vSphere/vCenter, including storage and failure-domain design.

  • Demonstrated ownership of backup, recovery, and DR architecture, with real recovery experience under pressure. Candidates should expect to be asked about a restore that went badly.

  • Genuine competence in both Windows Server and Linux at the architecture level. This role cannot be filled by a Windows-only or Linux-only engineer.

  • Patch and configuration management design across a mixed estate, with automation and infrastructure-as-code (PowerShell, Python, Terraform, Ansible or equivalent).

  • Experience operating in a 24x7 environment where downtime is externally visible.

  • Working understanding of identity and privileged access platforms (Okta, BeyondTrust or comparable PAM) as an integration partner.

  • Track record of leading technical work through people who do not report to you.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred

  • VCP/VCAP, Microsoft (Windows Server, Entra ID), RHCE, or equivalent depth demonstrated by work history; CISSP a plus.

  • Experience executing a directory, hypervisor, or backup platform migration.

  • Experience with a data center or facility build, migration, or consolidation.

  • Experience supporting broadcast, playout, or media asset management infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with hardening frameworks (CIS, STIG) applied in production rather than studied.

  • Media, broadcast, or another 24x7 operational background.

First-Year Success Measures

Timeframe

Expected Outcome

90 days

Current-state architecture documented across directory, virtualization, and data protection; unrecoverable or untested workloads identified and ranked; standing privilege and single points of failure catalogued; working relationships with application owners and business-unit engineers.

6 months

Target-state architecture and roadmap approved; hardening and build standards published and applied to new systems; recovery tiers defined with business-agreed RTO/RPO; at least one full recovery exercise completed with results reported honestly.

12 months

Demonstrated recovery capability against stated objectives, including an AD forest recovery exercise; measurable reduction in standing privileged access and in unsupported operating systems; hypervisor platform strategy decided and underway; provisioning and patching largely automated; team cross-trained with no single points of failure.


Working Conditions

  • Participates in an on-call rotation; serves as senior escalation for major platform incidents and recoveries.

  • Maintenance windows, migrations, and recovery exercises regularly fall outside business hours.

  • Occasional travel to sites/facilities.

  • Hybrid/onsite expectations.

job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Why we're hiring:

WPP Media, as part of WPP ET, is undergoing a significant transformation, modernising our ways of working, adopting cloud-native architectures, and prioritising AI and data-driven insights. This role is crucial for infusing AI-first thinking at every level. You will bridge the gap between high-level business strategy and hands-on technological exploration, acting as a catalyst for innovation. We need someone who can work closely with our teams to discover, design, and help deliver a truly reimagined future powered by AI, ensuring solutions align with our enterprise architectural principles and standards.

Are you a hands-on technologist with a solid understanding of the media or advertising business, eager to explore and apply cutting-edge AI? This isn't a traditional Enterprise Architect role focused purely on mapping and integration. Instead, we're seeking an aspiring architect who thrives on discovery and practical application.

You will be instrumental in exploring how emerging technologies, especially agentic AI, can fundamentally reimagine our business operations and client services. You'll also identify opportunities to accelerate our existing strategic programs, enhancing underlying systems (like ERPs) with AI rather than replacing them. This role is a unique opportunity to grow into a full Enterprise Architect by actively contributing to the strategic application of AI, working closely with product and engineering teams to turn vision into reality, all while learning to navigate and contribute to our architectural standards and governance processes.

Business Impact:

AI-Driven Innovation: Directly contribute to identifying, prototyping, and integrating agentic AI solutions that challenge conventional business models and create new value.

Operational Acceleration: Leverage AI to enhance the efficiency and intelligence of existing in-flight programs and core business systems.

Strategic Growth: Help shape the future technology landscape of WPP Media, defining how AI will underpin our next generation of products and services.

Learning & Development: Gain invaluable experience in enterprise-level architectural thinking, directly influencing major technology decisions and business strategy, including adherence to governance.

What you'll be doing:

  • AI Opportunity Identification: Actively research and identify high-impact opportunities for leveraging agentic technologies and broader AI/ML capabilities across our media business operations and client offerings.
  • Concept Prototyping & Validation: Work hands-on with cross-functional teams to prototype, test, and validate AI-driven concepts, demonstrating their potential to reimagine workflows or accelerate programs.
  • AI-First" Solution Design: Collaborate with Solution Architects and Product Owners to embed AI capabilities into the design of new products and enhancements for existing systems.
  • Business Process & AI Mapping: Assist in mapping current business processes, identifying specific areas where AI can be introduced for significant efficiency gains or new value creation, and contributing to high-level capability models.
  • Technology Trend Monitoring: Keep abreast of the latest advancements in AI, machine learning, and agentic systems, sharing insights and potential applications with the wider team.
  • Architectural Contribution & Governance Support: Contribute to defining and documenting architectural principles and patterns specifically tailored for AI-powered solutions, ensuring scalability, security, and ethical considerations. You will also support efforts to ensure new projects and solutions align with WPP's architectural standards and compliance guidelines.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Translate complex concepts into clear, actionable insights for business leaders, fostering understanding and buy-in for new initiatives.
  • Learning & Growth: Actively engage with senior architects and technical leaders, seeking mentorship and opportunities to expand your enterprise architectural knowledge and skills.
  • Focus on WPP ET goals that require architecting to align WPP Media to the rest of WPP ET, particularly in the area of AI capabilities 

Key 2026 Goals:

  • AI-Driven Innovation & Exploration: Actively contribute to the identification, exploration, and initial validation of innovative AI and agentic technology applications that either reimagine core business operations or accelerate strategic programs.
  • Strategic Solution Design: Collaborate with business and technology stakeholders to translate strategic objectives into high-level solution designs, ensuring alignment with defined business capabilities and technology roadmaps.
  • Architectural Standards & Governance Contribution: Support the application and evolution of WPP's architectural principles and governance frameworks, contributing to the development of design standards and ensuring solution compliance.
  • Continuous Architectural Development: Proactively engage in continuous learning and mentorship opportunities to deepen understanding of enterprise architecture practices, technology trends (especially AI), and their application within the media business.

What you'll need:

  • Media Business Acumen: Solid understanding of the media and advertising industry, including its key players, workflows, and operational challenges. Familiarity with common media production tools and workflows.
  • AI/ML Foundations: Demonstrated interest and foundational knowledge in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning concepts, including Generative AI and/or agentic systems. You should be excited by the potential of AI to transform business operations and client offerings.
  • Business Analysis & Requirements Gathering: Proven ability to gather, analyze, and document business requirements, translating them into actionable insights and technical specifications.
  • Business Process Understanding: Experience in analyzing business workflows and processes, with an eye towards identifying areas for improvement or re-imagination through technology.
  • Technical Acumen: Strong grasp of modern technology stacks, cloud platforms (e.g., Azure, AWS, GCP), APIs, data structures, and the software development lifecycle. Working knowledge of public cloud technologies and basic DevOps principles.
  • Solution-Oriented Problem Solving: Ability to break down complex business challenges into manageable parts, identify opportunities for technological intervention (especially AI), and propose practical, innovative solutions.
  • Communication & Collaboration: Strong oral, presentation, and written communication skills. Ability to clearly articulate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders and foster effective collaboration.
  • Stakeholder Engagement & Interpersonal Skills: Proven ability to build rapport, influence, and collaborate effectively with various stakeholders, including business leaders, product owners, solution architects, and development teams.
  • Growth Mindset & Curiosity: Eagerness to learn, adapt to new technologies, and proactively seek opportunities for professional development within the enterprise architecture domain. This includes an interest in Enterprise Architecture frameworks (like TOGAF®) and methodologies.
  • Collaboration Tools Proficiency: Proficiency in modern collaboration tools, including the Microsoft 365 ecosystem, for effective remote and hybrid teamwork.

Role Overview

 

The Payroll Executive will be responsible for supporting end-to-end payroll operations, ensuring accurate payroll processing, statutory compliance, employee query management, and payroll reconciliations. The role requires attention to detail, strong payroll knowledge, and the ability to coordinate effectively with internal stakeholders and payroll vendors.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Payroll Processing & Operations

  • Process monthly payroll activities and ensure timely and accurate salary disbursement.
  • Collect, validate, and compile payroll inputs including new hires, exits, salary revisions, leave data, and other employee-related changes.
  • Prepare payroll input and reconciliation files using Excel.
  • Verify payroll output reports received from payroll vendors, including salary registers, tax reports, and payroll summaries.
  • Support Full & Final Settlement (F&F) processing and validation.

Payroll Accounting & Reconciliations

  • Assist in payroll account reconciliations and payroll-related general ledger validation.
  • Support month-end payroll reporting and reconciliations.
  • Maintain payroll records and documentation for audit and compliance purposes.

Statutory Compliance

  • Support compliance activities related to Provident Fund (PF), Professional Tax (PT), Income Tax, Labour Welfare Fund, and other statutory requirements.
  • Coordinate with consultants/vendors for statutory challan generation and return filings.
  • Assist in quarterly e-TDS (Form 24Q) filings, revised returns, and Form 16 generation.
  • Track statutory payment and return filing timelines to ensure compliance.

Employee & Stakeholder Management

  • Respond to employee payroll queries and provide timely resolution.
  • Coordinate with HR, Finance, and business stakeholders to obtain payroll inputs and resolve payroll-related issues.
  • Maintain effective communication with payroll vendors and internal teams.

 

Audit Support

  • Support internal, statutory and tax audits by providing payroll-related data and documentation.
  • Assist in payroll reconciliations and audit requirements.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, Human Resources, or a related field.
  • Payroll, Taxation, or Finance certifications will be an added advantage.

Experience

  • 4 to 7 years of experience in payroll processing, payroll reporting, and statutory compliance.
  • Experience working with payroll systems and payroll vendors will be preferred.

Skills & Competencies

  • Good knowledge of Indian payroll processes and statutory compliances.
  • Understanding of Income Tax, Provident Fund, and payroll-related regulations.
  • Proficiency in Advanced Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Outlook.
  • Good verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Customer-focused approach towards employee query management.

Preferred Knowledge

  • Experience with payroll platforms such as ADP and Workday
  • Basic understanding of payroll accounting and statutory reporting.

Department: Treasury

Reporting To: Manager - Treasury

Job Location: Mumbai

Education Qualification Required: B Com/M Com

Number of Years of Experience Required: 2-4Yrs

Summary:

The Treasury Analyst is responsible for the day-to-day management of treasury operations, ensuring efficient cash flow, accurate financial reporting, and compliance with internal controls and regulations.

Key Responsibilities:

Daily:

  • Cash Management:
    • Prepare and share daily cash position reports with OpCo and regional teams.
    • Report cluster and cash balances to GL and Treasury Manager.
    • Manage fund flow and cash flow, including loan disbursements, payments, rollovers, and follow-ups.
    • Share bank debits with the Payments team and credits with the Collection team.
    • Share bank statements (collections) with relevant teams.
  • Accounting and Reporting:
    • Account for and approve treasury-related entries and share with the GL team for posting.
    • Prepare Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRSs).
    • Follow up with Collection and Payment teams to resolve open items in BRS.
    • Arrange entries for Conversion of EEFC balances to INR as needed.
  • Transaction Processing:
    • Prepare fund transfer letters, dial online transactions, and prepare checks for manual transfers.
    • Provide inward remittance purpose to banks for accurate credit allocation.

Weekly:

  • Prepare and share weekly cash flow forecasts.
  • Submit weekly cash reports to WPP Group Treasury.

Monthly:

  • Prepare and review intercompany cash pooling workings, entries, and payments, ensuring compliance with SOX controls.
  • Prepare Balance Sheet schedules (intercompany, expense, and income).
  • Generate stale cheque schedules.
  • Obtain balance confirmations and user access reports from banks.

Quarterly:

  • Obtain bank mandates from banks.

Yearly:

  • Ensure smooth dividend payout.
  • Manage timely renewal of LEI code.

As and When Required:

  • Handle documentation and setup for new account openings, bank mandate updates, net banking document execution, and signatory maintenance.
  • Maintain Board Resolutions as per OpCo or WPP SSC Treasury instructions.
  • Respond to audit queries (SOX, Statutory, Income Tax, Internal).
  • Perform other treasury activities as required.

Mandatory Responsibilities:

  • Comply with all Treasury Controls (SOX Controls) and CAS Controls.

job.title: Back End Engineer
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Senior FullStack Engineer
WPP Open · Engineering · Gurugram

About the job:

WPP Open is WPP's AI-enabled marketing operating system, used by brands and agencies around the world. Our engineering teams in India build and run it alongside colleagues in the UK and Europe. As a Senior Engineer you own a component or service, from its design and API to its tests and production health, and you mentor other engineers. The role is backend-heavy, and you also build the React interfaces for the features you deliver. Our interviews are practical and hands-on.

Responsibilities:

• Design, build, test and ship production code every sprint, test-first.
• Own a component or service end to end: its design, OpenAPI contract, data model, Playwright test suite, monitoring and runbook.
• Write design documents and architecture decision records for your component, and review other engineers' code with rigour and care.
• Choose between AWS Lambda and Kubernetes for your workloads, and build and maintain the CI/CD pipeline that ships them.
• Lead triage when your component fails, write post-incident reviews and fix the underlying causes.
• Build production AI features on the Anthropic and OpenAI APIs, and maintain your component's Claude Code configuration and MCP server.
• Explain technical trade-offs to product and delivery colleagues, including colleagues in other regions.
• Mentor less experienced engineers and help new joiners become productive quickly.

Minimum qualifications:
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

• 5 years of professional software development in TypeScript and Node.js or Python.

• 3 years of experience testing, maintaining or launching production software, and 1 year of experience with software design and architecture.

• Experience working in globally distributed teams across time zones, with stakeholders in other regions.

• Backend language and craft. You write idiomatic, strictly typed backend code in TypeScript with Node.js or in Python, with runtime validation at service boundaries using Zod or Pydantic. You understand concurrency in your language well enough to recognise blocking work and profile a misbehaving service, and you know NestJS, Fastify or FastAPI in depth.

• React and frontend. You choose and justify state-management approaches in React, keep rendering fast through memoisation, lazy loading and code splitting, and meet WCAG AA accessibility on the 
features you build. You contribute components to the design system and can build interfaces that stream responses from AI services.

• APIs and data formats. You design REST APIs with OpenAPI and own the contract for your service, including versioning, backwards compatibility, idempotency keys, rate limiting and webhooks. You know when to use JSON and when to use Protocol Buffers, and you check schema compatibility automatically in your pipeline.

• Data. You design PostgreSQL schemas and change them without downtime, tune slow queries and understand transaction isolation. You model data well in both DynamoDB and MongoDB, use Redis for caching, and choose the right store for each workload with clear reasons.

• Asynchronous systems and reliability. You design producers and consumers on queues such as SQS and BullMQ or Celery, with retries, dead-letter queues and idempotent handlers so that at-least-once  delivery is safe. You recognise when these safeguards are needed before anyone asks.

• Cloud and platform. You design services on AWS Lambda, with sensible function boundaries, concurrency settings, dead-letter queues and Step Functions or EventBridge where needed, all defined 
as code with AWS CDK or SAM. You operate workloads on Kubernetes, including Helm, autoscaling, rollouts and rollbacks, and you choose between serverless and containers for each workload.

• Testing and quality. You practise test-driven development and apply it to the design of whole components, not just individual functions. You write integration and contract tests with Testcontainers and
own your component's Playwright test suite, including test data, parallel runs and removing flaky tests.

• Observability and performance. You instrument services with OpenTelemetry, own the Datadog monitors, alerts and CloudWatch alarms for your component, and lead triage and post-incident reviews 
when it fails. You set performance budgets, profile under realistic load, and find memory leaks and blocking work in production.

• Security and identity. You implement OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect end to end, including the authorisation-code flow with PKCE and client credentials for service-to-service calls. You design role based access control, rotate secrets and keys, and secure your supply chain with dependency scanning and static analysis in the pipeline.

• Architecture and design. You design a service from a short brief, write design documents and architecture decision records that name the trade-offs, and design for backwards compatibility so that 
changes do not break the people who depend on your service.

• Engineering practices. You work trunk-based with GitHub Flow and hold others to it in code review. You build and maintain CI/CD pipelines, treat every dependency as something to pin and upgrade on a  regular cadence, and write documentation for the people who will read it. AI-first engineering and LLMs. You build production features on the Anthropic and OpenAI APIs, using tool calling, structured output and evaluations, and you track token usage and cost. You maintain the Claude Code configuration for your component, including CLAUDE.md, skills and subagents, and have built an MCP server that exposes your service to AI agents.

• Communication, collaboration and initiative. You communicate clearly and concisely, and you explain technical trade-offs to product, design and delivery colleagues in terms they can act on. You understand problems quickly and confirm shared understanding before acting. You collaborate well across locations and time zones, working asynchronously and handing over cleanly. WPP Open · Engineering · Gurugram

About the job:

WPP Open is WPP's AI-enabled marketing operating system, used by brands and agencies around the world. Our engineering teams in India build and run it alongside colleagues in the UK and Europe. As a Senior Engineer you own a component or service, from its design and API to its tests and production health, and you mentor other engineers. The role is backend-heavy, and you also build the React interfaces for the features you deliver. Our interviews are practical and hands-on.

Responsibilities:

• Design, build, test and ship production code every sprint, test-first.
• Own a component or service end to end: its design, OpenAPI contract, data model, Playwright test suite, monitoring and runbook.
• Write design documents and architecture decision records for your component, and review other engineers' code with rigour and care.
• Choose between AWS Lambda and Kubernetes for your workloads, and build and maintain the CI/CD pipeline that ships them.
• Lead triage when your component fails, write post-incident reviews and fix the underlying causes.
• Build production AI features on the Anthropic and OpenAI APIs, and maintain your component's Claude Code configuration and MCP server.
• Explain technical trade-offs to product and delivery colleagues, including colleagues in other regions.
• Mentor less experienced engineers and help new joiners become productive quickly.

Minimum qualifications:
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

• 5 years of professional software development in TypeScript and Node.js or Python.

• 3 years of experience testing, maintaining or launching production software, and 1 year of experience with software design and architecture.

• Experience working in globally distributed teams across time zones, with stakeholders in other regions.

• Backend language and craft. You write idiomatic, strictly typed backend code in TypeScript with Node.js or in Python, with runtime validation at service boundaries using Zod or Pydantic. You understand concurrency in your language well enough to recognise blocking work and profile a misbehaving service, and you know NestJS, Fastify or FastAPI in depth.

• React and frontend. You choose and justify state-management approaches in React, keep rendering fast through memoisation, lazy loading and code splitting, and meet WCAG AA accessibility on the 
features you build. You contribute components to the design system and can build interfaces that stream responses from AI services.

• APIs and data formats. You design REST APIs with OpenAPI and own the contract for your service, including versioning, backwards compatibility, idempotency keys, rate limiting and webhooks. You know when to use JSON and when to use Protocol Buffers, and you check schema compatibility automatically in your pipeline.

• Data. You design PostgreSQL schemas and change them without downtime, tune slow queries and understand transaction isolation. You model data well in both DynamoDB and MongoDB, use Redis for caching, and choose the right store for each workload with clear reasons.

• Asynchronous systems and reliability. You design producers and consumers on queues such as SQS and BullMQ or Celery, with retries, dead-letter queues and idempotent handlers so that at-least-once  delivery is safe. You recognise when these safeguards are needed before anyone asks.

• Cloud and platform. You design services on AWS Lambda, with sensible function boundaries, concurrency settings, dead-letter queues and Step Functions or EventBridge where needed, all defined 
as code with AWS CDK or SAM. You operate workloads on Kubernetes, including Helm, autoscaling, rollouts and rollbacks, and you choose between serverless and containers for each workload.

• Testing and quality. You practise test-driven development and apply it to the design of whole components, not just individual functions. You write integration and contract tests with Testcontainers and
own your component's Playwright test suite, including test data, parallel runs and removing flaky tests.

• Observability and performance. You instrument services with OpenTelemetry, own the Datadog monitors, alerts and CloudWatch alarms for your component, and lead triage and post-incident reviews 
when it fails. You set performance budgets, profile under realistic load, and find memory leaks and blocking work in production.

• Security and identity. You implement OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect end to end, including the authorisation-code flow with PKCE and client credentials for service-to-service calls. You design role based access control, rotate secrets and keys, and secure your supply chain with dependency scanning and static analysis in the pipeline.

• Architecture and design. You design a service from a short brief, write design documents and architecture decision records that name the trade-offs, and design for backwards compatibility so that 
changes do not break the people who depend on your service.

• Engineering practices. You work trunk-based with GitHub Flow and hold others to it in code review. You build and maintain CI/CD pipelines, treat every dependency as something to pin and upgrade on a  regular cadence, and write documentation for the people who will read it. AI-first engineering and LLMs. You build production features on the Anthropic and OpenAI APIs, using tool calling, structured output and evaluations, and you track token usage and cost. You maintain the Claude Code configuration for your component, including CLAUDE.md, skills and subagents, and have built an MCP server that exposes your service to AI agents.

• Experience with monorepo tooling such as Nx or Turborepo at scale.
• Experience with Kafka and change data capture.

• Experience configuring an identity provider such as Okta, Keycloak or Cognito.

job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth.

For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

 

ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE

JOB SUMMARY

As an Account Executive at GCI Health, you will play an important role in ensuring that audiences experience our clients’ brands consistently, at all touchpoints, driving the greatest impact while retaining and building new business. You will support account teams’ day-to-day activities, providing exceptional client service and participating in integrated marketing communications (IMC), planning, execution and measurement activities. Key responsibilities include crafting professional, client-facing communications – such as updates on media opportunities, status reports, campaign summary reports and general account activity reports – so being a proactive and detail-oriented team member is a must!

CORE JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Client Service:

  • Keep up with the industry. Learn everything you can about your clients and understand the trends and issues (e.g., media, business, political and cultural) that could impact them, their competitors and the overall patient journey.
  • Participate in client planning meetings and calls. Ask informed questions and absorb important details.
  • Create professional, actionable client-facing communications (e.g., updates on media opportunities, status reports, campaign summary reports and general account activity reports).
  • Demonstrate proficiency with document review systems (e.g., Veeva Vault). Be able to upload error-free, quickly and in high-pressure situations. 

Strategy:

  • Ask. Wonder. Learn. Read presentation decks, listen in meetings, understand not just what you are doing but why it is being done, and how it adds value to our clients’ businesses.
  • Be responsible for tactical execution of client programming and able to deliver first drafts of next-step recommendations, campaign materials, timelines and briefs.
  • Contribute to IMC programs in a way that creates value and showcases our “Do Something Different” approach to meeting client objectives. 

Media:

  • Develop and maintain media lists and leverage relationships in collaboration with the GCI Health media team. Study and deliver well-written materials.
  • Monitor and report client media coverage. Understand how to use media platforms such as Cision and Factiva. Translate and communicate to clients in a way that adds value to their business.
  • Research, develop and pitch fresh, thought-provoking stories, and help coordinate press materials and events (such as press kits, news releases and press conferences).
  • Know the media landscape – including editorial calendars and subscribing to media newsletters. 

Digital:

  • Monitor, pitch and help build relationships with key social influencers and community contacts to optimize digital channels.
  • Stay current on social media channels, trends and analytics tools and make recommendations to strengthen client campaigns.
  • Develop content for social and digital channels to support brand strategies and appeal to target audiences.
  • Communicate and collaborate with the GCI Health digital team, as appropriate. 

Creativity:

  • Organize and participate in brainstorming meetings and contribute ideas based on knowledge of the client and outside reading and research.
  • Know our capabilities and when to engage creative resources.
  • Be curious. Note the latest trends in media, culture, healthcare innovation, etc., and apply them to clients’ programs by presenting a thoughtful and comprehensive POV. 

Research and Insights:

  • Know research and measurement methodologies and resources.
  • Implement research and measurement tools for client campaigns so we can measure success.
  • Synthesize research for analysis and summary reports for teams and clients. 

Business Development:

  • Listen. Every client meeting can lead to opportunities to add value and grow the relationship.
  • Monitor social media and other channels for relevant opportunities that could lead to new business; proactively flag with supporting rationale to core account team.
  • Assist with case studies for client presentations, new business pitches and industry awards.
  • Participate in new business research projects. 

Collaboration:

  • Share ideas; jump in when needed and ask others for their opinions and builds.
  • Weigh potential solutions and compromises based on what they mean to us and our clients. Be ready to defend your position confidently and articulately.
  • If people disagree, help find a solution everyone’s happy with; know when to involve a manager. 

Communication:

  • Know your audience; use language, style and tone that appeal to them. Communicate efficiently.
  • Meet or beat deadlines. Clearly communicate with clients and teams when deadlines shift.
  • Be professional when communicating to co-workers, clients and external audiences; skip jargon and clichés. Write with clarity and accuracy.
  • Follow AP Stylebook (or AMA, pending client preference) guidelines when writing press materials; understand how to reference. 

Financial Management:

  • Learn “the business” of our business and how we make money through meeting billability targets.
  • Record billable hours daily in Maconomy and make supervisors aware of your time.
  • Follow agency procedures for client budgets and budget tracking.
  • Manage vendor relationships, costs and invoicing. 

Diversity and Inclusion:

  • Create an inclusive and welcoming environment.
  • Demonstrate flexibility in a changing work environment.
  • Bridge differences between and among yourself and others.
  • Seek out and use ideas, opinions, and insights from diverse sources and individuals.
  • Use self-awareness to deflect biases.
  • Consistently demonstrate integrity and credibility while building trust through inclusive behavior. 

Team Management:

  • Coach and mentor junior team members (account coordinators and assistant account executives) to help them learn our business and capabilities.
  • Delegate tasks to junior team members with clarity, including timetables and expected outcomes.
  • Identify and implement skills-development needs for team members.
  • Review the work of junior team members and provide constructive feedback and edits where appropriate. 

Accountability:

  • Fulfill all commitments of your role.
  • Admit mistakes and misjudgments. Figure out how to avoid them in the future.
  • Take responsibility for tough decisions and actions to get things done.
  • Be a problem-solver. 

Agency Responsibilities:

  • Help recruit top talent by knowing our capabilities, locations and talking about the company in a positive way.
  • Contribute to the agency in a meaningful way through participation in culture initiatives, staff meetings, manager meetings and by being supportive of and kind to colleagues.
  • Adhere to GCI Health’s confidentiality and disclosure agreements and code of ethics/conduct.
  • Participate in agency Learning and Development opportunities as appropriate and as agreed upon with your manager.
  • Do Something Different in your approach, involvement and agency contributions!

job.description:

Account Manager

SECTION 1: ROLE OVERVIEW

As an Account Manager, you will leverage your existing knowledge of the healthcare communications industry to play a pivotal role in managing client relationships and delivering high-quality, integrated communications programs. You will contribute to the success of the agency by overseeing the efficient execution of day-to-day tasks, ensuring that client objectives are met with precision and strategic foresight.

Your responsibilities will range from managing tactical and administrative processes to developing strong relationships with mid-level clients and overseeing creative, strategic, and digital planning. You will also have a hands-on approach in ensuring that projects are managed effectively, meeting deadlines and financial targets.

Under the guidance of senior team members, you will refine your leadership skills while providing mentorship to junior staff, supporting both their personal and professional growth. You will collaborate closely with clients and internal teams to deliver successful outcomes and will actively contribute to agency growth and new business development.

GCI Health has worked hard to nurture and build a business, environment and culture we are very proud of. You are always expected to behave in a positive manner, motivating all staff you work with and those in the wider team both professionally and personally. You are expected to be respectful, friendly, approachable and conscientious.

SECTION 2: KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Key responsibilities include:

Client Services Management

  • Excel in managing tactical and administrative processes, ensuring that day-to-day operations run smoothly and efficiently.
  • Train and oversee junior staff performance, providing guidance and support in their development.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with mid-level clients, serving as the primary point of contact for critical aspects of account management.
  • Develop a comprehensive understanding of client needs, business goals, and industry landscape to deliver tailored communication strategies.

Product / Task Leadership & Accountability

  • Become the go-to person for successful project management, staying on top of details, timelines, and overall execution.
  • Proactively communicate and manage deadlines, ensuring all team members and clients are informed throughout the process.
  • Lead day-to-day project management from inception to completion, overseeing project budgets and deadlines to ensure timely and on-budget delivery.

Business Management

  • Participate in client and new business presentations, showcasing the agency’s capabilities and industry knowledge.
  • Supervise the client’s internal regulatory review process, ensuring compliance with industry standards.
  • Take ownership of all business and financial deliverables, ensuring flawless execution and flagging potential issues early.
  • Demonstrate a strong understanding of the healthcare industry, integrating this knowledge into day-to-day work.

Team Orientation / Collaboration

  • Foster a positive and collaborative team environment, ensuring effective communication and teamwork.
  • Mentor junior team members, offering support and guidance to help them succeed in their roles.

Personal Development and Growth

  • Actively manage your personal brand as you grow your career, consistently delivering improved products and services.
  • Work with a defined career path and action plan, taking responsibility for your development within the agency.
  • Continuously seek opportunities to enhance your skills and contribute to the agency’s overall success.

SECTION 3: EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS REQUIRED

Key experience and skills required to perform this role are:

  • A genuine passion for the healthcare industry, with a strong understanding of local, regional, and global healthcare environments.
  • Experience managing client accounts, particularly within the healthcare communication space, with a focus on mid-level clients and integrated campaigns.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring attention to detail.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with a focus on relationship-building and client satisfaction.
  • A proactive approach to project management, with the ability to manage timelines, budgets, and internal/external resources effectively.
  • Experience working with and mentoring junior staff, offering guidance and fostering their development.
  • Strong financial and business acumen, with the ability to flag issues early and drive profitability across accounts.
  • Ability to adapt and respond to the evolving digital and social media landscape, using these tools to enhance client programs and communications.
  • Ability to thrive under pressure while maintaining a positive attitude and a solutions-oriented mindset.

SECTION 4: REPORTING STRUCTURE

This role reports to a Senior Vice President or Managing Director, who will provide guidance and leadership support.

As an Account Manager, you will also work closely with senior team members and will have a key role in mentoring junior team members, offering them guidance and support in their daily tasks and long-term career development.

job.title: Business Security Director
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Why we're hiring:

We're looking for a Business Security Director to partner with one of WPP's most strategically important technology platforms.

This role will act as the dedicated security leader for WPP Open — our AI-powered marketing and business operating platform — helping ensure that security, trust, resilience and client assurance are embedded into how the platform evolves and scales.

Working at the intersection of platform security, product security, AI risk and client trust, you'll collaborate closely with product, engineering, AI and operational teams to shape security outcomes across a high-growth, highly innovative environment.

This is an opportunity to influence how one of WPP's most important technology investments manages security at scale while enabling innovation and business growth.

What you'll be doing:

Security Leadership & Business Partnering

  • Act as the primary security partner for WPP Open.
  • Build strong relationships across product, engineering, AI and architecture teams.
  • Translate enterprise security strategy into practical platform-specific outcomes.
  • Champion security as an enabler of innovation rather than a barrier to delivery.
  • Represent WPP Open within broader security governance and leadership forums.

Product & AI Security

  • Partner with product and engineering teams to strengthen secure software development practices.
  • Support the ongoing evolution of platform, application and API security controls.
  • Help shape the governance and assurance of AI-enabled capabilities and agentic workflows.
  • Drive a risk-based approach to emerging challenges including AI misuse, prompt abuse and data protection.

Client Trust & Security Assurance:

  • Help ensure robust controls around client data protection, segregation and confidentiality.
  • Support client assurance activities and security commitments for some of the world's leading brands.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders to maintain trust and confidence in WPP Open's security posture.

Identity, Resilience & Risk:

  • Support the evolution of modern identity and access security models across the platform.
  • Contribute to platform resilience, continuity planning and recovery readiness.
  • Work closely with cyber incident response teams on security events, investigations and risk management activities.
  • Help define and communicate security metrics, risk indicators and platform security trends to senior stakeholders.

What you'll need:

  • Significant experience in cyber security, product security, platform security or business-aligned security leadership roles.
  • Experience partnering with engineering, product and business teams in fast-moving technology environments.
  • Strong understanding of security challenges associated with cloud-native platforms, SaaS products and modern software delivery.
  • Knowledge of areas such as AI security, identity and access management, API security, client data protection and platform resilience.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication and influencing skills.
  • A pragmatic approach, balancing security requirements with product innovation and business objectives.

Nice to Have

  • Experience securing AI-enabled products, platforms or digital services.
  • Familiarity with recognised security frameworks such as ISO 27001, ISO 42001, SOC2, NIST AI RMF or OWASP AI Top 10.
  • Experience working with cloud environments including Azure, AWS or Google Cloud.

The role is responsible for leading and overseeing end-to-end cloud operations, ensuring the availability, reliability, security, performance, and resilience of cloud platforms and services. It manages service monitoring, incident response, and incident resolution for production applications and cloud infrastructure, while ensuring operations teams are skilled and enabled to execute cloud-related requests with speed and diligence. The role also provides governance over a large third-party managed services organisation, ensuring delivery against agreed KPIs, SLAs, and operational commitments through effective service reviews, metrics reporting, performance management, and continuous service improvement.

What you'll be doing:

Responsible for overseeing cloud operations, driving operational excellence, and improving the operational landscape through automation and AI-driven solutions delivered by internal resources and third-party partnerships.

Product:

  • Multi-cloud (AWS, Azure & GCP)
  • Databases
  • Citrix
  • CMDB & scope management
  • FinOps

Automation: Define and drive the cloud operations strategy through automation, AIOps, and AI-driven capabilities to enable predictive operations, intelligent incident management, and operational excellence. The role also champions self-service capabilities, operational dashboards, and auto-healing frameworks to enhance service resilience, efficiency, and scalability.

Management & reporting:

  • Define and execute the Cloud Operations strategy and operating model, aligning operational objectives with business and technology priorities.
  • Own the operational governance of a large third-party managed services provider, ensuring delivery against contractual commitments, KPIs, SLAs, OLAs, and service quality standards.
  • Drive vendor performance through Management Service Reviews (MSRs), governance forums, performance scorecards, and continuous service improvement initiatives.
  • Provide executive oversight of ITSM processes, including Incident, Major Incident, Problem, Change, and Service Request Management.
  • Act as the senior operational escalation point for critical incidents, ensuring effective stakeholder communication and timely service restoration.

  • Ensure cloud operations comply with security, risk, audit, regulatory, and governance requirements.
  • Lead operational readiness, capacity planning, resilience, disaster recovery, and business continuity for cloud services.
  • Collaborate with business, architecture, engineering, cybersecurity, and platform teams to ensure seamless service delivery and continual improvement.
  • Own performance reporting and provide clear, actionable insights to support operational governance and decision-making.
  • Ensure cloud infrastructure is regularly checked to maintain availability, meet performance SLAs, and complete performance tuning and runbook activities when required.

  • Solid experience in IT Infrastructure and Cloud Operations, with significant experience leading enterprise-scale cloud operations.
  • Proven experience managing cloud platforms (Azure, Google, and/or AWS Cloud Platform) and hybrid cloud environments.
  • Demonstrated experience leading large Cloud Operations teams, including governance of third-party managed service providers.
  • Proven experience managing vendor performance through KPIs, SLAs, OLAs, contractual governance, Management Service Reviews (MSRs), and continuous service improvement.
  • Strong understanding of cloud operations, infrastructure management, site reliability, operational resilience, and service lifecycle management.
  • Experience driving operational transformation through automation, AIOps, AI-enabled operations, and self-service capabilities.
  • Strong knowledge of ITSM processes, including Incident, Major Incident, Problem, Change, Request, Availability, Capacity, and Service Level Management.
  • Strong understanding of enterprise IT operations and service management platforms, including ServiceNow (e.g., ITOM Pro), and other industry leading monitoring, observability, and automation tools.
  • Good understanding of cloud security, risk management, compliance, business continuity, and disaster recovery principles, along with familiarity with vulnerability management and security tooling such as Qualys, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE), and Wiz, as well as cloud-native security and patching capabilities across Azure, Google & AWS Cloud Platform.
  • Familiarity with cloud-native monitoring, observability, and AIOps platforms, as well as leading enterprise solutions such as Grafana, Prometheus, ELK Stack, Dynatrace, Splunk, or similar technologies.

We’re looking for a Customer Success Lead to drive client adoption, build user capability and ensure customers realise lasting value from WPP Open Pro.

Customer Success sits at the heart of the client experience, helping customers move beyond simply accessing the platform to using it confidently, independently and effectively. You’ll own a portfolio of clients, leading their journey from onboarding and training through to sustained adoption and measurable outcomes.

This is a hands-on leadership role combining client relationship management, platform expertise and team development. You’ll work closely with WPP agencies, production partners and internal teams to deliver the right level of support for each client, whether through self-serve, blended or managed delivery models.

Alongside managing your own portfolio, you’ll lead and develop members of the Business Solutions team, setting high standards for delivery and helping the function scale as the Open Pro client base grows.

What you’ll be doing

Driving adoption and client value

  • Own adoption across your client portfolio, helping users progress from initial access to confident, active and self-sufficient use of Open Pro.
  • Identify and remove barriers to adoption, increasing platform usage and the value clients get from it.
  • Build client capability through coaching, training and ongoing guidance, reducing reliance on hands-on support over time.

job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth.
