job.title: Bureau Chief, Mansion
job.description:
Job Description:


Mansion Bureau Chief, Features
in New York, NY



The Wall Street Journal’s Features team is seeking a dynamic, experienced bureau chief to run Mansion, our luxury real estate section. Through its digital coverage and weekly print section, this section serves a broad and sophisticated audience: wealthy homeowners and real-estate professionals tracking the market and its biggest trends; aspirational readers who turn to it as a dream book; and anyone interested in social, cultural and economic forces shaping the world through the lens of real estate. 


This is an opportunity to lead a high-profile team that is prized for its ability to break major news, uncover market-moving shifts, produce deeply reported stories with real authority, as well as smart, buzzy features that capture the culture around homeowning.


Working collaboratively with columnists and reporters across Features and with teams throughout the newsroom, the ideal candidate is a self-starting editor with deep experience in real estate and home coverage and a sharp instinct for conceiving distinctive and highly visual digital stories. This editor should know how to turn strong reporting and ideas into journalism that travels across platforms and reaches audiences in different ways—from vertical video and social carousels to newsletters and the WSJ app.


The bureau chief will work closely with graphics, video, audience and platform editors to determine the best ways to package, present and amplify Mansion journalism, helping each story reach the right audiences in the right formats. 


A proven ability to find the stories where real estate intersects with investing, wealth, how people live and where they choose to live is essential.


The bureau chief will set the section’s editorial agenda, identify the biggest stories and opportunities, develop ambitious reporting and push the team beyond the expected. The goal is to build on Mansion’s position as an essential source for understanding the real-estate market and the people, money, culture and forces shaping how and where we live—and to ensure that journalism reaches and engages audiences wherever they encounter The Journal. 


You will:

  • Assign and edit multiple stories each week that explore the best of real estate and homeownership, from market and investment stories to architecture and design, delivering smart, engaging and useful reading for a broad audience. 
  • Manage and coach dedicated reporters and columnists on the Mansion desk, while building strong partnerships across Features and the broader newsroom to bring the best reporters and ideas to real estate coverage. 
  • Generate ambitious, highly shareable story ideas for the team that have clear news value, a strong real-estate hook and sharp, distinctive execution. 
  • Bring deep experience covering real estate and a strong understanding of the property market, along with a well-developed network of sources across the industry to break news, uncover trends, develop ambitious features and identify story lines that The Journal can own, from original reporting and exclusive access to distinctive franchises and deeper examinations of the forces reshaping how and where people live. 
  • Easily modulate between editing surprising, engaging and well-reported feature stories with fast, news-driven deal reporting. Embody the Features mission to simultaneously inform and entertain our audience. 
  • Work collaboratively and egolessly with others—both with Features editors as well as with our style and culture teams of reporters.
  • Know how to amplify traditional profiles, trends and event stories with humanizing detail and a sharp eye for shareable, well-crafted narratives that can become distinctive, high-impact Features stories. 
  • Embrace audience data, using metrics alongside strong editorial judgment, great taste and imaginative ideas to shape smarter real estate coverage. 
  • Ensure the top-tier execution and ethical standards of the Wall Street Journal and WSJ. Magazine are consistently met: that work is of impeccable quality across all platforms, and that The Journal’s codes of conduct and overall Standards & Ethics rules are scrupulously met. 

You have:

  • 5 to 8+ years experience as an editor on real estate or similar topics, including editing fast-breaking news, reported feature stories, and well-developed enterprise or longer-form features.
  • Experience editing complex subject matter.
  • An ability to identify potential legal issues.
  • An ability to enhance storytelling for our mobile audience, with a sophisticated understanding of how to capture and sustain audience attention across platforms. 
  • A proven history of finding unexpected takes on the real estate world, as well as an eye for elevated cultural and visually sumptuous stories that appeal to a general audience. 
  • Great contacts and a dogged, indefatigable sense of how to make stories happen.
  • A sense of humor, including a demonstrated ability to find clever, intelligent ways into stories that are being widely covered. 
  • A meticulous approach to getting facts and details exactly right, knowing how to push your team to avoid errors and bulletproof high-profile, visible stories with an attention to detail.
  • Visual thinking and a vested interest in how stories will look and present across platforms.
  • A collaborative, team-player attitude, an upbeat outlook and an entrepreneurial spirit as we grow and evolve coverage needs.

You will report to the Deputy Coverage Chief, Features.  This is a fulltime position based in our New York, NY office.  To apply, please submit your resume, a cover letter explaining how you would approach the job and a link to a portfolio of your relevant work by December 7. If necessary, include a very brief description of the role you played in each example. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage early submission as the position may be filled before the deadline.

job.title: Director of Legal Operations
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team

 

The Legal department has deep expertise in all core practice areas relevant to a global media and information company, including labor and employment, commercial agreements across all our businesses, privacy, intellectual property, M&A, litigation, corporate governance, compliance, media law and a variety of other specialties.


The team is also responsible for the company’s compliance program, including screening for compliance with international sanctions, enforcement of company policies—such as the Dow Jones Code of Conduct—and bolstering internal systems and controls.


We work in our Midtown Manhattan office 3 days each week.

 

You Will

  • Build a Legal Operations Function: Serve as the first head of Legal Operations at Dow Jones. You will establish the function and develop a clear multi-year strategy. This role, which will have one direct report to start, will report to the General Counsel of Dow Jones, and will join the Legal leadership team. 
  • Strategic Planning & Execution: Assist in various key projects across the department. You will track department goals, manage the legal roadmap, and help ensure we are hitting our milestones.
  • Financial Management: Assist with the legal budget. This includes outside counsel spend management, accruals, and finding "value-based" fee arrangements to replace the billable hour where possible.
  • Technology & Data: Serve as the manager and visionary for our tech stack (CLMs, e-Billing, IP Management, AI integration, and agentic tools). You don’t just use the tools; you optimize them to drive global legal team transformation and provide data-driven insights to the executive team. To start, AI integration and AI-powered solutions (evaluating current tools and scoping the need for next-generation agentic solutions) alongside process improvement will be a key focus and strategic priority.
  • Global Operational Scaling & Change Management: Partner closely with a globally distributed legal team across multiple international regions to harmonize processes and drive adoption of new technologies.
  • Vendor Management: Oversee our relationships with law firms and ALSPs (Alternative Legal Service Providers). You’ll run RFPs when needed and hold our partners accountable.
  • Project Management: Assist with various projects throughout the department. Whether it's implementing a new privacy compliance workflow, streamlining the workflow on contracts, or helping to coordinate legal resources on large projects, you provide the structure that frees up time across the department.
  • Knowledge Management: Help the Legal team build and maintain our internal core contract templates, playbooks, and training materials that empower the wider company to move faster.
  • M&A/Integration: Work closely with the M&A team on possible M&A opportunities and any resulting integration efforts. 

 

You Are

  • The Architect: You see a messy process and instinctively want to build a workflow for it.
  • The Translator: You can speak Legal (risk mitigation/precedent) and Business (ROI/efficiency) fluently.
  • The Diplomat: You can deftly handle an inflated bill just as effectively as you can pitch a new software spend to the CFO.

 

You Have

  • Experience: Minimum of 12 years of operations experience, and at least 5 years specifically within a Legal Operations function required. We are looking for someone who has worked in operations in a global legal department. Experience building a Legal Operations function from inception is strongly preferred. 
  • Education: A Law Degree (JD), MBA, or commensurate experience is valuable, but not required. We value operational excellence, project management experience, and other experiences that assist in navigating a growing, international business.
  • Tech Savvy: Deep experience with Enterprise Legal Management (ELM) software, AI-powered legal solutions, agentic tools, and Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) platforms, with a proven track record of leveraging technology for global legal team transformation, is a plus.
  • Industry Knowledge: Experience in the Media/Entertainment or Tech sectors is a plus.
  • Flexibility: The willingness to work in our Midtown Manhattan office 3 days a week.

job.title: Executive Director - Chemical Markets Price Reporting
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

As Executive Director - Chemical Markets Price Reporting, you will lead Dow Jones Energy's global chemicals price reporting business. You will oversee the editorial teams responsible for the assessment and publication of benchmark prices, assessments and market-moving news across global petrochemical and chemical markets from our PCW brand.

You ensure the integrity, quality, transparency, and market relevance of chemical price assessments while maintaining the highest ethical and methodological standards. You will lead a global team of price reporters and editors responsible for market coverage across key chemical value chains - including aromatics, olefins, plastics, polymers, syngas, methanol, feedstocks, and emerging chemical markets.

You will drive editorial excellence, benchmark innovation, and market engagement, while ensuring compliance with legal requirements and industry standards. You will partner closely with Product, Standards & Compliance, Risk, and other Editorial leaders to ensure Dow Jones Energy's chemicals assessments remain trusted, transparent, and indispensable to global commodity markets.

You will report to the SVP - Markets & Price Reporting.

About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Our offerings support institutional investors, analysts, and traders navigating spot, wholesale, and retail markets, as well as emerging segments tied to the global energy transition.

Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.

You Will:

  • Lead and develop a global team of chemicals price reporters, editors, and market specialists, fostering a culture of editorial excellence, accountability, and collaboration

  • Ensure all chemical market assessments are developed, maintained, and published in accordance with the highest standards of price assessment integrity, market transparency, governance, and ethical conduct consistent with Dow Jones’ and The Wall Street Journal’s values

  • Lead methodology development, periodic methodology reviews, market consultations, and stakeholder engagement processes to ensure pricing methodologies remain robust, representative, and responsive to evolving market dynamics

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with producers, consumers, traders, brokers, exchanges, trade associations, and other market participants to strengthen market engagement, data integrity, and confidence in Dow Jones Energy's petrochemical and chemical markets assessments

  • Partner with Standards & Compliance, Legal, and Risk teams to ensure ongoing compliance with applicable benchmark regulations, internal controls, audit requirements, and governance frameworks

  • Partner with Product to execute the strategic roadmap for global chemicals market coverage, including identifying opportunities for new benchmarks, market expansion, and portfolio optimization

  • Monitor benchmark performance, market adoption, customer feedback, and competitive developments - recommending changes to methodologies, coverage, and editorial priorities as appropriate

  • Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain high-performing editorial talent, ensuring appropriate succession planning, capability development, and organizational resilience across the chemicals price reporting organization

  • Act as a senior spokesperson and subject matter expert for chemicals markets, representing Dow Jones Energy at industry conferences, customer engagements, webinars, and regulatory forums

You Have:

  • 15+ years’ experience in commodity price reporting, market intelligence, or related information services organization

  • Deep knowledge of global chemicals and petrochemical markets, including physical market structures, trading practices, supply chains, and pricing mechanisms

  • Significant leadership experience managing geographically dispersed editorial, price reporting, or market analysis teams

  • Demonstrated experience developing, managing, or launching benchmark price assessments, methodologies, or market intelligence products

  • Strong understanding of IOSCO Principles for Oil Price Reporting Agencies and familiarity with benchmark regulation, governance, assurance, and audit requirements

  • Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to cultivate relationships with senior leaders and external market participants

  • A university degree -OR- relevant professional experience

job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

The Print Team supports the end-to-end lifecycle of Dow Jones’ print publications—including The Wall Street Journal, Barron’s, Investor’s Business Daily, and the New York Post.

Operating across ad intake, production workflows, plant operations, printing, packaging, single copy and amenity sales, Reprints and Licensing, and distribution; the team collaborates with internal cross-functional partners and external vendors, distributors, and the USPS to ensure quality, content freshness, safety, and cost efficiency from creation to final delivery.

About the Role

Production department: Printing and packaging of various newspaper titles including The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, Investors business daily and New York Post. You will perform daily press operations in the manufacturing of Dow Jones' and contract print publications in a cost-effective manner, with the highest quality standards available using existing technology. This includes Preparing, Operating and Maintain newspaper printing presses and all associated pressroom equipment. You will report to the Foreman/Woman and be based in White Oak, Maryland.

You Will:

  • Prepare presses for nightly operation of Dow Jones & Co. publications.
  • Perform press operations to continuously improve upon the Production Quality Score, which integrates key performance measures such as reproduction quality, content freshness, productivity, and cost-effective materials consumption.

  • Assist in the training of new employees.
  • Meet established performance standards, attend recommended training and complete active assignments.

  • Make pasters, web presses, push rolls, hang printing plates, set color and registration and general equipment cleaning and maintenance.
  • Meet customer expectations for reproduction quality, content freshness and productivity, while managing materials consumption cost-effectively.

You Have:

  • 4-5 Years of newspaper press experience.

  • High School Graduate/GED or equivalent work experience preferred.
  • Good color perception and are mechanically inclined.
  • Previous experience in a production environment preferably in cold web offset newspaper printing production environment.
  • Good verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong problem-solving skills.
  • Proficient in the use of business PC applications and press controls.

job.title: Principal - Finance Operations (Dow Jones Technology)
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

 As Principal - Finance Operations, you will transform Technology Finance Operations from a manual, spreadsheet-driven function into an AI-enabled, systems-oriented operating model that delivers greater speed, transparency, and operational leverage. 

You will own the business and financial operating cadence for Technology Operations while helping redesign how planning, governance, and execution works across both capital and operating investments. You will lead the redesign of the FY28 budget process, modernizing how Product, Engineering, and Design triads operate alongside PMO partners, business stakeholders and executives, and build scalable operating systems that allow Technology to accelerate with precision and accountability. 

This is a rare opportunity to build an operating model rather than inherit one. You will help shape how Technology plans investments, governs execution, and measures performance across a $300M+ portfolio while partnering directly with senior Technology and Finance leadership. 

You will report to the Vice President - Head of Financial Operations. 

About the Team:

Technology Operations is in the middle of a significant operating-model transformation: shifting from initiative tracking to OKR-driven governance, driving a vendor-partnered efficiency transformation, consolidating location strategy around strategic hubs, and redesigning processes with automation and AI-enabled capabilities at the core. Business Operations helps translate these strategic priorities into measurable operational and financial outcomes.

Working across Technology, Finance, Sourcing, Human Resources, the PMO, and external vendors, our team provides the operational discipline, financial stewardship, and governance needed to turn strategy into execution, enable better investment decisions, and build a simpler, more scalable operating model.

You Will:

  • Own the Technology Operations business management function, establishing the operating rhythm for planning, forecasting, decision support, governance, and execution

  • Lead the redesign of the FY28 budget process

  • Oversee the operating cadence for the $300M+ Product & Technology budget

  • Reengineer recurring financial and operational workflows by replacing manual processes with automation, intelligent workflows, and durable management systems

  • Partner with Finance, Sourcing, Human Resources, PMO, and Technology Executive and other stakeholders to translate strategic priorities into annual and multi-year operating plans

  • Improve governance and planning across triads by strengthening decision-making, planning discipline, accountability, and operating transparency in partnership with PMO leadership

  • Build and continuously evolve executive dashboards, KPIs, and operating reviews

  • Oversee vendor and investment governance across a complex technology portfolio

  • Establish scalable governance and financial controls across planning, forecasting, reporting, capitalization, and monthly operating reviews

  • Identify and deliver cost optimization opportunities while protecting service quality, resiliency, and long-term transformation objectives

  • Continuously raise the standard for business operations, financial stewardship, systems thinking, and execution excellence

You Have:

  • 12+ years’ experience in business operations, financial operations, FP&A, PMO, strategic planning, or related leadership roles supporting technology, infrastructure, or enterprise operations

  • Significant experience managing budgets, forecasts, business cases, capitalization planning, and executive financial reporting within complex organizations

  • A proven track record of redesigning operating models, governance frameworks, planning processes, or business management functions

  • Demonstrated success leading cross-functional transformation in ambiguous, high-impact environments while influencing senior leaders across multiple functions

  • Strong expertise in financial operations, vendor management, investment governance, cost optimization, and executive reporting

  • Experience designing executive dashboards, KPIs, and operating review mechanisms that improve business decisions

  • Proven ability to translate strategic priorities into structured plans, measurable outcomes, and repeatable operating systems

  • Ability to influence senior stakeholders and align organizations without direct authority.

  • A systems-thinking mindset with sound business judgment and a bias toward simplification, standardization, and continuous improvement

  • Experience designing, implementing, or leading the adoption of automation, analytics, dashboards, or AI-enabled workflows that materially reduced manual work in finance, planning, or business operations

  • Comfort working hands-on with automation, advanced analytics, and modern technology to improve cycle time, quality, and operational effectiveness

job.title: Principal Product Designer - Market Data
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

As Principal Product Designer - Market Data, you will own the design strategy for our Market Data platform—the real-time quotes, charting, watchlists, screeners, and visualization systems that power how millions of people read and act on financial markets across The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, and Investor's Business Daily. This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who sets direction across our financial brands and is the go-to design expert for how Dow Jones presents market data.

Market Data connects across every one of our financial brands, and this role sets the design strategy that spans all of them. Your decisions will establish shared patterns—for quotes, charts, tables, portfolios, and alerts—that these brands build on. You will own the direction for how investors of every kind, from first-time savers to sophisticated professionals, interpret dense, fast-moving data and turn it into confident decisions, balancing the distinct needs of each brand against the consistency and quality users expect wherever they encounter our data.

And this reach won't stop at the consumer. Market and pricing data runs across much of Dow Jones—so your influence will extend well beyond the consumer brands into our professional and enterprise products, from Factiva and Dow Jones Risk & Compliance to Dow Jones Energy, wherever market data underpins the experience. Where data meets the broader product, you will be the design lead who makes it cohere.

This is a role of real influence and scope. You will shape strategy with senior leadership, resolve tension between individual brand priorities and platform consistency, define the market-data patterns that live in our Index Design System, and mentor senior designers across the financial brands. You will be the design authority for your domain—navigating ambiguity and setting the standard others in your area build on.

You will report to the VP of Product Design within the Design & Research organization.

About the Team:

Our Design & Research org brings together world-class designers and researchers with a unified purpose: to connect people to the news and information that matters most. We're the strategic force that transforms deep user understanding into exceptional product experiences across our entire portfolio—from The Wall Street Journal to Factiva.

Our integrated approach ensures that research insights directly shape design decisions, while design explorations reveal new research opportunities. Together, we're building coherent, accessible experiences that honor our 135-year legacy while pushing us boldly into the future. We're a globally distributed team spearheading a digital transformation at Dow Jones, newly staffed by industry leaders from Google, LinkedIn, The New York Times, and more. Through our combined expertise in design craft and research rigor, we ensure that millions of users can depend on our platforms for truth in a world full of noise.

You Will:

  • Own the design strategy for the Market Data platform across our financial brands—setting a coherent, multi-year direction for quotes, charting, watchlists, screeners, portfolios, and data visualization that spans The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, and IBD, and connecting it to measurable outcomes like engagement, retention, and revenue

  • Shape strategy with senior leadership. Present your design direction for the Market Data platform to senior design, product, and business leaders—and to executives where the work warrants—building the partnerships that advance it across brands and making the case for how well-designed data experiences create competitive advantage

  • Solve the hard, ambiguous problems in your domain—developing new patterns, methods, and approaches for presenting complex financial information across multiple brands, and building a deep understanding of the problem space that lets you see opportunities ahead

  • Shape the market-data patterns in our Index Design System. Establish the charting, data-table, real-time, and visualization standards that become the norm across the financial brands—knowing when consistency serves the user and when a brand's audience warrants a tailored approach—and help adjacent teams adopt and evolve them

  • Extend your influence beyond our consumer brands into the wider portfolio—the professional and enterprise products, from Factiva and Risk & Compliance to Newswires and OPIS, where market and pricing data is just as central—so the experiences built on our data share the same clarity, rigor, and craft. Be the design lead wherever data shapes the product

  • Set a high bar for craft. Define what excellence looks like for dense, real-time financial information—typography, information density, motion, and the accessibility of complex tables and charts—and ensure consistent quality across the brands through design reviews and audits

  • Connect design to outcomes. Partner with Research and analytics to tie your decisions to engagement, retention, and subscription metrics, and help teams across the financial brands understand which measures matter for market-data experiences

  • Mentor and grow senior designers across the financial brands, shape a strong design culture, and strengthen the talent pipeline through the standards you set and the craft you share

You Have:

  • 10+ years of product design experience, including significant time owning complex, systems-level or platform work, with a track record of setting design direction that spans multiple products or brands

  • Deep expertise designing data-rich experiences—financial data, analytics, dashboards, data visualization, or other complex information display—where clarity, density, and trust matter as much as visual polish

  • A portfolio that demonstrates strategic impact across multiple products or brands: platform or design-system contributions, cross-team pattern-setting, and strong end-to-end craft on sophisticated products

  • A proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, translating design strategy into business terms and building alignment across teams whose priorities compete

  • Mastery of data visualization and information design—charting, tables, real-time data, progressive disclosure—and the judgment to know when complexity serves the user and when it gets in the way

  • Strong systems thinking and deep experience with design systems, including establishing patterns that other teams adopt and evolve

  • Excellence in Figma, with the ability to set standards for design communication, specifications, and documentation across teams

  • A deep command of design fundamentals and accessibility standards (WCAG), with particular fluency in making dense, complex data usable for everyone

  • A track record of mentoring designers and helping raise the craft and quality of the teams around you

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity—setting direction in your domain amid shifting priorities and emerging technology, and acting as the go-to expert others turn to

  • Bachelor's degree in Design, HCI, related field -OR- equivalent experience 

Nice to Have

  • Experience designing for financial services, investing, trading, or fintech products

  • Familiarity with real-time or streaming data systems and the constraints they place on design

  • Working knowledge of financial concepts—markets, instruments, portfolio construction—sufficient to partner deeply with domain experts

  • Background in news media, publishing, or other content-heavy products

  • Experience designing across a multi-brand portfolio

  • Experience contributing meaningfully to a design system

  • An external presence through speaking or writing on data visualization, information design, or design at scale

  • International or cross-cultural design experience

job.title: Principal Product Designer - Subscription Growth (Acquisition)
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

As Principal Product Designer - Subscription Growth (Acquisition), you will define the future of subscriber growth across Dow Jones' portfolio of brands, including The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, Investor's Business Daily, and future subscription products.

In this senior individual contributor role that operates at the intersection of design strategy, business strategy, and growth, you'll establish the long-term vision for how prospective customers discover, evaluate, and subscribe across our Commerce ecosystem - spanning registration, paywalls, shop experiences, pricing and packaging, checkout, identity, and experimentation.

You will partner closely with Product, Marketing, Brand, Engineering, Research, Analytics, and executive leadership to solve highly ambiguous challenges and shape investment priorities that accelerate subscriber growth. Your work will define scalable Commerce patterns, influence our acquisition platform strategy, and connect design decisions to measurable business outcomes across multiple brands.

Beyond delivering exceptional product experiences, you'll mentor senior designers, elevate design quality across Commerce, and establish standards that scale throughout the organization.You will report to the Director of Product Design, Commerce.

About The Team:

Our Design & Research org brings together world-class designers and researchers with a unified purpose: to connect people to the news and information that matters most. We're the strategic force that transforms deep user understanding into exceptional product experiences across our entire portfolio—from The Wall Street Journal to Factiva.

Our integrated approach ensures that research insights directly shape design decisions, while design explorations reveal new research opportunities. Together, we're building coherent, accessible experiences that honor our 135-year legacy while pushing us boldly into the future. We're a globally distributed team spearheading a digital transformation at Dow Jones, newly staffed by industry leaders from Google, LinkedIn, The New York Times, and more. Through our combined expertise in design craft and research rigor, we ensure that millions of users can depend on our platforms for truth in a world full of noise.

You Will:

  • Define the long-term design strategy for subscriber growth across multiple Dow Jones brands.

  • Lead highly ambiguous, business-critical initiatives spanning registration, identity, paywalls, shop experiences, pricing, packaging, checkout, and experimentation.

  • Partner with senior leadership across Product, Marketing, Brand, Engineering, Research, and Analytics to shape roadmap priorities and strategic investments.

  • Create scalable acquisition patterns, frameworks, and interaction models that extend our Index Design System and can be reused across brands.

  • Drive experimentation strategy by identifying high-impact opportunities throughout the acquisition funnel and translating insights into long-term product improvements.

  • Translate customer research, behavioral data, market trends, and business goals into experiences that improve acquisition performance while maintaining a high bar for user experience.

  • Lead strategic design explorations, vision work, and cross-functional workshops that align teams around future Commerce investments.

  • Mentor junior and mid-level designers through design reviews, coaching, and thoughtful feedback that elevates craft across the organization.

Dow Jones Risk is a global provider of best-in-class risk data, technology solutions, due diligence and managed services for managing regulatory and reputational risk. For 20 years, its market-leading data has helped financial institutions and businesses have greater control managing Financial Crime Compliance, Third Party Risk Management, Sanctions Compliance and Trade Compliance. With a global team of expert researchers covering more than 60 languages, Dow Jones applies the same rigor to its data that it has always brought to its journalism, offering the most accurate and complete risk datasets on the market.

job.title: Senior Data Analyst - Dow Jones Energy Product Management
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Our offerings support institutional investors, analysts, and traders navigating spot, wholesale, and retail markets, as well as emerging segments tied to the global energy transition.


Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.



About the Role:

This is an exciting time to join our small but growing Commercial Product Management team where you will be supporting a number of key sectors including: Energy & Feedstocks, Coal, Metals and Mining, Renewables & Clean Energy and Chemicals.


We are seeking a highly analytical and detail-oriented Senior Data Analyst to support business performance, revenue management, customer analytics, sales operations, product strategy, and executive decision-making. The position requires a combination of advanced Excel, SQL, Python, business intelligence, financial analysis, data visualization, and strong business judgment.


You will work across large and complex datasets to develop reporting, dashboards, analytical models, and actionable insights for product and leadership teams. You are comfortable working independently on ambiguous analytical problems, reconciling data from multiple sources, automating recurring processes, and communicating findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. You will also serve as a key analytical partner to the Product, Sales, Finance, Customer Care, Consulting, and leadership teams. You will report to the Vice President - Product Management. 



You Will:
  • Commercial & Revenue Optimization: Own end-to-end reporting for the Book of Business (ACV, renewals, new business, win/loss), building bottoms-up financial models, scenario analyses, and churn diagnostics to drive pricing, budgeting, and revenue retention strategies
  • Advanced Data Engineering & SQL: Query, transform, and aggregate complex datasets across multiple source systems using optimized SQL to resolve data discrepancies and ensure unified, cross-system reporting integrity
  • Data Quality & Governance: Establish rigorous validation processes, data cleansing protocols, and repeatable quality assurance checks to maintain accuracy and reliability across all core business metrics
  • Business Intelligence & Dashboards: Design and maintain scalable, user-friendly Power BI/Looker Studio dashboards that deliver actionable visibility into product performance, sales activity, customer health, and financial KPIs for non-technical stakeholders
  • Process Automation & AI Integration: Streamline recurring workflows using SQL, Python, Excel/VBA, and Power Query, while exploring AI/BigQuery solutions to scale self-service analytics and reduce manual reporting dependencies
  • Customer & Usage Behavioral Analytics: Synthesize product adoption, API/web activity, and usage data into customer health scores and engagement metrics that empower Sales and Account Management teams to mitigate churn Risk
  • Product Portfolio Strategy: Conduct product performance and entitlement analyses to evaluate pricing packages, support new product launches, and inform portfolio optimization or sunsetting initiatives
  • Cross-Functional Stakeholder Partnership: Serve as a strategic analytics partner across Sales, Finance, Product, and executive leadership, effectively communicating complex methodologies and managing ad-hoc analytical priorities to guide business decisions



You Have:
  • 3+ years’ professional experience in data analytics, commercial analytics, financial analysis, market research, or a related analytical role
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel; including complex formulas, PivotTables, XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, SUMIFS, nested logic, and data manipulation, VBA, Excel Macros, or Power Query
  • Experience with some or all of the following technologies:
    • Python (particularly Pandas and data analysis/automation)
    • BigQuery, Snowflake, SQL Server, Athena, or other cloud/data warehouse platforms
    • Power BI, Looker Studio, Tableau, or similar BI platforms
  • Experience with B2B data/information, industry analysis, and/or applied software products (highly desirable)
  • Domain knowledge in chemicals/energy or other related industry areas
  • An interest to pursue a career in product management and want to leverage your existing analytical skill set while deepening your product management capabilities and expertise
  • Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Finance, Business, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field -OR- equivalent work experience

job.title: Senior Director - AI Operations & Enablement
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Our Technology team drives the evolution of our Technology, Engineering, Data, Product and User Experience functions. With a keen focus on delivering cutting-edge solutions, we shape the digital landscape for our customers, readers and users. From revolutionizing visuals to optimizing tools and harnessing the power of data, mobile, video and social platforms, our team is committed to providing a seamless and immersive experience across all touchpoints. Collaborating closely with our newsrooms and strategic partners, we spearhead the development of groundbreaking products and technologies.

About the Role:

As Senior Director - AI Operations & Enablement, you will be an operator-builder who pairs executive-grade strategic judgment with hands-on technical fluency in modern AI tooling. You will be the trusted force-multiplier for the most consequential Tech Ops priorities at Dow Jones: reengineering how work gets done across Product & Technology, prototyping AI-enabled workflows directly, and turning fragmented, manual processes into scalable, AI-native operating models. In this high-autonomy role, you will diagnose the as-is, design the to-be, and ship the change - for quick wins and full rebuilds across a 130-year-old global news and information business. You will report to the SVP - Head of Technology Operations.

You Will:

  • Operate as a Strategic Force-Multiplier

    • Independently own and drive critical Tech Ops priorities end-to-end, with the judgment to know when to escalate and when to ship

    • Translate executive intent into structured plans, decisions, and outcomes

    • Represent Tech Ops in cross-functional forums where the SVP cannot be present, with full credibility to commit and decide

  • Reengineer How Work Gets Done

    • Lead wholesale process reengineering across Tech Ops and adjacent Product & Technology functions

    • Design target-state operating models that materially improve speed, quality, and cost

    • Define measurable efficiency outcomes and own them through delivery

  • Build AI-Native Workflows Directly (Hands-On)

    • Prototype AI-enabled automations and internal tools 

    • Use modern AI coding assistants and agentic development tooling to compress build time

    • Integrate AI capabilities into the SaaS stack the business already runs on

    • Set the technical bar for what "AI-native" means inside Tech Ops

  • Bridge Technology and the Business

    • Build trusted relationships with leaders across Product, Technology, GM-led business teams and our parent News Corp organization

    • Translate fluently between technical capability and business outcome

    • Drive enterprise-wide AI adoption 

    • Influence more efficient governance processes

  • Scale What Works through Systems Thinking 

    • Convert one-off wins into reusable playbooks, frameworks, and internal products

    • Document, train, and enable others to extend the operating model 

    • Identify when a workstream is mature enough to staff out

You Have:

  • At least 15 years’ progressive experience spanning technology operations, product or program management, management consulting, or transformation roles 

  • Demonstrated ownership of cross-functional process reengineering at enterprise scale

  • Strong systems thinking mentality

job.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Our Technology team drives the evolution of our Technology, Engineering, Data, Product and User Experience functions. With a keen focus on delivering cutting-edge solutions, we shape the digital landscape for our customers, readers and users. From revolutionizing visuals to optimizing tools and harnessing the power of data, mobile, video and social platforms, our team is committed to providing a seamless and immersive experience across all touchpoints. Collaborating closely with our newsrooms and strategic partners, we spearhead the development of groundbreaking products and technologies.

About the Role:

As Senior Machine Learning Engineer in the AI & ML foundations team, you will design and build the core systems behind our LLM applications: the orchestration layer, the reusable tooling and the evaluation harness that keeps it trustworthy in production. In this role, you will not be applying AI research or model training - but to real problems in production. You will report to the Director, Data Science & Insights.

You Will:

  • Design and build the orchestration, prompting, and workflow layers behind production AI features

  • Create composable tools and integrations, including retrieval and MCP servers and clients

  • Build evaluators, dashboards, and alerts that track accuracy, latency, cost, and hallucination

  • Harden the platform for production scale: caching, reliability, incidents, and model rollbacks

  • Set the technical bar through architecture decisions, design reviews, and mentoring

You Have:

  • At least 2+ years’ experience in software/ML engineering - which includes at least 1 years’ experience building LLM systems in production

  • Expert Python, hands on with LLM APIs and cloud platforms (AWS, Snowflake, Vertex)

  • Deep experience orchestrating multistep LLM workflows as execution graphs (e.g. LangChain/LangGraph).

  • Experience building agent harnesses: memory compression, skill disclosure, and tool design

  • Strong prompt engineering: tuning, versioning, and evaluation of prompts and model configs

  • A proven track record in AI evaluation, observability, and retrieval over enterprise data

  • Ability to explain complex AI concepts and tradeoffs clearly to nontechnical stakeholders

  • Fluency with agentic coding tools (e.g. Claude Code) and their architecture patterns (a strong plus)

job.title: Senior Manager, Creative Operations & Business Enablement
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team

The Brand and Experiences group plays an integral role in positioning the company for advancement and growth. We are responsible for the outward expression and inward embodiment of our Brand.  We develop the core capabilities, tools, and assets required to extend the Brand and empower GTM functions across the business by activating the Brand through campaigns, events, sponsorships, and tradeshows.  We do this by partnering with other areas of marketing, product, and sales groups to create high-impact opportunities to grow subscribers, sponsors, and accelerate the growth agenda.


The organization consists of a number of key, senior-level COE roles in areas such as Brand and Experiential Marketing, as well as senior capability leads. Together, this team will collaborate to build a unified, scalable, and consistent approach to marketing the brand to create awareness and drive preference.


About the Role

In this role, you will help strengthen how Brand operates and partners with the broader business by supporting the design, implementation and continuous improvement of Brand's operating model, processes and ways of working.


This role will partner closely with Ops leadership to understand business needs, assess Brand's capabilities, identify operational gaps, and translate those insights into practical processes, RACI, engagement models and enablement.


You Will:

Business Enablement

  • Partner on discovery with business units to understand their needs, workflows, pain points and opportunities to improve how they engage Brand.
  • Help define and communicate how and when teams should engage Brand, including the types of support and capabilities Brand provides.
  • Develop and maintain RACI, decision rights, engagement models and ways of working with key business partners.
  • Develop roadshows, playbooks, onboarding and other enablement that make it easier for teams across the business to understand and work with Brand.

Brand Capabilities & Insights

  • Help build and maintain a clear view of Brand's capabilities, services and outputs.
  • Gather and analyze information through surveys, workflow and asset analysis, stakeholder feedback and other sources to understand how Brand's capabilities are being used.
  • Identify capability gaps, recurring needs and opportunities to evolve how Brand supports the business.
  • Translate insights into recommendations for processes, ways of working and future capabilities.

Creative Operations & Process Improvement

  • Map current-state workflows and help design improved future-state processes.
  • Identify friction, unclear handoffs, unnecessary approvals and gaps across the creative lifecycle.
  • Develop and implement improved workflows, governance, RACI, escalation paths, SLAs and operating cadences.
  • Ensure operational processes support the realities of strategy and creative development while improving clarity, consistency and speed.

Tools & Technology Enablement

  • Help identify tools and technology that could improve Brand's workflows, creative processes and operational effectiveness.
  • Evaluate existing enterprise capabilities and emerging solutions, including opportunities to leverage AI and automation.
  • Partner with internal teams such as Technology, Procurement, Legal and Compliance, as well as external vendors, to understand requirements and support implementation of new capabilities.
  • Coordinate pilots, onboarding, training and adoption of new tools and features across Brand.
  • Partner with vendors such as Asana and existing enterprise technology partners to understand available capabilities and identify opportunities to improve how Brand works.
  • Track adoption and feedback to determine whether new tools are delivering the intended operational value.

Operating Model & Continuous Improvement

  • Support the ongoing evolution of Brand's operating model as business needs and capabilities change.
  • Monitor how new processes and ways of working are performing and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Pilot new approaches, gather feedback and support implementation and adoption.
  • Maintain the playbooks, standards and operating frameworks that enable consistent ways of working across Brand.
  • Help measure whether operating-model changes are improving clarity, collaboration, speed and effectiveness.

You Have:

  • 10+ years of experience in creative operations, production operations, workforce planning, or a related function, including experience operating at a senior manager level or equivalent scope.
  • Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional initiatives, partnering with senior stakeholders to assess business needs, align priorities, and drive organizational change.
  • Proven ability to design, implement, and optimize operating models, workflows, and processes, translating complex business challenges into scalable solutions that improve efficiency and effectiveness.

job.title: Staff Data Engineer
job.description:
Job Description:


Staff Engineer, Snowflake Platform


About the team
The Data Architecture & Platform Engineering team runs the data infrastructure behind Dow Jones products, analytics, and AI across B2B, B2C, and internal use cases. We own the Snowflake footprint which serves as the foundation of all DJ structured data, the surrounding platforms and patterns, and the governance framework. We build for scale, reliability, security, and cost efficiency.


About the role
This is an individual-contributor leadership role focused on Snowflake infrastructure at the Dow Jones enterprise scale. You'll own the platform end to end: account architecture and administration, security and access control, and the DevOps machinery that makes Snowflake safe and easy to use across dozens of teams and every business unit.


You will own the Snowflake platform's AI story: efficient, cost-managed access to Cortex and other AI features, optimized patterns for LLM-assisted workflows, and standards that let engineers across DJ build with AI on top of
governed data.


You'll ship the hard parts yourself, set the standards other teams follow, and mentor the engineers who work in and around Snowflake. You lead through influence: design reviews, working code, written arguments, and mentoring.


You'll partner with security, compliance, finance, product, and engineering leaders to turn DJ's data-platform goals into infrastructure that holds up over time.


You'll split your time between hands-on Snowflake work on the highest-stakes projects; standards and platform-level decisions; and mentoring engineers across levels.


What you'll do
• Own the Snowflake footprint across Dow Jones: accounts, warehouses, roles, databases, and the operating model behind them.
• Design and evolve RBAC, column and row-level policies, masking, tagging, and data classification for every business unit.
• Build and maintain the DevOps pipeline for Snowflake: Terraform, CI/CD for schema and object changes, automated testing, and change management.
• Set and enforce standards for security, network policies, private connectivity, SSO, SCIM, and secrets management.
• Optimize cost and performance: resource monitors, warehouse right-sizing, query analysis, credit budgeting, and FinOps reporting.
• Design for reliability at DJ scale: replication, failover, disaster recovery, incident response, and observability across the platform.
• Explore and implement emerging AI tooling to accelerate our modern data engineering practices.
• Lead architecture and design reviews for major Snowflake initiatives.
• Anticipate scalability, reliability, security, and cost problems before they land.
• Hunt technical debt in the platform to reduce complexity so downstream teams get more done with less.
• Debug the problems no one else can. Lead during incidents and get to root cause fast.

job.title: Summer 2027 Bartley Fellowship - Arts Criticism Internship
job.description:
Job Description:


Summer 2027 Bartley Fellowship - Arts Criticism Internship 

Job Description:

The Wall Street Journal's Arts in Review section is seeking aspiring journalists—juniors, seniors or recent graduates (within one year of graduation) with a strong editing background at their school newspapers or elsewhere—for a 10-week paid summer internship. The in-person internship is an opportunity to get hands-on experience working alongside some of the best opinion writers and editors in the world.

The internship—formally the Bartley Fellowship—honors the Journal’s former Opinion editor, Robert L. Bartley. Opportunities will be awarded to individuals interested in the arts who intend to pursue a career in journalism or cultural criticism.

The Arts intern is one of several fellows selected each year through an application process that is overseen by senior editors. Bartley Fellows are assigned to a department within the Opinion section—Arts in Review; Books; or Features (Op-Eds and Columns). The fellow will assist in producing Arts in Review’s content for the print and digital editions of the Journal—editing, fact-checking, liaising with writers, writing display copy, proofing, contributing to social media and digital production. Though this is not a writing fellowship, the Bartley fellow will be encouraged to produce a Masterpiece column, of which more below. They may also pitch articles or projects to editors elsewhere in the Opinion section.

Internships are paid, and generally take place during June, July and August, though start dates can be flexible. 

If you are interested in applying for the Opinion, Books or Arts in Review Bartley Fellowships, please submit separate applications for each position.


About Arts in Review 


Arts criticism is recognized at the Journal as an Editorial Page function, and as such operates under the umbrella of the Opinion section. Like the rest of the Opinion section, in our Arts reviews we believe in rendering clear, independent judgments that are as well argued as they are deeply informed.

In its Arts reviews, the Journal covers the full spectrum, from high art to TV, movies, theater and the many forms of popular music. Our approach is strictly art-for-art’s-sake: We review things because they are intrinsically interesting, not to fulfill a quota or make a political statement. We believe in the past and its traditions, but are keenly interested in the new—not in novelty for its own sake but in the ways those traditions are being extended and new ones invented. And we prize above all a lively, lucid prose style free from jargon of all kinds.


Guidelines and Application Deadline

Though a reporting and/or writing background is a plus, the fellowship is primarily an editing internship. Therefore applicants should have experience editing arts or arts-related copy for their college newspaper, literary magazine, or a comparable publication. Students from any discipline may apply, but preference will be granted to those concentrating in literature, history, a foreign language, classics, pre-law, music, theater, art history, studio art, architecture, philosophy, political science or archaeology—via coursework (though not necessarily a major) or sustained leisure-time activity.

An appreciation for both the Western and non-Western canons is desirable, as is an understanding of current issues in the arts. A demonstrated ability to multitask and meet daily deadlines is critical for success, as is attention to detail and a focus on accuracy. Applicants should be familiar with technology as it relates to journalism. Social media experience with a publication or brand would be a plus.

Applicants will be expected to demonstrate familiarity with our section’s content (student applicants without campus-wide access to the WSJ can purchase discounted subscriptions at https://www.wsj.com/studentoffer).

If you’d like to be considered, please submit the following in one single, complete PDF file:

  • A cover letter
  • Your résumé
  • Full text of your two best clips
  • Your response to the following prompt in no more than 800 words: Write a “Masterpiece” column. In these essays that appear every Saturday, a writer discusses a single work of art (painting, book, film, etc.) and explains why, in their view, it is of surpassing cultural significance. (Examples: https://www.wsj.com/news/types/masterpiece)

All materials must be received by Nov. 30, 2026. Only complete applications that include a cover letter, résumé and responses to the prompt will be considered. Please do not include any additional materials, such as transcripts, recommendation letters, etc. In order to be considered, you must be a U.S. citizen, or a holder of a green card or visa that will allow you to work in the United States. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and we endeavor to make selections by the end of February. Only finalists will be contacted.


About Bob Bartley


Throughout his 30 years as The Wall Street Journal’s Editorial Page Editor, Bob Bartley inspired principled and original thinking that changed and shaped the society in which we live. He also devoted attention to teaching and motivating talented young people, many of whom have gone on to careers in journalism at the Journal and elsewhere. The Bartley Fellowships are consistent with that legacy.

Bob Bartley achieved many honors during his long tenure here, including a Pulitzer Prize and, shortly before his death in December 2003, the Presidential Medal of Freedom. In awarding that medal, President George W. Bush cited Bob as “one of the most influential journalists in American history.” The Robert L. Bartley Fellowships will help to perpetuate not only Bob’s memory but, above all, the principles and priorities to which he devoted his distinguished career.


About the Opinion Section


Following the American newspaper practice, the heads of News and Editorial report independently to the publisher of the Journal and CEO of Dow Jones, Almar Latour. The Editorial staff is responsible for the Opinion content published on WSJ.com, the editorial and op-ed pages of The Wall Street Journal in print, and criticism of books and the arts, which are recognized at the Journal as an Opinion function.

While The Wall Street Journal’s news pages are committed to informing our readers, our editorials are dedicated to advocating a consistent philosophy and positions that emanate from it. That philosophy can be summed up as “free markets, free people.” We have stood for these fundamental principles even in times—and places—when they were not considered fashionable. While specific issues differ in various parts of the world, we view those issues through a consistent lens everywhere; for example, while protectionism is more popular in some parts of the world than others, our publications around the world are committed uncompromisingly to free trade.

We believe in the individual, in his wisdom and his decency. We oppose all infringements on individual rights, whether they stem from attempts at private monopoly, labor union monopoly or from an overgrowing government. Our section is not easily pigeonholed or predictable. We resist the label “conservative,” in the sense of preserving the status quo, because we think it too confining, too devoid of the optimism inherent in trusting individual wisdom and decency.

It is also important to state clearly what our section does not represent. It is not partisan. Unlike many American publishers, we do not endorse political candidates, and from time to time we have important disagreements with all leading political figures. We view issues through the lens of our philosophy and let our readers decide which person or party best serves to protect market capitalism and self-government.

We believe that the ultimate function of opinion journalism is the same as the rest of the newspaper: to inform. But in opinion journalism we have the additional purpose of making an argument for a point of view. We often take sides on the major issues of politics and society, with a goal of moving policies or events in what we think is the best direction for the country and the world. Our experience over many years is that even those who disagree with us on particular issues—or even on broader philosophical grounds—nevertheless respect us for the clarity, consistency and eloquence with which we present our point of view. In stating our own views forcefully, we hope to raise and sharpen the level of debate and knowledge. And we hope that our editorials reflect not merely the passing whim of passing editors, but a body of thought shaped by a century of tradition.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. EEO/Disabled/Vets

Applicants who are able to demonstrate familiarity with our section’s content will be especially attractive (student applicants without campus-wide access to the WSJ can purchase discounted subscriptions at wsj.com/studentoffer).

Students from any discipline may apply, but historically, we’ve been most interested in students concentrating on Journalism, Communications, Economics, Political Science, International Studies, History, a Foreign Language, Statistics, Finance, Pre-Law, Science, Business, Marketing, Religious Studies or Philosophy. Students from outside these disciplines are welcome to apply and should include a three-sentence case in their cover letter for why their field of study would be an asset for the section.

If you’d like to be considered, please submit the following in one single, complete PDF file:

  • A cover letter
  • Your résumé
  • Links to or cited full text of your three best clips
  • Your response to one of the following prompts in no more than 600 words:  Write an editorial either consistent with the WSJ’s philosophy in response to a current event in the news or defending your most controversial opinion. Write a sample letter to the editor responding to a recent WSJ editorial, Op-Ed or column. Compare and contrast two opposing arguments from any reliable, professional source(s) on the same topic. Submit an original investigative Op-Ed or original Opinion piece that is suitable in terms of style, tone of voice and topic for publication in the Journal.

All materials must be received by Nov. 30, 2026. Only complete applications that include a cover letter, résumé and responses to the prompt will be considered. Please do not include any additional materials, such as transcripts, recommendation letters, etc. In order to be considered, you must be a U.S. citizen, or a holder of a green card or visa that will allow you to work in the United States. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we endeavor to make selections by the end of February. Only finalists will be contacted.


About Bob Bartley


Throughout his 30 years as The Wall Street Journal’s Editorial Page Editor, Bob Bartley inspired principled and original thinking that changed and shaped the society in which we live. He also devoted attention to teaching and motivating talented young people, many of whom have gone on to careers in journalism at the Journal and elsewhere. The Bartley Fellowships are consistent with that legacy.

Bob Bartley achieved many honors during his long tenure here, including a Pulitzer Prize and, shortly before his death in December 2003, the Presidential Medal of Freedom. In awarding that medal, President George W. Bush cited Bob as “one of the most influential journalists in American history.” The Robert L. Bartley Fellowships will help to perpetuate not only Bob’s memory but, above all, the principles and priorities to which he devoted his distinguished career.


About the Opinion Section


Following the American newspaper practice, the heads of News and Editorial report independently to the publisher of the Journal and CEO of Dow Jones, Almar Latour. The Editorial staff is responsible for the Opinion content published on WSJ.com, the editorial and op-ed pages of The Wall Street Journal in print, and criticism of books and the arts, which are recognized at the Journal as an Opinion function.

While The Wall Street Journal’s news pages are committed to informing our readers, our editorials are dedicated to advocating a consistent philosophy and positions that emanate from it. That philosophy can be summed up as “free markets, free people.” We have stood for these fundamental principles even in times—and places—when they were not considered fashionable. While specific issues differ in various parts of the world, we view those issues through a consistent lens everywhere; for example, while protectionism is more popular in some parts of the world than others, our publications around the world are committed uncompromisingly to free trade.

We believe in the individual, in his wisdom and his decency. We oppose all infringements on individual rights, whether they stem from attempts at private monopoly, labor union monopoly or from an overgrowing government. Our section is not easily pigeonholed or predictable. We resist the label “conservative,” in the sense of preserving the status quo, because we think it too confining, too devoid of the optimism inherent in trusting individual wisdom and decency.

It is also important to state clearly what our section does not represent. It is not partisan. Unlike many American publishers, we do not endorse political candidates, and from time to time we have important disagreements with all leading political figures. We view issues through the lens of our philosophy and let our readers decide which person or party best serves to protect market capitalism and self-government.

We believe that the ultimate function of opinion journalism is the same as the rest of the newspaper: to inform. But in opinion journalism we have the additional purpose of making an argument for a point of view. We often take sides on the major issues of politics and society, with a goal of moving policies or events in what we think is the best direction for the country and the world. Our experience over many years is that even those who disagree with us on particular issues—or even on broader philosophical grounds—nevertheless respect us for the clarity, consistency and eloquence with which we present our point of view. In stating our own views forcefully, we hope to raise and sharpen the level of debate and knowledge. And we hope that our editorials reflect not merely the passing whim of passing editors, but a body of thought shaped by a century of tradition.

job.description:
Job Description:


Summer 2027 Internship – Brand Intern Application Deadline: November 13, 2026 We encourage you to submit your application as early as possible, as internship applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. AMER Internship Dates: June 7, 2027 – August 13, 2027 (You must be available to work full-time, in-office during this period.) Our interns work on meaningful projects alongside our teams, gaining hands-on skills that make an impact on the business. We believe the best way to learn is by doing — that’s why you’ll be paired with a mentor, connected with senior leaders, and included in professional development sessions. You’ll also join a diverse global intern community, sharing experiences and building networks that last beyond the program. Our goal is to provide a supportive, engaging, and fun environment where your work feels valued and your growth comes first. Check out our Dow Jones Internship Program page to learn more and hear directly from past interns about their journeys. At Dow Jones, you’ll have the chance to start your career in an environment where collaboration, trust, and impact come first. About the Role: We’re seeking a Brand Design Intern to join our Marketing team. In this hands-on role, you’ll help create new brand identities and support cohesive design experiences across digital, print, and spatial touchpoints. You’ll work with senior designers on projects spanning multiple brands—including The Wall Street Journal, WSJ Events, MarketWatch, Barron’s, IBD, and other Dow Jones companies. This role is ideal for someone resourceful, proactive, and eager to learn in a fast-paced environment. You’ll gain exposure to high-visibility projects while also rolling up your sleeves on the essential day-to-day tasks that keep brand systems running. As a Brand Design Intern, you will: Assist in creating new brand identities from the ground up (logos, color palettes, typography, art direction) and brand guides, moodboards, and toolkits to communicate with stakeholders, partners, and brand ambassadors. Support senior designers on projects that deliver full brand experiences, including: Visual concepts and mockups Digital and media assets (emails, ads, landing pages, digital signage, social graphics campaign collateral, podcast art) Print and spatial applications (event materials, invitations, onsite design recommendations) Help build and maintain design systems (typography, composition, hierarchy, color theory, etc.) in Figma, including templates, guidelines, and scalable components. Collaborate across teams to ensure design consistency across multiple channels and formats. Conduct competitive research to spot trends, best practices, and opportunities for brand differentiation. Translate research findings into clear insights that guide creative strategy. You Have: Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, or a related field. Strong knowledge of digital design principles and fundamentals; Proficiency in Figma (or similar tools such as Sketch, Adobe Creative Suite). Strong attention to detail and the ability to produce polished, professional work. Comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment with shifting priorities. Resourceful, self-driven, and proactive—able to ask the right questions and seek solutions independently. Open to feedback and eager to learn. Some knowledge of UI/UX, animation, or print is a plus, but not required. Program Eligibility:  Enrollment in a 4-year undergraduate degree program Graduating in Dec 2027 – July 2029 (U.S.)   Does not require sponsorship for employment visa status (now or in the future) in the country where applying. job.title: Summer 2027 Internship Program – Customer and Market Research Intern
job.description:
Job Description:


Application Deadline: November 13, 2026
We encourage you to submit your application as early as possible, as internship applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

AMER Internship Dates: June 7, 2027 – August 13, 2027
(You must be available to work full-time, in-office during this period.)

You Will:


As part of our Customer Insights team, you will support primary research projects providing exposure to qualitative and quantitative research. We are looking for someone who is curious, analytically minded, comfortable learning new tools and methods, and motivated to turn consumer feedback into clear, evidence-based insights.


In this role, you will gain hands-on experience across all phases of the research process from programming quantitative surveys to running statistical analyses and synthesizing findings into insights.


  • Survey Scripting & Execution: Program, test, and field quantitative surveys in Qualtrics, ensuring data quality, branching logic, and seamless respondent user experience.
  • Fieldwork & Study Support: Assist in managing participant recruitment, sample monitoring, fieldwork tracking, and quality assurance across active qualitative and quantitative studies.
  • Data Cleaning & Quantitative Analysis: Clean survey datasets, perform crosstabs and statistical significance testing, and surface key audience trends.
  • Qualitative Synthesis & AI Augmentation: Review interview transcripts and session recordings to extract themes, customer quotes, and pain points leveraging AI-enabled tools.
  • Reporting: Assist in translating data into charts, tables and visualizations and narrative-driven presentations for cross-functional stakeholders.

You Have:


  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Market Research, Marketing, Economics, Social Sciences, Psychology, or a related field

About the Role: As an Experimentation Intern at Dow Jones, you will focus on understanding reader behavior and optimizing the subscription journey through testing. Working closely with cross-functional teams, you will gain hands-on experience designing, tracking, and evaluating A/B and multivariate tests across our iconic consumer brands, including The Wall Street Journal, Barron’s, and MarketWatch. Role based in New York City, NY. Must work from the NYC office 3x a week (Tuesday through Thursday). This internship is embedded within the Subscription Audience team and provides cross-functional exposure to teams across the organization (Acquisition, Engagement, Subscriber Revenue, Retention, Marketing Operations, Brand Marketing, Product, etc.). You Will: Research industry trends and evaluate competitor tactics to pitch your own test ideas, seeing your hypotheses evolve from an initial concept into a live digital experiment. Manage the end-to-end experiment pipeline by setting up cross-platform automations that keep tests moving smoothly from backlog grooming to real-time status updates. Build out a smart, data-rich experiment repository that maps test results to specific site features and conversion levers to easily calculate win rates and overall CVR impact. Partner with analysts to monitor live A/B and multivariate tests, diving into behavioral data and user funnels to uncover what drives readers to subscribe. Translate complex experiment results and performance dashboards into clear, exciting takeaways for cross-functional partners in Product, Engineering, and the Newsroom. You Have: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree, preferably in a quantitative field (Business Analytics, Data Science, Statistics, Economics, or related fields). Coursework or foundational knowledge of experimentation principles (hypothesis testing, A/B testing concepts, or statistical significance). Basic foundational knowledge of SQL and data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau). Exposure to or strong interest in learning experimentation and paywall platforms Proficiency with Excel or Google Sheets for data manipulation and analysis. Ability to synthesize experimental data into clear, easy-to-understand recommendations for non-technical stakeholders. High attention to detail and a strong commitment to data integrity. Curiosity about digital audience behavior, user experience, and subscription growth strategies. Program Eligibility:  Enrollment in a 4-year undergraduate degree program Graduating in Dec 2027 – July 2029 (U.S.)   Does not require sponsorship for employment visa status (now or in the future) in the country where applying. job.description:
Job Description:

We encourage you to submit your application as early as possible, as internship applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

We’re looking for a curious, creative and organized intern to support our audio and video team. .

job.description:
Job Description:


The Wall Street Journal internship program is an opportunity primarily for college juniors to work with our award-winning data and visual investigations teams in New York. Graduate students enrolled in a degree program by the application deadline – October 31– who are returning to school in the fall are also eligible to apply. Graduating seniors should apply to WSJ News Associates.


Applicants should be excited at the prospect of scraping poorly formed websites, reviewing massive datasets, analyzing satellite imagery, geolocating and chronolocating videos and photos, and digging through public records, including FOIA requests. Contribute reporting, data analysis, open-source reporting and visual verification to ambitious investigative projects and quicker-turn visual stories. 

Work cross-functionally with reporters and editors across the newsroom

Be immersed in audience-first visual storytelling that aims to reveal critical information through maps, video, satellite imagery, and interactive graphics.

You have:

An analytical approach to journalism, with experience cleaning, analyzing, and visualizing data to support reporting. 

The ability to scrape and mold unstructured data using tools like Python, R and SQL.
